summary: Write, from the code, how a tester reaches each Mobile item, using the cheap model
logs: paths: 1205 items returned for 1205 asked; 0 areas returned nothing

items.where: Open the side menu, tap Settings, scroll to the Support section, tap About (shows v + version)
steps: From the first screen after signing in, open the side menu (the button at the top left, labelled 'Open menu' in the code; the drawer has a Settings row).
Tap Settings, then scroll down to the Support section.
Tap the About row (it shows the app version on the right).

Look for: the AGI Mobile name, the version, the line 'Private Local Mode and AGI Cloud, on your device.', a Build Info card (Build, Platform, Runtime), a Resources card (Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, Acceptable Use Policy, Open Source Licenses, EU AI Act Transparency) and 'AGI Automation LLC · USA' at the bottom. Compare with Expected: product and company information is shown.
items.needs: none
items.note: The About row is at apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:902 (the Settings code line 623 moved); the About screen content is at apps/mobile/app/(app)/about.tsx:333 as stated. The side menu button's visible text was not found in the code (only its accessibility label 'Open menu' at apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:2323), so the tester must identify it by position.

items.where: Settings > Support > About > Support section: Email Support (always), Contact Support (only when signed in and in Cloud mode), Help Center and Service Status (web pages)
steps: From the side menu, tap Settings, scroll to Support, tap About.
Scroll to the Support card in the About screen.
Tap Email Support: the mail app should open addressed to contact@agiworkforce.com. If no mail app is set up, an alert should appear instead.

If signed in with an AGI Cloud account in Cloud mode, tap Contact Support and check that a support tickets screen opens. Also tap Help Center or Service Status and check that a web page opens. Compare with Expected: a visitor can reach the company.
items.needs: Email Support needs a mail app on the device; Contact Support needs a signed-in AGI Cloud account in Cloud mode
items.note: The Support card is at apps/mobile/app/(app)/about.tsx:266-329 and the Email Support row at line 324-328, which moved from the cited lines 283 and 135. The address comes from apps/mobile/src/features/support/contact.ts. The settings root also has a 'Help Center' row (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:887) and a 'Report App Issue' row, which were not part of this item.

items.where: Menu icon (top left of the chat screen) > Cloud > Log in or sign up
steps: Open the menu icon at the top left of the chat screen to open the side drawer.
Tap the Cloud segment of the Local and Cloud switch while signed out.
On the sign-in screen, type your email in the Email address field and tap Continue, or tap Continue with Google.
Finish the sign-in in the browser sheet or on the code or password screen.
Check that the app is now in AGI Cloud with no sign-in prompt left. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: signed out; an email inbox or a Google account
items.note: The same Cloud segment is also in Settings (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:1063); I did not confirm the drawer's handler calls the sign-in path.

items.where: Menu icon > Cloud > Log in or sign up > type a new email > Continue
steps: Open the sign-in screen as in S3.01.
Type an email address that has no AGI account in the Email address field.
Tap Continue. The app moves to the Create an account screen with your email filled in.
Look for the Create an account screen with a Continue button under the email field. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: signed out; an email address with no AGI account
items.note: The app sends unknown emails to sign-up straight away (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/MobileSignIn.tsx:265-266), so the Create an account instead button only appears for a remembered account.

items.where: Menu icon > Cloud > Log in or sign up > new email > Continue > Continue
steps: Follow S3.02 with a new email and tap Continue on the Create an account screen.
Look for the Verify your email screen and the line that says Enter the code sent to your email address.
Leave the screen without entering a code, then try to use Cloud chat.
Compare with Expected: the account should not be usable until the email is confirmed.
items.needs: signed out; an email inbox you can read
items.note: The app sends the email code as soon as the email is accepted (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/MobileSignUp.tsx:125-126).

items.where: Menu icon > Cloud > Log in or sign up > new email > Continue > Continue > Verify your email
steps: Reach the Verify your email screen as in S3.03.
Tap the Verification code field and type or autofill the code from the email.
Tap Verify and continue.
If the code is wrong, read the red error text, then tap Send a new code and check that a new email arrives.
With the right code, look for the app moving on to the next screen. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: signed out; an email inbox you can read
items.note: This screen accepts only the emailed code; authenticator codes are handled by the sign-in screen, not here.

items.where: Menu icon > Cloud > Log in or sign up > your email > Continue > Enter your password > Forgot password or try another way
steps: Type the email of an existing account with a password and tap Continue.
On the Enter your password screen, tap Forgot password or try another way.
The built-in account screen opens. Its wording comes from Clerk, not this repo.
Look for a reset option that sends a code or link to your email. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: signed out; an account with a password; an email inbox

labels.text: Forgot password or try another way

items.note: The reset request itself runs in Clerk's native view (apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx:384), which is not in this repo.

items.where: Open the password-reset link from your email on this phone > Recover your AGI account > Open Web Account
steps: Open the password-reset link from your email on this phone.
The app opens the Recover your AGI account screen.
Tap Open Web Account. The AGI web account opens in the in-app browser.
Look for a new-password step. The app itself has no password field and does not sign you in. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: signed out; a reset link from email on this phone
items.note: Expected says the password is set in the app, but this screen only hands off to the web (apps/mobile/app/(auth)/reset-password.tsx:28-38).

items.where: Menu icon > Cloud > Log in or sign up
steps: Open the sign-in screen.
Look above the Email address field for Continue with Google and Continue with GitHub. On iPhone builds, Continue with Apple may also show.
Tap Continue with Google and finish in the browser sheet.
Look for the app signed in to AGI Cloud. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: signed out; a Google or GitHub account (an outside account)
items.note: The providers come from EXPO_PUBLIC_AGI_AUTH_PROVIDERS and default to Google and GitHub (packages/client/client-runtime/src/authProviders.ts:17).

items.where: Menu icon > Cloud > Log in or sign up > Email address > Continue
steps: Open the sign-in screen.
Type a work email for an organisation that uses single sign-on in the Email address field.
Tap Continue.
Look for a browser sheet opening your organisation's sign-in page. The app has no separate SSO button.
Finish there and check the app is signed in. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: signed out; an account in an SSO organisation
items.note: The app starts SSO only when the account lookup returns enterprise_sso (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/MobileSignIn.tsx:202-203); which organisations are set up was not checked.

items.where: Log in or sign up > Email address > Continue (the browser sheet that opens)
steps: Type a work email on a company domain that has single sign-on set up, and tap Continue.
Look whether the browser sheet opens the company's sign-in page without asking you for an organisation name.
Compare with Expected: entering the work email should route you to that organisation.
items.needs: a work email on an SSO domain
items.note: The domain lookup runs on Clerk's side; the app only reads the enterprise_sso answer (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/MobileSignIn.tsx:202-203).

items.needs: a passkey registered on this phone
items.note: Searched for passkey sign-in: passkeySignInEnabled (packages/client/client-runtime/src/authProviders.ts) is not called by any file in apps/mobile, and the sign-in screen has no passkey button; only the error text in apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/authErrorMessage.ts:48-49 mentions it.

items.where: Menu icon > Cloud > Log in or sign up > your email > Continue > Enter your password > Continue
steps: Sign in with an account that has two-step sign-in turned on.
Enter the email, tap Continue, enter the password, and tap Continue.
If the second step is an email code, look for Check your email, type the code, and tap Continue. You can also tap Use an email code instead.
If the second step is not an email code, the built-in account screen opens. Look for More sign-in options and backup codes there.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an account with two-step sign-in turned on
items.note: The plan says the owner still has to enable Authenticator and Backup codes in the Clerk Dashboard, and backup codes show only in Clerk's native view, which is not in this repo.

items.where: Open the password-reset link from your email on this phone > Recover your AGI account > Lost Your Email or Two-Factor Device?
steps: Open the recovery link from your email on this phone while signed out.
Look for the Recover your AGI account screen.
Tap Lost Your Email or Two-Factor Device?. The account recovery page opens in the in-app browser.
Look for the recovery steps on that web page. The app does not restore access itself. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: signed out; a reset link from email on this phone

labels.text: Lost Your Email or Two-Factor Device?

items.note: Only an https link on the AGI host ending in /auth/reset-password opens this screen (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:931-938).

items.where: Menu icon > Cloud > Log in or sign up > type an email > Continue
steps: Enter an email that has no AGI account and tap Continue. The app moves to Create an account with the email filled in.
On Create an account, enter an email that already has an account and tap Continue.
Look for the message This email already has an account. and the Log in instead link.
Tap Log in instead and check it returns you to sign in. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: signed out; one unused email and one email with an account
items.note: Create an account instead appears only for a remembered account that no longer exists (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/MobileSignIn.tsx:265-270 and 753).

items.where: Menu icon > Cloud > sign in (S3.01) > Review the Terms for AGI Cloud
steps: Sign in to an AGI Cloud account that has not accepted the current Terms, or one where the Terms version has changed.
Look for the Review the Terms for AGI Cloud screen with the line Version dated and the checkbox.
Tap Read Terms or Read Privacy Policy to open them.
Tick the checkbox and tap Agree and continue.
Look for the app opening AGI Cloud without the screen coming back. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account whose Terms are not yet accepted

labels.text: Review the Terms for AGI Cloud

items.note: The Terms screen appears only after the age answer is confirmed (apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx:172-176).

items.where: First launch > Your age
steps: Use a fresh install, since the age answer stays on the device.
On the Your age screen, type a number in Enter your age and tap Continue.
Do the under-age check last, on a throwaway install: an age under the minimum shows the refusal screen with Continue in Local Mode.
With an adult age, look for the app moving on to onboarding. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a fresh install; a throwaway install for the under-age test
items.note: Signed-in users also get a Your age question on the AccountAgeCheck screen (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/AccountAgeCheck.tsx:66).

items.where: First launch > Start chatting > I understand, continue > What should AGI call you?
steps: On a fresh install, tap Start chatting on the intro screen.
If the disclosure appears, read it and tap I understand, continue.
On What should AGI call you?, type a name in Your name and tap Continue, or tap Skip for now.
Open Settings and look for the name at the top. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a fresh install; no account needed
items.note: The name is saved to both local and Cloud personalization (apps/mobile/app/(public)/onboarding.tsx:317-319).

items.where: First launch > Start chatting > I understand, continue > What best describes your work?
steps: On a fresh install, tap Start chatting, then accept the disclosure if it appears.
On What should AGI call you?, type in the What best describes your work? field (placeholder For example, product design).
Tap Continue.
Open Settings and look for the saved work description. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a fresh install; no account needed
items.note: The answer is free text, not a list of roles, and saved as occupation; whether replies use it was not checked.

items.where: Settings > Memory > Import memories icon (top right of the Memory screen)
steps: Open Settings and tap Memory. Memory must be turned on for the import icon to show.
Tap the import icon at the top right of the Memory screen.
Pick a source (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or Other), then paste memories or tap Choose a text or JSON file.
Tap Preview, then the import button, and look for the Added memories message and Done. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a text or JSON export from another assistant, or pasted text

labels.text: Choose a text or JSON file

items.note: The import icon has no visible word (its label is Import memories in apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/memory.tsx:720), and the import button text is a translation key that was not checked in the locale files.

items.needs: a desktop app signed in to Managed Cloud, and a phone
items.note: The pairing screen sits under Settings > Remote control > Connections, but FEATURES.companion is false (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:16), so the row is hidden and the Remote screen shows FeatureUnavailable (apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/index.tsx:183); the pairing screen cannot be reached in this build.

items.where: Settings > Notifications > Turn on notifications
steps: Open Settings and tap Notifications.
Look for the Turn on notifications card: Get alerts when an agent needs approval, finishes or fails.
Tap Turn on notifications and choose Don't Allow in the system prompt.
Look for the card to change to Open Settings, then open the screen again later. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a phone where notifications are not yet allowed
items.note: After a denial the card offers Open Settings, which opens the phone's settings (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/notifications/index.tsx:216).

items.where: First launch > Start chatting
steps: On a fresh install, read the intro screen notes about settings, local chats and AI mistakes.
Tap Start chatting, then accept the disclosure if it appears.
Fill in or skip What should AGI call you?
On the device step, tap Continue (or Continue without downloading) to reach the chat.
Look for the first chat screen opening. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a fresh install
items.note: Onboarding has no first-chat tips; the empty chat screen was not checked for them.

items.where: First launch > Continue without downloading > chat in Local mode; later Settings > Data Controls > Sync to AGI Cloud > Sync Local Chats to Cloud
steps: On a fresh install, skip sign-in at the device step with Continue without downloading, then send a message in Local mode.
Check that the chat works without an account, and that local chats stay on the device.
Later, sign in (S3.01), then open Settings and tap Data Controls.
Under Sync to AGI Cloud, tap Sync Local Chats to Cloud, read the summary, and confirm.
Compare with Expected: the chosen chat text is copied and the local originals stay on the device.
items.needs: a fresh install for the guest step; a Cloud account for the sync step
items.note: The sync copies chat text only; files and memory stay on the device (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/index.tsx:561).

items.where: Side menu > New chat
steps: Open the side menu.
Tap New chat.
Look for an empty chat screen with a message box ready to type in, not an old conversation.
items.needs: none
items.note: The composer's accessibility labels are New local chat or New AGI Cloud chat (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx).

items.where: Side menu > Recents > tap a conversation title
steps: Open the side menu.
Under Recents, tap a past conversation.
Look for its earlier messages and a message box that lets you continue it.
items.needs: an existing conversation

items.where: Side menu > Search icon (Search)
steps: Open the side menu.
Tap the Search icon in the header.
Type a word that appears in a conversation title or message.
Look for matching past conversations and tap one to open it.
items.needs: at least one past conversation containing the word
items.note: Search opens the route apps/mobile/app/(app)/search.tsx; I read the button and handler but not the result list.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Archived Chats
steps: Open Settings.
Find the Cloud group and tap Archived Chats.
Look for a list of archived conversations.
Try opening, restoring and deleting one, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with at least one archived chat
items.note: The route is apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/archived-chats.tsx. I did not confirm the restore and delete controls, or how Settings is opened.

items.where: Side menu > Recents (pinned rows show a pin icon)
steps: Open the side menu.
Find a conversation that has been pinned, shown with a small pin icon.
Tap it and confirm it opens the conversation.
items.needs: a pinned conversation
items.note: I found the pin icon in apps/mobile/src/features/drawer/components/DrawerContent.tsx but no separate Pinned section or filter label. Expected says a pinned section or filter, so check whether one exists.

items.where: Side menu > Projects
steps: Open the side menu.
Tap Projects.
Look for the list of projects.
Tap New project and check that a create form opens.
items.needs: none

items.where: Side menu > Projects > tap a project
steps: Open the side menu and tap Projects.
Tap a project name.
Look for the project name, its instructions entry, and tabs named Chats and Sources (Work, Artifacts and Routines appear only in some cases).
items.needs: a project
items.note: I did not confirm the exact visible text for the description summary.

items.where: Side menu > Projects > tap a project > Chats
steps: Open the project as in S4.07.
Tap the Chats tab.
Look for the project's conversations and tap one to open it.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a project with at least one conversation

items.where: Side menu > Projects > tap a project > Sources
steps: Open the project as in S4.07.
Tap the Sources tab.
Look for the project's files and the controls to add or remove them.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a project and a file to upload
items.note: I found the tab but not the add or remove controls inside it.

items.where: Side menu > Projects > tap a project > instructions entry
steps: Open the project as in S4.07.
Tap the instructions entry on the project home (ProjectInstructionsEntry).
Edit the instructions and save.
Open a chat in that project and check the instructions apply.
items.needs: a project the account can edit (not archived or shared with it)
items.note: The instructions entry only shows when the project can be edited or already has instructions. I did not find its visible words.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Work
steps: Open the side menu.
Tap AGI Work (it may sit under the More item).
Look for the New task button and a field to state a goal.
Check that you can reach your recent work from this screen.
items.needs: a plan that includes AGI Work
items.note: The item is hidden unless the plan and grant allow it. I did not find a visible word for the More item.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Work > filter Running
steps: Open AGI Work as in S4.13.
Tap the Running filter.
Look for tasks that are in progress and their live status.
Tap Finished and check that only finished tasks remain.
items.needs: a running AGI Work task
items.note: The filter chips are All, Needs you, Running and Finished.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Work > tap a task
steps: Open AGI Work and tap a task.
Look for the status, Started on, Mode, Model, and the sections Latest output and Activity.
Look for the action buttons (Pause this task, Resume this task, Stop this task) and any pending approval.
items.needs: a task
a task waiting for approval
items.note: No separate approvals inbox found. The nearest candidate is the Needs you filter in AGI Work (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/runPresentation.ts), and approvals are resolved from the task sheet. I did not confirm that the filter gathers every pending approval.

items.where: Side menu > Schedules
steps: Open the side menu and tap Schedules.
Look for the list of schedules and the Create schedule button.
Open a schedule's actions and check for Run now, Pause or Resume, and Delete.
Compare the cadence and status shown on each card with Expected.
items.needs: a schedule (create one first if none exists)
items.note: The schedules screen is titled Scheduled runs. I did not confirm how the card actions menu is opened.

items.where: Side menu > Schedules > tap a schedule
steps: Open Schedules and tap a schedule card.
Look for the prompt, the cadence and the next run.
Expand the run history on the card and check it lists past runs.
items.needs: a schedule that has run at least once
items.note: The history toggle's visible label was not found. Check that the card's detail shows the prompt.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Code
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Code.
Look for the list of coding sessions.
Start a new session and check that a sheet offers Task, Repository and Network access.
items.needs: a Cloud account allowed to use AGI Code
items.note: The new-session button's visible words and the runtime choice were not found.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Code > tap a session
steps: Open AGI Code and tap a session.
Look for the transcript and any file changes or diffs.
Type a message in the composer at the bottom and check that it steers the next turn.
items.needs: an existing coding session
items.note: The route is apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/code/[threadId].tsx. I did not find the visible words for the diff view.

items.where: AGI Code > Add device (devices section)
steps: Open AGI Code and find the devices section.
Tap Add device to pair a new device, or open the Remote screen.
Look for linked devices with status, and the Disconnect control.
items.needs: a second device or the desktop app to pair
items.note: The Remote screen has no drawer item of its own. I did not confirm the link from AGI Code to it, and I did not find a rename control.

items.needs: a session running on a second linked device
items.note: The viewer route is apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/code/[threadId].tsx, the same as S4.20. I did not find how a remote session is opened from a device.

items.where: Side menu > Library
steps: Open the side menu and tap Library.
Look for files, images, videos and documents, and the filter chips.
Tap a filter such as Images and check that the list narrows.
Open an item and look for open or download actions.
items.needs: some generated or uploaded files
items.note: The download action was not confirmed.

items.where: Side menu > Library > Artifacts
steps: Open Library.
Tap the Artifacts filter chip.
Look for the list of artifacts.
Tap one and check it opens (its label starts with Open artifact).
items.needs: at least one generated artifact

items.where: Side menu > Images
steps: Open the side menu and tap Images.
Look for the Create an image section with the Describe an image box.
Type a prompt, check the style and size options, and tap Create image.
Look for the new image and the list of your images.
items.needs: a Cloud account allowed to create images
items.note: I did not confirm the style or size options on this screen.

items.where: Side menu > Images (Your images), or Library > Images
steps: Open the side menu and tap Images, and look for Your images.
Or open Library and tap the Images filter chip.
Check that generated and uploaded images both appear.
Open one and look for download and remix actions.
items.needs: some images
items.note: The remix action was not confirmed.

items.where: Side menu > Library > Images (media jobs list)
steps: Open Library and choose a generation filter such as Images.
Look for the media jobs list.
Check each job's status: Queued, Generating, Failed or Done.
Tap a finished job and check it links to its result.
items.needs: at least one image or video generation job
items.note: The media jobs section is rendered in apps/mobile/src/features/library/index.tsx when the filter is a generation filter. I did not confirm which chips count as generation filters, and I did not find the list heading.

items.where: Open menu > More > Reports
steps: Tap the "Open menu" button to open the side drawer.
Tap "More" to expand the folded items, then tap "Reports".
Look for the "Reports" title and a list of report rows, each showing its title, date, source count and model.
Tap one report row to open it, then check for its sections, the "Sources retrieved" line and the sources appendix, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account in Managed Cloud mode, with at least one research report (run Research from the composer first)
items.note: The Reports item is folded under More and only shows in Cloud mode when signed in; signed out it shows "Sign in to read your reports". The "Open menu" button is at apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx; I did not trace its onPress line by line to confirm it opens the drawer.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors
steps: Tap "Open menu", then tap "Settings" at the bottom of the drawer.
Scroll to the "Cloud" section and tap "Connectors".
Look for the heading "Connect your tools to AGI Cloud", the "Connected" filter and one card per connector showing its status.
Tap a connector, then check for the "Connect" or "Disconnect" button and the "Reconnect" button when a connection needs it.
items.needs: a signed-in Managed Cloud account; a third-party account (for example Google) to complete a real connection
items.note: Connectors are also reachable at the route /(app)/connectors. The Cloud rows only appear when Cloud mode is available, and the Reconnect label is in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/index.tsx.

items.where: Settings > General > Models, then "Change model" or "Browse Models"
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings", then "General".
Tap the "Models" row. The screen titled "Models" opens.
Tap "Change model" at the top card, or "Browse Models" at the bottom, to open the model picker.
Look for the picker groups "Recent", "Favorites" and "On device", then pick a model and check that it becomes the selected model, as in Expected.
items.needs: none for the picker; the Cloud models need a plan that includes them
items.note: Capabilities, context size and price were not found as visible text in ModelPickerSheet.tsx or models.tsx (searched for context, price and pricing), so the picker may not show them. The screen is also reached from the composer's model control (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx).

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings", then scroll to the "Cloud" section and tap "Usage".
Look for the "Plan usage" section with its limit buckets and reset times.
Check the "Credit balances" card for the included, bonus and purchased credit amounts.
Scroll to "Where your usage went" and try the day, week and month options, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in Managed Cloud account; a paid account to see plan limits
items.note: The session and weekly bucket names come from managedUsageBucketLabel, which I did not open. The Usage screen also shows "Buy credits" and "Use reset" buttons that change balances, so do not press them in a test.

items.where: Settings > Account > Subscription
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings", then the "Account" section, and tap "Subscription".
Check the "Your plan" card for the "Current plan" value, the "Renews" or "Access ends" line, and the "Billing" row.
For a paid plan, look for the "Manage billing" row. Its presence depends on the portal flag.
Check the plan buttons ("Upgrade plan", "Adjust plan" or "Choose plan") and compare with Expected. Invoices and card details were not found in the code.
items.needs: a signed-in account; a paid store-billed account to see renewal and manage rows
items.note: Partial by design: FEATURES.billing is false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts, which disables the billing portal link (portalEnabled in cloud-billing/index.tsx). Invoices, payment method and card text were searched for and not found, so expect those to be missing. Plan changes go through the App Store or Google Play; web-billed plans show "Managed on the web".

items.where: Settings > Profile card, or Settings > Device > Appearance / Notifications, or Settings > Assistant > Personalization
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings".
Tap the profile card at the top of the page to open the "Profile" screen, then look at the name and details shown there.
Back in "Settings", tap "Appearance" under "Device", change a theme option, and go back to check that the choice stays.
Tap "Notifications" under "Device" or "Personalization" under "Assistant", change one setting, then reopen it and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account to see cloud rows such as Personalization
items.note: The "Profile" screen is at apps/mobile/app/(app)/profile/index.tsx, and the profile card in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx opens it. Settings is the drawer item labelled "Settings" (translation key in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/common.json). Whether each change saves was not checked, since that is behaviour.

items.where: Settings > Support > Report App Issue, and Settings > Support > Help Center
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings", then scroll to the "Support" section.
Tap "Report App Issue", then choose a type among "Bug Report", "Feature Request" or "General Feedback".
Type a message into the text box and check that the button reads "Submit Feedback" or "Email Feedback" as Expected describes.
Go back, tap "Help Center" and check that it opens the help page in the browser.
items.needs: none for the form; a network connection to submit
items.note: The form submits to the app's feedback endpoint or opens the email app, depending on configuration. Do not press Submit unless the tester is allowed to send a real report. The section label "Support" is in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx.

items.where: Chat tab top bar on the first screen after sign-in: 'Open navigation drawer' button at the left, 'Chat or Work' switch in the middle, temporary chat toggle at the right
steps: Sign in and open the Chat tab (first screen).
Look at the top bar: menu button at the left, Chat/Work switch in the middle, temporary chat toggle at the right.
Tap the menu button to open the drawer and check the shell is still shown.
Compare with Expected: a persistent header with the primary actions for this view.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The Chat tab bar shows no conversation title or brand text in the code read; the brand mark is only in the drawer.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Local' / 'Cloud' switch at the top of the drawer; product areas are in the drawer list below
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Look at the switch under the search icon: it shows 'Local' and 'Cloud'.
Tap 'Cloud' (or 'Local') and watch the drawer list and the Chat screen change.
Compare with Expected: the user can switch between product areas or modes from the shell.
items.needs: a signed-in account; Cloud needs an account with cloud unlocked
items.note: Switching to Cloud is blocked when cloudUnlocked is false.

items.where: Settings > 'Workspace' > 'Personal' row and any team rows (not in the drawer)
steps: Open the drawer with 'Open navigation drawer' and tap 'Settings'.
Tap the 'Workspace' row.
Look at the list: 'Personal' plus any team workspaces, and which one is active.
Tap another workspace row and check for the 'Workspace changed' alert, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account; a team workspace in the same account to see a second row
items.note: Expected says the switcher is in the shell, but the drawer has no workspace control; the switch is on the Settings Workspace screen. The file useWorkspaceSwitcher.ts named in Code no longer exists; the switch calls switchWorkspace in apps/mobile/src/features/team/switchWorkspace.ts.

items.where: 'Open navigation drawer' button at the top left of the Chat tab (opens and closes the drawer)
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer' to open the sidebar.
Tap outside the drawer or swipe it closed to hide it.
Tap the button again to expand it.
Compare with Expected: the navigation hides and expands again.
items.needs: phone width (on a wide window the sidebar is permanent)
items.note: On the permanent tablet sidebar no collapse-to-rail control was found in the code read.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Search' icon at the top right of the drawer (opens the Search screen, not an inline filter)
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Tap the search icon at the top right of the drawer.
Type part of a chat title in the search field.
Compare with Expected: results filter to matching conversations.
items.needs: a signed-in account with some chats
items.note: The drawer has no inline search field; searching happens on the separate Search screen (apps/mobile/app/(app)/search.tsx).

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'New chat' (first row in the drawer list)
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Tap 'New chat'.
Look at the Chat screen: a new empty chat should open.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: 'New chat' is only in the drawer; no New chat button was found in the Chat tab top bar.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Pinned' heading (appears after the Projects section, above 'Recents')
steps: Long press a chat row in the drawer and choose 'Pin'.
Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Look for the 'Pinned' heading and the pinned chat under it.
Compare with Expected: pinned items sit in their own section.
items.needs: a chat to pin
items.note: In the code the Pinned section comes after the Projects section, not at the very top of the list.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Recents' heading and its chat rows
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Find the 'Recents' heading.
Tap a conversation row under it.
Compare with Expected: the conversation opens.
items.needs: a signed-in account with chats

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Projects' heading > project name > chevron 'Show chats in' the project
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Under 'Projects', tap the chevron beside a project that has chats.
Look for the chats listed under that project and the 'See all' link.
Compare with Expected: recent chats are shown grouped under their projects.
items.needs: a project with chats in it
items.note: The Projects section is on by default (FEATURES.projects is true in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts).

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'See all chats' > the chats list with headings 'Pinned', 'Today', 'Yesterday', 'This Week', 'Older'
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Tap 'See all chats' at the bottom of Recents.
Look at the date headings on the chats list.
Compare with Expected: Today, Yesterday, This week, Older.
items.needs: chats from several days
items.note: The drawer itself does not group by date; grouping is on the chats list. The code heading is 'This Week' (capital W), and the date headings are literal English, not translated.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > a chat title under 'Recents' or 'Pinned'
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Look at a conversation row: its title, a dot if unread, a pin icon if pinned.
Tap the active-looking row and note its highlight.
Tap another row and check that the chat opens and the highlight moves.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least two chats
items.note: The row accessibility hint 'Long press for more actions' is a literal string in apps/mobile/src/features/drawer/components/DrawerContent.tsx.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Projects' heading > a project name
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Tap a project name under 'Projects'.
Look at the project page that opens.
Compare with Expected: the project opens.
items.needs: a project
items.note: No long-press actions were found on the drawer project row; project actions live on the project page (apps/mobile/app/(app)/projects/settings/[id] route).

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'More' > 'AGI Work'
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Tap 'More' if needed, then tap 'AGI Work'.
Look at the task cards: each shows its state and origin.
Tap a card and check that the task opens.
items.needs: a Cloud account with AGI Work enabled
items.note: The AGI Work row is in the folded More list and shows only when FEATURES.cloudTasks and showAgiWork are on.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Search' icon > type a word; result rows show a kind icon (chat, project, file, library, artifact, destination)
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer'.
Tap the search icon, then type a word.
Look at the icon at the left of each result row.
Compare with Expected: each row shows its resource type.
items.needs: a signed-in account with chats or projects
items.note: Kind icons appear only while searching, and the icon in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/ChatsListScreen.tsx has no accessibility label in the code read. Drawer rows show no type icon, only a pin and an unread dot.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'More' > 'AGI Work' > 'Running' filter
steps: Start a cloud task that is running.
Open the drawer, tap 'More' if needed, then 'AGI Work'.
Tap the 'Running' filter.
Compare with Expected: the running task is marked as running, and its card label includes the state.
items.needs: a Cloud account with a running task
items.note: Drawer chat rows show no running marker in the code read; the marker is on AGI Work task cards only.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'More' > 'AGI Work' > 'Needs you' filter
steps: Open the drawer, tap 'More' if needed, then 'AGI Work'.
Tap the 'Needs you' filter.
Look for a card with a warning border and the line 'Waiting for your approval' or 'Waiting for connector input'.
Compare with Expected: blocked items are marked.
items.needs: a Cloud task waiting for approval or input
items.note: The drawer chat rows have no needs-input marker in the code read.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > a chat row with a dot; or 'See all chats' > 'Unread' filter
steps: Open the drawer and find a row with a small dot (unread).
Long press the row and tap 'Mark as read'.
Look again: the dot should be gone.
Compare with Expected: unread marker clears when read.
items.needs: a chat with a new reply you have not opened
items.note: The code read does not confirm that opening a chat clears the dot by itself; only the Mark as read action was confirmed.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > long press a chat row (actions sheet); or 'See all chats' > the row's 'More actions for' button
steps: Long press a chat row in the drawer.
Read the actions: Rename, Pin, Move to project, Duplicate, Mark as read, Archive (Cloud), Delete.
Or open 'See all chats' and tap the row's 'More actions for' button.
Compare with Expected: share, rename, pin, archive, move and delete are present.
items.needs: a signed-in account with chats; Archive and Share show only for Cloud chats
items.note: Drawer rows have no visible overflow button; the ⋯ button exists only on the chats list. Share is shown only for non-temporary Cloud chats.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > long press a chat row > 'Rename'; the title becomes an editable 'Chat title' field
steps: Long press a chat row in the drawer.
Tap 'Rename'.
Type a new title and press the Done key on the keyboard.
Compare with Expected: the new title shows in the row and persists after reopening.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a chat
items.note: No Escape-key cancel was found in the code; the inline field cancels on blur, and Done saves.

items.where: 'Go back' button on screens that have one (for example the Notifications screen); Android hardware back button
steps: Open Settings, then open a sub-page such as Workspace.
Tap the back control at the top left (labelled 'Go back' on screens that set it) or swipe from the left edge on iPhone.
Look at the screen: it should return to the previous screen.
Look for a forward control: none was found in the code read.
items.needs: none
items.note: No forward navigation control was found in the code read; back is the only in-app history control.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > search icon > type 'Notifications' > the 'Notifications' result (phone); on tablet the 'Open notifications' pip button
steps: Open the drawer and tap the search icon.
Type 'Notifications' and tap the result.
Look at the list: unread rows are marked 'Unread,' in their label.
Tap 'Mark as read' on a row, or 'Mark all as read', and check the unread state clears.
items.needs: an account with notifications
items.note: On a phone the drawer menu button shows the unread count in its label but does not open notifications; the notification route is reached through search.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Settings' > the profile header at the top > 'Profile' screen
steps: Tap the button labelled 'Open navigation drawer', then tap 'Settings'.
Tap your profile header at the top of Settings.
Look at the 'Profile' screen: 'Chats' and 'Messages' counts and the AGI Cloud section with 'Subscription' and 'Log Out'.
Tap 'Log Out' and check the confirmation text, then dismiss it without confirming. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The drawer footer has no profile control; the entry is the Settings profile header.

items.where: Settings > 'About' > 'Support' section ('Help Center', 'Service Status', 'Report App Issue')
steps: Open the drawer, tap 'Settings', then 'About'.
Look at the 'Support' section.
Tap 'Report App Issue' to check that the feedback form opens, then go back.
Compare with Expected: help centre, support contact, feedback and shortcuts are in one place.
items.needs: none
items.note: No keyboard-shortcuts item and no separate support-contact item was found on the About screen; the 'Support' heading is the only group.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > 'Upgrade' chip at the bottom of the drawer, next to 'Settings'
steps: Sign in to a Free Cloud account and switch the drawer to Cloud.
Open the drawer and look at the bottom: 'Upgrade' appears beside 'Settings'.
Tap 'Upgrade'.
Compare with Expected: the plan upgrade flow opens (currently the Subscription screen).
items.needs: a Free account signed in on a build with native purchases, in Cloud mode
items.note: Owner hold: FEATURES.billing is false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts, so Upgrade leads to the Subscription screen (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/cloud-billing.tsx), not a live purchase flow.

items.where: Any screen after sign-in: turn off the device's Wi-Fi or network
steps: Turn off Wi-Fi or mobile data on the device.
Look at the top of the screen for the banner.
Turn the network back on.
Compare with Expected: the banner clears when back online.
items.needs: a device or simulator whose network you can switch off

labels.text: You're offline. Local chats still work on this device.

items.where: Any main screen on a phone-width window (for example Chat) > tap the menu button at the top left of the header, labelled "Open navigation drawer" for screen readers
steps: Sign in and open the Chat screen on a phone-width window (or an iPhone).
Tap the menu button at the top left of the header. It has no visible words; its accessibility label is "Open navigation drawer".
Check that navigation slides in from the left as a drawer over the content.
Press Escape on a keyboard, or tap the dimmed area beside the drawer, or use the Back gesture or key.
Check that the drawer closes and focus returns to the content behind it, as Expected says.
items.needs: a Free or paid account signed in; phone width (below the tablet split-view threshold)
items.note: "Open navigation drawer" is an accessibility label, not visible text; the button shows only a menu icon. The code opens the drawer with a Back/Escape handler (src/features/shell/useDrawerDismiss.ts), but I did not confirm from code where focus lands after closing.

items.where: Tablet or wide window (iPad, or a resized window wide enough for the permanent sidebar) > the navigation sidebar stays on the left beside the content instead of a phone drawer
steps: Open the app on an iPad, or resize the window to a wide size.
Sign in and look at the left edge of the Chat screen.
Check that the navigation list stays visible next to the content.
Make the window narrow again and check that navigation returns to a slide-in drawer.
items.needs: a tablet, or a window wide enough for the permanent sidebar
items.note: This is a layout rule with no control of its own: src/shared/hooks/useResponsiveLayout.ts sets usesPersistentDrawer when the viewport is wide enough for the drawer width plus a minimum content width, and app/(app)/_layout.tsx uses drawerType 'permanent' when it is true. I did not read the exact width constants in this pass, and I did not confirm whether the menu button is hidden on the permanent sidebar.

items.where: Open a temporary cloud chat > its menu > "Share link"; then open the copied link on the phone (the https://agiworkforce.com/open/... address opens the app)
steps: Sign in with Cloud mode on, and open a temporary cloud chat.
Open the chat's action menu from the screen header.
Tap "Share link" and copy the link that appears.
Open that link on the phone, or in another app that opens links.
Check that the same chat opens directly in the app, as Expected says.
items.needs: a paid or Cloud account; a temporary cloud chat; a second app to open the link from (for example Notes)
items.note: Share link appears only for temporary cloud chats in the code I read. I did not find a stable link control for projects or tasks in apps/mobile, and the link route apps/mobile/app/(app)/open/[target]/[id].tsx redirects to home for an invalid target or id. The app scheme is agiworkforce and the https://agiworkforce.com/open/ prefix is declared in apps/mobile/app.config.js.

items.where: Open a chat or project that is gone or not in this account (for example from an old link) > "This chat is not available" or "Project unavailable" message; an address the app does not have > "Page Not Found" with "Go Home"
steps: Sign in with an account that cannot see a chat or project (or use one that was deleted).
Open that chat or project from its link.
Look for the loading state first ("Loading Cloud project" or the message skeleton), then for the unavailable screen.
Check that the message on screen matches Expected: a clear unavailable message, not a blank screen.
For a missing page, open an address the app does not have and check that "Page Not Found" appears with a "Go Home" button.
items.needs: a second account, or a conversation or project that was deleted; for the missing page, a way to open an unknown address
items.note: I did not confirm how a person types an unknown address into the app, so the missing-page step may need a tester-side link. The loading text "Loading Cloud project" is in apps/mobile/app/(app)/projects/[id].tsx, and the chat loading state is a message skeleton in apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx.

items.where: Settings > Device > Appearance: switch between Light and Dark; page and panel backgrounds change
steps: Sign in and open the side menu, then tap Settings.
Open Device > Appearance.
Tap Light, then Dark.
Compare page background with the panel and card backgrounds in each theme with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Token names are in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/tokens.ts; the cited ThemeVars.tsx path was not checked for a UI effect.

items.where: Raised panels: long-press a chat in the side menu to open its action sheet, and open Create Schedule
steps: Sign in and open the side menu.
Long-press a chat row.
Compare the action sheet panel with the page behind it in Light and Dark.
Open the Rename dialog from the sheet and compare its panel background.
items.needs: a chat in the side menu
items.note: Only the visible result is checkable; the elevated token name is not shown in the UI.

items.where: Any screen text: Settings > Device > Appearance, then Dark, then compare primary and muted text
steps: Open Settings > Device > Appearance.
Tap Dark.
Read the bold option names and the grey description lines.
Compare how readable the grey text is with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The 4.5:1 contrast claim needs a contrast meter; the tester can only judge visibly.

items.where: Divider lines between rows: Settings > Device > Appearance
steps: Open Settings > Device > Appearance.
Look at the thin lines between the System, Light and Dark rows.
Switch Light and Dark and compare the line strength.
Compare the lines with Expected (subtle, not heavy).
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Device > Accent Color, then pick a colour swatch
steps: Sign in and open the side menu, then tap Settings.
Open Device > Accent Color.
Tap a colour such as Blue or Rose.
Check that the selected accent shows on the selected mark and on buttons, and that its text is readable.
items.needs: none
items.note: Accent is turned off when the system high-contrast setting is on (apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/useTheme.ts).

items.where: Message status text: a message that is queued offline or fails to send in the chat
steps: Turn off Wi-Fi and mobile data on the phone.
Send a chat message.
Look for the status text under the message (Message queued offline or Message failed to send).
Compare the success, warning and error colours with Expected in Light and Dark.
items.needs: a phone you can turn offline
items.note: The labels are accessibility labels; the visible text was not confirmed.

items.where: Font families: visible in any heading and body text across the app
steps: Open Settings > Device > Appearance and read the Theme heading and option names.
Open a chat and read the reply text.
Compare the font look with Expected (one sans, one editorial, one monospace).
items.needs: none
items.note: The font declarations are in apps/mobile/tailwind.config.js and apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx; the editorial face was not confirmed in any screen.

items.where: Heading sizes: the Appearance screen title and the Theme heading
steps: Open Settings > Device > Appearance.
Compare the size and weight of the screen title with the Theme heading.
Open another settings screen, such as Accent Color, and compare the title style.
Check the headings match across screens.
items.needs: none

items.where: Body text size: no in-app text-size control was found; device text size changes app text
steps: Open Settings > Device > Appearance and read the description lines.
Change the phone's text size in the phone's own settings.
Reopen the app and compare the body text size.
items.needs: a phone where you can change text size
items.note: No in-app text-size setting was found; the code reads the device font scale (apps/mobile/src/shared/components/TextScaleBoundary.tsx).

items.where: Small caption text: the grey description line under each Appearance option
steps: Open Settings > Device > Appearance.
Read the grey line under Light: Bright neutral interface.
Compare its size with the bold option name above it.
Check it is at least as large as 12 px and easy to read.
items.needs: none

items.where: Code text in a chat reply: any reply that contains a code block
steps: Ask the chat for a short code sample.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare the code text with the body text around it.
Check the code uses a monospace face and a different size.
items.needs: a Free or paid account
items.note: The monospace family is declared in apps/mobile/tailwind.config.js; the code block copy control was not matched to a visible label.

items.where: Line spacing in a chat reply that has several lines
steps: Ask the chat a question that gets a multi-line answer.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Look at the gap between lines in one paragraph.
Compare the line spacing with Expected.
items.needs: a Free or paid account

items.where: Paragraph gaps in a chat reply with several paragraphs
steps: Ask the chat for a reply with three or more paragraphs.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Measure the gap between two paragraphs by eye.
Check the gap is the same between every pair.
items.needs: a Free or paid account

items.where: Bullet-list indentation in a chat reply
steps: Ask the chat for a nested bullet list.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Look at the indent of the first and second levels.
Check each level indents by the same step.
items.needs: a Free or paid account

items.where: Padding inside a code block in a chat reply
steps: Ask the chat for a short code sample.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Look at the space between the code text and the edge of its box.
Compare the padding on the top, bottom and sides.
items.needs: a Free or paid account
items.note: The copy control label for code blocks was not confirmed.

items.where: Table cell padding in a chat reply that contains a table
steps: Ask the chat for a small table, such as three columns and three rows.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Look at the space inside each cell.
Compare the padding across cells.
items.needs: a Free or paid account
items.note: Cell padding is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageContentRenderer.tsx.

items.where: Space between two chat turns (one question and one reply, then the next question)
steps: Send a first message in a chat and wait for the reply.
Send a second message.
Measure the gap between the turns.
Check it matches the gap used between other turns.
items.needs: a Free or paid account

items.where: Chat: under an AI reply, its action row (Good response, Bad response, Copy Message)
steps: Send a message and wait for the reply.
Look at the action row below the reply.
Compare the gap between the reply text and the action row with Expected.
Check the row sits the same distance below each reply.
items.needs: a Free or paid account
items.note: How the action row is opened was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: Chat screen: the message box at the bottom of the screen
steps: Sign in and open the chat screen.
Tap into the message box.
Look at the space between the box edge and the typed text and buttons.
Compare the padding with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: No fixed visible words for the composer were found outside the placeholder cases.

items.where: Left and right page margins on any screen; compare a phone and a wider device
steps: Open the chat screen on a phone.
Look at the left and right margins of the messages.
Repeat on a wider screen (rotate or use a larger device) if available.
Compare the margins with Expected (margins grow with width).
items.needs: a phone, optionally a wider device
items.note: The rule is in apps/mobile/src/shared/layout/contentColumn.ts.

items.where: Side menu: the chat list rows
steps: Sign in and open the side menu.
Look at the chat rows.
Compare the height of each row with the others.
Check all rows have the same height.
items.needs: a few chats in the side menu
items.note: Row labels come from a translation key that was not found as text.

items.where: Settings > Device: each menu row, and the Appearance options
steps: Sign in and open the side menu, then tap Settings.
Look at the rows under Device (Appearance, Accent Color, General).
Open Device > Appearance and look at its option rows.
Compare the row heights with Expected (one row height across menus).
items.needs: none

items.where: Side menu: long-press a chat > Rename, then the Rename chat dialog
steps: Sign in and open the side menu.
Long-press a chat row.
Tap Rename.
Look at the inner space around the Rename chat title, the field and the Cancel button.
items.needs: a chat in the side menu
items.note: Compare with another dialog, such as Settings > Account > Delete if present, for matching padding.

items.where: Schedules > Create Schedule: the form fields and their labels
steps: Sign in and open the side menu.
Tap the Schedules row and then Create Schedule.
Look at the space between each field label and its input.
Compare the gap between fields with Expected.
items.needs: a plan that allows schedules
items.note: The Schedules row label comes from a translation key that was not found as text; Create Schedule may show View Plans on plans without schedules.

items.where: Settings > Device > Appearance: the icons beside System, Light and Dark
steps: Sign in and open the side menu, then tap Settings.
Open Device > Appearance.
Look at the icons on the left of the System, Light and Dark rows.
Check the icons look like one family with the same stroke weight and size.
items.needs: none
items.note: Icons are from lucide-react-native (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/appearance/index.tsx).

items.where: No control picks a button size. Sizes are sm, md and lg in one component.
items.needs: none
items.note: Plan file button.tsx is now apps/mobile/components/ui/Button.tsx (sizes sm 36px, md 44px, lg 52px min height). Large buttons appear on screens such as apps/mobile/app/(auth)/reset-password.tsx, which a tester reaches only by a password-reset link, so the effect is hard to see from the UI.

items.where: Corner shape of the chat composer and send controls (inner rule, no setting).
steps: Sign in and open a chat.
Look at the corners of the message box at the bottom and the round send control.
Compare with the radius values in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/tokens.ts (radii scale) and the use of radii.full in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx.
items.needs: none
items.note: No label; the radius ladder itself is only visible through the shapes on screen.

items.where: Soft shadow under floating surfaces such as toast messages (inner rule, no setting).
steps: Sign in, then trigger a short message such as copying text from a message.
Look for the soft shadow under the toast that appears near the bottom.
Compare with the shadow values in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/tokens.ts (elevation e1 to e4) and the toast use at apps/mobile/src/shared/components/Toast.tsx.
items.needs: none
items.note: The toast trigger is not verified in the code; the shadow scale is defined in tokens.ts and used by Toast.tsx line 93.

items.where: Stacking order of toasts, overlays and full-screen lock (inner rule, no setting).
steps: Sign in and open a chat with text on screen.
Trigger a toast message and check it sits above the chat content.
Compare with the named layers in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/tokens.ts (zIndex: control, overlay, modal, notification, fullscreen).
items.needs: none
items.note: The plan's CloudSyncErrorBanner.tsx file no longer exists; toasts (zIndex.notification) and the app lock overlay (zIndex.fullscreen in apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/AppLockOverlay.tsx) are the current users.

items.where: Timing of animations such as toast slide-in (inner rule, no setting).
steps: Sign in and trigger a toast message.
Watch the toast slide in and out and note it is quick, not slow.

Compare with the named durations in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/tokens.ts (motion: instant 90, quick 160, moved 260, reveal 700, ambient 2000, orbit 3000 ms) and the use of motion.quick in apps/mobile/src/shared/components/Toast.tsx.
items.needs: none
items.note: Named easing curves are in tokens.ts (motionCurves) and are not visible as a control.

items.where: Reduce Motion is a phone setting outside the app, read by the app at startup and live. There is no in-app switch in apps/mobile.
steps: On the phone or simulator, turn on the system Reduce Motion setting (iOS path: Settings > Accessibility > Motion > Reduce Motion; this path is the phone's own and is not in the repo).
Open AGI Mobile and go to a chat where the loading spinner shows (apps/mobile/components/ui/LoadingIndicator.tsx uses a spinning AgiMark).
Look at the spinner and any looping mark: it should stop or be replaced by a gentle change.
Compare with the rule in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/useReduceMotion.ts and the check in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/__tests__/accessibilityPreferenceCoverage.test.ts.
items.needs: a phone or simulator where the Reduce Motion setting can be changed
items.note: No in-app control exists for reduced motion; only the OS setting is read (useReduceMotion.ts). The OfflineBanner cited in the plan does not loop, so it was not used as an example.

items.where: Drawer > Settings > Device > Appearance, then choose System, Light or Dark.
steps: Sign in and tap Open menu to open the side drawer, then tap Settings.
Under the Device group, tap Appearance.
Tap Dark and look at the whole app, including code blocks in a chat, for a dark background.
Tap Light, then System, and check the app follows the device's light or dark setting.
items.needs: a Mac or phone where the system light or dark setting can be changed
items.note: Cloud and Local modes store their theme choice separately (appearance/index.tsx), so check the choice in the mode you are using. Whether code blocks follow the theme was not verified in code.

items.where: Phone setting outside the app: high contrast is read from the system. There is no in-app switch.
steps: On the phone, turn on the high-contrast setting (iOS: the Darker Colors setting, which the code reads as isDarkerSystemColorsEnabled; Android: the high text contrast setting, read as isHighTextContrastEnabled). These device paths are not in the repo.
Open AGI Mobile and check text and borders look stronger.
Check the accent colour is replaced by neutral colours, as in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/useTheme.ts (accent is null when high contrast is on).
items.needs: a phone or simulator where the system contrast setting can be changed
items.note: The code is in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/useSystemHighContrast.ts; the high-contrast palette is in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/tokens.ts (highContrastColors). The device menu path is the phone's own, so confirm it on the device.

items.where: Drawer > Settings > Device > Appearance (selected row shows a check mark; pressing a row shows a pressed state).
steps: Sign in, tap Open menu, then Settings, then Appearance.
Press and hold the System row and check it shows a pressed state.
Release and check the row you picked now shows a check mark and is marked selected.
Look for a disabled state on a greyed-out control elsewhere, and compare with the pressed and selected states in apps/mobile/components/ui/PressableBox.tsx.
items.needs: none
items.note: Focus and hover states are not verified in the code on this screen; the disabled example was not located. The plan's pressable-box.tsx path is now PressableBox.tsx.

items.where: Drawer > Settings > About for the brand mark. The app icon is on the phone's home screen.
steps: Sign in, tap Open menu, then Settings, then About.
Look at the brand symbol at the top of the About screen (apps/mobile/app/(app)/about.tsx).
Close AGI Mobile and look at its icon on the home screen.
Compare with the icon files named in apps/mobile/app.config.js (icon ./assets/icon.png and the Android adaptive icon).
items.needs: a phone or simulator with the app installed
items.note: Icon sizes per platform are set in app.config.js and cannot be checked from inside the app; the brand mark also appears on the sign-in screen (apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx).

items.where: First screen after sign-in (the new chat). On a phone, tap "Open menu" then "New chat" from a conversation.
steps: Sign in with a signed-in account.
Look at the first screen before typing: it should open on the new chat, not a chat that already has messages.
If a conversation is open, tap "Open menu" (top left), then tap "New chat" in the sidebar.
Compare: the greeting and the message box sit in the middle of the empty area, not at the top of an empty transcript.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The centred start view is built in apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx (testID chat.new-chat.middle). ChatEmptyState.tsx is not referenced from any file under apps/mobile/app. The greeting wording changes with the time of day.

items.needs: none
items.note: No reading-width cap found for chat messages. MessageBubble.tsx uses maxWidth '85%' (lines 686, 2301), and MessageList.tsx does not use contentColumn. contentColumn('reading') in apps/mobile/src/shared/layout/contentColumn.ts is used only by other screens (Toast, ApprovalModal, AgentsScreen, CustomizeScreen and similar) and MemoryUsedChip/ConversationExportSheet. Searched apps/mobile for contentColumn( and READING_COLUMN_MAX_WIDTH.

items.where: Conversation screen on a phone-width window: tap "Open menu" at the top left to open the sidebar, and close it again.
steps: Sign in and open any chat from the list.
Tap "Open menu" at the top left of the chat header.
Look: the sidebar slides over the chat.
Tap the dimmed area beside the sidebar, or swipe it left, to close it.
Tap "Open menu" again and compare: the sidebar reopens.
items.needs: none
items.note: On a wide window the sidebar stays permanently open and the "Open menu" button is not shown (the slot is blank).

items.where: Chat message box: tap "Expand message" at its top right corner after typing a long message.
steps: Open a chat, or tap "New chat".
Type several lines into the message box until it grows.
Tap the "Expand message" button at the top right of the box.
Look: a full-screen editor covers the screen with the same text and a send control.
Close the editor and check you are back in the chat with your text kept.
items.needs: none
items.note: The "Expand message" button only appears once the text is multi-line. The close control's visible words were not found in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ComposerFullScreenEditor.tsx, so check its label on screen.

items.where: Sidebar > Reports > tap a report in the list.
steps: Tap "Open menu" (top left) in a chat to open the sidebar.
Tap "Reports".
Tap a report in the list.
Look: the report opens on a full screen with a "Reports" header and a back control, and the report text fills the screen.
items.needs: a saved research report on the account
items.note: "Reports" appears in the sidebar only when the research feature is switched on. The empty state says "Research reports are saved to your Managed Cloud account."

items.where: A chat that contains an image: tap the image in the message.
steps: Open a chat that has an image in it (a photo you sent, or a generated image).
Tap the image.
Look: the image opens over the chat on a full-screen dark viewer.
Use the viewer's close control, or swipe it away, and check you are back in the chat.
items.needs: a chat with an image in it
items.note: The viewer's close and counter wording was not confirmed by exact visible text. The "Open image" link in MarkdownImage.tsx opens an outside browser, not this viewer.

items.where: Any long chat: the message box at the bottom of the screen.
steps: Open a chat with many messages.
Scroll the transcript up and down.
Look: the message box stays fixed at the bottom while the messages move above it.
items.needs: a chat with enough messages to scroll

items.where: Chat message box: type a long prompt; the box grows and shows "Expand message" at its top right.
steps: Open a chat, or tap "New chat".
Type a long prompt of several sentences into the message box.
Look: the box grows taller as you type instead of staying one line.
Once it is multi-line, check the "Expand message" button appears at the top right of the box.
items.needs: none
items.note: The code caps the box at a maximum height of 160 and scrolls past that; compare what you see with that.

items.where: Any chat with a long transcript: the messages scroll, the header and message box stay in place.
steps: Open a chat with a long history.
Scroll the messages up and down.
Look: the header at the top and the message box at the bottom do not move while the messages scroll.
items.needs: a chat with a long transcript

items.where: An artifact card in a chat reply: tap the card, then look at the toolbar at the top of the full-screen artifact.
steps: Open a chat where the assistant made an artifact (a document or code).
Tap the artifact card in the reply.
Look at the top toolbar: "Download artifact", "Copy content" and "More artifact actions" should be visible.
Scroll the artifact body down.
Compare: the toolbar stays at the top while the content scrolls.
items.needs: a chat that has an artifact in it
items.note: "Copy content" is a default value passed to copyControlLabel in the file, so the on-screen text may change with copy status.

items.where: Chat screen when the window is resized: narrow windows show the sidebar over the chat, wide windows keep it beside the chat.
steps: Open a chat in a narrow window (phone size).
Tap "Open menu": the sidebar slides over the chat.
Widen the window (iPad or wide simulator) past about 1000 points.
Look: the sidebar now stays beside the chat and "Open menu" is gone.
items.needs: a window that can be resized (tablet or wide simulator)
items.note: The threshold is in apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useResponsiveLayout.ts (280 sidebar plus 720 content). The app's _layout.tsx uses useTabletLayout, which was not opened.

items.where: Chat message box: tap "Add to chat" to open a bottom sheet.
steps: Open a chat, or tap "New chat".
Tap "Add to chat" beside the message box.
Look: a sheet rises from the bottom of the screen with attachment, mode and feature options.
Drag the sheet down, or tap outside it, to close.
Compare: the options appear as a bottom sheet, not a small popover.
items.needs: none
items.note: The model picker is also a bottom sheet, but the only entry found in code is "Choose a model", shown when the retired-model notice appears (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx). The regular model entry was not confirmed.

items.where: Chat screen on a tablet-width window: the sidebar stays on the left and the chat fills the right.
steps: Open the app on an iPad simulator, or widen the window past about 1000 points.
Open a chat.
Look: the sidebar stays on the left as a fixed column and the chat sits beside it.
Tap a different chat in the sidebar and check the chat on the right changes.
items.needs: a tablet-width window
items.note: Threshold in apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useResponsiveLayout.ts. The sidebar is a permanent drawer in apps/mobile/app/(app)/_layout.tsx.

items.where: Chat screen on a phone: header clear of the notch, message box clear of the home bar, and the layout lifts when the keyboard opens.
steps: Open a chat on an iPhone simulator.
Look: the header sits below the notch and the message box above the home indicator.
Tap the message box so the keyboard opens.
Look: the message box rises above the keyboard and the latest message stays visible.
items.needs: a phone-size simulator

items.where: Sidebar width when the window is resized (wide or narrow).
steps: Open a chat in a narrow window and tap "Open menu" to show the sidebar.
Look: the sidebar is at most 300 points wide and no more than 88 percent of the window.
Widen the window past about 1000 points and look: the sidebar is a fixed 280 points beside the chat.
items.needs: a window that can be resized
items.note: Limits are constants in apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useResponsiveLayout.ts. A minimum width for the chat column is not a separate control.

items.where: Conversation menu > Export > Print (top right of a chat).
steps: Open a chat that has messages.
Tap "Conversation menu" at the top right.
Tap "Export".
Tap "Print" in the export sheet.
Look: the system print preview shows the conversation text without the app's buttons. Cancel the dialog.
items.needs: a chat with messages (a printer is optional)
items.note: Printing uses the system print dialog. Report printing was not found; only conversation printing was.

items.where: Reset password screen (opened from a password recovery link, not from a menu) > Open Web Account button
steps: Open the password recovery link so the Reset password screen opens (the app routes to (auth)/reset-password).
Read the text: "Password recovery opens in your AGI web account."
Look at the filled teal button "Open Web Account" (default primary style).
Compare the label colour with the button fill: it should be readable.
Compare with Expected: the main action has the emphasised primary style.
items.needs: a password recovery link (or a way to open the reset-password route)
items.note: The screen is reached by a deep link (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx routes segments reset-password), so there is no in-app menu path; the primary style itself is the default variant in apps/mobile/components/ui/button.tsx (teal fill).

items.where: Reset password screen > Lost Your Email or Two-Factor Device? button
steps: Open the Reset password screen (same route as S8.01).
Look at the buttons under the text: "Open Web Account" is filled, "Lost Your Email or Two-Factor Device?" and "Back to Sign In" have an outline style.
Compare the outline buttons with the filled one: they should look less prominent.
Check that the outline buttons sit beside the primary action.
items.needs: a password recovery link

labels.text: Lost Your Email or Two-Factor Device?

items.note: The outline style is set by variant="outline" in apps/mobile/app/(auth)/reset-password.tsx; the outline colours are in apps/mobile/components/ui/button.tsx.

items.where: Schedule form for an existing schedule > Delete Schedule button
steps: Open an existing scheduled task (the Schedules screen is opened from "Create schedule" or the schedule list; how Schedules is opened from the main menu was not traced).
Open the edit form of that schedule.
Scroll to the bottom and find the red "Delete Schedule" button.
Look at the label colour (danger colour) and check it is readable.
Compare with Expected: the irreversible action uses the distinct destructive style.
items.needs: a paid account with at least one scheduled task (Scheduled tasks need Basic)
items.note: The destructive style is variant="destructive" in apps/mobile/components/ui/button.tsx (text colour agentError); other destructive buttons also exist, e.g. apps/mobile/src/features/sites/SiteDetailScreen.tsx.

items.where: Chat screen (phone width) > Open menu icon at the top left of the chat header
steps: Open any chat from the chat list.
Find the icon-only button at the top left of the chat header (a menu icon, no words).
Tap it: the side drawer should open.
Check that the button has an accessible name "Open menu" (for example with VoiceOver, if the tester uses it).
Compare with Expected: the icon-only button has an accessible name.
items.needs: a chat with messages; a phone-width layout (not the wide persistent drawer)
items.note: The button is not shown when the wide persistent drawer is used (usesPersistentDrawer), so a Mac window that is wide may show a different header.

items.where: Add to chat (plus button under the composer) > Camera > camera screen > torch icon at the bottom
steps: Open a chat and tap the "Add to chat" button next to the message box.
Tap "Camera" in the sheet and allow camera access.
On the camera screen, tap the torch button (only shown on the back camera); its label is "Turn torch on".
Tap it again: the label should change to "Turn torch off" and the torch should toggle.
Compare with Expected: a button that shows an on or off pressed state.
items.needs: a phone with a back camera and a torch; camera permission (not possible on a Mac without a camera)
items.note: The torch label "Turn torch on" / "Turn torch off" is in apps/mobile/app/(app)/camera.tsx and the selected state is set with accessibilityState; a Mac tester may not be able to run it.

items.where: Chat reply that asks for tool approval > Allow / Deny buttons under the request
steps: Start a cloud chat whose agent asks to use a tool (the tool approval card appears).
Look at the row of buttons for the decision (Allow and Deny).
Check whether the row is announced as one labelled group (it is not, per the code).
Compare with Expected: related buttons are grouped under one label.
items.needs: a cloud account and a request that needs tool approval

labels.text: Sent to the agent with Allow or Deny

items.note: Known unfinished: the approve and deny row is not exposed as a labelled button group. The visible words Allow and Deny come from TOOL_APPROVAL_ACTION_LABELS, whose source file was not found; the label text is only visible in the code as a hint.

items.where: Chat > ask a question whose answer contains a web link > tap the link in the reply
steps: Open a chat and ask for an answer that includes a web address or link (for example, a question that needs sources).
Look at the reply: links should be styled as links (coloured text).
Tap a link and check that its destination opens.
Compare with Expected: the link is styled as a link and opens its destination.
items.needs: a cloud or local chat that returns links
items.note: MessageContentRenderer.tsx is the renderer for message text, but no link-open call was found in it; the opening behaviour may live in another file, so it was not verified.

items.where: Projects tab > Search projects field; or Settings > Personalization > Full Name field
steps: Tap the Projects tab at the bottom.
Tap the search field with the text "Search projects" and type a word.
Check the list filters as you type, and that the field has a clear button.
Alternatively open Personalization and tap the "Full Name" field, then type a name.
Compare with Expected: a single-line field with a visible label or accessible name.
items.needs: none for the Projects search; the Personalization field needs a signed-in account
items.note: The Personalization row is labelled "Personalization" in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx (the Settings screen entry from the menu was not traced).

items.where: Chat tab > message box at the bottom (placeholder "Type or hold to talk")
steps: Open the Chat tab and tap the message box at the bottom.
Type one line, then press the Return key on the keyboard.
Check that the cursor moves to a new line inside the same box and the text is not sent.
Compare with Expected: a multi-line text area that accepts new lines is used.
items.needs: none; the placeholder may differ when offline
items.note: The composer's accessible name is "Message input" (ChatInput.tsx); the placeholder depends on state (line 1657), so the exact visible word may change.
