items.where: Search icon in the drawer (opened from the Open menu icon) > Search field with placeholder "Search"
steps: Open the side drawer from the menu icon at the top left of the chat screen.
Tap the search icon in the drawer (its word is a translation key "search"; no visible word was found).
Type text in the field with placeholder "Search".
Check that the list of chats, projects, files and artifacts filters as you type.
Compare with Expected: a search field that filters the list.
items.needs: a few chats to search
items.note: The search screen is apps/mobile/app/(app)/search.tsx, which renders ChatsListScreen; the drawer search icon's route was inferred and not traced.

items.where: Connectors > Add custom MCP > Auth token (optional) field
steps: Open Connectors from the Settings screen.
Tap "Add custom MCP".
In the modal, tap the "Auth token (optional)" field and type a few characters.
Check that the characters show as dots (masked), not plain text.
Compare with Expected: secret entry uses a masked field.
items.needs: a signed-in account (cloud connectors)
items.note: The field is secureTextEntry in AddCustomConnectorModal.tsx; the Settings screen entry from the menu was not traced.

items.where: Sign-in screen > type email > Continue > Use an email code instead > Verification code field
steps: On the sign-in screen, tap "Email address" and type your email.
Tap "Continue".
Tap "Use an email code instead" if it is shown.
Look for the field labelled "Verification code" with the text "Enter the code sent to" and your email.
Type the code from your email (or paste it) and check that it accepts a one-time code.
items.needs: an email inbox you can read (the code is sent by an outside email service)
items.note: The code field uses textContentType oneTimeCode in MobileSignIn.tsx; whether the "Use an email code instead" link is always shown was not fully traced.

items.where: Settings > Notifications > Quiet hours > Days row (Sunday to Saturday)
steps: Open Notifications from Settings and tap "Quiet hours".
Open the time and focus screen and find the "Days" row with one letter per day.
Tap a day letter and check that it toggles on or off.
Check the day shows as checked (selected).
Compare with Expected: independent on or off choices with checked state.
items.needs: none
items.note: The day toggles use accessibilityRole checkbox in TimeFocusScreen.tsx; how the Notifications screen is opened from the main menu was not traced.

items.where: Chat > Add to chat > style row (opens the style selector) > Normal, Concise, Explanatory, Learning, Formal
steps: Open a chat and tap the "Add to chat" button.
Find the style entry in the sheet and tap it (its visible label was not found in the code).
In the style list, tap "Concise" and check that the selected row is marked selected.
Tap "Formal" and check that the selection moves.
Compare with Expected: one choice at a time, all options visible, with checked state.
items.needs: none
items.note: The style row in AddToChatSheet.tsx calls onOpenStyleSelector, but its visible text was not found; the options use accessibilityRole radio.

items.where: Settings > Device Integrations > calendar row switch
steps: Open Device Integrations from Settings.
Find the calendar row with a switch on its right.
Tap the switch and check it turns on or off immediately.
Compare with Expected: an immediate on or off setting with switch semantics.
items.needs: a device with calendar access (the switch asks for permission)
items.note: The calendar switch is in apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/integrations.tsx; the Settings entry from the main menu was not traced.

items.where: Open menu (top left of a chat) > drawer > Local | Cloud segmented control
steps: Open the side drawer from the menu icon.
Find the two-part control with the segments "Local" and "Cloud".
Tap "Local" and check it is highlighted; tap "Cloud" and check the highlight moves.
Compare with Expected: a small set of exclusive options shown as joined segments.
items.needs: a Cloud-enabled account to change to Cloud (Cloud is disabled otherwise)
items.note: The control is labelled "Chat execution mode" (tablist) and is also in Settings (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx).

items.where: Settings > Models (row shows the current model) > model list; or the Choose a model control in the chat
steps: Open the Models row from Settings (the row is labelled "Models").
Tap a model in the list.
Check the chosen model is marked selected and the row value updates.
Compare with Expected: one value chosen from a list.
items.needs: none; some models need a paid plan
items.note: The Choose a model control appears in the retired-model notice in the chat; the model list is ModelPickerSheet and the Settings screen entry was not traced.

items.where: Settings > Models, or Choose a model > search field "Search models…"
steps: Open the model picker (Models row or Choose a model).
Tap the field with the placeholder "Search models…" and type part of a model name.
Check the list filters as you type.
Tap a result and check it is chosen.
Compare with Expected: type to filter, then pick one.
items.needs: none
items.note: The search field has accessibilityLabel "Search models" and a listbox-like list; keyboard arrow navigation was not verified.

items.where: Settings > Voice > Speed slider (also Pitch)
steps: Open Voice from Settings.
Find the row labelled "Speed" with a value such as 1.00x.
Drag the slider or tap near its ends, and check the value changes in steps.
Compare with Expected: one value set on a scale by dragging.
items.needs: none
items.note: The slider is VoiceSlider in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/voice/index.tsx, not the personalization file cited in the plan, which has no slider.

items.where: Schedules > Create schedule > Repeat set to once > Date field "Choose a date"
steps: Open the schedules screen and tap the "Create schedule" button.
Choose the once recurrence option (its word was not found in the code).
Tap the "Date" field showing "Choose a date".
Pick a date on the calendar and check the field shows that date.
Compare with Expected: a date picker is used where a date is entered.
items.needs: a paid account that allows scheduled tasks (Basic or higher)
items.note: On iOS the calendar is inline; on other platforms the native picker is used, per ScheduleDateTimeField.tsx.

items.where: Schedules > Create schedule > recurrence with a time > "Preferred time" field "Choose a time"
steps: Open "Create schedule" and choose a recurrence that shows a time (the time row appears for supported recurrences).
Tap the "Preferred time" field showing "Choose a time" or its value (default 09:00).
Change the time in the spinner and tap done if shown.
Check the field shows the new time.
Compare with Expected: a time control is used where a time is entered.
items.needs: a paid account that allows scheduled tasks
items.note: The spinner display is used only on iOS (Platform.OS === 'ios' in ScheduleDateTimeField.tsx); the recurrence word that shows the time was not traced.

items.where: Schedules > Create schedule > Time zone row (shows the current zone) > search field "Search time zones"
steps: Open "Create schedule" and scroll to the zone row labelled with "Time zone:" and the zone name.
Tap the row to open the time zone list.
Type part of a zone name in the "Search time zones" field.
Check the list filters, and that the device zone is the default.
Compare with Expected: a searchable list of zones, defaulting to the device zone.
items.needs: a paid account that allows scheduled tasks
items.note: The row's accessibility label is "Time zone: <zone>"; the default device zone comes from getDeviceTimezone() in ScheduleForm.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Accent Color > colour swatches (Neutral, Blue, Cyan, Green, Lime)
steps: Open Settings and tap "Accent Color".
Tap a swatch such as "Blue" and check the swatch is selected.
Check the accent colour changes in the app (for example, buttons turn blue).
Compare with Expected: a colour choice from swatches.
items.needs: none
items.note: The swatches are in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/accent-color/index.tsx; the swatch labels are in that file's ACCENTS list.

items.where: Chat > Add to chat > File
steps: Open a chat and tap the "Add to chat" button.
Tap "File" in the sheet.
Pick a file from the device document picker and confirm.
Check that the file appears as an attachment above the message box.
Compare with Expected: a file input chooses files from the device.
items.needs: a file to upload on the device
items.note: The picker is DocumentPicker.getDocumentAsync in apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx; mobile file types depend on the execution mode.

items.where: Projects tab > open a project > tabs "Chats", "Sources", "Artifacts", "Routines" ("Work" when shown)
steps: Tap the Projects tab at the bottom and open any project.
Look at the row of tabs at the top of the project.
Tap "Sources" and check its panel appears and its tab is marked selected.
Tap "Artifacts" and then "Routines", checking each panel changes.
Compare with Expected: a tab row that switches panels, with the selected tab marked.
items.needs: a project (create one first if none exists)
items.note: Tabs use accessibilityRole tab with accessibilityState selected; the visible name of the Projects bottom tab was not found exactly, and "Work" appears only when showWork is true.

items.where: Open menu > New chat > send a message that makes the assistant use a tool (for example a web search) > tap the Agent activity row under the reply
steps: Tap Open menu, then tap the new-chat button in the chat header (New chat).
Send a question that needs a tool, such as a web search.
Find the Agent activity row under the assistant reply.
Tap the row; it should expand to show the activity and collapse on a second tap.
Compare with Expected: the row's expanded state changes on each tap and the header is labelled as a button.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can send chat messages that use tools
items.note: The row's accessible name is built as Show or Hide plus the summary, and it only appears when the reply has tool activity.

items.where: Open menu > New chat > ask a question that returns web sources > tap View N sources under the reply
steps: Tap Open menu, then the new-chat button (New chat).
Ask a question that returns web sources.
Under the reply, tap the View N sources row (N is the number of sources).
Look for the expanded list titled Sources (or Sources so far while the answer is still streaming).
Compare with Expected: the block shows and hides, and the expanded state changes on each tap.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a question that returns web sources
items.note: The number in the row is filled in from the source count, for example View 3 sources.

items.where: Settings > Voice > open the voice call screen > tap the audio route button in the live voice bar (Audio route, Automatic)
steps: Open Settings and tap Voice.
Start a voice call from the voice screen (the start control was not confirmed in the code).
In the live voice bar, tap the audio route button, labelled Audio route followed by the current route.
See whether a list of routes opens (Automatic, Speaker, Bluetooth, Headset) and choose one.
Compare with Expected: the list opens, and the button label changes to the chosen route.
items.needs: a microphone and a device that supports switching the audio route
items.note: The picker returns nothing on platforms without audio route switching, so it may not appear on a given device.

items.where: Open menu > long-press a chat in the list > choose from the menu (Rename, Archive, Delete and others)
steps: Tap Open menu to open the side list of chats.
Long-press a chat title.
Look for the action menu that opens for that chat, listing actions such as Rename.
Compare with Expected: the menu opens for the chat you pressed and lists its actions; tapping outside closes it.
items.needs: a chat in the list
items.note: Archive appears only for AGI Cloud chats, and some items depend on the chat's state.

items.where: Open menu > Notifications, then look at the priority tag on each notification
steps: Tap Open menu.
Tap the notifications link (its accessible name reads Open notifications with the unread count).
Look at the small tag on each notification row, such as High or Critical.
Compare with Expected: each notification shows a small status or priority marker attached to it.
Also open Agents, tap an agent, and look for the status badge at the top of the agent screen.
items.needs: a notification with High or Critical priority (not every account has one)
items.note: The shared badge component is apps/mobile/components/ui/Badge.tsx; the notifications link may not show in the menu on every build, so confirm it on screen.

items.where: Search > type Artifacts > tap Artifacts > look at the small label on each artifact card
steps: Tap Search (the search icon in the side menu).
Type Artifacts and tap the Artifacts result under Go to.
Look at the small label on each non-image artifact card; it shows the artifact's language or kind.
Compare with Expected: the label names what the item is; it is a type label, not a free tag the user adds.
items.needs: at least one artifact in the account
items.note: No user-editable tag control was found; the only label on a card is the computed kind or language, so the word varies per artifact.

items.where: Open menu > New chat > send any message > look at the author name for your message (You) and for the reply (the model name or AGI)
steps: Tap Open menu, then the new-chat button (New chat).
Send any message and wait for the reply.
Look at who wrote each message: your message is marked You, the reply uses the model name or AGI.
Compare with Expected: the two authors are told apart, and a screen reader hears the author label on the message.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can get a reply
items.note: No picture avatar was found; the author marker is a text name in the message's accessible label, and the visible name rendering was not confirmed in code.

items.where: Open menu > Agents > tap an agent that is running > look at the bar and the Step N of M line under it
steps: Tap Open menu; if Agents is not listed, tap More first.
Tap Agents, then tap an agent whose status is running or waiting.
Look at the progress bar and the line that reads Step N of M, when both counts are known.
Compare with Expected: the bar fills as steps complete and the line changes.
For a spinner, open Projects while cloud projects are syncing and look for Loading projects.
items.needs: a running cloud agent
items.note: The Step line only appears when both the completed and total step counts are known.

items.where: Open menu > More > Schedules, while the list is loading for the first time
steps: Tap Open menu.
Tap More if Schedules is folded, then tap Schedules.
Look during the first load: three grey placeholder cards appear before the list.
Compare with Expected: the placeholders stand in for schedule cards and are replaced when the data arrives.
items.needs: a signed-in account; a slow connection makes the placeholders easier to see
items.note: The placeholders show only during the first load, so on a fast connection they may pass too quickly to see.

items.where: Open menu > long-press a chat > Archive > look at the bar at the bottom: Chat archived. Find it in Settings, Archived chats. with Undo
steps: Tap Open menu.
Long-press an AGI Cloud chat, then tap Archive.
Look for the bar that appears above the bottom edge with the archive message and an Undo button.
Wait and watch: it should leave by itself after about 5 seconds (about 8 seconds when it has a button).
Compare with Expected: it does not block the screen and it dismisses itself.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud chat (signed in)

labels.text: Chat archived. Find it in Settings, Archived chats.

items.note: Durations come from TOAST_DURATION_MS (5 seconds) and TOAST_ACTION_DURATION_MS (8 seconds) in apps/mobile/src/shared/components/Toast.tsx.

items.where: Open menu > New chat > turn on airplane mode > send a message > look at the alert above the message box: Message failed to send:
steps: Tap Open menu, then the new-chat button (New chat).
Turn on airplane mode.
Type a message and send it.
Look at the alert above the message box; it has alert semantics and starts with Message failed to send:.
Compare with Expected: a clear error appears inline with the cause, and the reply can be retried from the banner.
items.needs: a way to make sending fail, such as airplane mode
items.note: The exact wording depends on the error, so the message after the colon varies.

items.where: Open menu > New chat > send a message to a provider that needs consent > look at the strip above the message box with the Review button
steps: Tap Open menu, then the new-chat button (New chat).
Send a message to a provider whose use is not yet approved.
Look at the full-width strip above the message box; it has a globe icon, a message and a Review button.
Tap Review or the dismiss control to confirm they respond.
Compare with Expected: the strip sits in its own band, does not cover the chat, and can be dismissed.
items.needs: an account and a provider that triggers the consent strip
items.note: The strip shows only when consent is missing, and the trigger was not traced end to end; a usage-limit banner is also rendered in the same screen.

items.where: Open menu > scroll to the bottom of the chat list > tap Load older chats (also Settings > Data Controls > Archived chats > Load more)
steps: Tap Open menu.
Scroll to the bottom of the chat list.
Tap Load older chats and wait for the next page.
Compare with Expected: the next page of chats appears, and the button goes away when no older chats remain.
Optionally open Settings > Data Controls > Archived chats and tap Load more.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account with more chats than one page
items.note: The Library list loads more by scrolling and has no button, so it is not a pagination control.

items.where: Open menu > More > Schedules, with no schedules in the account
steps: Tap Open menu, then More if needed, then Schedules.
Look at the empty state: it shows the title No Schedules and a short description.
Look for the Try a template section and the Create Schedule button.
Compare with Expected: the message says what the view is for and gives a next step.
items.needs: a paid account that can create schedules (a Free account sees the locked title instead)
items.note: A Free account sees the title Scheduled tasks require Basic instead of No Schedules, with a View Plans button when purchases are available.

items.where: Open menu > (the chat list fails to load on an AGI Cloud account) > tap Retry under the error text
steps: Turn on airplane mode, then tap Open menu to open the chat list.
Look for the red error text and the Retry button in the list.
Turn off airplane mode, tap Retry, and check that the chats load.
Compare with Expected: the error sits in the list with a recovery button, and the list fills once Retry works.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a network failure (airplane mode)
items.note: The same pattern exists for projects: Retry loading projects appears on the Projects tab when syncing fails.

items.where: Chat > Model button at the bottom of the message box > Search models…
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Tap the model button at the bottom of the message box (its accessibility label starts with "Model:").
In the sheet, tap the search field that says "Search models…" and type part of a model name.
Check that the list narrows to matching models only. Note: this picker lists models; files, projects and skills are not in it (files are searched in Library > "Search library").
items.needs: none
items.note: The code searches models only; the Expected line also names files, projects and skills, which this picker does not list.

items.where: Chat > Model button at the bottom of the message box > model list
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Tap the model button at the bottom of the message box.
In the sheet, tap a different model row (rows show "selected" for the current one).
Send a message and check the model shown on the button or the reply matches the model you picked.
items.needs: none
items.note: Models that are locked for the account show a lock reason in the row, such as upgrade or sign-in needed.

items.needs: a connector with two or more linked accounts
items.note: Searched apps/mobile for account selection in connector code. Settings > Connectors > a connector shows an "Account" row that lists linked accounts (ConnectorAccountSummary.tsx), but I found no control to choose which account a task or chat uses.

items.where: Settings > Workspace
steps: Sign in with a cloud account that belongs to a team workspace.
Tap Settings, then the "Workspace" row.
Read the list: "Personal" and each team workspace name are shown, with a check mark on the active one.
Tap a row that is not checked; the screen switches workspace and the check mark moves to it.
items.needs: a cloud account in a team workspace

items.where: Chat > project bar above the message box > No project > pick a project
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Tap the project bar that says "No project" (its accessibility label is "Select a project for this chat").
In the picker, read the line "Choose the project context for this chat." and tap one of your projects.
Check the bar now shows the project name (accessibility label "Active project: ...").
items.needs: a Cloud account with at least one project

labels.text: Choose the project context for this chat.

items.note: The code also reaches the project picker from Add to chat; that menu label was not confirmed.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals (scope of tool approvals); the approval card in chat shows "Allow once", "Allow for this chat" and "Always allow"
steps: Open Settings and tap "Capabilities", then the "Action approvals" row.
Read the three choices: "Ask before every action", "Run read-only actions without asking", "Skip approvals".
In a Cloud chat, ask the assistant to do an action that needs approval.
In the approval card, compare the choices "Allow once", "Allow for this chat", "Always allow" and "Deny" with Expected (once versus always).
items.needs: a Cloud account; an action that asks for approval
items.note: No picker for API keys or site automation scope was found in the files read; this covers tool approvals only.

items.where: AGI Work > Scheduled tasks > Create schedule
steps: Open the menu and tap "AGI Work", then "Scheduled tasks".
Tap "Create schedule".
Open the repeat choice and pick "Once", "Daily", "Weekly" or "Monthly".
Save, then check the task's list entry shows the chosen cadence.
items.needs: a plan that includes Scheduled tasks
items.note: The code offers only Once, Daily, Weekly and Monthly; no custom rule option was found, unlike the Expected line.

items.where: Menu > Library
steps: Open the menu (drawer) and tap "Library".
Read the chips "All", "Images", "Videos", "Documents", "Uploads", "Generated files", "Artifacts" and tap one to filter.
Tap the search bar that says "Search library" and type a name.
Tap a file to open it, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: none (a few saved files help)

items.where: Chat > an answer that contains a table > tap a column header
steps: Ask the assistant for a table, for example a comparison of three items.
Look for the table in the answer and scroll it sideways if it is wide.
Tap a column header once; rows should reorder by that column.
Tap it again to reverse the order and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud or Local chat that returns a table
items.note: The sort logic is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageContentRenderer.tsx (headers are buttons with a sorted state); the header text itself is model output, so no fixed visible label was found.

items.where: Menu > Library (cards shown in the grid)
steps: Open the menu and tap "Library".
Check the items appear as cards in a grid.
Tap a card to open it.
Compare the card layout and opening with Expected.
items.needs: none (a few saved files, artifacts or projects help)
items.note: The grid uses a fixed test id "library-grid" in the code; the visible grid columns depend on screen width.

items.where: Menu > Images (or Menu > Library > Images chip)
steps: Open the menu and tap "Images".
Check the images show as a gallery of thumbnails.
Tap one image to open it in a larger view.
Compare the larger view with Expected.
items.needs: a few images (generated or uploaded)
items.note: The code opens the library with an image id; the larger viewer itself was not traced.

items.where: Chat > a request that runs tools > the "Worked for" line under the reply
steps: Send a Cloud request that uses tools (for example one that searches or runs an action).
When the reply is done, find the line that starts with "Worked for" and its elapsed time.
Expand the activity to list the steps in order and check each step's state (for example Paused, Failed, Stopped wording).
items.needs: a Cloud account; a request that runs tools
items.note: Step order and per-step duration display were not traced in full.

items.where: Settings > Security and login > Recent security activity
steps: Sign in with a cloud account and open Settings.
Tap "Security and login".
Find the section titled "Recent security activity".
Read the rows and check they are newest first, or that the row says "No activity recorded yet" when empty.
items.needs: a Cloud account (the row shows "Cloud mode required" in Local mode)
items.note: The newest-first ordering was not confirmed in the code read.

items.where: Settings > Connections > remote control screen > Show companion walkthrough
steps: Open Settings and tap "Connections".
Open the companion screen from the remote control screen.
Tap "Show companion walkthrough".
Tap "Next step" to move forward and check the dots and the current step against Expected; "Finish walkthrough" appears on the last step.
items.needs: none (Remote Control may be hidden in some builds)
items.note: The walkthrough shows dots (StepDots); a text counter such as "Step 2 of 4" was not found.

items.where: First launch > onboarding (name, model, Cloud sign-in)
steps: Install or reset to a fresh state and open the app.
Enter your name in the field labelled "Your name" and tap "Continue".
Choose a model and tap "Continue" or "Download model".
Look for "Sign in to use Cloud", then check that your choices were kept when the setup finishes.
items.needs: a fresh install (no account yet)
items.note: No step counter text was found; saving of choices at the end was not traced.

items.where: Chat > open an artifact full screen > the "Version" control (shows Version N of M)
steps: Open an artifact from a chat that has several saved versions.
Tap the version control that reads "Version N of M".
In the history sheet, read each version and tap "Restore version" for the one you want.
Use "Previous version" and "Next version" to step through; compare with Expected.
items.needs: an artifact with at least two versions
a Cloud Code session with changed files
items.note: The diff counts (file and line counts ending in "changed.") are in apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/CodeSessionView.tsx, but I did not confirm the menu path that opens a session or the on-screen diff view.

items.where: Chat > an answer with sources > "View N sources"
steps: Ask a question that uses web search so the answer has sources.
Tap the line that says "View 3 sources" (count varies) or "Sources so far" while streaming.
Read each source's title and origin, then tap one to open it.
Compare with Expected; the excerpt display was not traced.
items.needs: a Cloud account with web search enabled
items.note: The excerpt shown per source was not confirmed in the code read.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Plan usage
steps: Sign in with a Cloud account and open Settings.
Tap "Usage".
Read the "Plan usage" section: each meter shows its label and a reset line below the bar.
Tap the info control labelled "About usage limits" and compare the reset time with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account
items.note: The meter's assistive-tech values were not confirmed; the info control has an accessibility label.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities
steps: Open Settings and tap "Capabilities".
Read the header "What AGI can use" and the rows (for example "Action approvals", "Web search", "Image generation").
Each row shows its state as a value on the right.
Tap "Action approvals" to see the approval choices, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: none (some rows need a Cloud account)

items.where: Chat (Cloud) > an action that needs approval > approval card with "Allow once", "Allow for this chat", "Always allow", "Deny"
steps: Set Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals to "Ask before every action".
In a Cloud chat, ask the assistant to do an action that needs approval (for example a write or send action).
Read the approval card: it names the action and shows the choices.
Tap "Allow once" or "Deny" and check the run continues or stops, as Expected says.
items.needs: a Cloud account; a tool action that needs approval
items.note: Which actions ask depends on the policy and the tool, so the card may not appear for every action.

items.where: Settings > Connectors
steps: Sign in with a Cloud account and open Settings.
Tap "Connectors".
Read each connector card: the "Connected" filter and the connected state shown on the card.
Open a connector and tap "Disconnect" (a confirmation asks first), then compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account; at least one connector
items.note: The code maps states to connected, needs reauthorization and not responding; a visible "Expired" word was not found.

items.needs: a Cloud or Local chat with a model that lacks a feature
items.note: Searched apps/mobile/src/features/chat and apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker for "not support", "doesn't support", "can't send" and similar; ChatInput.tsx near line 880 is attachment handling, and no visible capability-warning notice was found.

items.where: Remote control (AGI Work > Tasks > open a running task) > agent detail
steps: Start a long task in Cloud mode so it runs in the background.
Open the task from the task list and check the card shows its progress bar and current state.
Watch the card update while the task runs, then tap "Expand tool call log" to see the latest actions.
Compare with Expected (steps done, latest action).
items.needs: a Cloud account; a running task; Remote Control may be hidden in some builds
items.note: The progress bar is in apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/AgentDashboard.tsx; the path from the task list to the agent screen goes through the companion screen, and the exact entry label was not confirmed.

items.where: Chat > ask for a place or an itinerary > the map card in the answer
steps: Ask the assistant for a place, for example "show me a map of a city" or a day plan.
Find the map card in the answer and tap its action buttons.
Check the map shows the place with its overlay labels (route pill, attribution).
Tap a choice or action and see whether the answer or conversation updates, as Expected says.
items.needs: a Cloud or Local chat that returns an interactive card
items.note: Feedback from the choice into the conversation was not traced in full.

items.where: Chats > search icon in the header > type Notifications > under Go to, tap Notifications
steps: Sign in and open the Chats screen.
Tap the search icon in the header (it has no visible text; the code labels it 'search').
Type Notifications (or inbox) in the Search box and tap Notifications under Go to.
Look at the title Notifications and the line under it: 'N unread notifications' or 'All caught up'. Unread rows show a bold title and a small dot, and their screen-reader label starts with 'Unread,'.
Tap an unread row to open it, or tap Mark read on it, then check that the row turns to the read style and the count goes down.
Check that the newest item is at the top.
items.needs: a signed-in account; at least one notification (an unread one shows the unread style); the cloud chat feature must be on, otherwise the screen shows nothing
items.note: The unread-count button in the header (DrawerButton.tsx) opens the same inbox only on wide layouts; on phone the search route is the path found in code, and the Mark all as read button is icon only.

items.needs: none
items.note: Not built on mobile, as the plan's ledger says (D-2026-09-28-27). I searched apps/mobile for keyboard handlers (keyCommand, useKeyCommands, onKeyPress, hardwareKey, keydown, shortcut) and found only Android launcher shortcuts in native/android/withAGIShortcuts.cjs, which are not an in-app palette. The Search screen (app/(app)/search.tsx) has no keyboard shortcut and no Enter-to-run.

items.where: Projects > New project
steps: Open Projects (the Projects entry in the side drawer, which opens from the menu button).
Tap the floating "New project" button at the bottom right.
Type a name in the "Project name" field and tap "Create project".
Look for the new project in the Projects list, compared with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The side drawer's menu button has no visible label in the code I read.

items.where: Chat > Conversation menu > Rename
steps: Open a chat.
Tap the "Conversation menu" button in the chat header.
Tap "Rename"; the "Rename chat" box opens with the field "Enter a new title".
Change the title and tap "Rename".
Look for the new title in the chat header, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a chat

items.where: Chat > Conversation menu > Archive
steps: Open a Cloud chat that is not temporary.
Tap the "Conversation menu" button and tap "Archive".
Note that no confirmation appears first; a message appears: "Chat archived. Find it in Settings, Archived chats." with an "Undo" button.
Go to Settings > Archived Chats and check the chat is there, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account and a Cloud chat

labels.text: Chat archived. Find it in Settings, Archived chats.

items.note: Archiving has no confirm step; it relies on the Undo message, which is different from Expected's first option only in that it does not ask first.

items.where: Chat > Conversation menu > Delete
steps: Open a chat.
Tap the "Conversation menu" button and tap "Delete".
Read the "Delete chat?" dialog, which names the chat in quotes.
Tap "Cancel" to check nothing is removed, then repeat and tap "Delete", and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a chat

items.where: Chat > Conversation menu > Delete (on a chat that is only on this device)
steps: Open a chat that is kept only on this device (not a Cloud chat).
Tap the "Conversation menu" button and tap "Delete".
Read the "Delete chat?" dialog: it says the chat is deleted from this device and cannot be restored.
Tap "Delete" and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a chat kept only on this device
items.note: There is one Delete button and no second confirmation. Deleting a Cloud chat is not shown as permanent; the dialog says to restore it from Recently deleted on the web.

items.where: Chat > Conversation menu > Share > Create link
steps: Open a saved Cloud chat (not a temporary chat).
Tap the "Conversation menu" button and tap "Share".
Read the dialog "Share a link to this chat?", which says anyone with the link can read the chat until it expires or you revoke it.
Tap "Create link"; the system share sheet opens with the link.
Compare with Expected: the link goes to the system share sheet, not a box in the app.
items.needs: a Cloud account and a saved chat

labels.text: Share a link to this chat?

items.note: For a temporary chat the menu shows "Share link" and first asks to save the chat.

items.where: Library > long-press an item > Share
steps: Open Library from the side drawer.
Long-press a picture or file and tap "Share", or tap Select, pick one item and tap "Share" at the bottom.
Look for the system share sheet with that file.
Compare with Expected: the file goes to the system share sheet.
items.needs: an item in the Library and a device
items.note: I found no link-creation option for files, only the system share sheet.

items.where: Chats search > Artifacts > open the artifact > Publish icon > Publish > Who can open this
steps: On Chats, use the search field and type the artifact's title.
Under "Artifacts" in the results, tap the artifact.
Tap the globe button labelled "Publish artifact to a public link", then tap "Publish" in the dialog.
Under "Who can open this" choose "Anyone with the link", "Only people you invite" or "Everyone in this workspace", then compare with Expected.
Tap "Unpublish" and confirm "Unpublish this artifact?" to take it down.
items.needs: a Cloud account and an artifact that can be published
items.note: The publish button's label is "Publish artifact to a public link" in the code (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx).

items.where: Chats search > Artifacts > open the artifact > Publish artifact to a public link > Publish
steps: Open a Cloud artifact that can be published (a page or app).
Tap the globe button "Publish artifact to a public link".
Read "Publish to a public link?" and tap "Publish".
Look for the published link and the "Copy publication link" button, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account and a previewable artifact
items.note: In local mode the app says "Switch to AGI Cloud to publish" instead.

items.where: Settings > Privacy > Chat privacy > Shared links
steps: Open Settings, then Privacy, then Chat privacy, then Shared links.
Read each row for its title and "Expires" date, or "This link has expired".
Tap "Revoke" on a row and read "Revoke this link?".
Tap "Revoke" to confirm and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account with at least one shared link
items.note: The screen offers Share and Revoke only; I found no control to change the expiry or the access of a link.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Invite by email
steps: Open Settings, then Workspace.
Scroll to the administration section and tap "Invite by email".
Type an address in "Email address", pick a role (Member, Admin or Viewer), and tap "Send invitation".
Look at the pending invitations list; tap an invitation and choose "Resend invitation" or "Revoke invitation", and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud workspace where the account can manage the team, and a second email address
items.note: The administration section only shows when the account can manage the team.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Change role for <member name> > Change role
steps: Open Settings, then Workspace, as an admin of the workspace.
On a member who is not you, tap "Change role".
In the sheet "Role for <name>", pick a role and tap "Save role".
Look at the member's role in the list, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud workspace, an admin account, and a second member in the same workspace
items.note: Ordinary role changes save without a separate confirmation; only an ownership transfer asks more.

items.where: Chat > Add to chat > File
steps: Open a Cloud chat and tap "Add to chat" next to the message box.
Tap "File"; the device file chooser opens.
Pick a file.
Look for the file attached to the message before sending, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud chat and a file on the device
items.note: The "File" card only appears in Cloud mode; "Photos" and "Camera" are the other upload cards.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > (choose a connector) > Connect
steps: Open Settings, then Connectors.
Tap a connector that is not connected yet.
Tap "Connect <name>"; for an OAuth service the browser opens the service's sign-in page, and for a key service the "Connect {connectorName}" sheet asks for the key.
Finish the authorization and return to the app, then look for the card showing "Connected", and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account and an account on the outside service

items.where: Settings > Connectors > (connector showing "Authorization expired") > Reauthorize
steps: Open Settings, then Connectors, then the connector that shows "Authorization expired".
Tap "Reauthorize" and complete the authorization in the browser.
Return to the app and look for the connector showing as connected again, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a connection whose authorization has expired (hard to set up)
items.note: I did not confirm in the code that the connector's settings are kept after reauthorizing; that is not verified.

items.needs: several connected accounts for one service
items.note: I searched apps/mobile for an account picker, a default account or several accounts for one connector (cloud-connectors and services/connectors.ts); the only match was "Reset ... to default" for tool permissions, so no picker was found.

items.where: Chat > (a long conversation) > warning line under the header
steps: Open a long chat with many messages.
Look for the line "Chat is getting long. Start a fresh chat for faster responses." with a "New chat" button.
Tap "New chat" to start a fresh chat, or open the "Conversation menu" and tap "What is in context" to see the details, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: a long conversation

labels.text: Chat is getting long. Start a fresh chat for faster responses.

items.note: I did not check the length at which the warning appears.

items.where: Chat > usage warning banner above the message box
steps: Use a Free or other account until its usage limit is reached, then open a chat.
Look for the usage banner; if a reset time is known, tap "Notify me when it resets".
Tap the banner's action to open the recovery screen (Subscription), or tap "Dismiss usage warning".
Compare the banner's text (which limit, when it resets, what to do) with Expected.
items.needs: a usage limit that has been reached
items.note: The wording of the limit and the reset time come from server data; I did not find that text in the app code.

items.where: Settings > Subscription > Usage top-ups
steps: Open Settings, then Subscription.
Look for the "Usage top-ups" section: "Credits add to your plan and don't expire."
Tap a credit amount to start a purchase, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account; the purchase needs store products and in-app purchases switched on by the owner
items.note: Partial: the section shows only when store products load; in-app billing is not finished (owner switch and waitlist), and the Expected purchase dialog from the limit screen was not found.

items.where: Settings > Subscription > Compare plans (or Upgrade, then Subscription)
steps: Open Upgrade from the side drawer, or open Settings, then Subscription.
Tap "Compare plans" to see the plan list with prices and features.
Tap "Upgrade plan" or "Choose plan" if shown, and compare with Expected.
If the row shows "Unavailable in the app", plan changes are not available in the app.
items.needs: a Cloud account
items.note: Partial: plan prices and the pick action depend on the billing flag and store products, which are not finished.

items.where: Settings > Subscription > Manage billing
steps: Open Settings, then Subscription.
Look at the "Access ends" or "Renews" row, and check the date shown.
Tap "Manage billing"; the web billing page opens in the browser (for a store subscription, a "Subscription managed elsewhere" dialog appears first).
Compare with Expected: cancellation is done on that page or in the store, not in the app.
items.needs: a paid Cloud account
items.note: Partial: the app has no in-app cancel dialog; cancellation links out to the store or web billing.

items.where: Settings > Subscription > Manage billing
steps: Open Settings, then Subscription.
Tap "Manage billing".
Look at the web billing page in the browser for the card on file, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid Cloud account
items.note: Partial: the card is not changed in the app; the app links to web billing.

items.where: Settings > Account > Email > Delete Account
steps: Open Settings, then Account, then Email.
Tap "Delete Account" (a sensitive action).
Read the "Confirm it is you" dialog and enter a password, an email code, or an authenticator or backup code.
Look for the action continuing only after verification, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account and the way to confirm it is you
items.note: I did not find a passkey option in the "Confirm it is you" dialog; the strategies are password, email code, authenticator code and backup code.

items.where: Chat > Start voice mode (first use asks for the microphone)
steps: Open a chat and tap "Start voice mode" (the accessibility label of the voice button).
On the system microphone prompt, read the text "AGI Mobile uses the microphone for voice input and real-time voice conversations with AI." then choose Don't Allow.
Tap voice again and read the "Voice input unavailable" alert with "Open Settings" or "Not now".
Compare with Expected; the message says microphone access is off and how to turn it on.
items.needs: a microphone and a way to deny the permission

labels.text: Microphone access is off. Enable microphone permission in Settings to use voice.

items.note: The system prompt text is in apps/mobile/app.config.js.

items.where: Chat (Cloud) > a tool call that is awaiting approval > Allow once / Allow for this chat / Always allow / Deny
steps: Open a Cloud chat and ask for an action that a tool needs approval for.
Look for the tool row in the chat that shows the action and its decision buttons.
Tap "Allow once" or "Deny" for that call only, then compare with Expected.
For a broader scope such as "Allow for this chat" on a destructive tool, read the confirmation dialog first.
items.needs: a Cloud account and a request that triggers a tool approval (set by the server policy)
items.note: I did not identify which tool triggers an approval; the trigger depends on server policy.

items.where: Chat screen > send a message that asks the agent to use a connected outside tool > the tool approval card that shows "Allow" and "Deny"
steps: Sign in and open a chat that runs in AGI Cloud.
Ask the agent for an action that uses a connected outside tool.
When the approval card appears, read the notice text and the destination it names.
Compare with Expected: the card should show what is being sent and let you allow or deny that one call.
items.needs: a Cloud account with a connected outside tool; a chat that triggers a tool approval

labels.text: Private data from this chat could be sent outside AGI

items.note: The notice is rendered by apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CloudToolApprovalControls.tsx; which tool actions trigger it is decided by the server, and the code does not show what destination text is listed on the card.

items.needs: a desktop app paired on Managed Cloud (for a real test)
items.note: Pairing exists in code but is hidden in this build: apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts sets companion to false, and apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/remote-control.tsx returns a feature-unavailable screen when the flag is off. The QR scanner is apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/QRScanner.tsx. Searched the settings and companion folders for a reachable entry point and found none while the flag is off.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory > add or edit memory sheet, then close it with unsaved text
steps: Open the Settings screen and go to the Assistant section, then tap Memory.
Tap the control that adds or edits a memory (the exact button label was not found in the code).
Type some text into the memory field without saving.
Close the sheet without saving, then compare with Expected: a "Discard changes?" alert should appear with "Discard" and "Keep Editing".
Repeat with a new schedule on the schedule create screen; the same guard is used there, but I could not find the screen's entry label.
items.needs: a Free account or a Cloud account
items.note: The schedule create screen (apps/mobile/app/(app)/schedules/create.tsx) uses the same guard, but no visible entry label for it was found; the memory add button label was not found either.

items.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Export > sheet "Export Conversation" > Export as Markdown
steps: Open any chat that has messages.
Tap the control labelled Conversation menu in the chat header.
Tap Export.
Tap Export as Markdown (or Export as PDF or Export as Text) and choose where to share the file.
Compare with Expected: the sheet should offer formats and the exported file should contain the conversation.
items.needs: a chat with at least one message
items.note: The sheet also offers Print and Copy All Messages, and an empty chat shows "Nothing to Export" instead.

items.where: Open a chat > on an assistant answer, tap Message actions > Report… > choose a category > Send
steps: Open a chat that has an answer from the assistant.
Tap Message actions on that answer (or long-press it) and tap Report….
Choose a category (for example Other) and optionally write a note.
Tap Send and compare the result with Expected: the confirmation should say the report was sent or saved on this device.
items.needs: a chat with an assistant answer
items.note: The confirmation can also read "Saved on this device. Nothing was sent." when delivery is stored locally; the report sheet also appears on media in the Library viewer.

items.where: Settings > Support > Report App Issue
steps: Open Settings and go to the Support section, then tap Report App Issue.
Choose General Feedback (or the bug option) and type a message.
Tap Submit Feedback (or Email Feedback when the app sends by email).
Compare with Expected: the "Thank You!" alert should appear with "Your feedback has been submitted.".
items.needs: none
items.note: The feedback screen is the route /(app)/feedback; the Settings entry point and its Support section were confirmed in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Support > Export Diagnostics > Share diagnostics? > Continue
steps: Open Settings, go to the Support section, and tap Export Diagnostics.
Read the alert "Share diagnostics?" and its text.
Tap Continue to share, or Cancel to stop.
Compare with Expected: the consent text should say what is sent, and nothing should be shared after Cancel.
items.needs: none
items.note: The consent is asked on every tap; no saved preference was found in the code.

items.where: Settings > Account > Email > Export Cloud Data
steps: Sign in to an AGI Cloud account, open Settings, and go to the Account section.
Tap the Email row to open the cloud account screen.
Tap Export Cloud Data and wait for the share sheet.
Compare with Expected: the export should be delivered as a file to share or save. The code does not show a confirmation step first.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: The export is shared through the system share sheet (shareCloudDataExport), not a download, and there is no request dialog before it runs; failure alerts are "Export failed" and "Export not saved".

items.where: Settings > Account > Email > Delete Account > Delete Account
steps: Sign in to an AGI Cloud account, open Settings, tap the Email row in the Account section.
Scroll to Delete Account and tap it.
Read the "Delete Account" dialog text: it schedules deletion, names what is deleted, and says erasure cannot be undone once it begins.
Tap Delete Account to confirm, or Cancel to stop. Compare with Expected: the dialog should explain what is deleted and require this confirmation.
Use a throwaway test account only, because the deletion is scheduled for real.
items.needs: a throwaway signed-in AGI Cloud account (not a real one)

labels.text: Erasure is processed after the deadline and may take longer. Once erasure begins, it cannot be undone.

items.note: The dialog text is built in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-account/deleteAccountConfirmation.ts, and the scheduled state can be cancelled from the same screen.

items.where: Header button "Open notifications, N unread" (only shown in the wide layout with the permanent sidebar), then the Notifications screen
steps: Make the app window wide enough for the permanent sidebar (a Mac window, not a phone-width window).
Make sure there is at least one unread notification, so the bell button appears in the header.
Turn on VoiceOver and move across the header button; it should announce "Open notifications, N unread".
Tap the bell. On the Notifications screen, move through each notification row; each should read as one button with its title and time.
Compare with Expected: every control has a name that says what it does.
items.needs: a notification in the inbox (unread) and a wide window; on phone width the code shows no link to this screen
items.note: On phone width the code has no visible route to the Notifications screen; only the wide-layout bell was found.

items.where: Settings > Device (section title), then the other section titles Assistant, Cloud, Support
steps: Open Settings from the side menu.
Turn on VoiceOver and use the heading navigation (VO + Command + H) to move between section titles.
Confirm the section names Device, Assistant, Cloud and Support are reached as headings.
Open a settings page such as Settings > Device > General and check its page title is a heading.
Compare with Expected: each screen has a top heading and sections are headings.
items.needs: none
items.note: Section titles are marked as headers in the code; the settings page title comes from the shared shell.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Remote control > Connections (row "Open Remote" or "Pair a computer"), then the Remote screen, then the help button "Show companion walkthrough"
steps: Open Settings, go to the Remote control section and tap Connections.
Tap "Open Remote" (or "Pair a computer" if not paired).
On the Remote screen, tap the help icon labelled "Show companion walkthrough".
Check that the walkthrough opens as a full-screen dialog with focus inside it; press Tab (or swipe with VoiceOver) and confirm focus stays inside.
Press Escape (or use the "Skip walkthrough" button) and confirm the dialog closes.
Compare with Expected: focus moves into the dialog, stays there, and Escape closes it.
items.needs: a paired or unpaired account with the Remote feature enabled (shown only when the companion feature is on)
items.note: The walkthrough is a modal with accessibilityViewIsModal; the code shows Dismiss and Skip buttons, and onRequestClose is wired to skip, so Escape should be the same as Skip.

items.needs: device
items.note: No code for restoring focus to the opening control was found. I searched apps/mobile for restoreFocus, returnFocus, "focus restor" and "restore focus" and got no matches.

items.where: Chat screen > "Message input" field > send a message and wait for the reply
steps: Turn on VoiceOver and open a chat.
Focus the "Message input" field and type a short question.
Send it and let the reply finish streaming.
Listen for the short spoken announcements (a "responding" message when the reply starts and an outcome message when it ends) without the focus moving.
Compare with Expected: a short announcement is heard and focus stays where it was.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a working AI reply and VoiceOver on
items.note: The announcement text is not shown on screen; the tester has to listen for it.

items.where: Chat screen > a message with agent activity > "Show agent activity" > the tool step or approval row > "Allow" / "Deny" buttons
steps: Open a chat in which the agent runs a tool that needs approval.
Tap the agent activity line whose label starts with "Show agent activity" to expand it.
Read the tool step: it should say its state (running, done, failed or waiting for approval).
For a step waiting for approval, check the buttons labelled "Allow" and "Deny" and the "Decision for" group.
Compare with Expected: each step's state is announced and approve/deny controls have labels.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a tool request that needs approval
items.note: The approval buttons use the shared labels; the exact button set depends on the approval scope shown.

items.where: Settings > Device > Appearance (the text size comes from the device's own text-size setting, not an in-app control)
steps: Change the device text size to a larger setting (the system Text Size or Larger Text option).
Reopen the app and go to Settings > Device > Appearance.
Check that the row labels and values wrap or stay on one line, with values capped at about 200%.
Open the chat list (Chats) and check the header title and subtitle are still readable.
Compare with Expected: text grows up to about 200% and nothing is cut off.
items.needs: a device with text-size control; the text-size option itself is not in the app
items.note: The code caps font scaling at maxFontSizeMultiplier 2 on settings rows and the chat list title, but there is no in-app text-size control to find.

items.where: Device Reduce Motion setting (not an app control); effect seen on looping or moving animations in the app
steps: Turn on Reduce Motion in the device accessibility settings.
Open the app and go to a screen with a loading or offline indicator.
Check that looping or travelling animations stop or are replaced by a static display.
Compare with Expected: the animations stop or change while Reduce Motion is on.
items.needs: a device that lets the tester turn on Reduce Motion
items.note: The app reads the OS reduce-motion flag through AccessibilityInfo; I did not find a visible in-app switch for it.

items.where: Settings > Device > Voice > "Open Voice Companion", then the live voice bar button "Show captions" / "Hide captions"
steps: Open Settings > Device > Voice.
Tap "Open Voice Companion" (this row appears only when the on-device recognizer is available).
Start a voice conversation and speak.
Tap the captions button (labelled "Show captions" or "Hide captions") in the voice bar.
Compare with Expected: spoken words appear as live captions while the conversation runs.
items.needs: a microphone and a device with an on-device speech recognizer; the "Open Voice Companion" row is hidden otherwise
items.note: Live voice is also available inside a chat through the chat voice composer, but I did not confirm the button that starts it.

items.where: Settings > Device > Voice > "Open Voice Companion", then the live transcript shown under the voice bar when captions are on
steps: Open Settings > Device > Voice and tap "Open Voice Companion".
Turn captions on ("Show captions") and have a short spoken exchange.
Read the transcript area (testID live-voice-transcript) that lists each turn.
Go back to the chat that the voice session came from and look for the conversation text.
Compare with Expected: a readable text transcript is kept with the chat.
items.needs: a microphone and an on-device speech recognizer
items.note: The code shows the transcript while captions are on, but I did not confirm that the voice turns are saved into the chat history.

items.where: Settings > Device > General > "App language"
steps: Open Settings > Device > General.
Tap "App language" and choose a right-to-left language.
Go back and look at the app layout: menus, rows and text should mirror (text aligned to the right, start and end swapped).
If the layout does not change, check whether the app asks you to restart it.
Compare with Expected: the whole layout mirrors correctly.
items.needs: a device or app setting that lets the app use a right-to-left language
items.note: The code applies the right-to-left layout through applyLayoutDirection; I did not confirm which languages are offered or whether a restart is needed.

items.where: Chat screen > a message bubble that mixes Arabic or Hebrew text with English text
steps: Open a chat and send a message that has an Arabic or Hebrew paragraph and an English paragraph (or ask for a reply that contains both).
Look at each paragraph in the message bubble.
Check that the Arabic or Hebrew paragraph is right-aligned and the English paragraph is left-aligned.
Compare with Expected: each paragraph is shown in its own direction.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a chat that can show mixed-direction text
items.note: The code applies right-to-left style per paragraph (directionStyle in MessageContentRenderer); I did not find a left-to-right paragraph style of dir=auto, so the English paragraph may depend on the default.

items.where: Chat screen > "Message input" field (a Japanese, Chinese or Korean keyboard)
steps: Switch the Mac keyboard to a Japanese, Chinese or Korean input method.
Open a chat, focus the "Message input" field and type a phrase so it is still being converted (underlined).
Press Enter to confirm the conversion.
Check that the message is not sent and the composed text stays in the field.
Compare with Expected: Enter confirms the composition and never sends the message.
items.needs: a Japanese, Chinese or Korean input method on the keyboard
items.note: The code shows a multiline field with blurOnSubmit false, and I found no explicit composition handling; Enter is not wired to send in this file.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage
steps: Open Settings and go to the Cloud section, then tap Usage.
Look at any date shown, such as "Expires ..." or "Next expiry ...".
Look at the numbers, such as counts with thousands separators.
Change the device region or language in the device settings, reopen the screen and compare the date and number format.
Compare with Expected: dates and numbers follow the user's locale.
items.needs: a cloud account with credits that have an expiry date (for the date to appear)
items.note: Dates are formatted with the device locale in cloud-usage; the context-window number is formatted by Intl in plans.

items.where: Settings > Account > Subscription
steps: Open Settings and go to the Account section, then tap Subscription.
Look at the "Current Plan" section and any plan button showing a price, such as "Upgrade · price".
Compare the currency symbol and number format with the device region.
Compare with Expected: the price shows the right currency symbol and number format.
items.needs: a store account (App Store or Google Play); prices come from the store, so they can show only in an app-store build
items.note: Price text comes from the store (nativeIap.priceFor) and is not formatted in the app; the sandbox store may not show prices on a Mac.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Reflect (the follow-up count line in the recap)
steps: Open Settings, go to the Cloud section and tap Reflect.
Look at the ongoing-work lines that show a follow-up count.
Find a line with exactly one follow-up and one with more than one.
Compare with Expected: "1 follow-up" and "2 follow-ups" follow the language's plural rules.
items.needs: a cloud account with some recap data (ongoing work with follow-ups)
items.note: Other plural strings are in app/(app)/settings/memory-import.tsx, app/(app)/scan.tsx and ArtifactChangesView.tsx, but their entry screens were not traced.

items.needs: device
items.note: The ledger has no code location for this item and I did not find a specific long-label or translated-copy layout check in apps/mobile; I did not search exhaustively.

items.where: Drawer (top-left menu) > New chat
steps: Sign in, or stay on the chat tab if it is already open.
Tap the menu button at the top left to open the drawer, then tap New chat.
Look for an empty conversation area with no earlier messages, a greeting at the top, and the composer at the bottom with its text field.
items.needs: none
items.note: The empty new-chat canvas is drawn in app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx (testID chat.new-chat.middle). The ChatEmptyState component cited in the plan is only used for a saved conversation that has no messages (chat/[id]), not on the new-chat screen.

items.where: Drawer > Settings > Personalization > Nickname (type your name), then Drawer > New chat
steps: Open the drawer and tap Settings, then tap Personalization.
Type a name in the Nickname field and leave the screen so it saves.
Open the drawer and tap New chat.
Look at the greeting at the top of the new chat, which should read with your name, for example Good morning, <name>.
items.needs: a signed-in account, or a local chat (no account needed), and a name to type
items.note: The name comes from the nickname first, then the first word of the full name, then (in Cloud) the account first name. The greeting text is built in packages/platform/utils/src/greeting.ts. The plan cites ChatEmptyState, which is not the new-chat greeting (see S12.01).

items.where: Drawer > Settings > Personalization > Nickname (clear the field), then Drawer > New chat
steps: Open the drawer, tap Settings, then tap Personalization.
Clear the Nickname field (leave it empty) and leave the screen so it saves.
Open the drawer and tap New chat.
Look at the greeting: it should be a plain time-of-day phrase such as Good morning with no name and no personal details.
items.needs: none (a local chat works without an account)
items.note: No separate on/off switch for personalization was found. Clearing the nickname sets nameOptedOut, and the greeting then has no name. If a Full Name is still saved in local mode, its first word is still used. The line How can I help you? is not shown on the new-chat screen.

items.needs: none
items.note: Searched apps/mobile (src, app, components) for TaskChip, taskChip, Quick task and Task categor: nothing found. TaskChips.tsx does not exist. The + sheet has Create image, Create video and Create file rows, which are not one-tap task shortcuts that set up the next message.

items.where: New chat > + (Add to chat, left of the composer text field) > Attach from Library
steps: On the new-chat screen, tap the + button at the left of the composer.
Look at the Add to Chat sheet, under the Camera, Photos and File cards, for the Attach from Library section.
If recent files are listed there, tap one to attach it to the next message.
Compare with Expected: the recently used files should be offered in one step.
items.needs: a file to upload in an earlier chat (so there is a recent file to offer)
items.note: Recent files come from recentMobileFiles in apps/mobile/src/features/search/mobileGlobalSearch. The Attach from Library section only appears when there are library items, and in Cloud mode it also loads the cloud library.

items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account that can use connectors
items.note: The connector suggestion chips (NewChatConnectorSuggestions.tsx) render only inside ChatEmptyState, which MessageList shows for a saved conversation with zero messages (chat/[id]), not on the new-chat screen. The new-chat + sheet has a Connectors row (Manage connectors), which lists connectors but does not recommend them. Searched apps/mobile for NewChatConnectorSuggestions and ChatEmptyState usage.

items.where: New chat > + (Add to chat) > Web search toggle
steps: Switch to Cloud (Drawer > Cloud), then open the new-chat screen.
Tap the + button at the left of the composer to open the Add to Chat sheet.
Turn on the Web search switch row.
Close the sheet, type a question that needs current facts, send it, and check that the answer uses web results.
items.needs: a Cloud account granted web search, and a model that supports search
items.note: The row appears only in Cloud mode when the account has canUseWebSearch and the model supports search. The plan's TaskChips.tsx source no longer exists.

items.where: New chat > + (Add to chat) > Deep research switch
steps: Switch to Cloud, then open the new-chat screen.
Tap the + button and find the Deep research row in the Add to Chat sheet.
Turn on the Deep research switch and close the sheet.
Send a question and look for the Research chip above the composer (accessibility label Deep Research active).
items.needs: a Cloud account whose plan grants deep research, and a model that supports research and search (which plan includes it was not verified)
items.note: The row is hidden unless FEATURES.research, Cloud mode, the model's research and search capabilities, and canUseDeepResearch are all true.

items.where: New chat > + (Add to chat) > Create image
steps: Switch to Cloud, then open the new-chat screen.
Tap the + button and tap Create image in the Add to Chat sheet.
Look at the new-chat heading: it should change to Create an image, and the composer is now in image mode.
Type a prompt and tap send; look for a generated image in the reply.
items.needs: a Cloud account granted image creation (canUseImages) and an image model in the catalogue
items.note: The Create image row only shows when FEATURES.imageGen, Cloud mode, an image model and canUseImages are all present.

items.where: New chat > + (Add to chat) > Create video
steps: Switch to Cloud, then open the new-chat screen.
Tap the + button and tap Create video in the Add to Chat sheet.
Look at the new-chat heading: it should change to Create a video, with duration and aspect options.
Type a prompt and send; look for the video generation start (a notice may appear if the request is blocked).
items.needs: a Cloud account granted video generation (canUseVideoGeneration)
items.note: The row only shows when FEATURES.videoGen, Cloud mode, a video model and canUseVideoGeneration are all present. Blocked requests show an alert from resolveMobileVideoGenerationRequest.

items.where: New chat > empty composer > Start voice mode (round button at the right end of the composer)
steps: Open the new-chat screen and leave the composer text field empty.
Look at the right end of the composer for the round button with the voice action.
Tap it. A voice intro sheet may show first; continue through it.
Look for the voice conversation screen (hands-free voice mode) and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone, microphone permission, and a plan with voice (canUseVoice)
items.note: The button shows only when the composer is empty and voice is allowed. Typing /voice in the composer also opens voice mode.

items.where: New chat > header switch Chat or Work > Work
steps: Open the new-chat screen and look at the header switch with the words Chat and Work.
Tap Work.
Look for the Work state: an approval mode control appears above the composer.
Send a task that needs several steps and tools, then compare with Expected (planned, multi-step work).
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account (if signed out, tapping Work opens sign-in)
items.note: The switch is the segment with accessibilityLabel Chat or Work. The hint text says Your next messages run as AGI Work: planned, multi-step work with tools.

items.where: Drawer > AGI Code > New session
steps: Sign in and open the drawer.
Tap AGI Code.
Tap New session on the AGI Code screen.
Look at the New session sheet: Task, Repository, Network access and Start session sections should appear, which is the coding-agent setup.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account; a GitHub repository is needed to pick a repository
items.note: The coding entry is not in the new-chat + sheet; it is the AGI Code drawer item. The plan's cited line numbers moved but the feature is present.

items.where: New chat > top-right eye-off icon (Enable temporary chat) > Turn on
steps: Open the new-chat screen and look at the top-right corner for the eye-off icon.
Tap it. An alert titled Turn on temporary chat? appears.
Tap Turn on. The icon now shows a Temporary label in purple.
Send a message, then check that the chat does not appear in your chat history after it finishes (compare with Expected).
items.needs: none
items.note: The toggle is rendered in app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx header. Whether a temporary chat is kept out of history is not judged here.

items.where: New chat > composer bottom row, the model name beside the + button
steps: Open the new-chat screen.
Look at the bottom row of the composer, next to the + button: the model name is shown there.
Tap the model name. The model picker sheet opens.
Close the picker without changing anything and compare the name shown with the model you expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The model name is shown from the selected model (getShortDisplayName), so its text varies. The word Fast appears only when fast mode is on. The button is hidden in image and video modes.

items.where: Drawer > Cloud (mode toggle) > New chat, read the line under the greeting
steps: Open the drawer and tap Cloud in the mode toggle.
Tap New chat.
Look just under the greeting for a line that reads Workspace: <name>, with a building icon (organization) or a person icon (personal).
Compare the name with the workspace you expected.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account; a second account in the same organization to check an organization workspace
items.note: The line shows only in Cloud mode when a workspace resolves. The mode toggle is imported by the drawer (DrawerContent.tsx); its exact placement was inferred from the import, not seen on screen.

items.where: New chat > + (Add to chat) > Project, then pick a project in the Projects picker
steps: Make sure at least one project exists (create one from the drawer if needed).
On the new-chat screen, tap the + button and tap Project in the Add to Chat sheet.
Choose a project in the Projects list.
Look for the line In <project name> under the greeting, with an X to start outside it (compare with Expected).
items.needs: at least one project already created
items.note: The In <name> line is drawn in app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx with testID chat.new-chat.project. The Project row shows Choose until a project is picked.

items.where: First launch after sign-up or install: the onboarding hero screen (shown when onboarding-done is not set)
steps: Start from a fresh install, or reset the onboarding flag, and open the app past the age check.
Read the hero screen: it shows the tagline Your AI workspace for everyday work. and the list of key notices.
Tap the main button at the bottom of the hero screen to continue.
Compare the intro with Expected: a short overview of the key features before the first chat.
items.needs: a fresh install or a reset of the first-run flag

labels.text: Your AI workspace for everyday work.

items.note: The onboarding intro is a single hero screen with a feature sentence (Chat, write, code, research, and organize projects in one place.). No per-feature tour for the new-chat controls was found. The exact text of the hero button was not checked.

items.where: New chat > type in the Message input > switch to another screen > back to New chat
steps: Open the new-chat screen and type a few words into the Message input field, without sending.
Open the drawer and go to another screen (for example Settings), then go back to New chat.
Look at the composer: the typed words should be back in the field.
Optionally fully close and reopen the app and compare the field again (persistence across reload is not confirmed in code).
items.needs: none
items.note: The draft is restored by getDraft in ChatInput.tsx with draftKey new-chat (set in app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx). Restore after a full app reload was not verified in the code.

items.where: New chat > header switch Chat or Work > Work while signed out (opens sign-in); or Drawer > Cloud while signed out
steps: Sign out (or use a fresh install) and open the new-chat screen in Local mode.
Look for the line Run AI privately on this device, no account needed. in the download-model banner.
Tap Work in the header switch; a sign-in step opens instead of Work.
Compare with Expected: local use works without an account, and Cloud use prompts sign-in.
items.needs: a signed-out or Free account

labels.text: Run AI privately on this device, no account needed.

items.note: No numeric guest limit (for example a message count) was found in the code, so the stated-limits part of Expected could not be checked. Searched apps/mobile for guest-related limit code with no match.

items.where: First screen after sign-in (New chat) > message box that shows "What's on your mind?" > type > Send message button on the right of the box
steps: Sign in and wait for the New chat screen.
Tap the message box that shows "What's on your mind?".
Type a short sentence, for example "Hello, this is a test".
Tap the send button on the right of the box (accessibility label "Send message").
Compare: your text appears as a sent message and the box is cleared.
items.needs: none
items.note: The placeholder changes with state (for example "Type or hold to talk", "Reply to AGI" or "Offline, message will send on reconnect"). "Send message" is an accessibility label on an icon, not visible text.

items.where: First screen after sign-in (New chat) > message box "What's on your mind?"
steps: Tap the message box.
Type "First line".
Press Return on the keyboard (this does not send).
Type "Second line".
Compare: the box shows two lines. Send, then check that the sent message keeps the line break.
items.needs: none
items.note: The field is multiline and nothing binds Return to send. Whether the line break survives in the sent message was not checked in code.

items.where: Message box "What's on your mind?" on the New chat screen; the box grows as you type
steps: Tap the message box.
Press Return and type until the text is more than about eight lines long.
Compare: the box grows taller as lines are added, stops growing at a cap, then scrolls inside the box.
items.needs: none
items.note: The code caps the field at a maximum height of 160 with a scroll, so the exact cap is not confirmed on screen.

items.where: New chat > message box > "Expand message" control (small icon at the top right of the box; appears once the text is multiline)
steps: Type several lines so the box is multiline.
Tap the small expand icon at the top right of the box (accessibility label "Expand message").
Compare: a full-screen "Message" editor opens.
Tap "Collapse editor" (top left) to return to the box.
items.needs: none
items.note: The expand control opens a full-screen editor. No drag handle or resize control was found, so the box itself does not get taller on demand.

items.where: New chat > message box > "Expand message" > full-screen "Message" editor > "Collapse editor"
steps: Type some text and tap the "Expand message" icon at the top right of the box.
In the full-screen "Message" editor, add or change text.
Tap the top-left icon with the accessibility label "Collapse editor".
Compare: you are back in the message box and the edited text is kept.
Optionally tap the send button at the top right of the full-screen editor.
items.needs: none
items.note: The code opens an in-app full-screen editor only. No external editor option was found.

items.where: New chat > message box > send button on the right of the box (accessibility label "Send message")
steps: With the box empty, look at the send button and note it is dimmed.
Type a sentence.
Tap the send button.
Compare: the message is sent and the box is cleared. While offline, the box says "Offline, message will send on reconnect" instead.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Offline, message will send on reconnect

items.note: The disabled state is shown by the dimmed button. The only visible reason text found is the offline placeholder. The "Sending when the upload finishes" accessibility label covers uploads.

items.where: New chat > send any message > while the reply streams, the send button becomes the stop control (accessibility label "Stop generating")
steps: Send a message that gets a long reply.
While the reply is streaming, look at the right of the box where the send button was.
Tap that button (accessibility label "Stop generating").
Compare: the reply stops and the text produced so far stays on screen.
items.needs: none
