items.note: "Stop generating" is an accessibility label; the visible control is an icon. Whether produced text is kept was not checked in code.

items.where: New chat > message box > Shift+Return on a hardware keyboard
steps: Tap the message box and type "one".
Press Shift+Return on a connected keyboard.
Compare: a new line appears in the box and the message is not sent.
items.needs: a hardware keyboard (for example the Mac keyboard connected to the simulator)
items.note: No Shift+Enter handler exists in the composer code. The newline comes from the multiline field, and Return is not bound to send, so test Shift+Return and plain Return the same way.

items.needs: a hardware keyboard
items.note: Searched apps/mobile for undo and redo in the chat composer. No composer undo or redo handler was found. The only "Undo last change" label is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx, which is the artifact editor, not the composer.

items.where: New chat > message box > long press > Paste (text, from the system menu); New chat > "Add to chat" (+) > "Paste image" (image)
steps: Copy a sentence in another app.
Long-press the message box and choose Paste.
Compare: the text appears in the box.
Copy an image, tap "Add to chat" (+), then tap "Paste image".
Compare: the image appears as an attachment in the strip above the box.
items.needs: a sentence and an image on the clipboard
items.note: The long-press Paste menu comes from iOS, not app code. Large pasted text becomes a "Pasted text" chip (see S13.14).

items.needs: formatted text copied from a web page
items.note: Searched ChatInput.tsx and src/features/chat for HTML or rich-text normalization on paste. None was found; the message box is a plain multiline text field. Whether iOS pastes plain text was not verified in code.

items.where: New chat > message box > paste a very long block of text; it appears as a "Pasted text" chip above the box
steps: Copy a long text (several pages) from another app.
Paste it into the message box.
Compare: a "Pasted text" chip appears above the box with its size, instead of filling the box.
Tap the chip to expand the text back into the message box.
items.needs: a long text on the clipboard
items.note: The chip's accessibility hint reads "Expands the pasted text back into the message input". The size threshold is in ChatInput.tsx and was not checked.

items.where: Open a long conversation > warning line above the message box: "Chat is getting long. Start a fresh chat for faster responses."
steps: Open a conversation with many long messages.
Look at the line above the message box.
Tap the warning line to open the context details.
Compare: the warning shows only for a long chat, and no character or token count appears while you type.
items.needs: a long conversation

labels.text: Chat is getting long. Start a fresh chat for faster responses.

items.note: No character or token counter was found in the composer. The only length indicator is this warning, which appears when the context budget is not ok.

items.where: Message box on the New chat screen (draft is saved on the device)
steps: Type a sentence in the message box but do not send it.
Force quit the app (or reload the page on web).
Reopen the app and sign in again if asked.
Compare: the typed sentence is back in the message box.
items.needs: none
items.note: Drafts are saved on the device by apps/mobile/src/features/chat/draftStore.ts, keyed per conversation. Not checked on a device.

items.where: Message box after a send fails
steps: Type a sentence and tap the send button.
Wait for the send to fail (offline sends are queued, so use a failing server response if you can).
Compare: the sent text is put back at the top of the message box.
items.needs: a way to make the send fail; offline does not fail, it queues
items.note: The restore is in code (restoreSentText in ChatInput.tsx), but no visible notice for a restored draft was found. The only failed-send alert found is "Pasted text not sent", which applies to large pasted text.

items.where: Message box on each chat; the draft is kept per conversation
steps: In one chat, type "draft A" and do not send.
Open a different chat from the chat list.
Compare: that chat's message box is empty.
Type "draft B" there, then go back to the first chat.
Compare: "draft A" is still there and "draft B" is not.
items.needs: two conversations
items.note: Drafts are keyed by conversation in apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx and ChatInput.tsx (draftKey).

items.where: New chat > message box > type "/"
steps: Tap the message box.
Type "/".
Compare: a "Command suggestions" list shows /image (Generate an image), /voice (Start voice conversation), /compare (Compare model responses) and /export (Export conversation).
Type "/im" and compare: the list filters to /image.
Tap a command to choose it.
items.needs: none
items.note: Some commands depend on account or boundary (the code shows a cloud boundary tag). Keyboard selection was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: New chat > "Add to chat" (+) > "Skills" > pick a skill
steps: Tap the + button (accessibility label "Add to chat") at the left of the message box.
Tap "Skills" in the sheet.
Pick a skill.
Compare: the skill name shows as a chip above the box, and the next message runs with it.
Optionally tap the X on the chip (accessibility label "Clear selected Skill") and compare that the chip is gone.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account (the chip says "selected for the next Cloud message"); plan requirement not confirmed
items.note: "Clear selected Skill" is an accessibility label on the X icon.

items.where: New chat > "Add to chat" (+) > "Skills", "Project" or "File"; chips and the attachment strip appear above the message box
steps: Tap + > "Skills" and pick a skill; compare the skill chip above the box, then tap its X and compare it is removed.
Tap + > "Project" and pick a project; compare the project bar appears; its "Clear project" control removes it.
Tap + > "File" and pick a file; compare it appears in the "Attached files" strip with a Remove control.
Compare each chip is removable and shows its name.
items.needs: a Cloud account, a file to upload, and at least one project and skill
items.note: No page-context chip was found in the composer. The project bar is ProjectSelectorBar (accessibility label "Clear project").

items.where: New chat > "Add to chat" (+) > "Web search" or "Connectors"
steps: Tap the + button and tap "Web search".
Look at the row in the sheet: it shows a "selected" state when on.
Close the sheet and look above the message box.
Compare: sources should show as chips before sending.
items.needs: a Cloud account; a connected connector for the Connectors row
items.note: No chip for web search or connector sources was found in ChatInput.tsx. Only the Research and Run code chips appear above the box, so the Expected chip row does not match the code.

items.where: New chat > "Add to chat" (+) > "Deep research" or "Run code"; chips appear in a row above the message box
steps: Tap the + button.
Tap "Deep research" or "Run code" to switch it on.
Close the sheet.
Compare: a chip labelled "Research" or "Run code" appears above the message box.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account; a model that supports research or code
items.note: The chip appears only when the model and account support the tool; the row has the accessibility label "Active chat tools".

items.where: New chat > "Add to chat" (+) > "Create file" > "Document", "Presentation" or "Spreadsheet"
steps: Tap the + button and tap "Create file".
Choose an output: Document, Presentation or Spreadsheet.
Compare: the "Create file" row shows the chosen format.
Send a message and check that the reply is that kind of file.
items.needs: a Cloud account with the code feature on (the row only shows in Cloud text mode)
items.note: Expected lists table, code and slides, but the code offers only docx, pptx and xlsx (labelled Document, Presentation and Spreadsheet). The cited chatExecutionStore.ts line no longer holds the format choice; it is stored in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/store/outputFormatStore.ts.

items.where: New chat > "Add to chat" (+) button at the left of the message box
steps: Tap the + button.
Compare the sheet lists Camera, Photos, Paste image and File.
Scroll the sheet: compare Create image, Create video, Create file, Web search, Deep research, Run code, Study and learn, Project, Connectors, Skills and Choose style are there.
Close the sheet and compare it closes without adding anything.
items.needs: phone width; a Cloud account to see the Cloud rows
items.note: Which rows appear depends on account, plan and mode, so not every row shows for every account.

items.where: New chat > microphone icon in the message box controls (accessibility label "Tap to record, hold for push-to-talk")
steps: Tap the microphone icon.
Speak a sentence.
Tap the square "Stop recording" control.
Compare: the spoken words appear in the message box and nothing is sent.
Tap "Send message" yourself to send it.
items.needs: a microphone and microphone permission

labels.text: Tap to record, hold for push-to-talk

items.note: Stop recording drops the transcript into the box. The separate "Send recording" control sends it in one tap, so do not use it for this check.

items.where: New chat > empty message box > round "Start voice mode" button on the right; or long-press the microphone icon
steps: Make sure the message box is empty.
Tap the round button with the accessibility label "Start voice mode".
Compare: a hands-free voice conversation opens.
Speak and check that a reply is spoken back.
items.needs: a microphone and microphone permission; voice mode available on the account (not confirmed)

labels.text: Tap to record, hold for push-to-talk

items.note: The "Start voice mode" button shows only when the box is empty and voice mode is available. The microphone hint says long press opens voice conversation mode.

items.where: Chat screen > type a message while a reply is still streaming > tap the "Queue message" button beside the stop button
steps: Start a chat and send any message so that a reply begins to stream.
While the reply is still streaming, tap the composer and type a second message.
Look for the "Queue message" button next to the stop control (it appears only while a reply streams and the composer has text).
Tap "Queue message". Check that the composer clears and a queued-message chip appears above it, and that the reply keeps streaming.
When the first reply finishes, check that the queued message is sent automatically.
items.needs: an account that can send a chat message and get a streaming reply
items.note: The "Queue message" button has an icon only (clock) with this accessibility label, so no visible text is shown; the queued chip shows the message text, not a visible label.

items.where: Chat screen > after queuing a message, the queued chip above the composer > pencil icon "Edit queued message" or X icon "Cancel queued message"
steps: Queue a message as in S13.38 while a reply is streaming.
Look above the composer for the queued chip that shows the queued message text.
Tap the pencil (Edit queued message) icon: the text goes back into the composer and the chip disappears; check that it is not sent yet.
Queue a new message again, then tap the X (Cancel queued message) icon: check that the chip disappears and the message is not sent when the reply finishes.
items.needs: an account that can send a chat message and get a streaming reply
items.note: Both controls are icon buttons (pencil and X); their words are accessibility labels, not visible text. Edit returns the text to the composer, and cancel removes it without sending.

items.where: Chat screen > a managed cloud agent reply that is still running > "Message the agent" under the agent activity, then "Send to the agent"
steps: Start a managed cloud agent task from chat and wait until its run is in the running state.
Under the agent activity shown for that running run, tap "Message the agent".
Type guidance into the box that shows "Add instructions or change course".
Tap "Send to the agent" and check that the note "Sent. The agent reads your message at its next step." appears and the run keeps going without stopping.
Note: a second entry point "Message the agent" exists in the Tasks run detail (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/components/CloudRunSteerSection.tsx:75), and the tester may use either.
items.needs: an account with managed cloud agent access and a cloud agent run that is currently running
items.note: The entry point is shown only when a chat message carries a managed cloud agent run reference and that run is running (AgentActivityTimeline.tsx:1176, MessageBubble.tsx:1026); how a tester reaches such a run from the first screen was not confirmed, and the tab name Chat was not checked against the tab layout.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > File (AGI Cloud mode only)
steps: On the Chat screen, switch the mode toggle to AGI Cloud.
Tap the + button labelled Add to chat at the left of the message box.
Tap the File card in the sheet titled Add to Chat.
In the phone's file chooser, pick a PDF or text file.
Look at the composer: the file should appear as a chip, and after sending the message the file should be attached to it.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a file on the phone
items.note: The File card is shown only when the mode is AGI Cloud (AddToChatSheet.tsx:720); the sheet has no File card in on-device mode.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Camera
steps: On the Chat screen, tap the + button labelled Add to chat.
Tap the Camera card in the sheet titled Add to Chat.
If asked, allow camera access; take a photo with the camera screen.
Look at the composer: the photo should appear as a thumbnail chip, ready to send.
items.needs: a phone with a camera; an account that has the camera capability (the Camera card is hidden otherwise)
items.note: The Camera card depends on the canUseCamera capability (AddToChatSheet.tsx:697), so a tester on an account without it will not see it.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Photos
steps: On the Chat screen, tap the + button labelled Add to chat.
Tap the Photos card in the sheet titled Add to Chat.
In the photo library, tap one photo, then confirm the picker.
Look at the composer: the chosen photo should appear as a thumbnail chip.
items.needs: a phone with at least one photo in the library

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Attach from Library (tap a file row)
steps: On the Chat screen, switch the mode to AGI Cloud.
Tap the + button labelled Add to chat.
Look for the Attach from Library section in the sheet and tap a file row (its label reads Attach <file name> from Library).
Look at the composer: the Library file should appear as an attachment chip.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one image or file already in its Library
items.note: The section appears only when Library items exist; it is hidden in an empty Library.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Photos (select several); AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File (select several)
steps: Tap the + button labelled Add to chat, then tap Photos.
In the photo picker, tap two or more photos, then confirm.
Look at the composer: every chosen photo should appear as its own chip.
Repeat with AGI Cloud mode and File, choosing several files, and check that each one is attached.
items.needs: several photos on the phone, and for the File part an AGI Cloud account and several files
items.note: The photo picker is multi-select (allowsMultipleSelection true) and the file chooser sets multiple: true.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Photos
steps: Tap the + button labelled Add to chat, then tap Photos.
Pick one photo and confirm.
Look at the message box area: the photo should show as a square picture (about 72 by 72) before sending.
items.needs: a phone with a photo in the library

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > File (AGI Cloud mode)
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap the File card.
Pick a PDF, then a spreadsheet (for example .csv or .xlsx), then a code file (for example .py).
Look at each chip: under the file name it should show the kind word: PDF, Spreadsheet or Code.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and one PDF, one spreadsheet and one code file
items.note: Other kinds show the words Presentation, Document, Text or File (AttachmentPreview.tsx:105-111).

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > File (AGI Cloud mode)
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File.
Pick a non-image file such as a PDF.
Look at the chip: it should show the file name and, under it, the kind and size (for example PDF and a size in KB or MB).
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a non-image file

items.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File.
Pick a large file (several megabytes) so the upload lasts a few seconds.
While it uploads, look at the bottom edge of the chip: a thin progress bar fills up.
Compare with Expected: the chip shows progress while the upload runs. The percentage (Uploading NN%) is only in the screen-reader label, not printed on the chip.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a large file
items.note: The progress label text is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/upload/uploadLifecycle.ts:46 and is not drawn on screen; only the bar is visible.

items.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > Photos or File, then wait for the upload
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then pick a photo under Photos.
Watch the chip while it uploads (progress bar).
When the bar disappears, check the chip has no Retry or Cancel overlay and the Send button is not held.
Compare with Expected: the code shows no visible Ready or Uploaded word, so judge whether the chip alone makes ready clear.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account
items.note: No visible 'ready' wording was found in AttachmentPreview.tsx; the word Uploaded only appears in a screen-reader label.

items.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File, then send; read the line under your sent message
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File.
Pick a long text or document file that is larger than the readable limit.
Type a short question and send.
Look under your sent message: a grey line should say Only part of <file name> was read because it is too long to read in full.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a long document
items.note: The notice is shown only for the AGI Cloud path (streaming header); on-device reading adds the text to the model input instead.

items.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File.
Pick a file type the chat cannot read (for example an executable or an unsupported archive, if the chooser lets you pick it).
Look for the alert titled Attachment not added: it should name the file and say it is not a supported file type.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a file the chat refuses
items.note: The chooser only offers types listed in services/docParser.ts, so a refused type may not be selectable; the alert text is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/attachmentValidation.ts:123.

items.needs: a password-protected PDF
items.note: The notice text is written only into the input sent to the model (apps/mobile/services/attachmentContext.ts:45), so no app-drawn notice was found; the File card that could attach a PDF is shown only in AGI Cloud mode (AddToChatSheet.tsx:720), where the password check runs on the server, which is not in this app's code. Searched apps/mobile for ENCRYPTED_PDF and password protected.

items.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > Photos (upload fails), then tap Retry on the chip
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, turn Wi-Fi and mobile data off, then tap Add to chat (+) and pick a photo.
Wait until the chip shows a failed state with a Retry overlay.
Turn the network back on and tap Retry on the chip.
Look at the chip: the upload should start again and the Retry overlay should go away when it finishes.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a way to switch the network off and on

items.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File, then tap the small X on the uploading chip
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File and pick a large file.
While the progress bar is moving, tap the small X on the chip's corner (screen reader label: Cancel upload of <file name>).
Look at the chip: it should disappear and the upload should stop.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a large file

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Photos, then tap the small X on the chip
steps: Tap Add to chat (+), then tap Photos and pick two photos.
Tap the small X at the top corner of one chip (screen reader label: Remove <file name>).
Look at the composer: that chip should disappear.
Send the message and check the sent message shows only the other photo.
items.needs: a phone with at least two photos

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Photos (pick the same photo twice)
steps: Tap Add to chat (+), then tap Photos and pick one photo.
Open Add to chat (+) again, tap Photos, and pick the same photo again.
Look for an alert titled Already attached that names the file and says Each file is attached once.
Check the composer shows the photo only once.
items.needs: a phone with a photo in the library
items.note: Duplicates are matched by attachment identity; a newly taken camera photo has a new identity, so it is not treated as a duplicate.

items.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File (pick several files, one refused)
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File.
Pick one acceptable file and one refused file together.
Look for the alert Attachment not added: it should name the refused file in quotes and give the reason.
Check that the accepted file still appears as a chip.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and one file the chat refuses
items.note: Per-file reasons are built in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/attachmentValidation.ts; a failed upload shows Retry on that chip (AttachmentPreview.tsx:392) rather than a named error.

items.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File (pick three or more files, one refused)
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File.
Pick three files, with at least one the chat refuses.
Look for one alert titled Some attachments not added that lists each refused file with its reason.
Check that the accepted files appear as chips in the composer.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and three files, one refused

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) (read the caption under the Add to Chat title)
steps: Tap Add to chat (+) with AGI Cloud mode on.
Read the grey line under the Add to Chat title: it should say Uploaded to AGI Cloud and kept in your Library until you delete them.
Open a temporary chat and tap Add to chat (+) again; the line should say Kept out of your Library and deleted with this temporary chat.
Compare with Expected: whether and how long files are kept.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account; a temporary chat for the second check

labels.text: Uploaded to AGI Cloud and kept in your Library until you delete them.

items.note: The on-device-mode caption (AddToChatSheet.tsx:131) says nothing about keeping files, so in on-device mode the explanation is missing.

items.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > Photos (pick a HEIC photo)
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap Photos.
Pick a HEIC photo from the library.
Look for the alert Attachment not added: it should say AGI Cloud cannot read the HEIC photo and to retake it with the in-app camera.
Compare with Expected: the alert names the alternative (retake with the camera).
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a HEIC photo on the phone

labels.text: retake it with the in-app camera

items.note: HEIC photos may be converted before this check (apps/mobile/src/features/media/image-normalization), so the alert may not appear; the on-device Office-file alert (switch to AGI Cloud for Office files) is not reachable from the sheet because the File card is hidden in on-device mode.

items.where: Chat screen > composer bar: the model name button beside the + (Add to chat) button
steps: Open the app and go to a new chat.
Look at the bottom bar of the message box, next to the + button.
Read the model name on that button.
Send a short message and compare the name on the button with the model shown under the answer (see S15.32).
items.needs: none
items.note: The name is computed by getShortDisplayName, so there is no literal visible string for it in the code.

items.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > any model row
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
In the Models sheet, look at the small grey text to the right of each model name.
Compare the text with the company or provider shown for that model.
items.needs: none
items.note: For providers with a logo, the row shows the logo icon and no provider text; the provider name text appears only for providers without a logo. The text itself is built from the provider name in service.ts.

items.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > open a model row's chevron (More models)
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Scroll the Models sheet to a model row that has a chevron on its right.
Tap the chevron to open the other models in that line.
Check that the related versions of one model line appear together under that row.
items.needs: none
items.note: The chevron has no visible words; its accessibility label is 'More <line name> models'.

items.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > Search models…
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Tap the field that says Search models….
Type part of a model name, such as a few letters.
Check that the list shrinks to the models whose names match.
items.needs: none

items.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > long-press a model row
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Press and hold a model row for about half a second.
Check that a small gold star appears on that row.
Scroll to the top of the Models sheet and check that the starred model is in the Favorites group.
items.needs: none
items.note: Long-press on a model that needs sign-in or an upgrade opens the upgrade path instead of favouriting.

items.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > Recent group at the top
steps: Pick any model from the Models sheet so the sheet closes.
Tap the model name in the composer bar again.
Look at the group titled Recent at the top of the list.
Check that the model you just used is listed there.
items.needs: none

items.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > top row labelled Auto
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Look at the rows at the top of the Models sheet, above Recent.
Tap the row named Auto and wait for the sheet to close.
Send a message and check the model shown under the answer (see S15.32) to see which model the product picked.
items.needs: none
items.note: Auto rows are built from the routing profiles in apps/mobile/lib/models.ts; the other profile names in that file are Instant, Best and Economy.

items.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > tap a model row
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Tap a model row that has no lock icon.
Check that the sheet closes and the composer shows the new name.
Send a message and check the model shown under the answer (see S15.32).
items.needs: none

items.where: Chat screen > side menu > AGI Cloud (mode switch) > tap the model name in the composer > Instant chip in the Models sheet
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Cloud in the mode switch.
Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Tap the chip labelled Instant under the search field.
Check that only the quick models remain in the list.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: The chip only filters to fast-speed models; the code has no visible text that says models are faster or slower. The Speed section with the Fast switch only states that fast answers cost more usage.

items.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > a model row with a lock icon and an Upgrade badge
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Find a model row with a lock icon and a yellow badge.
Read the badge text and compare it with Expected.
Tap that row and check that the upgrade options open.
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The badge reads Upgrade or Not included depending on whether purchases are available. The plan name (for example Max) appears only in the row's accessibility hint, not as visible text.

items.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > a model row with an Unavailable badge
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Look for a row with a grey Unavailable badge and a dimmed look.
Tap the row and check that nothing changes and the model is not selected.
items.needs: a live provider outage (cannot be made on demand) or an on-device model that is not on this device
items.note: The badge appears only when the server reports an outage, so a tester cannot force it. The visible line under the row says Unavailable right now. Try again soon or pick another model.

items.where: Chat screen > composer bar > reasoning effort button (appears for a reasoning model in AGI Cloud mode)
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Cloud, then open a new chat.
Choose a model that thinks (reasoning model) from the Models sheet.
Tap the effort button in the composer bar.
Move the effort slider to another level, then tap Done.
Check that the effort name changes on the slider and in the composer.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a reasoning model
items.note: The button is hidden for models without reasoning, so the tester must choose a reasoning model first.

items.where: Chat screen > + (Add to chat) > Choose style
steps: Tap the + button in the composer bar (labelled Add to chat).
Tap Choose style.
Pick Concise, Normal, Explanatory, Learning or Formal.
Send the same question twice, once with Concise and once with Explanatory, and compare the answer lengths.
items.needs: none
items.note: The styles are Normal, Concise, Explanatory, Learning and Formal, with the description Short, direct answers for Concise. There is no explicit longer-answer option, so the length preference is only a style.

items.where: Side menu > Local Mode (mode switch) > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > On device group
steps: Open the side menu and tap Local Mode in the mode switch.
Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Look for the group titled On device and a row with a chip icon.
Download a model if needed (Download badge), wait until it shows Ready, then pick it and check the composer name.
items.needs: a device with room for an on-device model (downloading is required for Ready)
items.note: The On device group title is in ModelPickerSheet.tsx. The Local Mode label is the switch's accessibility label.

items.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > pick a model, then close and reopen the app
steps: Pick a model from the Models sheet.
Close the app completely and open it again.
Go to a new chat and read the model name in the composer bar.
Check that it is the model you picked before closing.
items.needs: none
items.note: The choice is stored under the model-store key in apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/store.ts.

items.where: Open an existing chat > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > pick a model
steps: Open chat A and pick model X from the Models sheet.
Start a new chat and check its composer model name differs or stays as the default.
Go back to chat A and check the composer still shows model X.
Check that a different chat with no change still shows its own model.
items.needs: two chats
items.note: Selecting a model in an existing chat is saved for that conversation through setConversationModel in app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx.

items.where: Chat screen > under any finished assistant answer, the small line with provider and model
steps: Send a message in a chat and wait for the answer to finish streaming.
Look at the small text line under the answer.
Read the text, which joins the provider and the model name with a dot.
Compare it with the model you picked in the composer.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account for the AGI Cloud label
items.note: The footer is built in ProvenanceFooter.tsx; it is hidden while the answer is still streaming. An Auto answer shows the model as Auto.

items.where: Chat > send any message > look at your message and the reply
steps: Sign in, open a chat (or start a new one), type "Hello" in the message box and send it.
Look at your message: it sits on the right in a rounded bubble.
Look at the reply: it is plain text across the full width with no bubble.
Turn on a screen reader and move to your message: it is announced as "Your message: Hello" (the name "You" is only in that spoken label).
Compare with Expected: alignment and bubble style tell the two authors apart; no avatar or visible name was found in the code.
items.needs: a Free or paid account
items.note: Expected mentions an avatar, but the code draws no avatar; the author is told apart by alignment and bubble style, and the name appears only to screen readers.

items.where: Chat > send any message > your message in the transcript
steps: In a chat, type a short sentence in the message box.
Tap send.
Look at the transcript: the sentence you sent appears in your message bubble, unchanged.
items.needs: a Free or paid account

items.where: Chat > attach a file or image in the message box > send > the sent message
steps: In a chat, use the attach control in the message box to choose a photo or a file. The control's exact label was not checked in the code.
Send the message.
Look at the sent message: an image appears as a tile, and a file appears as a chip with its name and a detail line.
Tap the image tile (hint "Opens full screen") or the file chip (hint "Opens the file") and check it opens.
items.needs: a file or image to upload
items.note: The attach button's visible words were not found; if the file is missing from the phone, the app shows the alert "Could not open file" instead.

items.needs: none
items.note: Searched MessageBubble.tsx: the only chips on a sent user message are a quoted-text chip (text starting with "> " then a blank line) and a "Skill: " chip. No code adds connector, page, editor-selection or @mention chips to a sent message.

items.where: Chat > long-press your sent message > Copy Message
steps: Press and hold your sent message (about 0.4 seconds) to open the message actions.
Tap "Copy Message".
Paste into the message box.
Compare the pasted text with the sent message: it must match. (While a reply is still streaming the label reads "Copy Partial Response".)
items.needs: a sent message

items.where: Chat > long-press your sent message > Edit Message
steps: Press and hold your sent message and tap "Edit Message".
In the "Edit Message" dialog, change the text in the box labelled "Edit message text".
Tap "Send".
Look for a new reply to the edited text and the version pager ("1 / 2" style) under your message.
items.needs: a sent message in a chat
items.note: If an answer has unsaved edits, the app first asks before the edit replaces that answer.

items.where: Chat > long-press your sent message > Resend
steps: Press and hold your sent message to open the message actions.
Tap "Resend" without changing the text.
Look at the transcript: a fresh reply appears for the same message.
items.needs: a sent message in a chat
items.note: The action is hidden when the app reports that rerun is unavailable.

items.where: Chat > Edit Message on a sent message (S16.08) > version pager under your message
steps: Edit a sent message and send the edit, so the message has two versions.
Under the edited message, look for the pager with a left and right arrow and a count such as "2 / 2".
Tap the left arrow (screen-reader label "Previous version").
Check the count changes to "1 / 2" and the thread shows the earlier version and its reply. Tap the right arrow to go back.
items.needs: a sent message that has been edited
items.note: The label is built from the word "version" in code, so the spoken label reads "Previous version"; the pager appears only when the message has more than one version.

items.where: Chat > send a message with the network off > the failed message bubble
steps: Turn off the network on the test device.
In a chat, type a message and send it: the bubble shows a "queued" badge.
Turn the network back on and wait for the send to finish.
If the send fails, look at the bubble: it shows "failed to send" with a "Retry" button.
items.needs: a way to turn the network off on the test device
items.note: The failed badge appears only when an offline-queued message fails to go out; other send errors show as a banner on the chat screen, not on the bubble.

items.where: Chat > failed message bubble > Retry
steps: Make a send fail as in S16.15 so the bubble shows "failed to send".
Tap "Retry" next to it (or long-press the message and tap "Resend").
Check the same text and attached files are sent again.
Check the failed badge goes away and a reply appears, or a new failure replaces it.
items.needs: a way to turn the network off on the test device
items.note: Attachments are restored from the stored message before the retry is sent (chatExecutionStore.ts), and the retry count is limited with the alert "Retry Limit Reached".

items.where: Chat > send a second message while a reply is still running > the row above the message box
steps: Send a message and, while its reply is still streaming, type a second message and tap send.
Look above the message box: the second message appears as a row with a clock icon, with an "Edit queued message" and a "Cancel queued message" button.
Wait for the first reply to finish: the queued message goes out and appears in the transcript.
Optionally, with the network off, send a message: its bubble shows the "queued" badge until it goes out.
items.needs: a chat where a reply is still running (or the network off for the offline badge)
items.note: The row above the box shows only the message text with a clock icon and no visible "queued" word was checked; the "queued" badge belongs to offline sends.

items.where: Chat > type in the message box without sending > switch chats and come back; and a failed send
steps: In a chat, type a sentence but do not send it. Open another chat, then come back: the sentence is still in the message box for this chat.
In the first chat, send the sentence with the network off (see S16.15) so the send fails.
Check the sentence returns to the message box as unsent text, and that it does not appear as a sent message in the transcript.
Compare: sent messages appear in the transcript, while the unsent text stays in the box.
items.needs: a way to turn the network off on the test device
items.note: Drafts are stored per chat (draftKey is the chat id in app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx); no visible word "draft" was found in the code.

items.where: Chat tab > send a message and let the answer finish > read the line under the answer (provider · model)
steps: Open the Chat tab and send any message.
Wait until the answer stops streaming.
Look at the line under the answer: it shows the provider and model name.
Compare with your own message: your message is not labelled this way and the answer is.
Optional: the action button under the answer is named 'More message actions for <model name>' for screen readers (VoiceOver/TalkBack).
items.needs: none
items.note: Model name comes from answer provenance; 'AGI' is the fallback name in code. The footer text is built in ProvenanceFooter.tsx and not a fixed label.

items.where: Chat tab > send a message > watch the answer text appear
steps: Open the Chat tab and send a message that needs a long answer, such as 'Write five paragraphs about rivers'.
Watch the answer area while the reply is produced.
Check that text grows word by word, not all at once.
Check that headings, bold text and lists look formatted when they arrive.
items.needs: none
items.note: Streaming and markdown rendering are inner behaviour shown in MessageBubble.tsx; no separate control.

items.where: Chat tab > send a message > a working indicator appears above the answer
steps: Send a message in the Chat tab.
Before the first words appear, look for the working indicator.
Check that it is shown and disappears or changes when text arrives.
Optional: with a screen reader, the indicator is announced as 'Generating response'.
items.needs: none
items.note: Indicator default accessibility label is 'Generating response'; a turn status label can replace it.

items.where: Chat tab > send a message to a model that supports thinking > tap the thinking chip above the answer labelled 'Show reasoning'
steps: Pick a model that supports reasoning (see the model list) and send a message.
Look above the answer for the thinking chip showing 'Thinking for' and a time.
Tap the chip (screen-reader name 'Show reasoning').
Check that a sheet opens with the reasoning steps.
Tap 'Dismiss reasoning' to close it.
items.needs: a model that supports thinking
items.note: The chip only shows when the model supports thinking or reasoning text is present; which model does this is not stated in code.

items.where: Chat tab > send a message that uses a tool (for example web search) > tap the tool activity row under the answer
steps: Send a question that makes the assistant use a tool, such as a web search.
When the answer is done, find the tool activity row above or under the answer.
Tap the row to open the tool timeline.
Check each tool name, its status (for example completed or failed) and the result.
Tap a tool step to view its full output (screen-reader name 'View full output for <tool>').
items.needs: a Cloud or tool-enabled account (tools must be available)
items.note: Which tools run depends on the model and account; the code does not state a fixed prompt that triggers tools.

items.where: Chat tab > ask a question that needs web sources > tap a numbered citation marker in the answer
steps: Ask a question that needs current web information, such as 'What is the latest version of Node.js?'
Wait for the answer; look for small numbered markers in the text.
Tap a marker.
Check that it opens or highlights the matching source (screen-reader name 'Source <number>: <title>').
items.needs: a web-search capable account
items.note: Marker behaviour depends on whether numeric citations can link; this was not confirmed in a running build.

items.where: Chat tab > finished answer that used sources > tap the 'Sources' row under the answer
steps: Send a question that uses sources (see S17.06) and wait for the answer to finish.
Look under the answer for a row titled 'Sources'.
Tap the row to expand it.
Check that each source shows its title and host name.
Tap a source to open it.
items.needs: a web-search capable account
items.note: While the answer is still running the title reads 'Sources so far'.

items.where: Cloud chat > ask for a file (for example a PDF) > tap the file card on the answer
steps: Switch to Cloud mode and ask the assistant to create a file.
Wait for the answer to finish.
Look for a file card attached to the answer with the file name.
Tap the card to open it, or use its open control (screen-reader name 'Open <session label>').
Check the file name and type on the card.
items.needs: a Cloud account
items.note: Generated-file cards come from metadata in Cloud mode only (MessageBubble.tsx). The visible words on the card were not confirmed.

items.where: Chat tab > ask for a document or code > tap the artifact card under the answer
steps: Ask for a document, for example 'Write a one-page project plan as a document'.
Wait for the answer; look for a card on the answer with a type label.
Tap the card.
Check that the artifact viewer or panel opens with the content.
Close the viewer and check the card is still there.
items.needs: none
items.note: Card types are Content, Code, Email, Research, Image, Chart and Document; without a preview the card says 'Open to view details'.

items.where: Chat tab > ask for an image > tap the image in the answer (opens full screen) > use 'Save to Photos' or 'Share image'
steps: Ask the assistant to make an image, for example 'Draw a red bicycle on a beach'.
Wait for the image to appear inside the answer.
Tap the image to open it full screen.
Use 'Save to Photos', 'Copy image' or 'Share image' from its menu.
Check that the image saves or shares and matches the picture on the answer.
items.needs: an account that can generate images
items.note: The exact prompt that triggers image generation is not written in code; the tester must ask for an image in plain words.

items.where: Chat tab > ask for a video > the video plays inside the answer; if generation fails, tap 'Retry video generation'
steps: Ask the assistant to make a short video.
Wait for the answer; look for the video inside it.
Press play and check that the controls work.
Look for a download control on the video.
If generation fails, tap 'Retry video generation' and compare the result with the first attempt.
items.needs: an account that can generate video
items.note: Playback and download controls were not confirmed by label; only the retry control's text was found.

items.where: Chat tab in Cloud mode > ask for a place or a choice > use the card in the answer
steps: Switch to Cloud mode.
Ask a question that returns a card, for example a place search or a choice.
Look for the card inside the answer.
Read the caption under a map card: 'Opens a provider search. Confirm the place before navigating.'
Tap a choice or action on the card and check the result.
items.needs: a Cloud account

labels.text: Opens a provider search. Confirm the place before navigating.

items.note: Cards are shown only in Cloud mode and only when the model returns them; the code does not define a prompt that always produces one.

items.where: Under a finished answer > tap the copy icon (screen-reader name 'Copy') > paste somewhere else
steps: Open a finished answer.
Tap the copy icon in the row under the answer.
Check that the icon or label changes to 'Copied'.
Paste into the message box or Notes.
Compare the pasted text with the whole answer.
items.needs: none
items.note: A copy failure shows a warning icon instead. 'Copy Message' is the same action in the long-press menu.

items.where: Under a finished answer > tap the speaker icon (screen-reader name 'Read aloud')
steps: Open a finished answer.
Find the speaker icon in the row under the answer.
Tap it.
Listen for the answer being read aloud.
Compare the spoken text with the answer.
items.needs: a sound output (speaker or headphones)
items.note: The icon has no visible word; the name is used by screen readers. If speech is unavailable, a reason shows in the control.

items.where: Under an answer that is being read aloud > tap the stop icon (screen-reader name 'Stop reading aloud')
steps: Start Read aloud on an answer (see S17.17).
While it is speaking, find the same control; its icon changes to a square.
Tap it (name 'Stop reading aloud').
Check that the speech stops at once.
Check that the control returns to the speaker icon.
items.needs: a sound output
items.note: Same button as Read aloud; it changes state.

items.where: Under a finished answer > tap the refresh icon (screen-reader name 'Regenerate response')
steps: Open a finished answer with no unsaved edits.
Tap the refresh icon in the row under the answer.
If a warning appears about unsaved edits, read it and choose to continue or cancel.
Wait for a new answer to the same question.
Compare the new answer with the old one and check the page shows '2 / 2' style paging.
items.needs: none
items.note: The button is hidden while a reply is still waiting for approval, and disabled while the conversation is streaming.

items.where: A failed answer > the red failure notice under the answer > tap 'Retry'
steps: Trigger a failed answer (for example by going offline before sending, then reconnecting, or use a turn that fails).
Read the red failure notice under the answer.
Tap 'Retry' in the notice (hint 'Tap to try again').
Wait for the new attempt.
Check the failure notice is replaced by the new answer or a new outcome.
items.needs: a way to make a turn fail (for example going offline)
items.note: The code does not give a fixed way to force a failure; the tester must find one.

items.where: A cut-off answer > tap 'Continue generating' under the answer
steps: Ask for a very long answer, for example 'Write a 3000-word story'.
When it stops mid-sentence, look below the answer.
Tap 'Continue generating'.
Check that the same answer continues from where it stopped and is not a new answer.
Check the button disappears when the answer is complete.
items.needs: none
items.note: The button shows only on the latest continuable answer; the cut-off check is in continuableAnswer.ts.

items.where: Long-press a finished answer > 'Retry with Another Model' (or the dots button 'More message actions for <model>' > 'Retry with Another Model')
steps: Open a finished answer.
Long-press the answer text, or tap the dots button under it.
Tap 'Retry with Another Model' in the list.
Pick a different model in the model picker that opens.
Check that a new answer comes from the new model and the model name under it changes.
items.needs: a second model available to the account
items.note: A failure notice may also offer 'Switch model' instead.

items.where: Long-press a finished answer > 'Select Text' > select words > 'Quote in reply'
steps: Open a finished answer and long-press it.
Tap 'Select Text'.
Select part of the text in the box that opens.
Read the line that shows your selection.
Tap 'Quote in reply' and check the quote appears in the message box.
items.needs: none
items.note: The code offers 'Quote in reply' only (no separate 'revise' control); the quote is only offered when the chat screen wires reply quoting (MessageList.tsx).

items.where: Under an answer that has more than one attempt > the pager between the copy and read-aloud icons (shows '2 / 3' style)
steps: Regenerate an answer at least twice (see S17.19).
Find the pager under the answer, showing a count such as '2 / 3'.
Tap the left arrow (screen-reader name 'Previous response') and then the right arrow ('Next response').
Check the answer text changes to each attempt and the count updates.
Check the arrow is disabled at the first and last attempt.
items.needs: none
items.note: The arrows show no visible words; the names are the screen-reader labels.

items.where: Long-press a finished answer > 'Good Response'; or double-tap the answer
steps: Open a finished answer and long-press it.
Tap 'Good Response'.
Check the menu now offers 'Remove Good Response' for that answer.
Close and reopen the menu to confirm the state is kept.
Optional: double-tap the answer text; it also records a good response.
items.needs: none
items.note: The double-tap gesture has no visible label; it is set up in MessageBubble.tsx and not announced to the user.

items.where: Long-press a finished answer > 'Bad Response'
steps: Open a finished answer and long-press it.
Tap 'Bad Response'.
Check the menu now offers 'Remove Bad Response' for that answer.
Reopen the menu and check the state is kept.
Compare with the good response state: only one should be chosen at a time.
items.needs: none
items.note: Whether a detail sheet opens after a bad response (ResponseRatingDetails.tsx) was not checked in this item.

items.where: Long-press a finished answer > 'Report…' > choose a category > send
steps: Open a finished answer and long-press it.
Tap 'Report…'.
Read the sheet title 'Report this response'.
Choose a category and add a note, then send.
Check the result text, such as 'Report submitted for review' or 'Report saved on this device'.
items.needs: none
items.note: The menu label is written with a unicode ellipsis in code; the tester sees 'Report…'.

items.where: Long-press a finished answer > 'Export Message…' > 'Share Text' or 'Share...'; for the whole chat: chat menu > 'Share link'
steps: Open a finished answer and long-press it, then tap 'Export Message…'.
In the sheet, tap 'Share Text' to send the answer as text, or 'Share...' to export as PDF and open the system share sheet.
Check the system share sheet appears with the content.
For the whole conversation, open the chat's menu and tap 'Share link' (menu button not confirmed by label).
Compare the shared content with the answer.
items.needs: none
items.note: A single answer is shared through the export sheet, not a link. The conversation 'Share link' entry is in the chat screen menu; the menu button's visible label was not found.

items.where: Long-press the answer, or tap the "More message actions" icon under it > Export Message… > Export as PDF / Export as Text
steps: Sign in and get a finished answer from the assistant that has text in it.
Long-press the answer, or tap the three-dot icon under it (its label starts "More message actions").
Tap "Export Message…" in the menu. A sheet titled "Export Message" opens.
Tap "Export as PDF". A share sheet opens with a PDF of the answer.
Reopen the sheet and tap "Export as Text". Check that a plain text file is offered to share, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: a finished assistant answer with text
items.note: The sheet offers PDF and plain text only; there is no Markdown option in the code.

items.where: Sign in > send a message in a chat > wait for the answer to finish > look at the small grey lines under the answer
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Send a short question and wait until the answer stops streaming.
Look at the small grey line under the answer. It shows a token count and a time, for example "N tokens · 2.3s".
Look at the line below it. It shows the provider and model that answered, separated by " · ".
Compare with Expected. The code shows tokens and time only; no cost figure is shown.
items.needs: none
items.note: The usage line appears only when the server sent token or duration figures, and the model name appears in the provider line without the word "model".

items.where: Sign in > send a long question in a chat > if the answer stops with a provider error after some text, look under the partial text for the notice "Response may be incomplete" with "Retry"
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Send a prompt that gets a long answer.
If the answer stops partway with an error, the partial text stays on screen.
Look directly under the partial text for a red-tinted box that starts "Response may be incomplete" and includes the provider's error detail.
If the box shows "Retry", tap it and check that the answer is re-run. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a way to make the provider fail partway through an answer; no button triggers this
items.note: A reference id is appended when the server logged one, and Retry appears only when retry is available for that message.

items.where: Sign in > send a message in a chat > if the model declines, look under the answer for the notice "The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons." with "Switch model" and "Report"
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Send a message that the model is expected to decline.
When the answer shows the refusal, look for the box under it with the shield icon and the words "The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons."
Tap "Switch model" to check that it offers another model, or tap "Report" to check that the feedback screen opens.
Compare with Expected: a separate refusal box, not a generic error or a normal answer.
items.needs: a model that declines a message; the tester cannot choose this on purpose

labels.text: The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons.

items.note: The box shows only when the provider reports a refusal or content filter finish reason, so the tester cannot trigger it with a chosen prompt.

items.where: Sign in > send a long question in a chat > tap "Stop generating" while the answer is streaming > look at the answer
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Send a question that gives a long answer.
While the answer is still streaming, tap the send button, which changes to "Stop generating".
Look under the partial answer for the notice "Response stopped." Kept text stays on screen.
If no text had arrived, tap "Try again" to check that the turn is re-run. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The code shows "Try again" only when nothing arrived; when partial text was kept, the notice has no retry button, while Expected says to offer a retry.

items.where: Sign in > send a message in a chat > if the model returns nothing, look under the answer area for the notice "The model finished without returning a response. Try again."
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Send a message and wait for the turn to end.
If the turn ends with no text, no tool output and no files, look for the box with the text "The model finished without returning a response. Try again."
Tap the box, which is labelled "Tap to try again." for screen readers, and check that the turn is re-run.
Compare with Expected: an explicit message with retry, not an empty bubble.
items.needs: a provider that returns an empty stream; no button triggers this

labels.text: The model finished without returning a response. Try again.

items.note: The message is set when the stream closes with nothing in it, so the tester needs a provider that returns no output.

items.where: Chat list row title of a new chat (Open menu > See all chats)
steps: Sign in and start a new chat by typing a first message and sending it.
Tap the Open menu button at the top of the chat, then tap See all chats.
Find the new chat's row in the list and read its title.
Compare the title with Expected: it should be a meaningful title without you naming the chat.
items.needs: none
items.note: The code sets the title to the first 40 characters of the first message (chat.tsx around line 762), with 'New chat' as fallback. No AI-generated summary title was found in apps/mobile; a server-side title step is unknown.

items.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Rename
steps: Open a chat that already has a title.
Tap the Conversation menu button (icon only, accessibility label 'Conversation menu') at the top of the chat.
Tap Rename.
Type a new name in the Rename chat box and tap Rename.
Leave the chat, open See all chats, and check the new name is still shown.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Conversation menu button is an icon with no visible text. Rename is also in the long-press menu on a chat row in See all chats.

items.where: See all chats > long-press a chat row > Pin (or Unpin)
steps: Open Open menu > See all chats.
Long-press a chat row (or tap its More actions icon).
Tap Pin.
Check that the chat moves to the Pinned group at the top, and that the Pinned filter shows it.
Long-press the same row again and tap Unpin; check it returns to its date group.
items.needs: none
items.note: The same Pin and Unpin items also appear in the Conversation menu inside a chat.

items.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Archive; restore at Settings > Privacy > Archived chats
steps: Open a Cloud chat (archive is offered only for Cloud chats, not Local ones).
Tap Conversation menu and tap Archive.
Read the message 'Chat archived. Find it in Settings, Archived chats.' and check the chat is gone from See all chats.
Open Open menu > Settings > Privacy > Archived chats.
Tap Restore on the chat and check it comes back to See all chats.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a Cloud chat
items.note: Archive is not offered for Local chats, per the code comment in useConversationActions.ts.

items.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Delete
steps: Open a chat you are willing to delete.
Tap Conversation menu and tap Delete.
Read the Delete chat? box, which states what is lost, then tap Delete.
Check the chat is gone from See all chats and you are returned from the chat screen.
items.needs: a chat you can delete
items.note: The Cloud text says the chat is removed from every device and can be restored from Recently deleted on the web; the Local text says it cannot be restored.

items.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Move to project
steps: Open a chat that is not in a project.
Tap Conversation menu and tap Move to project.
In the Move to project list, tap a project name.
Check the toast 'Moved to <project name>' appears.
Open the project from the Projects tab and check the chat is listed there.
items.needs: at least one Project
items.note: Move to project is only offered when another project exists or the chat is already in one (canMove in the code).

items.where: Chat tab > new chat > Chat or Work switch (Chat / Work)
steps: Sign in on an account whose plan includes AGI Work, and start a new chat in Cloud mode.
Before sending anything, tap Work in the Chat or Work switch.
Send a message and check it is answered as planned, multi-step work with tools.
Send a second message and compare how it runs with Expected: later turns should follow the chosen mode.
items.needs: a signed-in account whose plan includes AGI Work and Cloud mode; the switch is hidden on a chat that already started
items.note: The switch only offers Chat and Work (not agent or plan), and it is hidden once the conversation has started, so changing the mode later in a chat is not shown in this control.

items.where: Chat tab > top-right eye-off button (Enable temporary chat) > Turn on temporary chat?
steps: On the Chat tab, tap the eye-off button at the top right.
Read the Turn on temporary chat? box, which states the consequence.
Tap Cancel and check nothing changes; tap the button again and tap Turn on.
Check the button now shows the word Temporary.
Tap Temporary again to turn it off.
items.needs: none
items.note: The same switch is also listed at Open menu > Settings > Privacy > Temporary Chat. The code stores it as a setting (isTemporaryChat), not per conversation.

items.where: Open a long chat > scroll up > round down-arrow button (Scroll to bottom)
steps: Open a chat with enough messages to scroll.
Scroll up several screens.
Look for the round button with a down chevron that appears over the thread.
Tap it and check the view jumps to the latest message and the button hides.
items.needs: a conversation long enough to scroll
items.note: The button has no visible words; 'Scroll to bottom' is its accessibility label only.

items.where: Open a chat > long-press a message > Branch Conversation from Here
steps: Open a chat with at least one reply.
Long-press a message (about half a second).
Tap Branch Conversation from Here.
Check the toast 'Conversation branch created' and the new chat titled '<chat title> (branch)'.
For alternate answers, look for the Previous and Next arrows under a reply that has more than one version and tap them.
items.needs: a chat with messages; not available in temporary chats
items.note: No tree view was found: each branch is a separate chat, and switching uses the Previous and Next arrows on alternate answers.

items.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Export > Export as Markdown
steps: Open a chat that has messages.
Tap Conversation menu and tap Export.
Read the Export Conversation list: Export as PDF, Print, Export as Text, Export as Markdown, Copy All Messages.
Tap Export as Markdown and choose where to save or share the file.
Open the file and check every message is in it, in order.
items.needs: none

items.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Share
steps: Open a signed-in Cloud chat that is not temporary.
Tap Conversation menu and tap Share.
Read Share a link to this chat? and tap Create link.
Choose a app from the share sheet to send the link.
Open the link in a browser that is not signed in and check the chat can be read.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a Cloud chat

labels.text: Share a link to this chat?

items.note: For a temporary chat the menu item is Share link and first asks Save this chat to share it?. The read-only check is not visible in the code, so it is only a tester check.

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Privacy > Shared links
steps: Tap Open menu, then Settings, then Privacy.
Tap Shared links.
Find a link you created (S18.19), tap Revoke, and read Revoke this link?.
Tap Revoke again to confirm and check the link leaves the list.
Open the old link in a browser and check it no longer opens.
items.needs: a Cloud account with at least one shared link
items.note: Settings also has a separate Shared Links row (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx) that opens the same screen.

items.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > What is in context
steps: Open a chat that has messages and some context.
Tap Conversation menu and tap What is in context.
Read the sheet: the model, the percent of context used, and the list of context rows.
Check the rows cover files, instructions, memory and the token budget as Expected asks.
Tap Close context details to close.
items.needs: none
items.note: The rows come from summarizeContext; the exact row names were not checked against Expected.

items.where: Second device: Open menu > See all chats > open the same chat
steps: On device A (signed in), start or open a Cloud chat and send a message.
On device B, signed in to the same account, tap Open menu and then See all chats.
Find the same chat under Recent chats and open it; check the messages from device A are there.
Send a reply on device B and check it appears on device A after sync.
items.needs: two devices signed in to the same account
items.note: The Code line pointed to code that moved; sync is in apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts and apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts. Cross-device behaviour needs a second device to test.

items.where: Chat tab > type in the message box > Send message
steps: Open the Chat tab and tap the message box.
Type a short question.
Tap the round Send message button.

Look right under your message for the spinner with the word Preparing (or Working...) before any answer text appears. Compare with Expected: the app shows the request was accepted and work has started.
items.needs: none
items.note: Send message is an accessibility name on the button, not printed text. Preparing shows only when no reasoning or tool steps exist yet; no separate accepted message was found.

items.where: Chat tab > turn Wi-Fi and mobile data off > type in the message box > Send
steps: Turn off Wi-Fi and mobile data on the phone.
Type a message in the composer.
Tap Send.
Look at the composer placeholder and at your message bubble for the small queued tag. Compare with Expected: the request is shown as waiting in the queue.
items.needs: phone width, ability to switch off network

labels.text: Offline, message will send on reconnect

items.note: Queueing found here is the offline queue. Queueing behind a running turn is handled in ChatInput but no visible word for it was confirmed.

items.where: Chat tab > attach a file or photo > Send
steps: Open the Chat tab and attach a file or photo with the attach control.
Type a short question about it.
Tap Send.
Look under your message for the Preparing spinner before the answer starts. Compare with Expected: the app shows it is reading the context before the answer.
items.needs: a file to upload
items.note: The attach control name was not confirmed in code. Preparing shows only when no reasoning or tool steps exist yet.

items.where: Chat tab > ask a question that needs current web sources > the tool step row
steps: Open the Chat tab.
Ask a question that needs current web information, such as today's news on a topic.
While the answer is loading, look at the tool step row under the message.
Compare with Expected: the row shows Searching for with the query in quotes.
items.needs: a network connection; a question that triggers web search
items.note: The way to turn web search on was not confirmed in code; the query text is inside the quoted part of the label.

items.where: Chat tab > ask for a calculation or chart that runs Python > the code block
steps: Open the Chat tab.
Ask for something that needs code to run, such as a calculation or a chart.
While the code block is working, look for the label Running Python.
Compare with Expected: the code step shows it is running.
items.needs: a request that triggers code execution
items.note: The request that triggers code execution was not confirmed in code.

items.where: Chat tab > send a request that uses a connected connector > the tool step row under the answer
steps: Connect a service first in the app's connectors screen (apps/mobile/app/(app)/connectors).
Open the Chat tab and ask for something that uses that service.
Open the tool step row under the answer while the call is in progress.
Compare with Expected: the row shows Running and names the service.
items.needs: a connected service account (outside account may be needed)
items.note: The exact service name in the row was not confirmed in code; Running comes from the shared status table.

items.where: Chat tab > send a request that needs a tool approval > the approval row under the step
steps: Open the Chat tab and send a request that needs a tool the app asks permission for.
Look for the Needs approval line in the activity row.
Read the choices: Allow once, Allow for this chat, Always allow, and Deny.
Compare with Expected: the turn waits and shows approve and deny controls.
items.needs: a request that triggers an approval
items.note: The approve and deny buttons are in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CloudToolApprovalControls.tsx; the scope labels come from packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/tool-approval-presentation.ts.

items.where: Chat tab > send a request where the assistant needs a detail > the question card
steps: Open the Chat tab and send a vague request, such as asking for a plan without details.
When a question card appears in the answer, read the questions.
Pick an option or type in the Something else... box and answer.
Compare with Expected: the turn shows it is waiting for your answer and lets you reply.
items.needs: a request that triggers a clarifying question
items.note: No separate waiting-for-input word was found; the question card itself is the visible state.

items.where: Effect seen in the Chat tab when the first words of an answer arrive
steps: Send a message in the Chat tab.
Watch the Preparing or Working spinner under your message.
Compare with Expected: when the first words arrive, the spinner row is replaced by the answer text.
items.needs: none

items.where: Effect seen in the Chat tab while the answer is being written
steps: Send a question that needs a long answer.
Watch the answer bubble while the spinner is still showing.
Compare with Expected: text grows in the bubble before the answer is complete.
items.needs: none

items.where: Effect seen in the Chat tab when an answer contains lists, tables or code
steps: Ask for an answer that includes a bulleted list, a table or a code block.
Watch the answer while it is still streaming.
Compare with Expected: the list, table and code block show in their formatted form before the answer ends.
items.needs: none

items.where: Chat tab > select image mode in the composer > type a description > Send
steps: Open the Chat tab and switch the composer to image mode.
Type a description, such as a simple picture of a cat.
Tap Send.
Look for the Generating Image... card and its Stop generating button. Compare with Expected: generation progress is shown.
items.needs: an account that can create images
items.note: The control that switches the composer to image mode was not confirmed in code. Video progress shows Generating video… in VideoGenProgress.tsx.

items.where: Chat tab > send a request that uses steps > the activity row under the answer
steps: Open the Chat tab and send a request that uses tool steps.
Wait until the answer ends.
Look at the activity row under the answer for the words Worked for and a time.
Compare with Expected: the spinner has stopped and the turn is shown as completed.
items.needs: a request that uses tool steps
items.note: The label is built from a time value, so the full text is Worked for followed by the elapsed time.

items.where: Chat tab > send a request with several steps where one step fails > the activity row
steps: Open the Chat tab and send a request that runs several steps.
Wait for a run where some steps fail while others succeed.
Look at the activity row under the answer.
Compare with Expected: the row says Finished with errors, which is distinct from Worked for and from Failed.
items.needs: a request that makes some steps fail (not controlled by the tester)
items.note: Whether a partial run can be made to happen on demand was not confirmed in code.

items.where: Chat tab > send a message > tap Stop generating (square button)
steps: Send a long request in the Chat tab.
While the answer streams, tap the square Stop generating button.
Look at the composer and the answer for a stopping state.
Compare with Expected: the surface shows the stop is in progress until it takes effect.
items.needs: none
items.note: In the Chat tab the composer does not receive a stopping state (stopPending is only passed by the cloud-code composer), so no Stopping word was found there. Stopping the task is the cloud-code session wording.

items.where: Chat tab > send a long request > tap Stop generating
steps: Send a long request in the Chat tab.
Tap the Stop generating square button while the answer streams.
Wait for the turn to end.
Look for the notice Response stopped. with a Try again button under the partial answer, and check the text that arrived is kept.
items.needs: none

items.where: Chat tab > send a long request > turn off Wi-Fi and mobile data during the answer
steps: Send a long request in the Chat tab.
While the answer streams, turn off Wi-Fi and mobile data on the phone.
Look at the spinner under the answer for the words Reconnecting.
Turn the network back on and compare with Expected: the turn resumes when possible.
items.needs: phone width, ability to switch off network
items.note: Whether the turn resumes is decided by the server and was not verified from code.

items.where: Effect seen when a streaming chat is reopened after the app is closed
steps: Send a long request in the Chat tab.
While it streams, close the app fully and reopen it.
Open the same chat again and look for the answer continuing, not starting over.
Compare with Expected: the work is picked up and shown as resuming rather than restarting.
items.needs: none
items.note: No visible resuming word was found for chat turns; the research plan card shows Starting... while a resume runs (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/research/ResearchRunCard.tsx).

items.where: Chat tab > send a message after the rate limit is reached > the failure notice under the turn
steps: Send messages in the Chat tab until a rate limit is reached (the app cannot force this).
Read the failure notice under the turn.
Look for the words Try again in and a time.
Compare with Expected: the notice says the turn was rate-limited and when to retry.
items.needs: an account that hits a rate limit
items.note: The message text comes from the server; the time is shown only when the server gives one. The path for this string is apps/mobile/services/failureCopy.ts.

items.where: Chat tab > send a message after the plan's usage is used up > the paywall sheet
steps: Use up the plan's usage in the Chat tab (or use an account at its limit).
Send another message.
Read the sheet that opens.
Compare with Expected: the sheet says the feature is not included and points to Upgrade or Choose a plan.
items.needs: a Free account at its limit
items.note: Upgrade to and Update billing are the other titles this sheet can show, depending on the plan state.

items.where: Chat tab > choose a cloud model > send after the sign-in has expired
steps: Sign in, then let the sign-in expire (or sign out in another place).
Open the Chat tab, choose a cloud model and send a message.
Read the error that shows under the composer or the turn.
Compare with Expected: the error says sign in is needed and offers to sign in again.
items.needs: a Clerk sign-in that can expire

labels.text: Sign in to use AGI Cloud.
Sign in to resume this AGI Cloud task.

items.note: No separate sign-in button was confirmed next to these messages; the tester should check whether one appears.

items.where: Chat tab > send a request that needs your desktop > the activity row
steps: Pair a desktop and then turn it off or let it go offline.
In the Chat tab, send a request that needs that desktop.
Open the activity row under the answer.
Compare with Expected: the row says Waiting for followed by the desktop name.
items.needs: a paired desktop that is offline
items.note: If no device name is known the row says Waiting for your device.

items.where: Chat tab > send a message while the model provider is down > the failure notice under the turn > Retry or Switch model
steps: Send a message in the Chat tab while the provider is unavailable (the tester cannot force this).
Read the failure notice under the turn.
Look for the Retry button and the Switch model button.
Compare with Expected: the turn says the provider is unavailable and offers retry or another model.
items.needs: a provider outage (not controlled by the tester)
items.note: The wording of the outage message comes from the server; the Switch model button shows only for the errors that offer it.

items.where: Chat tab > send a message that is too long or has a bad attachment > the failure notice under the turn
steps: Send a message that is too long, or attach a file the app cannot use.
Read the failure notice under the turn.
Look for the text Tap to try again and the Try again action.
Compare with Expected: the notice explains what to change so you can fix it and send again.
items.needs: a file to upload that the service rejects
items.note: The explanation words come from the server copy in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/upstream-error-copy.ts, not from the app.

items.where: Chat tab > send a request > connection fails after some answer text has arrived > the answer stays
steps: Send a long request in the Chat tab.
Turn off the network after some answer text appears, and keep it off until the turn gives up.
Read the answer text that is still shown.
Compare with Expected: the text that arrived is kept and the failure is marked with Response may be incomplete.
items.needs: a way to cut the network during an answer
items.note: The failure text is shown after the partial answer; the exact wording after the prefix comes from the server.

items.where: Open the drawer (menu button, top left) > Recent chats > tap a chat, or Drawer > See all chats > Chats > tap a chat
steps: Sign in, open a chat that has a finished answer and, if you can, one that was stopped part way.
Force-quit the app completely (swipe it away in the app switcher) and open it again.
Open the drawer and tap the same chat in Recent chats, or tap See all chats and then the chat in the Chats list.
