Check that the messages are still there and that each answer shows the same final state as before the restart (finished, failed or stopped). An answer that was still streaming when the app closed should show as stopped, not as still running.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account; a chat with at least one finished answer; for the stopped case, a chat stopped before quitting the app
items.note: Restore is persisted on the device only for chats in Local mode that are not temporary (chatMessageStore.ts partialize); other chats come back from the server, so the check depends on the chat's execution mode. An answer cut off by the app closing is marked stopped (stoppedByAppExit), and an interrupted image or video shows 'Video generation stopped when the app closed. Retry to generate it again.' (chatCloudMessageStore.ts). The drawer's visible label text in common.json was partly unreadable in the tool output, so verify the exact drawer menu wording on screen.

items.needs: a device; a long-running turn started on the phone, then the app closed or sent to the background
items.note: Searched apps/mobile for background, resume, reopen, keeps running and in the background. The only background code found is background fetch for alerts (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx around lines 710-740, apps/mobile/services/backgroundFetch) and the upload message 'Upload stopped in the background' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/upload/uploadLifecycle.ts:52). app.config.js gates background tasks on v1Feature('dispatch'). No visible control or label for a chat turn continuing after the UI closes was found, so the Expected behaviour could not be tied to a screen. Code location in the plan is unverified.

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt that asks for several paragraphs, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Write three short paragraphs about the water cycle, with a blank line between each.
Look at the reply: each paragraph should be a separate block with space between them, matching Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Paragraph spacing has no control of its own; it is reached through any chat reply.

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt that asks for headings, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Answer with a # heading, a ## heading and a ### heading, each followed by one sentence.
Look at the reply: the three headings should show as styled headings, with no # marks showing.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt that uses bold, italic and strikethrough, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Reply with one sentence in bold, one in italic, and one with strikethrough text.
Look at the reply: bold, italic and struck-through text should show, with no asterisk or tilde marks.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt for a numbered list, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Give a numbered list of four steps for making tea, starting the list at 5.
Look at the reply: the list should show numbers that are indented, starting at 5 as the prompt asked.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The start value depends on what the model writes; the tester should confirm the prompt was followed before judging.

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt for a bulleted list, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Give a bulleted list of three fruits.
Look at the reply: each item should show a bullet marker and be indented.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt for a nested list, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Give a bulleted list of two fruits, and under the first fruit add two indented sub-items.
Look at the reply: the sub-items should sit under their parent, indented further than the parent.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt for a task list, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Make a task list with one unchecked item (- [ ]) and one checked item (- [x]).
Look at the reply: each item should show a checkbox, and the checked one should show as ticked.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The checkbox element has an accessibility role of checkbox; the tester should confirm the boxes match the prompt.

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt that starts with a quote mark, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Reply with a two-line quotation written with > at the start of each line.
Look at the reply: the quotation should show as an indented block that looks different from normal text.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt that asks for a divider line, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Write one sentence, then a line with three dashes (---), then one more sentence.
Look at the reply: a horizontal divider line should sit between the two sentences, with no dashes showing.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt that uses inline code, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Write a sentence that includes the word `print` in backticks.
Look at the reply: the word should show in a monospace style with a background, and differ from the text around it.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt that asks for a code block, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Show a short Python function inside a fenced code block with three indented lines.
Look at the reply: the code should show in a monospace block, keep its indentation and line breaks, and show a copy control.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat: an answer containing a link. Tap the link to open it; long-press the link for the menu with Open, Copy Link and Share Link
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Reply with one sentence that includes the link [example site](https://example.com).
Look at the reply: the link text should show underlined and in the link colour.
Tap the link and look at the page that opens; long-press the link to see the menu.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat: an answer containing a bare web address. Tap the address
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Reply with one sentence that includes the bare address https://example.com with no brackets.
Look at the reply: the address should show as a link, and tapping it should open the page.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt that asks for a table, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Make a table with columns Name, Age and City and three rows.
Look at the reply: the table should show a header row and aligned cells in a grid.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt that asks for a wide table, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Make a table with 12 columns named Col 1 to Col 12 and two rows of values.
Look at the reply on a phone-width screen: the table should scroll sideways rather than being cut off.
items.needs: a signed-in account, phone width
items.note: The sideways scroll is the SideScroller used for tables in the renderer.

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt with an inline formula, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Write one sentence that includes the formula $E = mc^2$ inside the sentence.
Look at the reply: the formula should show as typeset maths within the sentence, not as raw LaTeX.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The formula is drawn in a WebView by MathBlock.tsx.

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt with a display formula, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Show the formula $$x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$$ on its own line.
Look at the reply: the formula should show as a centred block of typeset maths.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt that uses escaped symbols, read the reply
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Write the text \*not italic\*, the price \$5 and the name my\_file.
Look at the reply: the asterisks, dollar sign and underscore should show as plain characters with no backslashes.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt for a long answer, and watch the reply while it is still being written
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Write a long answer with a heading, a bulleted list and a bold word.
Watch the reply while it types: the heading, list and bold text should show formatted before the reply finishes, not as raw # or * marks.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The streaming row uses a separate rendering path in MessageBubble.tsx; the tester must watch during the stream.

items.where: Chat: start a new chat, send a prompt for a code block, and watch the reply while it is still being written
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Show a long Python script inside a fenced code block.
Watch the reply while it types: the code should show in a code block as soon as the opening fence arrives, before the closing fence.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Closing an open fence is handled by closeUnterminatedCodeFence in packages/platform/utils/src/markdownSource.ts. Catching the stream mid-fence depends on timing; no separate control was found.

items.where: In a chat answer that contains raw HTML tags such as a script tag
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Include this exact text in your reply: and bold.
Look at the reply: no alert should appear, and raw HTML blocks should not run or show as live content.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Raw HTML blocks are dropped by dropHiddenHtmlBlocks in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/markdownHiddenHtml.ts; the tester may see the HTML text removed rather than shown.

items.where: Chat: tap a link in an answer; long-press a link for Open, Copy Link and Share Link
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Reply with one link [example site](https://example.com) and one email link [mail us](mailto:test@example.com).
Tap the web link: it should open in the in-app browser, not in the chat.
Tap the mail link: it should open the mail app; compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: javascript: and data: links match no open path in the link resolver (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/answerLinks.ts), so tapping one does nothing; the tester may not be able to produce one from a reply.

items.where: Chat: long-press an answer, then tap Select Text. Drag-select across the text in the sheet
steps: Start a new chat and get an answer with a heading, a list and a code block.
Long-press the answer bubble.
Tap Select Text.
Drag from the heading down through the list and the code block; compare what is highlighted with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Inline answer text is set not selectable in the bubble; selection happens in the Select Text sheet. A second action list in MessageBubble.tsx uses the lower-case label Select text; the tester should use the sheet menu label as shown.

items.where: Chat: long-press an answer, then tap Export Message, then Export as PDF. Or open the chat's actions menu, tap Export, then Export as PDF or Print
steps: Get an answer with a heading, a table, a code block and a formula.
Long-press the answer, tap Export Message, then tap Export as PDF.
Open the PDF or print preview and compare the headings, table, code and formula with the answer on screen.
Optionally open the chat's Export sheet and tap Print to compare.
items.needs: a device with a share or print option
items.note: The menu label in code is Export Message followed by an ellipsis character; the chat-level Export entry is in apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx.

items.where: In a chat answer with Arabic or Hebrew headings, list items or paragraphs; the text lines up to the right
steps: Start a new chat.
Send: Reply in Arabic with a heading, a bulleted list of two items, and one paragraph.
Look at the reply: the Arabic text should read right to left and line up to the right.
items.needs: a signed-in account, and a prompt that asks for Arabic or Hebrew text
items.note: The direction rule is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageContentRenderer.tsx (directionStyle, applied to headings, list items and paragraphs), so the Code line that said unverified is now backed by code.

items.where: Chat > ask the assistant for a flowchart or diagram; a Mermaid block that fails to draw shows the message below it
steps: Sign in and open a chat.
Send a message asking for a diagram, such as a flowchart of a simple process (the model decides the output, so this may need a retry).
If the diagram cannot be drawn, look for the text "This diagram could not be drawn." followed by "Its source is kept below." with the diagram source as readable text under it.
Compare with Expected: the block should show a readable fallback, not disappear or break the message.
Also check that an assistant reply with a fenced block in an unknown language (for example a language name the app does not know) shows the raw text in a plain box, instead of vanishing.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account; the failure depends on the model output, so a tester may need several tries

labels.text: This diagram could not be drawn.

items.note: The Code line's quoted text is gone and the line numbers moved: the unknown-card fallback is now InteractiveCardBlock.tsx around lines 1160-1190 (testID interactive-card-fallback, text comes from the server), and the unknown-language fallback is AssistantSurface.tsx around line 635 (testID answer-fallback, raw text, no visible label, classified in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/assistantFence.ts); the navigation words "Chat" and the way to ask for a diagram were not verified in a screen file.

items.where: Chat > send a message that asks for code > read the bar above the finished code block
steps: Sign in and open a chat.
Type in the message box: Write a short Python function that adds two numbers, in a code block. Send it.
Wait until the reply finishes.
Look at the small grey text at the top-left of the code block. Compare with Expected: it should show the language name in lower case (for example python). A block with no language shows Plain text.
items.needs: none
items.note: The name shown is the language written in the reply's code fence, lower-cased; the app does not pick it.

items.where: Chat > send a message that asks for code > look at the colours in the finished code block
steps: Sign in and open a chat.
Type in the message box: Write a short Python function that adds two numbers, in a code block. Send it.
Wait until the reply finishes; the block is not coloured while it is still streaming.
Look at the keywords, strings and numbers in the code. Compare with Expected: different parts of the code should have different colours.
items.needs: none
items.note: Highlighting is on by default in code blocks and no setting turns it off; the colouring is decided in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CodeCard.tsx and apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/syntaxHighlight.ts.

items.where: Chat > send a message that asks for code > tap the copy button in the top-right of the code block (its accessible name is Copy code)
steps: Sign in, open a chat and ask for a short code sample in a code block. Wait until the reply finishes.
Tap the copy icon in the header bar of the code block.
Paste into the message box (or any text field) and compare the pasted text with the code block.
Compare with Expected: the pasted text should be exactly the code, with no language name or header text, and the icon should briefly show a check mark.
items.needs: none
items.note: The button is icon-only. Its accessible name is Copy code, and after a copy it reads Copied, or Could not copy on failure (apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useCopyAction.ts).

items.where: Chat > send a message that asks for code > tap the download icon in the code block header (its accessible name is Download plus the file name, for example Download code.py)
steps: Sign in, open a chat and ask for a short Python function in a code block. Wait until the reply finishes.
Tap the download icon in the header bar of the code block.
In the sheet that opens, choose a place to keep the file (for example Files), then open the saved file.
Compare with Expected: the file should have a sensible extension (for example .py for Python) and its content should match the code block.
items.needs: none
items.note: The download button is icon-only and opens the system share sheet (shareFile in apps/mobile/services/fileCreation.ts), not a direct save. Unknown languages get a .txt file.

items.where: Chat > ask for a change as a diff > look at the added and removed lines in the diff code block
steps: Sign in and open a chat.
Type in the message box: Show the change as a unified diff inside a diff code block: rename the variable x to total in this Python snippet, x = 1 then print(x). Send it.
Wait until the reply finishes.
Compare with Expected: added lines should have a green fill and removed lines a red fill, each line on its own row.
items.needs: none
items.note: The colour comes from the diff code block (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CodeCard.tsx, DiffCodeLines). Whether the model writes a diff fence is up to the reply. Artifact version changes use a similar colour view under Show changes in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx.

items.where: Chat > ask for a diff > read the diff block; Settings > AGI Code > Show + and - signs in diffs
steps: Sign in and ask for a diff in a diff code block, as in S21.09. Wait until the reply finishes.
Read the lines: each line should keep its own row, and the hunk header lines (starting with @@) should be readable.
Open the side menu, tap Settings, then tap AGI Code.
Turn on Show + and - signs in diffs, go back to the chat and open the same diff. Compare with Expected: + and - signs now show at the start of changed lines, with their colours.
items.needs: none (the AGI Code row may depend on the account mode; not traced)
items.note: The side-menu entry word Settings comes from the shared translation file, and the Settings row labelled AGI Code is in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx. Hunks are shown as text from the model's reply, not reformatted by the app.

items.where: Add to chat (the button labelled Add to chat next to the message box) > Add to Chat sheet > turn on Run code, then send a request that runs code
steps: Sign in to a Cloud account whose plan includes cloud code execution, and choose a model that supports code execution.
Tap the button labelled Add to chat next to the message box.
In the sheet titled Add to Chat, turn on the Run code row.
Type: Run this Python code and show the output: print(sum(range(10))). Send it, then wait for the reply.
Compare with Expected: a Run code row should appear in the reply with its output, showing the printed result 45.
items.needs: a Cloud account with cloud code execution granted, and a model with code execution
items.note: The Run code row is only offered in Cloud mode (appMode === 'cloud'); no local sandbox was found in the mobile app. How to switch to Cloud mode was not traced.

items.where: Chat > Run code reply > tap the Run code row > read the Output heading
steps: Run S21.12 first so that a Run code row exists.
Tap the Run code row to open its details.
Look under the heading Output (or Response for non-code tools).
Compare with Expected: the printed text of the program (45 for the example) should appear under Output.
items.needs: a Cloud account with cloud code execution granted, and a model with code execution
items.note: Long output is cut to 12 lines in the row; a full-output control exists with accessible name View full output for Run code.

items.where: Chat > Run code reply > tap the Run code row > look for the red Stderr heading
steps: Run this Python code and wait for the reply: import sys then print('ok') then print('problem', file=sys.stderr).
Tap the Run code row to open its details.
Compare the Output section (ok) with the Stderr section (problem).
Compare with Expected: Stderr should show in its own section, in red, separate from Output.
items.needs: a Cloud account with cloud code execution granted, and a model with code execution
items.note: The Stderr section appears only when the program writes to the error stream.

items.where: Chat > Run code reply > the right-hand label on the Run code row (for example 450ms or 1.2s)
steps: Run S21.12 in Cloud mode.
Look at the Run code row in the reply, on the right-hand side.
Compare with Expected: a time such as 450ms or 1.2s should show after the run finishes.
items.needs: a Cloud account with cloud code execution granted, and a model with code execution
items.note: The duration chip shows only when the run reports a duration; otherwise the row shows Script or Result.

items.where: Chat > Run code reply > read the status word on the Run code row, then tap the row and read Exit code
steps: Run S21.12 (success) and then a failing program such as: import sys then sys.exit(3).
Read the status word on each Run code row: Done for success, Failed for failure.
Tap the failing row and look for the line Exit code 3.
Compare with Expected: success shows Done and exit code 0 in green; the failure shows Failed and a red exit code line.
items.needs: a Cloud account with cloud code execution granted, and a model with code execution
items.note: A sandbox error shows as Code execution failed: <error> from apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/toolCallAccumulator.ts.

items.where: Chat > reply with a generated file card > tap the file card to open it > tap the download icon at the top (accessible name Download artifact)
steps: Sign in to a Cloud account with a chat that produces a file (for example: Create a CSV file with three rows of sample data).
Look for the file card in the reply, showing the file name.
Tap the file card to open the full screen view.
Tap the download icon at the top (accessible name Download artifact), then check the file that is saved or shared.
Compare with Expected: the file should be listed and openable or downloadable.
items.needs: a Cloud account; a reply that produces a file
items.note: The link from a code run to a generated file card was not traced end to end; the card is built from generatedFile data in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/InlineArtifactCard.tsx and GeneratedFileCard.tsx. The download icon is icon-only.

items.where: Chat > Run code reply (after the run has finished) > tap Run again under the code
steps: Run S21.12 in Cloud mode and wait until the row shows Done or Failed.
Under the reply's code block, find the button labelled Run again.
If the approval setting is Ask every time, a dialog titled Run this code again? appears; tap its Run again button.
Compare with Expected: a new run should appear with its own output and status, and the earlier run should stay visible.
items.needs: a Cloud account with cloud code execution granted, and a model with code execution
items.note: Partly unfinished: the server side needs AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1 and E2B_API_KEY in production, which a tester cannot set; if the run fails, record it. The button is hidden while a run is still going or when cloud execution is not granted.

items.where: Chat > '+' button > turn on 'Web search' > ask a question > teal [1], [2] markers in the answer
steps: Sign in and open the Chat screen. Make sure the 'Cloud' button in the mode toggle is selected.
Tap the '+' button (its accessibility label is 'Add to chat'), turn on 'Web search', then close the sheet.
Ask: 'What are the latest headlines about renewable energy? Cite your sources.'
When the answer finishes, look for small teal bracket numbers such as [1] in the text.
Tap one [n] marker. Compare with Expected: the source should be identified (title shown) and openable through 'Open page'.
items.needs: A signed-in account that is allowed web search (the 'Web search' row is hidden otherwise), and a network connection
items.note: In answers the citation is a teal [n] text marker; the pill chip with [n] and a title is used in Deep Research 'Sources' lists (research/ResearchSourcesAppendix.tsx).

items.where: Chat > answer with web search > tap a teal [n] marker > preview alert
steps: Get an answer with web search on, as in S22.01, with a teal [n] marker in the text.
Tap the [n] marker.
Compare with Expected: a popup shows the source title, the site, 'Published' date when known, and a snippet when known.
Tap 'Cancel' and tap the marker again, then tap 'Open page' and check the source opens.
items.needs: A signed-in account with web search on, and a network connection
items.note: A phone has no hover, so the preview is a tap that shows a native alert (previewCitation in CitationChip.tsx), not a hover card. Date and snippet appear only when the source has them.

items.where: Chat > answer made with web search > tap the 'Sources' pill under the answer
steps: Get an answer with web search on, as in S22.01.
Tap the 'Sources' pill under the answer (it says 'View N sources').
Check the sheet: a query line, a 'Citations' heading for cited sources, and a 'More' heading for the rest.
Check each row shows publisher and date, the title, and a snippet when there is one.
Tap a row. Compare with Expected: the source opens in the in-app browser.
items.needs: A signed-in account with web search on, and a network connection
items.note: While the answer is still streaming the title reads 'Sources so far'. Search steps also show a 'Searching for' card in the tool timeline (WebSearchToolCard.tsx).

items.where: Chat > ask for a chart > the chart in the answer
steps: Sign in and open the Chat screen.
Ask: 'Make a bar chart of monthly sales for January to June: 10, 14, 9, 17, 20, 12.'
When the chart appears in the answer, press and drag across the bars or line.
Look at the text line under the chart: it changes to show the value at that point.
For a pie chart, tap a slice to select it and tap again to clear. Compare with Expected: values show on touch and a legend-style readout appears.
items.needs: None beyond sign-in. The model must return a chart, so ask for one; the app has no button that makes a chart
items.note: Charts come from a chart block in the answer (AssistantSurface.tsx 'chart' fence, or a mermaid xychart/pie block); whether the model returns one is not under the tester's control.

items.where: Chat > chart in an answer > 'Show data' button under the chart
steps: Get a chart in an answer, as in S22.08.
Tap 'Show data' under the chart. A table of the chart values appears.
Tap a value in the table and check it can be selected.
Tap 'Save image' and check a picture of the chart is saved or shared.
Compare the table values with the chart. Compare with Expected: the data is inspectable and can be saved.
items.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must contain a chart
items.note: The code has no JSON view and no CSV download for chart data. 'Save image' exports a PNG.

items.where: Chat (Cloud mode) > ask about places > map in the answer > 'Full screen map' control
steps: Select 'Cloud' in the mode toggle on the Chat screen.
Ask: 'Show me the main museums in Paris on a map.'
Wait for the answer. A map with pins should appear under the text.
Tap the expand control on the map (its label is 'Full screen map').
Compare with Expected: the map shows markers. If the map cannot load, the text 'Map preview is unavailable. Place names are listed.' appears instead.
items.needs: A managed Cloud account with map tiles available. This depends on production state and is not verified here

labels.text: Map preview is unavailable. Place names are listed.

items.note: The map appears only in Cloud mode and only when the answer has located places (a 'map' block). Whether production tiles are configured is not verified in code.

items.where: Chat (Cloud mode) > a task where the agent asks to use a tool > approval card in the activity timeline with 'Allow once', 'Allow for this chat', 'Always allow', 'Deny'
steps: Select 'Cloud' in the mode toggle and start a task that makes the agent use a tool needing approval.
When the agent pauses, find the approval card. Check it shows the tool summary and its parameters.
Read the buttons: 'Allow once', 'Allow for this chat', 'Always allow', 'Deny'.
Tap 'Deny' (or 'Allow once') and check the card shows the decision.
For 'Always allow' on a destructive tool, check a confirmation alert with 'Cancel' appears. Compare with Expected: the card states what will happen and offers approve or deny.
items.needs: A Cloud account with a tool or connector that needs approval; the UI does not let the tester choose when it asks
items.note: The card is CloudToolApprovalControls.tsx, shown in AgentActivityTimeline.tsx and ToolCallTimeline.tsx. The code does not show how often a tool asks for approval, so the trigger is unsure.

items.where: Chat > ask for a comparison table > the table in the answer > 'Expand table'
steps: Ask: 'Compare three phone plans in a table: price, data, and contract length.'
Find the table in the answer and check its columns and rows read clearly.
Tap a column heading to sort the rows.
Tap the 'Expand table' icon to open the table full screen, then tap 'Close table'.
Compare with Expected: the answer shows a readable comparison table.
items.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must contain a table
items.note: A separate product comparison card exists (cards/ProductComparisonCard.tsx). Column headings sort only when the cell has no link.

items.where: Chat > ask for a mind map > the 'Diagram' bar under the drawing > 'Expand diagram' or 'Show source'
steps: Ask: 'Draw a mind map of the parts of a bicycle as a mermaid mindmap.'
Wait for the answer. A 'Diagram' bar appears under the drawing.
Tap 'Show source' to see the diagram code, then tap 'Show source' again to hide it.
Tap the 'Expand diagram' icon to open it full screen.
Compare with Expected: a drawn mind map with a central topic and branches.
items.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must contain a mermaid block
items.note: No mind-map code exists by name. A mind map is drawn only as a generic mermaid block, and whether mindmap syntax renders is not verified in code.

items.where: Chat > ask for a flowchart > the 'Diagram' bar under the drawing > 'Expand diagram' or 'Show source'
steps: Ask: 'Draw a flowchart of how a support ticket is handled, with decision points, as a mermaid flowchart.'
Wait for the answer. A 'Diagram' bar appears under the drawing.
Tap 'Show source' to see the diagram code, then hide it.
Tap the 'Expand diagram' icon to open it full screen.
Compare with Expected: a drawn flowchart with boxes and arrows.
items.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must contain a mermaid block
items.note: Flowcharts use the same generic mermaid path as mind maps; the code does not name flowcharts, so the drawing depends on the Mermaid runtime.

items.where: Chat > ask for a timeline > the 'Timeline' panel in the answer (numbered steps with status labels)
steps: Ask: 'Make a timeline of the steps to launch a small app, with dates and status.'
Find the 'Timeline' panel in the answer.
Check the steps are numbered in order, each with a date when given.
Check each step's status label: 'Complete', 'In progress' or 'Not started'.
Compare with Expected: the answer shows a drawn timeline of the steps.
items.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must contain a timeline block
items.note: The timeline panel is the 'timeline' answer block (AssistantSurface.tsx). The panel is a list of steps, not a line drawing. A mermaid timeline block takes the generic diagram path instead.

items.where: Chat > ask for an interactive HTML page > html code card > 'Preview HTML'
steps: Ask: 'Make a small interactive HTML demo with a button that counts clicks.'
When the html code block appears, tap 'Preview HTML'.
Tap the demo's button inside the preview and check the count changes.
Tap the 'Source' tab to see the code, then 'Preview' to go back.
Compare with Expected: the demo runs live inside the preview.
items.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must contain an html block
items.note: HTML and React previews run scripts in a sandbox (SafeArtifactPreview.tsx). Links in the preview ask 'Open link?' first.

items.where: Chat > ask for a small web app > artifact card in the answer > tap it > 'Preview' tab (and 'Open in Safari' when published)
steps: Ask: 'Build a small web page that shows a to-do list I can add items to.'
Tap the artifact card in the answer (it says 'Tap to expand').
In the full-screen view, check the 'Preview' tab shows the live page. Try adding an item.
Tap 'Source' and then 'Preview' again.
If the artifact has been published, find its publication link and 'Open in Safari' (iPhone) or 'Open in browser'. Compare with Expected: the app is previewed live and can be opened or expanded.
items.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must generate an app or page (the tester cannot force it)
items.note: The publish path needs a published artifact; whether this account can publish is not verified in code.

items.where: Drawer (menu button, top left) > Projects > New project (bottom pill). Fill Name, then tap Create project.
steps: Sign in and open the menu button at the top left, then tap Projects.
Tap the New project pill at the bottom of the screen (or Create Project on the empty screen).
Type a name in the Name field. The Create project button stays grey until a name is typed.
Tap Create project.
Look for the new project card in the Projects list, and compare with Expected. The code closes the sheet and does not open the new project by itself, so tap the card to open it as its own workspace.
items.needs: a signed-in account to save to the account; the project must appear after a sync
items.note: After Create project the editor only closes (useProjectEditor.ts); the project is not opened automatically, which differs from Expected's 'opens as its own workspace'.

items.where: Projects > long-press a project card > Edit project. Or open the project and use the More project actions button (three dots, top right) > Edit project.
steps: Open Projects and press and hold a project card.
Tap Edit project in the menu that opens.
Change the Name, and type or change the Description. The Description field is optional.
Tap Save project.
Check the card in the Projects list (or the project header) shows the new name and description, as Expected says.
items.needs: a project you can edit (not archived or shared with you)

items.where: Projects > open a cloud project > tap the coloured project icon at the top left of the project header. The sheet shows Icon and Colour.
steps: Open Projects and tap a cloud project card.
Tap the coloured icon at the top left of the header.
In the sheet, tap a different Colour swatch, then tap a different icon under Icon.
Close the sheet and look at the header icon. Then go back to Projects and check the card shows the same icon and colour, as Expected says.
items.needs: a cloud project on a signed-in account (Cloud mode)
items.note: The icon and colour picker exists only in the cloud project header; the create and edit form has no icon or colour control. Local projects have none in the code I read.

items.where: Projects > tap a project card. The header shows the name, description and a line with chat and file counts; the tabs below are Chats, Work, Sources (and Artifacts, Routines on cloud projects).
steps: Open Projects and tap a project card.
Look at the top header: the project name, then the description under it if one was set.
Read the grey line under the description, which shows chat and file counts and Last used.
Look at the tab row (Chats, Work, Sources) and tap Sources, then Chats to check the sections are there.
items.needs: a project that has at least one chat or file (for counts)
items.note: The header with counts is CloudProjectOverview, shown for cloud projects. The count words are chat/chats and file/files.

items.where: Projects > tap a project card > Chats tab > New chat. Existing chats are listed in the same tab.
steps: Open Projects and tap a project card, then stay on the Chats tab.
Look for the list of chats. If there are none, the empty text says No chats yet.
Tap a chat row to open it, then go back.
Tap New chat, send a message, then go back to the project and check the new chat is listed under the project.
items.needs: a project with chats; a second chat is useful
items.note: A second route exists: the project's menu in the Projects list has New chat in project, which sets the project and opens the chat screen.

items.where: Projects > tap a project card > Sources tab > Add sources. Tap a file row to preview it. The remove icon on a row deletes it.
steps: Open Projects, tap a project card, then tap the Sources tab.
Tap Add sources and pick a file from the document picker.
Wait for the file row to appear in the list (it may show an indexing state).
Tap the file row to preview it, then check the preview shows the file.
Tap the trash icon on the row and confirm Remove, then check the file is gone from the list.
items.needs: a file to upload; a signed-in account for cloud projects
items.note: The code has no download or share control on the Sources screen (I searched src/features/projects/components for Download, Save and Share); the file row opens a viewer only. Expected's 'download' cannot be checked in the UI.

items.where: Projects > tap a project card > Sources tab > Add sources (files) or Add text (typed text).
steps: Open Projects, tap a project card, then tap the Sources tab.
Tap Add text, type a Title and some content, then tap Add.
Check a new row appears in the Sources list with that title.
Tap Add sources and add a file, then check it appears too.
Check whether any Google Drive or connected-service option appears on the Sources screen (expected to be missing for now).
items.needs: a file to upload; a signed-in account for cloud projects
items.note: Files and text are reachable. I searched ProjectSourcesTab.tsx for drive and google and found no Google Drive entry, so the connected-service part of Expected is not in the UI code.

items.where: Projects > tap a project card > Instructions (the button under the header, next to the quick actions). Type in the box, then tap the check button at the top right.
steps: Open Projects and tap a project card.
Tap Instructions under the project header.
Type an instruction, such as a short style rule, then tap the check button at the top right to save.
Reopen Instructions and check the text is still there.
Open Chats > New chat in this project, ask a question, and check the reply follows the instruction as Expected says.
items.needs: a project you can edit (not archived or shared with you)
items.note: The instructions entry is hidden for archived or shared projects; the create and edit form also has a Custom Instructions box.

items.where: AGI Work (in the drawer, under Projects; it may sit under More) > New task. Choose a project under Project (optional), fill the goal, then tap Start task. The project's Work tab lists its runs.
steps: Open the menu button at the top left, then tap AGI Work (tap More if it is not shown).
Tap New task (the floating button), and pick a project under Project (optional).
Type a goal and tap Start task.
Open Projects, tap the project, then tap the Work tab.
Look for the new run in the Work list and its state, and compare with Expected. If the list is empty it says No work yet.
items.needs: a cloud account on a plan that includes AGI Work (the page says so if not)
items.note: Starting work is done from AGI Work, not from the project's Work tab; the project's Work tab only lists runs. The New task button is labelled in CloudTasksScreen.tsx.

items.where: Projects (drawer) > Search projects bar at the bottom of the list. Type part of a name or description.
steps: Open Projects and make sure you have at least two projects with different names.
Tap the Search projects bar at the bottom and type part of one project's name. Check only that project stays in the list.
Clear the search and type a word that appears only in a project's description. Check that project appears.
Type a word that matches nothing. Check the text No matches appears.
items.needs: a few projects with different names and descriptions
items.note: The search bar is hidden when there are no projects, and on the Shared with you filter.

items.where: Projects > tap and hold a project card > Delete. Or open the project, tap More project actions (three dots, top right) > Delete. Confirm with Delete.
steps: Note the project name and open its Chats tab to note a chat in it.
Open Projects, press and hold the project card, then tap Delete.
Read the Delete project? message, then tap Cancel first to check Cancel keeps the project.
Repeat, and tap Delete to confirm.
Check the project is gone from the Projects list, and its chat still appears in the chat list (not in the project), as Expected says.
items.needs: a project you own, and a test chat inside it
items.note: The client menu shows Delete with no visible owner check in useProjectActions.ts; the server decides who may delete. The confirm message says the sources are deleted and chats move out of the project.

items.where: Menu (button at top left) > Library > Uploads
steps: Sign in and open the menu with the button at the top left.
Tap Library.
Tap the chip Uploads in the row under the Library title.
Compare the grid with Expected: only files you uploaded should appear, and no generated files.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one uploaded file

items.where: Menu (button at top left) > Library > Generated files
steps: Sign in and open the menu with the button at the top left.
Tap Library.
Tap the chip Generated files in the row under the Library title.
Compare the grid with Expected: only files the assistant generated should appear.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one generated file

items.where: Menu (button at top left) > Library > Artifacts
steps: Sign in and open the menu with the button at the top left.
Tap Library.
Tap the chip Artifacts in the row under the Library title.
Tap one artifact card.
Compare with Expected: the list should show your artifacts and the tapped one should open in the Artifacts screen.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact
items.note: Artifacts shown are filtered to the current app mode (Cloud or Local), so an artifact made in the other mode will not appear.

items.where: Menu (button at top left) > Library > Images
steps: Sign in and open the menu with the button at the top left.
Tap Library.
Tap the chip Images in the row under the Library title.
Tap one image card.
Compare with Expected: the Images view should list your images and the tapped image should open full screen in a viewer.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one image

items.where: Menu (button at top left) > Library > Videos
steps: Sign in and open the menu with the button at the top left.
Tap Library.
Tap the chip Videos in the row under the Library title.
Tap one video card.
Compare with Expected: the video should open in a player and play.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one video

items.where: Library > Library options (the ... button at top right) > Sort saved files > Recently added
steps: Sign in and tap Library in the menu.
Tap the ... button at the top right (Library options).
Tap Sort saved files, then Recently added.
Compare with Expected: the newest files should be at the top of the grid.
items.needs: a signed-in account with several files
items.note: There is no separate recent-files view. The sort is labelled Recently added and maps to the modified sort key, so it is not based on when a file was last used.

items.where: Library > search field at the bottom labelled Search library
steps: Sign in and tap Library in the menu.
Tap the search field at the bottom that says Search library.
Type part of a file name you know exists.
Compare with Expected: the grid should narrow to files whose name matches.
items.needs: a signed-in account with several named files

items.where: Library > filter chips row under the Library title: Images, Videos, Documents, Code, Charts, Research
steps: Sign in and tap Library in the menu.
Swipe the chip row sideways to reach the chips.
Tap Documents, then Images, then Videos.
Compare with Expected: the grid should show only the chosen file type each time.
items.needs: a signed-in account with files of more than one type

items.where: Library > long press a file card > Add to chat
steps: Sign in and tap Library in the menu.
Press and hold a document card (not a video).
Tap Add to chat in the menu that opens with the file name as title.
Compare with Expected: the app should open the chat screen with the file attached in the message box.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a document file
items.note: The Add to chat option is not offered for videos, and only appears in Cloud mode.

items.where: Library > top of the file grid (text ending in file storage used); and Settings > Storage
steps: Sign in and tap Library in the menu. Look just under the filter chips for a line ending in file storage used.
Compare the amount used with the limit shown in that line.
Open the menu, tap Settings, then tap Storage.
Compare with Expected: the storage breakdown should show how much your files use against the allowance.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The line only appears when the server returns storage numbers, and it is hidden inside Recently deleted.

items.where: Library > Library options (... at top right) > Recently deleted; to delete: long press a file > Delete
steps: Sign in, tap Library in the menu, then long press a file card and tap Delete.
Tap Delete on the Delete from Library? dialog.
Tap Library options (... at top right), then Recently deleted.
Long press the file, tap Restore, then go back to Library and check the file is back in the grid.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one file
items.note: The Recently deleted screen says files are erased after 30 days, and Delete permanently is also offered there.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > Library > tap an image tile
steps: Open the navigation drawer (the icon button labelled 'Open navigation drawer' in apps/mobile/src/shared/components/DrawerButton.tsx; its position on screen was not verified) and tap Library.
Tap any image tile in the Library grid.
Look for a full-screen black viewer that shows the image, with a row of icon buttons at the top and a Close (X) button at the top right.
Tap Close to return to the grid and compare with Expected: images open in a viewer.
items.needs: an image in Library (generated or uploaded)
items.note: Chat image attachments open the same viewer (accessibility hint 'Opens full screen' in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx).

items.where: Open navigation drawer > Library > tap a video file card
steps: Open the navigation drawer and tap Library.
Tap a video file card in the Library grid.
Wait for the video player to open over the Library screen, then press play.
Check that the video plays inside the app and compare with Expected: video files play in an in-product player. If it fails, the alert 'Could not play the video' appears.
items.needs: a video in Library
items.note: The in-app player's controls were not read in detail; the failure hint tells the user to long-press the video and choose Share.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > Library > tap an image tile
steps: Open the navigation drawer, tap Library, and tap an image tile to open the viewer.
Pinch two fingers apart on the image, then pinch them together.
Double-tap the image to zoom in, then double-tap again to zoom out.
Compare with Expected: viewers offer zoom. Zoom is by gesture only.
items.needs: an image in Library, and a phone or touch screen for pinch and double-tap
items.note: No on-screen zoom buttons exist; Expected says 'zoom controls', while the code offers pinch, double-tap, and screen-reader 'Zoom in' and 'Zoom out' actions (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ZoomableImage.tsx).

items.needs: none
items.note: No full-screen toggle was found: the image viewer always opens as a full-screen modal, and the only 'full screen' wording is the fallback label 'Full screen generated image' in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ImageFullScreen.tsx. I searched apps/mobile/src for 'full screen', 'fullscreen' and 'Full-screen' in the library, chat and file viewer folders.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > Library > long-press a file > Share
steps: Open the navigation drawer and tap Library.
Long-press a file card or image tile in the grid to open the action menu.
Tap Share. The app downloads the file to the phone and opens the system share sheet.
Compare with Expected: the original file can be downloaded. In the share sheet, check the save options the phone provides.
items.needs: a file in Library (an uploaded or generated file)
items.note: No control named Download exists for Library files; for images, the viewer's 'Save image to Photos' saves to Photos instead of the original file.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > Library > tap a CSV file > tap a cell > Copy cell
steps: Open the navigation drawer, tap Library, and tap a CSV file.
Tap a cell in the grid to select it.
Tap Copy cell, then paste into another app such as Notes.

Compare with Expected: copied content matches the selected cell. Plain text files also allow long-press selection of lines and the system Copy menu (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/artifact-viewers/TextFileView.tsx).
items.needs: a device, and a CSV file in Library
items.note: The text-file selection path relies on the system selection menu and was not exercised; the visible Copy buttons exist only for CSV and table grids.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > Library > tap an Office file > Share
steps: Open the navigation drawer, tap Library, and tap an Office document.
Look for the message 'Open it in another app to read it.' with a Share button.
Tap Share to open the system share sheet, which lists apps that can open the file.

Compare with Expected: the file opens in another app. The file viewer header also has a share icon labelled 'Share' plus the file name (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/artifact-viewers/FileViewerScreen.tsx).
items.needs: an Office document in Library

labels.text: Open it in another app to read it.

items.note: The Office-file routing is read from a code comment in DocumentFileView.tsx; the exact list of file types was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > Library > tap a file the viewer cannot render
steps: Open the navigation drawer, tap Library, and tap a file type that has no preview.
Look for the message 'Preview isn’t available for this file type.' with a Share button.
Tap Share to hand the file to another app through the system share sheet.
Compare with Expected: the app says there is no preview and offers Share as the download or open path.
items.needs: a file in Library of a type with no in-app preview

labels.text: Preview isn’t available for this file type.

items.note: Only Share is offered; there is no separate Download or Open button. Which file types lack a preview depends on apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/artifact-viewers/viewerKind.ts, which was not traced type by type.

items.where: Chat > open a reply that writes an artifact > tap the card under that reply (it shows the artifact title and type in capitals)
steps: Sign in and open a chat.
Ask the assistant for a small self-contained web page or a code file.
Wait until the reply finishes and a card appears under it.
Tap the card.
Compare: a full-screen viewer opens with the same artifact (Expected: the card opens the artifact).
items.needs: an account that can chat
items.note: Card and viewer are in MessageBubble.tsx and InlineArtifactCard.tsx; the card has no fixed visible words beyond the artifact title.

items.where: Chat > tap an artifact card > read the title at the top of the viewer (it reads 'title · TYPE')
steps: Open a chat with an artifact and tap its card.
Read the bold title at the top left of the viewer.
Read the title on the card in the chat.
Check the fallback: an artifact with no name shows the kind name, for example 'Web page' or 'Diagram'.
Compare with Expected: title shown on card and viewer, with a fallback.
items.needs: an artifact with a name and one without (for example a diagram or web page without a title)
items.note: The viewer title is built in ArtifactFullScreen.tsx from the artifact title, with the type appended after a middle dot.

items.where: Chat > tap an artifact card > read the capital-letter type word in the viewer header; the card shows the same word under its title
steps: Open a chat with an artifact of a known kind (for example a chart or a document).
Look at the small capital-letter word on the card, such as CHART or DOCUMENT.
Tap the card and read the type after the middle dot in the viewer header.
Compare with Expected: kind shown on card and in viewer.
items.needs: artifacts of two different kinds
items.note: Card shows the language if set, else a type label; viewer shows language or type in capitals. The word 'Spreadsheet' was not found in apps/mobile; the kind labels come from a shared package outside apps/mobile.

items.where: Chat > send a request that makes an artifact > while the reply is still writing, the card shows 'Writing…'; a stopped or failed write shows 'Stopped' or 'Failed' on the card
steps: Send a request that asks for a long artifact.
While the reply is still writing, look at the card for 'Writing…' under its title.
Stop the reply before it finishes, if the app offers a stop control.
Look at the card for 'Stopped' (title becomes 'Stopped artifact').
Compare with Expected: being written, finished, stopped or failed each shown.
items.needs: a model reply long enough to watch while it writes
items.note: A finished artifact shows no state word; it shows the normal card. What makes a write 'Failed' (the failed prop) was not traced and the stop control was not located.

items.where: Menu (side drawer) > Library > 'Artifacts' filter chip > tap an artifact; or in chat, tap an artifact card
steps: Open the side menu and tap 'Library'.
Tap the 'Artifacts' filter chip.
Tap an artifact to open it.
Compare: its content shows in a view (Expected: open from chat or a list).
items.needs: at least one saved artifact
items.note: Library opens the artifact gallery route (apps/mobile/src/features/artifacts/index.tsx) for the tapped item.

items.where: Chat > tap an artifact card > tap the X (accessibility name 'Close') at the top right of the viewer
steps: Open an artifact from its card in chat.
Tap the X icon at the top right of the viewer.
Check the viewer closes and you are back in the conversation.
Check the card is still under the reply.
Compare with Expected: closing hides it and it stays available.
items.needs: none
items.note: The X is an icon; its visible word is only the accessibility label 'Close' with hint 'Returns to the conversation'.

items.where: Chat > tap the same artifact card again; or Menu > Library > 'Artifacts' > tap the artifact
steps: Open an artifact, then close it with the X.
Tap the same card again or open it from Library > Artifacts.
Force-quit and reopen the app, then open the chat and tap the card.
Compare: the same artifact opens (Expected: reopen after close and after reload).
items.needs: an account with a saved artifact; a way to restart the app
items.note: No separate reopen toggle was found; reopening is done through the card or the list. The reload survival relies on the artifact store (apps/mobile/src/features/artifacts/store.ts) and was not run.

items.where: Chat > tap an artifact card; the viewer opens over the whole screen and closes with the X
steps: Tap an artifact card in chat.
Check the viewer fills the whole screen.
Tap the X to return to the conversation.
Compare with Expected: the artifact can be expanded to full screen and returned from.
items.needs: none
items.note: No separate expand button was found; the viewer is always a full-screen modal on open.

items.where: Chat > a reply or conversation with two or more artifacts > tap one artifact card > use the row of artifact titles under the viewer header to switch
steps: Open a conversation with at least two artifacts.
Tap one artifact card to open the viewer.
Look for the row of artifact titles under the header.
Tap another title in the row.
Compare: the viewer shows that artifact without closing (Expected: switch without leaving the viewer).
items.needs: a conversation with two or more artifacts
items.note: The switcher appears only when the conversation has more than one artifact; its row shows artifact titles, with no fixed visible words.

items.where: Chat > tap an artifact card > tap 'Preview' or 'Source' in the tab row under the viewer header (shown only for artifacts that can be previewed)
steps: Open an HTML or diagram artifact from its card.
Tap 'Source' and read the code.
Tap 'Preview' and read the rendered view.
Compare with Expected: switch between the rendered preview and the source.
items.needs: a previewable artifact (for example an HTML page)
items.note: Which kinds count as previewable (isPreviewable) was not traced.

items.where: Chat > tap an artifact with two or more versions > tap 'Previous version' to an older version > tap the More artifact actions button and look for 'Edit source'
steps: Open an artifact that has at least two versions.
Step back to an older version with the left arrow next to 'Version N of M'.
Tap the More artifact actions button (three dots).
Check that 'Edit source' is not listed for the older version.
Compare with Expected: the older version is viewable without changing it.
items.needs: an artifact with two or more versions (made by editing it first)
items.note: The code has no visible 'Read-only' label. Editing is only offered for the newest version of a non-generated file (canEditSource). Shared-copy read-only was not found.

items.where: Chat > tap an artifact with two or more versions > tap the 'Version N of M' button under the viewer header to open 'Version history'
steps: Open an artifact with more than one version.
Read the 'Version N of M' control under the header.
Tap it to open the 'Version history' sheet.
Tap a version row to show that version.
Compare: the viewer shows the chosen version and its number (Expected: see and pick any version).
items.needs: an artifact with two or more versions
items.note: The 'Version N of M' text is an accessibility label (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx), not a visible word.

items.where: Chat > tap an artifact with two or more versions > use the left and right arrows beside 'Version N of M' under the viewer header
steps: Open an artifact with at least three versions.
Tap the left arrow ('Previous version') and check the version number changes.
Tap the right arrow ('Next version').
Check the arrows are dimmed at the first and last version.
Compare with Expected: step to previous and next and see which version is shown.
items.needs: an artifact with two or more versions
items.note: The arrows are icon-only; their words are accessibility labels.

items.where: Chat > tap an artifact with two or more versions > step to an older version > tap 'Restore' in the version row under the viewer header
steps: Open an artifact with at least two versions.
Step back to an older version with the left arrow.
Tap 'Restore' (accessibility label 'Restore version N').
Check the viewer now shows the restored content as the newest version.
Open 'Version history' and check the versions in between are still listed.
items.needs: an artifact with two or more versions
items.note: No confirmation dialog was found on the restore path; restoring happens directly.

items.where: Chat > tap an artifact card > tap 'Download artifact' (download icon) in the top bar; if several formats exist, choose one in the 'Download as' sheet
steps: Open an artifact from its card.
Tap the download icon in the top bar.
If the 'Download as' sheet opens, tap a format such as Markdown, PDF, Plain text or Word.
Save or share the file in the system sheet that opens.
Compare: the file is in the chosen format (Expected: each choice saves that format).
items.needs: none; a way to view the saved file
items.note: Artifacts with one format save directly; generated files use the share sheet instead.

items.where: Chat > tap an artifact card > tap the copy icon ('Copy content') in the top bar, then paste elsewhere
steps: Open an artifact from its card.
Tap the copy icon in the top bar.
Check the icon changes to a check mark and the label reads 'Copied'.
Paste into Notes or the chat box.
Compare: the pasted text matches the artifact's content (Expected: a copy control puts that content on the clipboard and confirms).
items.needs: none
items.note: The copy icon is icon-only; 'Copied' is the accessibility label after success. Failure label is 'Could not copy'.

items.where: Chat > an artifact card shows a small chip under its title: 'Published', 'Workspace' or 'Invited'; viewer shows 'Private. Only you can open it until you publish it.' in AGI Cloud mode
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud and open an artifact that has been published or shared.
Look at the small chip on its card in chat (and in Library > Artifacts).
Open the artifact and check the publish area of the viewer.
For a private artifact, check the line 'Private. Only you can open it until you publish it.'
Compare with Expected: private, published, or workspace state is visible.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account; a published or workspace-shared artifact; a private one for the private line

labels.text: Private. Only you can open it until you publish it.

items.note: A private artifact shows no card chip; the private line appears only in cloud mode under the publish condition in ArtifactFullScreen.tsx.

items.where: Chat > open an HTML or React artifact that fails to render > the viewer shows 'This preview stopped with an error.' with 'Retry' and 'View source'
steps: Open an artifact whose page fails to run (for example an HTML page that throws an error on load).
Read the error panel: 'This preview stopped with an error.'
Tap 'View source' and check the source opens.
Go back to Preview and tap 'Retry'.
Compare with Expected: an error panel that explains the failure and offers source or retry.
items.needs: an artifact that fails to render (made by asking the assistant for a broken page)

labels.text: This preview stopped with an error.

items.note: A load timeout shows 'This preview did not finish loading.' instead; an invalid SVG shows "This image couldn't be rendered."

items.where: Chat > send a request for an artifact > while the reply is writing, tap the card titled 'Generating artifact' (it shows 'Writing…')
steps: Send a request that asks for a long artifact such as a code file.
While the card shows 'Writing…', tap the card.
Watch the viewer as the content grows.
Compare with Expected: the artifact view updates live while the reply writes.
items.needs: a reply that writes an artifact slowly enough to watch
items.note: Live update was traced in StreamingArtifactCard.tsx; the speed of growth was not run.

items.where: Phone screen: tap any artifact card in chat; the viewer opens as a full-screen slide-up view with the X at the top right
steps: On a phone-sized screen, tap an artifact card in chat.
Check the viewer covers the full screen with no side panel.
Check the buttons in the top bar are large touch targets.
Tap the X to return.
Compare with Expected: full-screen reader with touch controls.
items.needs: phone width (the iPhone build or a phone-sized simulator)
items.note: This is a layout rule: the viewer is a full-screen Modal (overFullScreen, slide animation) in ArtifactFullScreen.tsx, so its effect is only seen on screen.

items.where: Chat (first screen after signing in) > ask for a document > tap the document card in the answer > read the title at the top of the full-screen view, shown as the title followed by " · Document"
steps: Sign in and open Chat.
Send a message that asks for a written document, for example a short one-page plan.
Wait for the answer to show a document card, and read the title shown on the card.
Tap the card to open the document full screen.
Compare the title at the top of the full-screen view with the title on the card, and check that it is not blank.
items.needs: A signed-in account that can generate documents in Chat
items.note: The card and viewer use the document's title, and the default comes from the artifact title helpers (artifactTitle.ts, artifactDisplayTitle falls back to artifactKindTitle), which I did not confirm end to end; the old quoted lines in the plan are gone, so this is from the current files, and I could not confirm the exact default text a person would see for an untitled document.

items.where: Chat > open a document (tap its card) > tap the version counter in the top bar (accessibility hint "Opens the version history") > "Version history" sheet > tap a version row to view it, or tap "Restore" on an older row
steps: Open a document that has been changed at least once, for example by asking for changes in Chat, so it has more than one version.
In the document's top bar, tap the version counter (it shows the version number out of the total).
Read the "Version history" sheet: check that each past version is listed with its time.
Tap an older version row to view it, then check that the document shows that version's content.
Tap "Restore" on that older row, then check that the document content returns to that version and that a newer entry is kept in the history.
items.needs: A document with at least two versions (ask for a change once, or edit it, before starting)
items.note: The version counter is a button with an accessibility label rather than a visible word, and the times depend on formatVersionTime in apps/mobile/src/features/artifacts/versionSummary.ts, which I did not run.

items.where: Chat > open a document (tap its card) > tap the download icon in the top bar (accessibility label "Download artifact") > "Download as" sheet > tap "Word"
steps: Open a document in Chat so the full-screen view shows.
Tap the download icon in the top bar. It has no visible words; VoiceOver reads it as "Download artifact".
In the sheet headed "Download as", look for the option "Word" with the detail "A .docx document you can edit".
Tap "Word" and wait for the share or save step to appear.
Open the saved or shared file on the Mac and check that it is a Word document with the document's text.
items.needs: A signed-in account with a document open; a Mac app that opens .docx files
items.note: The Word option appears for document-type artifacts that are not slide decks (artifactExport.ts lines 88-96); the sheet only opens when there is more than one export choice, so a single-choice file would download directly.

items.where: Chat > open a document (tap its card) > tap the download icon in the top bar (accessibility label "Download artifact") > "Download as" sheet > tap "PDF"
steps: Open a document in Chat so the full-screen view shows.
Tap the download icon in the top bar. It has no visible words; VoiceOver reads it as "Download artifact".
In the sheet headed "Download as", look for the option "PDF" with the detail "A styled document".
Tap "PDF" and wait for the share or save step to appear.
Open the saved or shared file and check that it is a PDF with the document's title and text.
items.needs: A signed-in account with a document open
items.note: The PDF option appears for document-type artifacts (artifactExport.ts lines 88-95) and the export itself runs through apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/artifactExport.ts exportArtifact; I did not run it.

items.where: Chat > open a document (tap its card) > tap the download icon in the top bar (accessibility label "Download artifact") > "Download as" sheet > tap "Markdown"
steps: Open a document in Chat so the full-screen view shows.
Tap the download icon in the top bar. It has no visible words; VoiceOver reads it as "Download artifact".
In the sheet headed "Download as", look for the option "Markdown" with the detail "A .md file that keeps the formatting".
Tap "Markdown" and wait for the share or save step to appear.
Open the saved or shared file and check that it is a .md file whose formatting (headings, lists) is kept as Markdown text.
items.needs: A signed-in account with a document open
items.note: The Markdown option is listed first for document-type artifacts (artifactExport.ts lines 88-91); the sheet and download path were read from source only and not run.

items.where: Chat > tap an HTML artifact card (opens the full-screen artifact view) > tab "Preview"
steps: Sign in and open a chat that has an HTML artifact (a page the assistant made as an artifact).
Tap the HTML artifact card in the chat to open the full-screen artifact view.
Make sure the "Preview" tab is selected at the top (the other tab is "Source").
Look for a live, interactive page: buttons and links should respond when tapped, and the page should show its content, not the raw HTML text. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an HTML artifact in a chat (ask the assistant to make a small HTML page with a button if none exists)
items.note: The cited line SafeArtifactPreview.tsx:280 is the WebView that renders HTML (runsScripts is true for html); the tab label is only shown when the artifact is previewable. The card's own label was not checked.

items.where: Chat > tap an HTML artifact card > tab "Preview" > error box with "Retry" and "View source" buttons
steps: Open a chat and ask the assistant for an HTML artifact that throws a JavaScript error on load (for example a script line that calls an undefined function).
Tap the HTML artifact card to open it full screen, with the "Preview" tab selected.
Look for the error box with the text "This preview stopped with an error." and the error message under it.
Tap "Retry" to run the preview again, or "View source" to switch to the Source tab. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an HTML artifact that throws a JavaScript error (ask the assistant to make one on purpose)

labels.text: This preview stopped with an error.

items.note: The error box is drawn at SafeArtifactPreview.tsx:226-260 (the cited line 69 no longer holds it). The error reporter script in sandboxedArtifactHtml.ts:166 was not read in full, so the exact message shown for a given error was not checked.

items.where: Chat > tap an HTML artifact card > header icon "Download artifact" (down-arrow icon) > share sheet or "Download" choices
steps: Open an HTML artifact full screen (tap its card in the chat).
Tap the download icon in the top header, labelled "Download artifact".

If a choice list titled "Download" appears, pick the option that names the source file (for HTML it should be a source option, not PDF). If the system share sheet opens directly, that is the source file.
Save or open the shared file and check that it contains the same HTML code as the Source tab. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an HTML artifact in a chat
items.note: The source option label for HTML was not confirmed: artifactExport.ts builds it from codeFileFor(language), which was not opened, so the exact option text (likely "HTML file") is unverified. The cited line ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:228 no longer contains the quoted code.

items.where: Chat > "Cloud" mode (top mode toggle) > tap an HTML artifact card > header icon "Publish artifact to a public link" (globe icon) > alert "Publish to a public link?" > "Publish"
steps: Make sure the mode toggle at the top of the chat shows "Cloud" (not "Local"), and that you are signed in to AGI Cloud.
Open an HTML artifact full screen and tap the globe icon in the header, labelled "Publish artifact to a public link".
In the alert "Publish to a public link?", tap "Publish".

Look for the link box with the link text (shown with "Copy publication link" and "Share publication link" buttons) and the hint "Private. Only you can open it until you publish it." before publishing. Open the link in a browser and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account in Cloud mode (a Local-only device shows "Switch to AGI Cloud to publish"; a signed-out one shows "Sign in to AGI Cloud to publish")

labels.text: Publish artifact to a public link

items.note: The globe icon only shows when publishableKindFor(artifact) accepts the artifact kind, and publishableKindFor was not checked for html, so it is not confirmed that an HTML artifact shows the globe icon. The publish helper is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/services/artifactPublishing.ts:60 (publishArtifact).

items.where: Chat screen > send a message asking for Python analysis of some data > under the assistant's reply, the block titled "Code Execution" (status "Running Python…"); tap it to expand "Output"; the run's code is in the tool row, where "Run again" re-runs it
steps: Sign in and open a chat on the main chat screen.
Send a request that needs Python, for example: "Using this small table of numbers I type, calculate the average and draw a chart in Python." Type the numbers in the message.
Wait for the reply. Look for the block titled "Code Execution" under the reply; it shows "Running Python…" while it runs.
Tap the "Code Execution" block to expand it and check that the "Output" heading shows the printed result.

Look for the code the run used (its code card in the tool row) and for any chart drawn below the output, and compare with Expected: code, output and charts all visible. Optionally tap "Run again" to repeat the run.
items.needs: a Free or paid account; the run may ask for approval first (plan requirement not verified in the code); a phone or Mac with the app signed in
items.note: The plan's line numbers were stale; the feature was found in CodeExecutionBlock.tsx, MessageBubble.tsx (renders it) and CodeRunAgain.tsx. Chart display under the output was not traced to a visible label, and the entry route into the panel depends on the model deciding to run code, so the exact words in the reply are not known.

items.where: Chat screen > an assistant answer that contains a table > tap the table's "Download table as CSV" button (an icon; its label is that text), then the share sheet opens. Or open a CSV/spreadsheet file in the answer's artifact view and tap the share icon labeled "Share as CSV"
steps: Sign in and open a chat where the assistant has returned a table (ask for a small table, e.g. "make a table of 3 fruits and their prices").
Find the table's action buttons in the table header area and tap the one labeled "Download table as CSV".
Check that the share sheet opens with a file ending in .csv (the file name is built from the table title or "table").
Optional route: open a CSV file artifact and tap the icon labeled "Share as CSV", then check the share sheet and that a .csv file is offered.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a chat that contains a table; a phone or Mac to see the share sheet
items.note: The plan's line 394 moved; the table download control is now at MessageContentRenderer.tsx lines 373-379 and 438-442. The CSV download is also present in the spreadsheet viewer as "Share as CSV".

items.where: Chat screen > an assistant answer that shows a chart > tap "Show data" to see the numbers, and tap "Save image" at the bottom of the chart to save it as a picture through the share sheet
steps: Sign in and open a chat where the assistant returns a chart (ask for a simple bar or line chart of a few values).
Look at the chart's footer row for the buttons "Show data" and "Save image".
Tap "Save image"; the label changes to "Saving…" while it works, then the share sheet opens with a PNG picture of the chart.
If saving fails, check that the alert "Could not save the chart" appears instead of a share sheet.
Compare with Expected: the user can export the chart as an image file. Tap "Show data" to confirm the table of values is also visible.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a chat answer that contains a chart; a phone or Mac to see the share sheet
items.note: The plan's line numbers were stale; the export is at ReportChart.tsx lines 817-836 and the button at 910-924, and it calls exportPngImage in apps/mobile/services/fileCreation.ts. The only export is a PNG image, not a data file.

items.where: Chat > open a generated .pptx file card (the artifact opens full screen) > Download icon in the top bar (accessibility label "Download artifact")
steps: Sign in and open a chat that has produced a PowerPoint file (a generated .pptx). Open its card so it opens full screen.
Tap the download icon in the top bar (labelled "Download artifact" for screen readers).
The app downloads the file and opens the share sheet with the file. Check that the file is a .pptx and that it opens as a presentation.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a chat that has produced a .pptx file (a deck the server created); a phone or simulator to see the share sheet
items.note: A .pptx is only downloadable when the server created one (a remote generated file with an http(s) uri, handled in ArtifactFullScreen.tsx handleDownload, and the pptx mime/UTI is in apps/mobile/services/fileCreation.ts). The in-app export for a deck artifact offers only PDF, Markdown and Plain text (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/artifactExport.ts), so PPTX is not a choice in the export sheet. Download button has no visible text, only an icon.

items.where: Chat > long-press an answer > Export Message… > Export as PDF
steps: Open a chat that has an assistant answer with text.
Long-press the answer (or use the More message actions control under it).
Tap Export Message….
Tap Export as PDF and wait for the share sheet.
Compare: a PDF of the answer text opens or shares, with the formatting kept. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: none; a chat with a finished assistant answer
items.note: Only answer text (and documents or artifacts) becomes a PDF; no control was found that converts an uploaded Word or text file attachment itself to PDF. Artifacts also offer PDF under Download artifact (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx).

items.needs: none
items.note: Searched apps/mobile for spreadsheet, xlsx and PDF export. Spreadsheet attachments are accepted in Cloud mode (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/attachmentValidation.ts), but the only PDF export options found are for answers, conversations and text or markdown artifacts (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/artifactExport.ts, apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ConversationExportSheet.tsx). No spreadsheet-to-PDF control was found.

items.where: Chat > Add to chat > File, pick a PDF, then send a request to summarize it
steps: Open a chat (Cloud mode) or start a new one.
Tap Add to chat (the plus button by the message box).
Tap File and choose a PDF file.
Wait until the file chip above the message box is ready, type "Summarize this PDF", and send.
Compare: the answer gives a summary of the PDF content. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a PDF file with readable text; Cloud mode (the File row is shown only in Cloud mode)
items.note: The File row is shown only when the app is in Cloud mode (AddToChatSheet.tsx). The summary itself is produced by the model on the server (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/chat-attachment-hydration.ts), so the exact wording is not fixed by code.

items.where: Chat > Add to chat > File, pick a PDF, then ask a question about it
steps: Open a chat in Cloud mode.
