Tap Add to chat, then tap File and choose a PDF file.
Type a specific question about a fact in the PDF and send.
Compare: the answer gives the fact as it appears in the PDF. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a PDF file with readable text; Cloud mode
items.note: The File row is shown only in Cloud mode. Answers are produced by the server-side model path in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/chat-attachment-hydration.ts.

items.where: In the chat answer, after attaching a PDF with Add to chat > File and asking about one page
steps: Attach a multi-page PDF with Add to chat > File in Cloud mode.
Type "What is on page 3?" (use a page number that exists in the file) and send.
Compare: the answer describes page 3 and not another page. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a multi-page PDF file; Cloud mode
items.note: Page handling is server-side: each page is sent as a [Page n] marker and image (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/chat-attachment-hydration.ts:702). The page markers are not shown to the user. The page viewer shows Page N of M (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/artifact-viewers/PdfFileView.tsx:197).

items.where: Chat > Add to chat > File (attach a PDF), then ask for its text
steps: Attach a PDF with Add to chat > File.
Type "Write out all of the text in this PDF exactly as it appears" and send.
Compare: the answer contains the plain text of the PDF, without layout or tables. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a PDF with a text layer; a Cloud or local-mode chat
items.note: No button that shows or copies the extracted plain text was found. Local mode extracts PDF text on the phone (apps/mobile/services/docParser.ts, extractTextFromPdfBuffer). The old code location apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1052 now holds research-decision code, so it was not used.

items.where: Projects > open a project > Add sources (choose a scanned PDF), then ask about text that appears only in the scan
steps: Open the Projects tab and open a project.
Tap Add sources and choose an image-only (scanned) PDF.
Wait until the source row leaves the Indexing state.
Ask a question whose answer is only in the scanned pages, in a chat inside that project.
Compare: the answer uses text from the scan, and a failed source shows Couldn’t read. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a scanned (image-only) PDF; a project you can edit
items.note: The OCR transcription runs on the server in apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-extraction.ts. The Projects tab label and the project screen wording were not confirmed in apps/mobile, and the file picker used by Add sources was not traced. In a plain chat, scanned pages are sent to the model as images instead of OCR text.

items.needs: none
items.note: Searched apps/mobile and apps/web for table and tabular handling in PDF code. The only PDF path returns plain text and page text (apps/mobile/services/docParser.ts, apps/web/lib/server/pdf-attachment-content.ts); table rows and columns exist only for CSV files (docParser.ts parseCsvToText, rows and columns metadata). The cited apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:1702 is attachment replay, not table extraction.

items.where: Open an HTML artifact from the chat (tap its card to open the full-screen view), then tap the Download artifact icon (down-arrow) in the top bar. The app shares the file directly; there is no choice sheet for an HTML artifact.
steps: In a chat, ask Claude to make a single-page web page so an HTML artifact appears as a card.
Tap the artifact card to open the full-screen artifact view.
Tap the Download artifact icon (down-arrow, top bar).
Look at the share sheet that opens. It should offer one file ending in .html (the code names it 'HTML file', built from the file extension). Compare with Expected: a standalone HTML file.
items.needs: an HTML artifact in a chat (a web page made by Claude); a phone or simulator with a share sheet
items.note: The HTML export is the artifact source exactly as written (artifactExportOptions returns one 'source' option with extension html), and the label 'HTML file' is built from a template, not a literal string. For document and Markdown artifacts the Download sheet offers Markdown, PDF, Word and Plain text, with no HTML choice.

items.where: Open an artifact that has 2 or more versions (from a chat card or Library > Artifacts filter). Tap Show changes under the version bar to compare with the previous version. Tap the version button (Version N of M) to open Version history, then tap Restore on an older version. Restore is also offered under the version bar when viewing an older version.
steps: Make a second version: open an artifact and use More artifact actions > Edit source (or Ask for changes), save a change so the version bar shows v2/2.
Tap Show changes under the version bar and compare the changed lines with the previous version.
Tap the version button (Version N of M) to open the Version history sheet.
Tap Restore on version 1 in that sheet, or go back to version 1 with the previous arrow and tap Restore under the version bar.
Look at the artifact text. It should match version 1 again. Compare with Expected: an earlier version is restored.
items.needs: an artifact with 2 or more versions (make one by editing it); no paid plan is shown in the code for this feature
items.note: Show changes only appears when a previous version exists and the artifact is not a generated file. The More artifact actions menu also has Review changes (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactChangesReview.tsx), which is a second compare path. The version button and Restore labels are built from templates in code, so the tester sees 'Version N of M' and 'v2/2'-style text. Whether Restore saves a new version was not checked.

items.where: Chat > ask the assistant for a small web page > open the page it makes > tap the globe icon 'Publish artifact to a public link' in the top bar
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud and make sure the app is in AGI Cloud mode (not Local).
In the chat, ask the assistant to build a small one-page website.
Open the page the assistant creates so the artifact screen appears.
Tap the globe icon labelled 'Publish artifact to a public link'.
Tap 'Publish' in the confirmation box.
Compare: the globe icon turns green and a link appears under the page (Expected: the site is hosted).
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account

labels.text: Publish artifact to a public link
Switch to AGI Cloud to publish

items.note: The prompt step itself (how the assistant turns a request into an artifact) was not traced in these files; the path above starts at the artifact screen, and how that screen is opened from the chat was not traced either.

items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: No separate preview deployment was found. The only publish action creates a shared link (shareUrl in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/services/artifactPublishing.ts); 'Preview' in ArtifactFullScreen.tsx is an in-app view, not a shareable URL. Searched rg -i 'preview|deploy' in ArtifactFullScreen.tsx and artifactPublishing.ts, and rg -i 'deploy' across apps/mobile/src.

items.where: Artifact screen > globe icon 'Publish artifact to a public link' > 'Publish' > 'Open in Safari' (iPhone) or 'Open in browser' (Android)
steps: Open a page that was made by the assistant and tap the globe icon 'Publish artifact to a public link'.
Tap 'Publish' in the confirmation box.
Wait for the globe icon to turn green and for the 'Who can open this' section to appear below the page.
Tap 'Open in Safari' (or 'Open in browser' on Android).
Compare: the published site opens in the system browser at a public web address (Expected: a public URL).
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account

labels.text: Publish artifact to a public link

items.note: The 'Open in Safari' / 'Open in browser' text is returned by a function in ArtifactFullScreen.tsx and was not checked on screen; the 'Anyone with the link' visibility option is in PublishedArtifactControls.tsx.

items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: No control to roll a live published site back was found. The nearest control is 'Restore version N' with 'Version history' (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx and ArtifactVersionHistorySheet.tsx), but restoreArtifactVersion in apps/mobile/src/features/artifacts/store.ts only changes the local artifact and queues an artifact sync; it does not republish the live site. Searched rg -i 'rollback|roll back|rolled back' in apps/mobile/src and found only test comments.

items.where: Artifact screen > download icon 'Download artifact' (top bar)
steps: Open a code page made by the assistant (for example an HTML page) so the artifact screen appears.
Tap the download icon labelled 'Download artifact'.
If a choice list titled 'Download' appears, pick the option that says 'The source exactly as written'; otherwise the system share sheet opens with the file.
Compare: the share sheet offers a file with the page's source code (Expected: the owner downloads the source).'
items.needs: none
items.note: Only one source file is exported per artifact (artifactExport.ts); a multi-file site is not packaged as a project. The option label for code is built as a template in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/artifactExport.ts ('<EXT> file' or the file name), so its exact text was not fixed.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > Search (icon at the top of the menu) > type in the Search box
steps: Tap the button labelled "Open navigation drawer".
Tap the search icon labelled "Search" at the top of the menu.
Type a word from the title or text of an older chat into the box labelled "Search".
Look for chats whose title or message text contains that word. Tap one and check that it opens that chat. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account with at least two saved chats that contain a shared word
items.note: Chat search runs on the search route (app/(app)/search.tsx), which renders ChatsListScreen in search-only mode.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > Projects > type in the Search projects box
steps: Tap "Open navigation drawer".
Tap "Projects".
Type part of a project's name into the box labelled "Search projects" and check that the project appears.
Clear the box, type a word from a project's description, and check that the project appears. Tap it to open it and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account with at least one project that has a description
items.note: The search box is hidden when the Shared filter is chosen; the filter choice appears only in Cloud mode.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > Library > Search library
steps: Tap "Open navigation drawer".
Tap "Library".
Type part of a file name or image prompt into the box labelled "Search library".
Check that only matching items stay in the list. Type text that matches nothing and check the empty state. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Library with at least two saved files or images with different names
items.note: The Library search box is the only search control found for these items; the search text is applied after a short debounce.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > Library > Artifacts (filter chip) > Search library
steps: Tap "Open navigation drawer", then "Library".
Tap the filter chip "Artifacts".
Type part of an artifact's title or content into the box labelled "Search library".
Check that matching artifacts stay in the list. Tap one to open it and compare with Expected.
items.needs: at least one saved artifact (for example a code file or a chart made in chat)
items.note: The separate Artifacts gallery route (app/(app)/artifacts) has no search box in the code; artifact search is in the Library.

items.where: Settings > Connectors (connect a source), then Add to chat > Connectors (turn it on in a chat)
steps: Tap "Open navigation drawer", then "Settings", then "Connectors".
Pick a connector, sign in, and wait until it shows "Connected".
Open a chat, tap "Add to chat", then tap "Connectors" and turn on the connected source.
Ask a question whose answer is in that source. Check that the answer uses it and lists it among the sources. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account and an outside account for the work source (for example Google)
items.note: The connector names (Drive, Slack, Notion) were not checked against the code; the connector list is in the Connectors screen.

items.where: Add to chat > Web search (turn on), then ask a question in the chat; or Settings > Capabilities > AGI Cloud > Web search
steps: Open a chat and tap "Add to chat".
Turn on the row "Web search".
Ask a question about recent news or a current fact.
Look for "Searching for" under the question, then an answer with citations. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account whose plan allows web search, on a model that supports it
items.note: The Web search row in the sheet appears only in Cloud mode when the plan and model allow it.

items.where: Open navigation drawer > Projects > open a project > Open project sources (folder icon) > Add sources
steps: Tap "Open navigation drawer", then "Projects", then open a project.
Tap the button labelled "Open project sources".
Tap "Add sources" and add a file or text.
Open a new chat inside the same project and ask about the added content. Check that the answer uses it. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account, a project, and one file to upload

labels.text: The files this project’s chats can read.

items.note: No mobile control was found that limits chats to only one collection; the search over sources runs on the server (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts).

items.where: Chat with Web search on (see S34.07), then look under the answer at the "Searching for" line and the result cards
steps: Send a question that needs current web information with Web search on.
Watch the line "Searching for" under the question.
Look at each result card: it shows the page title, the site name and, when known, the date.
Compare the card text with what you see when you tap the card (S34.27). Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account with Web search on
items.note: Whether a snippet line appears depends on the provider data; the code reads a snippet when one is returned.

items.where: Chat with Web search on (see S34.07) > tap the "Sources" pill under the answer
steps: Send a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Tap the pill labelled "Sources" under the answer (it can show a count of sources).
Check that each source is a card with the page title, the site name and a link.
Tap a card to see that it opens the page. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account with Web search on
items.note: none

items.where: Chat with an answer that has citations > tap a numbered citation chip in the answer
steps: Open an answer that shows citation chips (small numbered links) in the text.
Tap one chip.
Check that a box opens with the source title, the site, and a snippet of text, with the buttons "Cancel" and "Open page".
Tap "Cancel" and check that you are still on the same answer. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a chat answer with citations (Web search on)
items.note: The phone has no hover; the tap is the only preview action. The snippet shows only when the source has one.

items.where: Chat with sources > tap the "Sources" pill under the answer; the full list opens with the heading "Sources" (or "Sources so far" while the answer is still running)
steps: Tap the "Sources" pill under an answer that has several sources.
Check that the full list opens in a sheet, with the heading "Sources" and, when cited, a section headed "Citations" and one headed "More".
Scroll to the bottom of the list and check that every source is there.
Close the sheet with "Close" and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a chat answer with at least four sources (Web search on)
items.note: The code splits sources into cited and other sources; a separate "used" versus "consulted" label was not found.

items.where: Chat with sources > tap a source card in the "Sources" list, or tap a citation chip then "Open page"
steps: Open the "Sources" list under an answer.
Tap one source row or card.
Check that the page opens in the in-app browser with the title and address of that source.
Go back to the chat and check that the answer is still there. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a chat answer with sources (Web search on)
items.note: A source with no http link cannot be opened and is shown as plain text.

items.where: Chat with Web search on > tap the "Sources" pill under the answer; the date sits under each card's site name
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and tap the "Sources" pill.
Look under the site name of each source card for a date.
Compare the dates with the page dates you see when you open the source.
Check that a source with no date shows no date line. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account with Web search on
items.note: Only a publication date is shown (from page_age); a retrieval date was not found in the code.

items.where: Chat with Web search on > ask a question that finds nothing, or where the search fails; read the line under the search and the notice under the answer
steps: Ask a question that web search cannot answer, such as a made-up name.
Look at the search line: it shows "No results for" followed by your query.
Look under the answer for the notice "Web search didn't return results for this turn" with a "Retry" button.
If the search fails, check for "The search failed. Try sending the message again." Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account with Web search on; a query with no results (a provider outage is hard to trigger)
items.note: A provider being unavailable is reported through the same notices; a separate unavailable text was not found in the mobile code.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (button beside the message box) > Deep research
steps: Sign in to a Managed Cloud account and open a chat.
Check the model picker shows a model that supports research; the toggle is hidden for other models.
Tap Add to chat beside the message box.
Turn on Deep research.
Type a research question and send it.
Look for a Deep research card in the reply that shows a phase such as Planning research. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Managed Cloud account on a plan granted Deep Research, and a research-capable model
items.note: The Deep research toggle shows only in Cloud mode, with a research-capable model and the canUseDeepResearch grant.

items.where: Chat screen > Deep research card in the reply > plan editor (phase Review the plan to start searching)
steps: Start a Deep research run (S35.01).
Wait until the card shows Review the plan to start searching.
Edit the text of Step 1 (placeholder Describe what to search), tap Remove step on a step, and tap Add a step.
Tap Approve plan.
Look that only the edited steps are searched and the card moves on. Compare with Expected.

items.where: Chat screen > Deep research card in the reply, while the run is going
steps: Start a run and approve the plan (S35.01, S35.04).
Watch the phase text under the card, for example Searching the web.
Read the counts line under the title (round, searches, sources) once a search has run.
Read the elapsed time at the top right of the card and check it keeps going.
Compare with Expected.

items.note: The counts line and elapsed time are hidden until there is a count or time above zero.

items.where: Chat screen > Deep research card in the reply > Research plan list (after plan approval)
steps: Start a run and approve the plan (S35.01, S35.04).
Look at the list of plan steps under the card once the editor is closed.
Check each step shows its text and an icon, and the step being searched changes as the run goes.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Managed Cloud account with Deep Research
items.note: Research plan is an accessibility label, not printed text. Status words (Queued, In progress, Done, Failed, Not run) are only spoken, not printed.

items.where: Chat screen > Deep research card or reply > Sources list
steps: Finish a Deep research run that used web sources.
Scroll below the reply to the sources block.
Read the heading with the count, then the numbered source chips with title and URL.
If there are more sources than the chip limit, use the expand control.
Compare the list with Expected.

items.note: The heading text is a template; the number is the count of sources.

items.where: Reports > open a finished report > Sources list at the end of the report
steps: Open Reports from the sidebar (S35.25).
Open a finished report.
Scroll to the end of the report.
Read the Sources list and tap a source chip, then Open page to see its web page.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Managed Cloud account with at least one finished report
items.note: Source chips take a snippet, but the code does not confirm the excerpt shows on screen; no separate collection view was found.

items.needs: a finished report with key findings and plan questions
items.note: Searched research files for findings and question grouping. The report shows one flat Key findings list (ReportsScreen.tsx) and Sections grouped by report headings (ResearchReportSections.tsx); no view grouping findings under each question was found.

items.where: Chat screen > Deep research card in the reply > Pause, then Resume
steps: Start a run and wait until it shows Searching the web (S35.01, S35.04).
Tap Pause; the button changes to Pausing.
Look for Research paused and the text Paused. Resume to continue from where it stopped.
Tap Resume.
Check the phase returns to searching and the counts continue from where they stopped. Compare with Expected.

steps: Start a run and wait until it is searching (S35.01, S35.04).
Tap Stop.
Look for the phase Research stopped and the text Stopped before it finished.

items.where: Reports > open a report from a run that was stopped or failed
steps: Stop a run (S35.18), or use one that failed.
Open Reports from the sidebar.
Find that run in the list and check its row for a small badge with a warning icon and a status word.
Open it and read the error box if one is shown.
Compare with Expected, which asks that a partial report is labelled as partial.

items.note: The report list shows the raw status word, and the reader does not print the word partial. The chat shows Sources so far for partial sources. Whether a partial report is produced depends on the server, not checked.

items.where: Sidebar > Reports > tap a report row
steps: Open the sidebar and tap Reports (it is in the folded group of the sidebar).
Tap a report row.
Check the title at the top of the reader, the summary, the Key findings list, the Sections box and the body text.
Scroll to the bottom and check the Sources list.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Managed Cloud account with at least one finished report
items.note: The sidebar route to the drawer group was read from DrawerContent.tsx, not run on a device.

items.where: Reports > open a report > Sections box (shown when the report has three or more headings)
steps: Open Reports and open a report with three or more headings.
Find the Sections box above the report body.
Tap a section name to jump to its heading.
Check the reader scrolls to that section. Compare with Expected.
In a chat reply, tap Show report sections to expand the outline.
items.needs: a Managed Cloud account with a report that has three or more headings
items.note: The outline in the reader shows only at three or more headings.

items.where: Reports > open a report > tap a source chip under Sources, then Open page
steps: Open a report that has sources.
Tap a source chip in the Sources list at the end of the report.
Look for the action sheet with Open page and tap it.
Check the source web page opens. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Managed Cloud account with a report that has citations
items.note: Tapping a number inside the body text was not confirmed in the code; the source chips are the confirmed path.

items.where: Reports > open a report (tables and charts appear in the body)
steps: Open a report whose body has a table.
Scroll the table sideways if it is wider than the screen.
Look for a chart drawn in the body of a report that has a chart block.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a report that contains a table or a chart; the code does not say which reports do
items.note: Charts are drawn from mermaid fenced blocks (ReportChart); no visible title for a chart was found.

items.where: Sidebar > Reports
steps: Open the sidebar and tap Reports.
If the list is empty, check for No reports yet and the line about turning on Research.
If there are reports, check each row shows a date, a source count and a model name.
Tap a row to reopen it, then go back.
Scroll to the bottom to load older reports. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Managed Cloud account; an empty list or one with past reports
items.note: The empty-state text says Turn on Research in the composer, but the toggle is labelled Deep research (AddToChatSheet.tsx).

items.where: Chat screen > Deep research card in a finished run > Run again
steps: Open a chat with a finished Deep research run (card shows Research complete).
Tap Run again.
Look for the card to start again with a new phase such as Planning research or Searching the web.
Compare the new results with the old ones. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Managed Cloud account with a finished research run
items.note: Pull to refresh on the Reports list only reloads the list; it does not rerun research.

items.where: Settings > Notifications > Research complete
steps: Open Settings and tap Notifications.
Find the Research complete row; its description reads When a research report is ready.
Turn it on, then start a Deep research run and leave the app.
Wait for the run to finish and check for a push notification or an in-app notice.
Compare with Expected, which also covers a failed run.
items.needs: a phone with notifications allowed for the app and a Deep Research run
items.note: The row shows only when the research feature flag is on and the server announces the group. The settings text mentions only ready reports, not failures; push taps open Reports (productLinks.ts).

items.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that needs current web facts > read the answer > find the small teal bracket markers such as [1] placed after claims > tap one
steps: Sign in and start a new chat on the first screen.
Ask a question that needs current web information, such as recent news on a topic.
Wait for the answer to finish streaming.
Look for teal bracket markers like [1] or [2] inside the answer text.
Tap a marker: a dialog opens with the source title, publisher and buttons Cancel and Open page.
Compare with Expected: each marker should point to the source for the claim next to it.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with web search available for the chat
items.note: The marker is drawn in MarkdownInline.tsx (CitationMarker), not MessageBubble.tsx:1972 as the plan says; whether the model writes a marker is up to the answer, and I did not confirm the on-screen control that turns web search on.

items.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > read the rows in the sheet
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Under the answer, tap the pill whose text is Sources.
In the sheet titled Sources, read the bold line of each row.
Compare with Expected: each cited source should show its title.
items.needs: a chat answer that used web search, so the answer has cited sources
items.note: The sheet shows the title on each row; the Sources pill is hidden for research reports, which use a separate list instead.

items.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > read the small grey first line of each row
steps: Open a web-search answer and tap the Sources pill under it.
Look at the small grey first line of each row.
Compare with Expected: each row should show the site domain, for example the publisher name, before the title.
items.needs: a chat answer that used web search
items.note: The publisher is shown as a domain taken from the URL, not a publisher name, unless the source supplies one.

items.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > tap a source row
steps: Open the Sources sheet under a web-search answer.
Tap a source row that has a web address.
Watch for the in-app browser to open the source page.
Compare with Expected: the source opens. A row with no valid web address is not tappable.
items.needs: a chat answer that used web search and a network connection
items.note: The web address itself is not printed on screen; the row only shows an accessibility hint, Opens in the in-app browser. Tapping a marker also offers Open page.

items.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > read the grey first line of a row, or tap a bracket marker and read the dialog
steps: Open the Sources sheet under a web-search answer.
Read the grey first line of a row: it shows the publisher then a date after a dot.
Tap a bracket marker in the answer and read the dialog body for a line that starts with Published.
Compare with Expected: the date shows when the source has one, and no date is shown when it is unknown.
items.needs: a chat answer that used web search, where the source reports a publication date
items.note: If the source has no date, no date appears; this is the expected behaviour in code.

items.where: Tap a bracket marker in a web-search answer and read the dialog for a line starting with Retrieved; or open the side drawer > Reports > open a saved report > scroll to the bottom
steps: In a chat answer with web search, tap a bracket marker such as [1].
Read the dialog body for a line that starts with Retrieved followed by a date.
Optionally open the side drawer, tap Reports, open a saved report, and scroll to the end.
Compare with Expected: the report shows the line Sources retrieved with a date.
items.needs: a chat answer with a source that has a retrieval time; for the report path, a saved research report
items.note: The retrieval date is shown once for the whole report, not per source, and the chat Sources sheet does not show it; how the side drawer is opened was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > look at the mark at the left of each row
steps: Open the Sources sheet under a web-search answer.
Look at the square mark at the left of each row: it holds the first letter of the site and has a Globe icon beside the domain in the search result cards.
Open a chat that cites a project file, if you have one, and look for the file icon on its citation chip.
Compare with Expected: web sources, file sources and chat sources should each show an icon for their type.
items.needs: a chat answer that used web search; for the file icon, a project with a file that a chat cites
items.note: Web sources do not get a type icon: the square mark shows a letter for the site, and the Globe icon shows only in the search result cards. File and past-chat citations have their own chips with icons; I did not confirm a path to open a project chat.

items.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > read the grey text under a row title, or tap a bracket marker and read the dialog body
steps: Open the Sources sheet under a web-search answer.
Read the smaller text under each row title, which is up to three lines.
Tap a bracket marker and read the body text of the dialog.
Compare with Expected: the excerpt shown should be the text that supports the claim.
items.needs: a chat answer that used web search and whose sources include snippets
items.note: The app shows the source snippet; it does not check that the snippet is the sentence that supports the claim, so the tester should judge that.

items.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > read the answer and compare each bracket marker with the sentence before it
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Find a sentence with a teal bracket marker such as [1] right after it.
Tap the marker: the dialog names the source for that marker.
If a marker has several numbers, tap it and pick one entry from the list, which has the button Dismiss sources.
Compare with Expected: each marker should sit at the claim that its source supports.
items.needs: a chat answer that used web search with several sources
items.note: Where a marker lands depends on the model's text; the code only moves markers next to their links, so placement is judged by the tester.

items.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > look at a source row that has no web address
steps: Open the Sources sheet under a web-search answer.
Look for a row without an external-link arrow at its right; such a row cannot be tapped.
Tap a bracket marker whose source cannot open; if the open fails, a dialog titled Could not open citation appears.
Compare with Expected: the product should say the source cannot be opened, not show a dead link.
items.needs: a chat answer with a source that has no valid web address, which is rare, so the tester may not find one
items.note: On mobile there is no text saying a source was not captured; an uncaptured source row is only greyed out and not tappable. The uncaptured-source notice exists only on web in apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchReportView.tsx, using the key counts.uncapturedSources, which mobile does not use.

items.where: Side menu > Projects (the list opens on the Projects screen, titled "Projects")
steps: Sign in and open the side menu.
Tap "Projects" in the menu.
Look for the "Projects" title and a list of your projects, each opening with a tap.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The app calls notebooks "Projects"; a notebook's own screen is titled "Notebook". The list is cloud-synced only in Cloud mode.

items.where: Side menu > Projects > "New project" (floating button); when the list is empty, "Create Project"
steps: Open Projects from the side menu.
Tap "New project" at the bottom, or "Create Project" if no projects exist.
Type a name in "Project name" and tap "Create project".
Look for the new project in the list, then close and reopen the app to confirm it is still there.
items.needs: a signed-in account (Cloud mode to check the account save)
items.note: Local projects are saved on the device, not the account; the account save applies to Cloud projects.

items.where: Side menu > Projects > open a project > the "..." button at the top right > "Edit project"
steps: Open a project of your own from the Projects list.
Tap the "..." button at the top right of the project screen (it has no visible text), then tap "Edit project".
Look for the "Edit Project" sheet with "Project name" and "Description" fields.
Change the Description, tap "Save project", then open "Edit project" again to check the new text.
items.needs: a project you own
items.note: The "..." button's visible text was not found in the code; "Edit project" is also reached by long-pressing a project card in the list.

items.where: Open a chat that belongs to a project > folder icon at the top of the chat (opens a sheet titled "<project name> sources")
steps: Open a chat that belongs to a project.
Tap the folder icon in the chat header (accessibility label "Open project sources").
Look for the sheet titled "<project name> sources" with the list of files, or "No sources added yet" if empty.
items.needs: a project with sources and a chat assigned to that project

labels.text: The files this project’s chats can read.

items.note: The source list opens as a full sheet over the chat, not as a rail beside it; the folder icon does not appear for chats without a project.

items.where: Side menu > Projects > open a project > "Sources" tab > "Add sources"
steps: Open a project and tap the "Sources" tab.
Tap "Add sources" and choose a file in the system picker (for example a PDF).
Watch the row for "Indexing" change to a final status.
Look for the file name in the list, and check that a chat in this project can use it.
items.needs: a file to upload (PDF) and a signed-in account
items.note: The mobile picker accepts image and attachment types from a shared list; PDF is not named by itself in the mobile code, so confirm it appears in the picker. Indexing happens on the server, which was not checked here.

items.where: Side menu > Projects > open a project > "Chats" tab > "New chat in project", then ask a question about a file in "Sources"
steps: Open a project that has a source file added under "Sources".
Tap the "Chats" tab, then start a chat in the project.
Ask a question that only the source file can answer.
Compare the answer with the file's content: it should use the source.
items.needs: a file to upload, and Local mode (the code adds source text to the chat only when the execution mode is local)
items.note: In the chat store, source text is added only when the execution mode is local (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts around line 2757); no cloud-mode path for sources was found in this file.

items.where: Side menu > Projects > open a project > "Instructions" row > type text > "Save instructions"
steps: Open a project and tap the Instructions row (accessibility label "Instructions"), or tap "Add instructions".
Type an instruction such as a reply style, then tap "Save instructions".
Start a new chat in the same project and ask a question.
Check the reply follows the instruction.
items.needs: a project you own; Local mode for the chat to apply the text (see note)
items.note: The chat store adds project instructions only when the execution mode is local (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts around line 2772); the Instructions row's visible text was not confirmed.

items.where: Chats tab (main chat screen) > "No project" pill above the message box > pick a project in the "Projects" sheet
steps: On the main chat screen, tap the "No project" pill.
In the sheet titled "Projects", tap a project name.
Look for the pill to change to that project's name.
Send a question and check the reply uses that project's sources or instructions.
items.needs: a project with sources or instructions, and Local mode for the context to apply

labels.text: Choose the project context for this chat.

items.note: The selector hides when there are no projects; the context is applied only in local mode per the chat store code.

items.where: Seen only as the same project list and sources in another app signed into the same account (none is shown in the mobile app itself)
items.needs: a second app signed into the same account (for example web or desktop)
items.note: Known unfinished and flag-off per the audit; no feature flag was found in the mobile project files, and the mobile app keeps local projects on the device ("Local project. Details, chats, and sources stay on this device." in apps/mobile/app/(app)/projects/[id].tsx).

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the switch labelled Memory at the top
steps: From the chat screen, tap Open menu, then tap Settings.
Under Assistant, tap Memory.
Look under MEMORY CONTROLS for the switch labelled Memory and turn it off.
Read the line Memory is off, so new memories can't be added or imported. and the Turn on button that appears.
Start a new chat and ask about a fact you saved earlier; the assistant should not use it while Memory is off.
Turn Memory back on and check the saved facts are used again.
items.needs: a saved memory first (see S39.10) to check the effect
items.note: The Memory screen is also reached from Profile > Local settings > Memory in Local mode. The exact place of the Open menu button on the chat tab was not confirmed in code.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the switch labelled Search and reference chats
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Turn off the switch labelled Search and reference chats.
Start a new chat and ask about something that was only in an older chat.
Check the assistant does not bring in excerpts from other past chats.
Turn the switch on and ask the same question again to compare.
items.needs: one older chat with a distinct topic
items.note: Code default is on for Local and off for Cloud (localSettingsStore and cloudSettingsStore).

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory (the list below the controls)
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Scroll down past the switches and the rows Memory summary and Replaced memories.
Read the count line under those rows, for example a number.
Scroll the list and check each saved memory appears as a card.
items.needs: a few saved memories (add them with S39.10 first); with none, the screen shows No memories yet
items.note: Local mode also opens this screen from Profile > Local settings > Memory.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the field Search memories...
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Tap the field with the placeholder Search memories....
Type one word that appears in a saved memory.
Check the list shows only matching memories.
Tap the clear control on the field, then tap the chip Pinned to filter to pinned memories.
items.needs: two or more saved memories with different words

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, with the chip All selected and the search field empty
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Make sure the chip All is selected and the search field is empty.
Look for section headings between the memory cards.
Compare the headings with the Expected topics.
items.needs: saved memories of several kinds (for example facts, preferences and decisions learned from chats)
items.note: Headings appear only when there are at least two topic groups. The code has no work or background topic: the groups are Preferences, About you, Decisions, Context, Summaries and Skills.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Reflect (Cloud mode only), then the section Work in progress
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud and switch to Cloud mode.
Open Settings and find the section Cloud.
Tap Reflect.
Look for the heading Work in progress and read the ongoing projects listed under it.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with some Cloud chats
items.note: The Work in progress section appears only when the recap has ongoing work.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the round + button Add memory at the bottom right
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory. Memory must be on.
Tap the round button labelled Add memory at the bottom right.
Type a fact in the field What should AGI remember? for example I prefer metric units.
Tap Save.
Check the new card appears in the list with the line Added by you.
Start a new chat and ask a question the fact would answer, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: Memory turned on

items.where: Chat tab: type Remember that ... in the message box and send
steps: Make sure Memory is on (Settings > Assistant > Memory).
Open the chat tab and type Remember that I like short answers.
Send the message.
Look for the status line Saved to memory: followed by the fact.
Open Settings > Assistant > Memory and check the fact is in the list.
items.needs: Memory turned on
items.note: A repeated fact shows an already-known message instead.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the switch labelled Generate memory from chat history
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Turn on Memory and turn on the switch Generate memory from chat history.
In a normal chat (not temporary) say a lasting fact, for example I work as a nurse in Leeds.
Wait for the reply to finish, then go back to Settings > Assistant > Memory.
Check a new card appears with the line Learned from a chat, or Learned from the chat title.
items.needs: Memory and the generate switch on; a normal chat
items.note: The client-side capture in the code runs only in Local mode and is off for temporary chats.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the pencil button Edit memory on a card
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Tap the pencil button labelled Edit memory on a card.
Change the text in the field labelled Memory content.
Tap Update.
Check the card shows the new text and the line Edited, then ask a chat question that uses it.
items.needs: a saved memory
items.note: A card edited within 60 seconds of being added still says Added.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, swipe a card to the left and tap the red trash button
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Swipe a memory card to the left to show the red trash button labelled Delete memory.
Tap it and read the alert Delete memory?
Tap Delete.
Check the card is gone and the count has gone down by one.
items.needs: a saved memory

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the red row Reset memory
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Tap the red row Reset memory.
Read the alert Reset memory? and tap Cancel first; check nothing was removed.
Tap Reset memory again in the alert.
Check the list says No memories yet and the count is zero.
items.needs: some saved memories
items.note: Reset also deletes chats? No: the alert says your chats are not deleted.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the pin button Pin memory on a card
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Tap the pin button labelled Pin memory on a card.
Check the card shows the badge Pinned.
Tap the chip Pinned to see only pinned memories.
Compare with Expected: pinned memories are kept at the top and win a conflict.
items.needs: two or more saved memories

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, read the small line under each memory card
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Add a memory yourself (S39.10) and read the line under it: Added by you.
Import memories (S39.21) and check the line says Imported.
Find a card learned from a chat and check it says Learned from followed by the chat title.
items.needs: a memory added by hand, an import, and a chat-learned memory
items.note: The chat-learned line uses the chat title when the chat is known.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, read the time line on each memory card
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory.
Add a memory (S39.10) and read the time line, which starts with Added.
Wait a minute, then edit the memory (S39.13).
Check the line now starts with Edited and shows a time such as 2m ago.
items.needs: a memory you can add and edit

items.where: Effect is seen in Settings > Assistant > Memory > Replaced memories
steps: Add a memory such as I live in Paris (S39.10).
In a chat, say a newer fact on the same topic, for example I now live in London.
Open Settings > Assistant > Memory and check the Paris memory is no longer in the main list.
Open Replaced memories and check the Paris memory is listed there.
Start a chat and ask where you live; the answer should use London.
items.needs: Memory on; a Free or paid account is not needed
items.note: The rule runs automatically on the same topic; the code does not show a control for it.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory > Replaced memories
steps: Create two memories on the same topic (see S39.19).
Open Settings > Assistant > Memory > Replaced memories.
Read the heading When memories disagree and the rule text.
Tap Use the replaced one instead on the entry to settle it.
Check the list now uses the replaced memory and a chat answer follows it.
items.needs: two conflicting memories

labels.text: Pinned, added, then newer memories win. The replaced one is kept here.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the upload button labelled Import memories at the top right
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory. Memory must be on.
Tap the upload button Import memories at the top right.
Pick a source under From (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or Other).
Paste lines into the box or tap Choose a text or JSON file, then tap Preview.
Select the items, tap the import button, and check the message Added N memories.
items.needs: a text or JSON file, or some pasted lines

labels.text: Choose a text or JSON file

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Data Controls > Local data > Export Local Data
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Data Controls.
Under Local data, tap Export Local Data.
Wait for the progress to finish and choose a place in the share sheet.
Open the saved file agi_data_export.json and find the memory_facts list.
Compare the saved memories with the list in Settings > Assistant > Memory.
items.needs: some saved memories; a way to open a .json file

labels.text: Chats, memory, settings and model details, exported on this device.

items.note: The file is JSON, not plain text. Cloud memory is exported with Export Cloud data in the AGI Cloud account section.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, read the scope line under the count
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud with a workspace and switch to Cloud mode.
Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory; the title says Cloud Memory.
Read the scope line under the count: Personal memories. Workspace memories stay in their workspace., or the workspace name line.
Start a personal chat and ask about a workspace memory; it should not appear.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account in a workspace, with a workspace memory and a personal chat

labels.text: Personal memories. Workspace memories stay in their workspace.

items.note: In Local mode the scope line reads Stored on this device only.

items.where: Chat tab: the eye-off button for temporary chat; or Settings > Device > General > Temporary Chat
steps: Open the chat tab and tap the eye-off temporary chat control, or turn on the switch Temporary Chat in Settings > Device > General.
Read the explainer text about temporary chats.
Send Remember that I like tea and ask a question about a saved memory.
Go to Settings > Assistant > Memory and check the new fact was not saved.
Start a normal chat and check the temporary chat content is not used as past-chat context.
items.needs: Memory on, with one saved memory

labels.text: Won't be saved or use memory, and attachments never leave this device.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then the switch Include sensitive topics in memory; in Cloud mode also Never remember
steps: Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Memory. Memory must be on for the switch to work.
Read the switch Include sensitive topics in memory and leave it off to stop sensitive topics being learned from chats.
In Cloud mode, tap Never remember, type a term in Term to never remember, and tap Add term.
In the chat tab, send Remember that my password is a fake test value; the reply should say Memory never stores ... so I left that out.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: Memory on; use a fake test value only, never a real credential; Never remember needs Cloud mode
items.note: The Never remember row appears only in Cloud mode; Local mode has no term list in the code.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Data Controls > Local data > Local chats > Delete all local chats (and separately Settings > Assistant > Memory > Reset memory)
steps: Note how many memories are in Settings > Assistant > Memory.
Open Settings, tap Assistant, then tap Data Controls and find Delete all local chats under Local chats.
Read the alert Delete all local chats? (it says memory stays), tap Cancel, then tap the button again and confirm.
Go back to Settings > Assistant > Memory and check the memories are still there.
Tap Reset memory on that screen, confirm, and check the chats in the chat tab are still there.
items.needs: some chats and some memories; this removes data, so use a test account
items.note: Deleting chats does not change memory and resetting memory does not delete chats.

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization (under Assistant) > Nickname
steps: Tap "Open menu" at the top left of a chat.
Tap "Settings" in the side menu.
Under "Assistant", tap "Personalization".
Type a name in "Nickname" (placeholder "What should AGI call you?").
Tap "Save personalization settings" (Save at the top right).
Start a new chat, ask "What is my name?" and check the reply uses that name.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The reply uses the nickname if set, otherwise the full name, per renderPersonalizationBlock in apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/personalization.ts.

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization > More about you
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings".
Under "Assistant", tap "Personalization".
Type interests, values or background into "More about you" (placeholder "Interests, values or background to keep in mind").
Tap "Save personalization settings".
Start a new chat and ask for a suggestion that depends on your background, and check the reply takes it into account.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The field is saved as aboutYou and sent to chat as "More about the user, in their words" in apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/personalization.ts.

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization > Occupation
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings".
Under "Assistant", tap "Personalization".
Type your work into "Occupation" (placeholder "e.g. Founder & Engineer").
Tap "Save personalization settings".
Start a new chat, ask for an example, and check the example fits your work.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The screen field is named Occupation, not role or profession; the saved text is sent to chat as "The user works as" with "Tailor examples accordingly".

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+ button by the message box) > Choose style
steps: Open a chat or start a new one.
Tap the "+" button labelled "Add to chat" next to the message box.
Tap "Choose style".
Tap "Explanatory" (or another option) in the style sheet.
Send a question and check the reply follows that one style.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a chat
items.note: Choosing Normal in the same sheet falls back to the saved style from Personalization.

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization > Response Length
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings".
Under "Assistant", tap "Personalization".
Under "Response Length", tap "Shorter" or "Longer" (or "Default").
Tap "Save personalization settings".
Start a new chat, ask a question, and compare the reply length with the choice.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization > Style Preset > Formal
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings".
Under "Assistant", tap "Personalization".
Under "Style Preset", tap "Formal" (description "Professional, precise language").
Tap "Save personalization settings".
Start a new chat, ask a question, and check the reply uses a more formal register.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The code has no separate formality control; Formal is the Style Preset value. The quoted line in the plan no longer matches, but the chip exists.

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization > Style Preset (or Chat > Add to chat > Choose style)
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings", then "Personalization".
Under "Style Preset", tap one preset: Default, Concise, Explanatory, Learning or Formal.
Tap "Save personalization settings".
Start a new chat, ask a question, and check the reply follows only that preset.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization > Response Style > Warmth
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings", then "Personalization".
Under "Response Style", tap the "Warmth" row.
In the sheet, tap "More" (warmer) or "Less" (cooler), or "Default".
Tap "Save personalization settings".
Start a new chat, ask a question, and compare the warmth of the reply.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The trait is set by Less, Default or More, not a slider.

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization > Response Style > Enthusiasm
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings", then "Personalization".
Under "Response Style", tap the "Enthusiasm" row.
In the sheet, tap "More" or "Less" (or "Default").
Tap "Save personalization settings".
Start a new chat, ask a question, and compare how energetic the reply sounds.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization > Response Style > Headers and lists
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings", then "Personalization".
Under "Response Style", tap the "Headers and lists" row.
In the sheet, tap "More" for headings and lists, or "Less" for prose.
Tap "Save personalization settings".
Start a new chat, ask a question that has several parts, and check whether the reply uses headers and lists.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization > Response Style > Emoji
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings", then "Personalization".
Under "Response Style", tap the "Emoji" row.
In the sheet, tap "Less" (no emoji) or "More".
Tap "Save personalization settings".
Start a new chat, ask a question, and check whether the reply has emoji.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization > Technical Level
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings", then "Personalization".
Under "Technical Level", tap "Beginner", "Intermediate" or "Expert" (or "Not set").
Tap "Save personalization settings".
Start a new chat, ask the same technical question, and compare the depth of the reply.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization > Response Language
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings", then "Personalization".
Under "Response Language", tap a language name, or "Match my message" to keep the default.
Tap "Save personalization settings".
Start a new chat, ask a question, and check the reply is written in the chosen language.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization > Custom Instructions
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings", then "Personalization".
Type standing instructions into "Custom Instructions" (placeholder "e.g. I prefer direct, technical answers...").
Tap "Save personalization settings", then start a new chat and check a reply follows them.
To switch them off, clear the "Custom Instructions" field, tap save, and check the next reply no longer follows them.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: No on/off switch for instructions was found; the only way to turn them off without the text being lost is not provided, so clearing the field deletes the text.

items.where: Open menu > Projects > (a project) > Instructions
steps: Tap "Open menu" and tap "Projects".
Tap a project in the list.
Tap the "Instructions" row.
Type into "Project instructions" and save.
Start a new chat inside that project, ask a question, and check the reply follows the project instructions.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a project
items.note: Project settings also has a switch, "Use your profile and instructions", in apps/mobile/src/features/projects/components/ProjectSettingsScreen.tsx that controls account instructions per project.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Choose style
steps: Open a chat with a saved conversation.
Tap "Add to chat" (+), then "Choose style".
Tap "Concise" and send a question.
Check the reply is short, then open Settings > Personalization and check the saved Style Preset is unchanged.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a chat
items.note: The choice is saved per conversation (chatStyleByConversation in apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatViewStore.ts).

items.where: Open menu > Settings > Personalization > Reset response style
steps: Tap "Open menu", then "Settings", then "Personalization".
Change a few Response Style or Style Preset choices.
Tap "Reset response style".
Check the choices return to Default, then tap "Save personalization settings" to keep them.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Reset covers style, length, technical level, language and the four Response Style levels only; name, occupation and instructions are kept.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Choose style > Explanatory
steps: Open a chat.
Tap "Add to chat" (+), then "Choose style".
Tap "Explanatory" (description "Reasoning and context").
Send a question and check the reply explains reasoning and context.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a chat

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Choose style > Concise
steps: Open a chat.
Tap "Add to chat" (+), then "Choose style".
Tap "Concise" (description "Short, direct answers").
Send a question and check the reply is short and direct.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a chat
items.note: Personalization > Style Preset also offers Concise, described as "Short, to the point" in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/personalization/constants.ts.

items.where: Chat screen (new chat) > top-right "Temporary" control (eye-off icon) > "Turn on temporary chat?" > Turn on
steps: Open the chat screen with no conversation selected.
Tap the eye-off icon at the top right of the header.
Read the alert "Turn on temporary chat?" and tap Turn on.
Look for the "Temporary" label with a purple background in the header; compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: No setting makes new chats temporary by default; temporary is one on/off value, switched from the header control or Settings > Privacy > Chat privacy > Temporary Chat.

items.where: Chat screen > top-right "Temporary" control > Turn on, then open a chat thread: the explainer banner appears under the header
steps: Turn on temporary chat from the header control on the new chat screen.
Send a message, then open that chat so the chat thread screen shows.
Look at the purple strip under the header with the explainer text.
Leave the chat and return to it; check whether the header "Temporary" label stays while the chat is open.
items.needs: none
items.note: The banner is shown only once per app session (hasShownThisSession), not for as long as the chat is open; the persistent indicator is the header "Temporary" label, and the banner is rendered only on the chat thread screen, not the new chat screen.

items.where: Chat screen > top-right "Temporary" control > read the alert text "Turn on temporary chat?"; in a chat thread, tap "Learn more" in the banner
steps: Tap the eye-off control on the new chat screen to open the "Turn on temporary chat?" alert.
Read the explanation text in the alert.
Turn on temporary chat, open a chat thread, and read the banner text.
Tap "Learn more" and check the Privacy screen that opens against the banner text.
items.needs: a Free or paid account; the cloud text appears in Cloud mode, the local text in Local mode

labels.text: Won't appear in history or use memory, and is normally deleted after 30 days.

items.note: Explanation text is fixed copy: cloud says it is normally deleted after 30 days, local says attachments never leave this device; the banner text is the same as the alert text.

items.where: Chat thread with temporary chat on > banner under header > "Personalized" switch (Cloud mode only)
steps: In Cloud mode, turn on temporary chat and open a chat thread so the banner shows.
Look at the line under the explainer: "Personalized" or "Unpersonalized" with a switch.
Switch it, then send a message in the temporary chat.
Compare the reply with Expected: the switch controls profile, instructions and response style, not memory.
items.needs: a signed-in account in Cloud mode; a Free account may not show the switch
items.note: The only temporary-chat choice found is the Personalized switch, which covers profile, instructions and style; memory is excluded in temporary chats by code (chatExecutionStore.ts:2798) with no separate choice, and the banner shows only once per app session.

items.where: Effect seen in Settings > Memory > "Memory summary" (memory count does not grow after a temporary chat)
steps: Open Settings > Memory and note the count shown under the list.
Turn on temporary chat, send a message that states a personal fact, and wait for the reply.
Go back to Settings > Memory and compare the count with the one you noted.
Open "Memory summary" and check that the new fact is not listed.
items.needs: a Free or paid account

items.where: Chat thread with temporary chat on > banner under header > "Personalized" switch (Cloud mode only)
steps: In Cloud mode, turn on temporary chat and open a chat thread.
Set the banner switch to "Unpersonalized".
Ask a question that depends on your saved instructions or profile.
Compare the answer with Expected: it should ignore custom instructions while the switch is off.
items.needs: a signed-in account in Cloud mode and saved custom instructions

labels.text: Personalized uses your profile, instructions and response style. Unpersonalized leaves them out.

items.note: The switch is hidden in Local mode, and the banner shows only once per app session, so reopen the app to see it again.

items.where: Settings > Privacy > Chat privacy (footnote under the retention group); temporary-chat banner in a chat thread
steps: Turn on temporary chat, open a chat thread and read the banner text.
Go to Settings > Privacy > Chat privacy.
Read the footnote under the group with "Shared links" and "Archived chats" (Cloud mode) and "Delete all chats".
Attach a file in a temporary chat and compare what the app says about how long it is kept with Expected.
items.needs: a file to upload; a Free or paid account

labels.text: Deleted and temporary chats are normally deleted for good after 30 days. A workspace legal hold can keep them longer.

items.note: The Local-mode banner says attachments never leave the device, but no file-specific retention text was found for Cloud mode; only the chat 30-day note exists.

items.where: Side menu (drawer) or Settings > top segmented control "Local" / "Cloud" > choose Local
steps: Open the side menu from the top left of the chat screen, or open Settings.
Tap the "Local" segment of the Local / Cloud control.
Start a new chat, send a message, and check that it is kept on this device.
Open Settings > Privacy and read "Local chats stay on this device unless you sync them." and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none for Local mode; a signed-in account to compare with Cloud

labels.text: Local chats stay on this device unless you sync them.

items.note: Whether a Local chat is uploaded to the account can only be confirmed indirectly; no on-screen proof was found.

items.where: Settings > Memory > Local segment (Local / Cloud) > Memory summary, which says "Stored on this device only."
steps: Switch to Local mode with the Local / Cloud control.
Open Settings > Memory.
Read the scope line under the list; expect "Stored on this device only."
Open "Memory summary" and read the info card: "On-device memory".
items.needs: none
items.note: No separate local-only memory switch was found; the device-only scope follows the Local mode toggle.

items.where: Settings > Storage > scroll to "Danger Zone" > "Delete everything"
steps: Open Settings > Storage and scroll to the bottom.
Tap "Delete everything" under "Danger Zone".
Read the alert "Delete all local data?", then tap "Delete Everything" and read the second alert.
Compare the result with Expected: the app should wipe local data, sign out and return to onboarding.
items.needs: a throwaway install or test account; this is destructive
items.note: "Clear cache" only removes temporary files; the full wipe is under Danger Zone.

items.where: Settings > Privacy: "Model training", "Telemetry off by default", "Data retention" card; "Chat privacy" > "Temporary Chat" and "Delete all chats"
steps: Open Settings > Privacy and read the three cards under "Our approach to privacy".
Open Settings > Privacy > Chat privacy and see "Temporary Chat" as its own switch.
Back on Settings > Privacy, scroll to "AGI Cloud privacy controls" in Cloud mode.
Check that training choices ("Use my chats", "Use my voice") are listed apart from history and retention, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account in Cloud mode for the training controls; "Data retention" card only in Cloud mode

items.where: Settings > Privacy: each card under "Our approach to privacy" has its own explanation line; "Chat privacy" > "Temporary Chat" footnote
steps: Open Settings > Privacy and read the body text under "Model training", "Telemetry off by default" and "Data retention".
Open Settings > Privacy > Chat privacy and read the footnote under "Temporary Chat".
Turn on temporary chat, open a chat thread and read the "Personalized" hint.
Compare each explanation with what the switch or setting does, against Expected.
items.needs: none for the Privacy cards; a signed-in Cloud account for the personalization switch

labels.text: Personalized uses your profile, instructions and response style. Unpersonalized leaves them out.

items.note: Explanations are fixed text per row; the explainer for a switch shows as a hint, not as a visible line, in the banner.

items.where: Settings > Privacy > "Data use & access" > scroll to "Where each feature processes your data"
steps: Open Settings > Privacy and tap "Data use & access".
Scroll to "Where each feature processes your data".
Read each feature row, starting with "Chat in Local Mode" and "Chat in AGI Cloud".
Compare the listed place (on this device, AGI Cloud, or the named provider) with Expected.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Where each feature processes your data

items.note: Rows marked iOS-only appear only on iPhone, so a Mac-simulated test may show fewer rows.

items.where: Side menu > Settings > Notifications > Daily brief (turn the switch on)
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud, then open the side menu and tap Settings.
Tap Notifications.
Turn on the Daily brief switch. Wait for the row 'Daily brief time, 08:00' to appear.
Open Schedules from the side menu and look for a schedule named Daily brief, which the app should have created. Compare with Expected: a recurring daily briefing is set up.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account, on a plan that allows scheduled tasks.
items.note: A second route is Schedules > Try a template > 'Daily briefing' (the template from packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts), which then needs Create Schedule. The delivery itself runs on the server and is not visible in the code, so the tester must wait for a run.

items.where: Side menu > Schedules > Create Schedule (form) > Preferred time and Time zone
steps: Open the side menu and tap Schedules, then tap Create schedule.
Set Recurrence to Daily and tap the Preferred time field to pick a time.
Scroll to the Time zone field and tap it. Pick a different zone from the list.
Tap Create Schedule and open the new schedule. Compare with Expected: the time and time zone you chose are shown.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account, on a plan that allows scheduled tasks.
items.note: The Daily brief time in Settings > Notifications offers only 07:00, 08:00 and 09:00 and uses the device time zone, with no time zone control. The zone can be set only on a schedule form.

items.where: Side menu > Schedules > (a schedule card) > switch on the card, or More actions > Pause / Resume
steps: Open the side menu and tap Schedules. Make sure at least one schedule exists, such as Daily brief.
Tap the switch on a schedule card to turn it off, or tap its More actions button and choose Pause.
Look at the card: it should show as paused, and the Paused filter should list it.
Tap the switch again, or choose Resume from More actions. Compare with Expected: the schedule pauses and resumes.
items.needs: A schedule already set up (for example Daily brief) on a signed-in AGI Cloud account.
items.note: A schedule paused for approval cannot be resumed from the card. The card says 'Paused for your approval, so approve or deny it in History.' instead.

items.where: Side menu > Settings > Time and focus > Quiet hours > Enable quiet hours
steps: Open Settings, tap Time and focus.
Turn on Enable quiet hours, then set the Days, Start time and End time so the current time falls inside the window.
Return to the app or switch away and back during that window.
Look for the alert 'Quiet hours are active' with the text 'This is a reminder, not a lock.' Compare with Expected: quiet hours are active on the device.
items.needs: None for the setting. Holding push notifications needs a second device or push delivery, which the tester cannot see from the app.
items.note: The holding of push notifications and nudges happens on the server (apps/web/lib/services/quiet-hours-service.ts). The app shows no visible sign of the hold, so only the setting and the on-screen alert can be checked from the UI.

items.where: Side menu > Settings > Notifications > Scheduled tasks (and Task and approval updates)
steps: Open Settings, tap Notifications. Turn on notifications if it asks.
Find the row Scheduled tasks, described as 'When a scheduled task runs, finishes or needs you', and set it on.
On a schedule card, tap More actions and choose Run now, then wait for the run to finish.
Look for a phone notification when the run completes. Compare with Expected: the user is notified when background work completes.
items.needs: A phone that allows notifications for the app, and a schedule to run (or an agent task).
items.note: Agent-task completion falls under Task and approval updates, which says 'finished or failed tasks'.

items.where: Side menu > Settings > Reflect (shows the page titled Reflect, with range choices 30 days, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year)
steps: Open Settings and tap Reflect. Sign in if asked.
Wait for 'Building your recap…' to finish.
Read the headline, the period label and the stats (Conversations, Active days, Most active day, Peak start time).
Compare with Expected: a reflection on how the user uses the product is shown.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account. Reflect may ask for memory to be on (ReflectMemoryRequiredError).
items.note: Reflect needs a signed-in cloud account and may show a memory-required message; the exact wording was not checked.

items.where: Side menu > Settings > Reflect > 1 year
steps: Open Settings and tap Reflect.
Tap the range choice 1 year (accessibility label 'Show the past 1 year').
Wait for the recap to load and read its period label, headline and stats.
Compare with Expected: a recap of the past year is shown.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account with enough chat history for the past year.
items.note: No screen or label named 'Annual recap' exists. The past-year recap is the 1 year range on Reflect, and the 365-day option is labelled '1 year'.

items.where: Side menu > Settings > Time and focus > Break reminders
steps: Open Settings, tap Time and focus, then tap the Break reminders row.
Choose a time, such as 30 minutes, from the menu. The row then reads 'After 30 min'.
Keep using the app until about that much time has passed in one day.
Look for the alert 'Time for a break?' with 'You have spent about 30 minutes in AGI today.' Compare with Expected.
items.needs: None. Use the app for the full chosen time, or pick 30 minutes to shorten the test.
items.note: The reminder counts active app time. The menu choices are Off, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours and 4 hours.

items.where: Side menu > Settings > Time and focus
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings, then tap Time and focus.
Look for the section Break reminders with its row, and the section Quiet hours with Enable quiet hours.
Change one value, go back, and open the page again.
Compare with Expected: the page holds break reminders and quiet hours, and the change is kept.
items.needs: None.
items.note: The same page can also be reached from Settings > Notifications > Quiet hours (the row reads 'Quiet hours. On' or 'Off').

items.where: Side menu > Schedules > Scheduled runs (header button); or on a schedule card, More actions > Show history
steps: Open the side menu and tap Schedules.
Tap the Scheduled runs button in the header.
Scroll the list of past runs. Compare with Expected: past outputs are kept as a browsable history.
Go back, tap More actions on a schedule card and choose Show history. Look for the heading Run History with the last runs.
items.needs: A schedule that has already run at least once (use Run now on a schedule card).
items.note: No label named 'saved editions' was found. The run list is the closest match, and the tester should check that past outputs can be opened.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Photos
steps: Sign in and make sure the mode control shows Cloud selected.
Tap Add to chat (the + button beside the message box).
Tap Photos and pick one photo.
Tap Message input, type 'What is in this photo?' and tap Send message.
Check that the reply describes the photo, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a photo file
items.note: In Local mode the app only reads text from the photo on the device (chatExecutionStore: 'cannot inspect the image pixels directly'), so test in Cloud. The owner's live check of the upload scanner (UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL) is still pending.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Photos
steps: Tap Add to chat, then Photos.
Select two photos in the picker (it allows several, in order).
Type 'Compare these two images: what is different?' in Message input and tap Send message.
Check that the reply compares both photos, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account, two photo files
items.note: The number of photos allowed per message depends on the plan (photoSelectionLimitForPlan); the 'up to 4 photos' cap in the sheet applies to image creation, not chat. Owner's live check of the upload scanner is still pending.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Paste image (or Photos for a saved screenshot)
steps: Take a screenshot on the device and copy it to the clipboard.
Tap Add to chat, then Paste image (this row only shows when the clipboard holds an image).
Type 'What does this screenshot show?' in Message input and tap Send message.
Check that the reply explains the screenshot, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a screenshot
items.note: 'Paste image' is hidden unless the clipboard has an image. Captured screenshots can also be attached with Photos.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > File (Cloud mode only) or Photos
steps: Make sure Cloud is selected, then tap Add to chat and tap File.
Pick a scanned PDF or a photo of a document.
Type 'Read this document and explain it' in Message input and tap Send message.
Check that the reply reads and explains the document, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a scanned PDF or a document photo
items.note: The File row appears only when the app is in Cloud mode. The PDF is recognised by mime type in AttachmentPreview.tsx; I did not confirm the file picker's accepted types.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Photos
steps: Tap Add to chat, then Photos, and pick a chart image.
Type 'What trends does this chart show? Give the main values.' in Message input and tap Send message.
Check that the reply names the data and the trend, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a chart image file
