items.note: No chart-specific control exists; this is a normal photo attachment. Owner's live check of the upload scanner is still pending.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Photos
steps: Tap Add to chat, then Photos, and pick a diagram image.
Type 'Explain the structure of this diagram.' in Message input and tap Send message.
Check that the reply describes the parts and how they connect, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a diagram image file
items.note: No diagram-specific control exists; this is a normal photo attachment. Owner's live check of the upload scanner is still pending.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Photos
steps: Tap Add to chat, then Photos, and pick a photo of handwritten notes.
Type 'Transcribe these notes.' in Message input and tap Send message.
Check that the reply gives the handwritten text, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a photo of handwriting
items.note: No handwriting-specific control exists. On-device (Local) mode reads only printed text, so use Cloud. Owner's live check is still pending.

items.where: Siri or Shortcuts (iPhone): Scan with AGI; then the Scan Text screen > Copy text
steps: On an iPhone, run the Shortcuts action or Siri phrase Scan with AGI.
On Scan Text, take a photo of a page with printed text.
Tap Copy text and check that the pill changes to Copied.
Paste into a note and check that the text matches Expected.
items.needs: an iPhone with AGI installed, a page with printed text
items.note: No in-app button opens the Scan Text screen; the route is reached only from the scan intent (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx). The drawer has a scan entry hidden as FULL_SCREEN. The Copy text pill shows only when text was found. The mobile chat also reads text from attached images on-device in Local mode.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Photos
steps: Tap Add to chat, then Photos, and pick an image with several of the same object (for example apples).
Type 'How many apples are in this picture?' in Message input and tap Send message.
Check that the reply gives a count, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account, an image with several countable objects
items.note: No counting control exists; the count depends on the model's answer. Owner's live check of the upload scanner is still pending.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Photos
steps: Tap Add to chat, then Photos, and select two different scene photos (selection keeps the order you tap).
Type 'Describe the differences between the first and second photo.' in Message input and tap Send message.
Check that the reply names the differences between the two scenes, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account, two scene photos
items.note: No scene-comparison control exists; this is the same as S43.02 with a comparison prompt. Owner's live check of the upload scanner is still pending.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Camera (or Photos)
steps: Tap Add to chat, then Camera, and take a photo of the device or error screen (or choose one with Photos).
Type 'My router shows this light. What should I check?' in Message input and tap Send message.
Check that the reply gives troubleshooting steps, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a device or error to photograph
items.note: The Camera row appears only when the camera capability is allowed. No troubleshooting-specific control exists. Owner's live check of the upload scanner is still pending.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Create image > Attach from Library (or Photos); or open a generated image > Change this image
steps: Tap Add to chat, then Create image (the chat switches to image generation).
Tap Attach from Library or Photos and pick an image; up to 4 photos can be attached, and the first is edited.
Type 'Make the sky sunset orange' in Message input and tap Send message.
Check that the new image is based on the chosen reference, as Expected says.
Optional: tap a generated image in the chat, tap Change this image, type in Describe the change, then tap Change the image.
items.needs: a signed-in account, an image to use as reference, an image-capable model
items.note: 'Change this image' shows only in Cloud mode for signed-in users on a model that edits images. The reference logic is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/actions/resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts (resolveReferenceImage); the quoted line from the audit is gone, but the feature is still there. I did not check how tapping a generated image opens it full screen.

items.where: Chat > Add to chat (+) > Create image, then type a prompt and send. Or Drawer > Images > Describe an image, then Create image.
steps: Sign in and open a chat in Cloud mode (image creation must be available on the account).
Tap the + button labelled Add to chat, then tap Create image.
Type a prompt in the message box and send.
Wait for the card Generating Image to finish, then check that a generated image appears in the conversation and matches Expected.
items.needs: A signed-in Cloud account with image access (a paid plan or free daily image quota)
items.note: Images screen is reached from the drawer label Images (src/features/drawer/components/DrawerContent.tsx).

items.where: Chat > Add to chat (+) > Create image > Image model
steps: Open a chat in Cloud mode and tap the + button labelled Add to chat.
Tap Create image.
Under the heading Image model, look at the list of models and tap a different model.
Check that the tapped row is now marked selected, then send a prompt.
Open the generated image and read the caption Generated with <model name> to compare with the model you picked.
items.needs: A Cloud account with image access and at least two image models offered
items.note: The model list comes from the shared catalog for the active kind; the Images screen itself has no model picker.

items.where: Drawer > Images > Attach photos (paperclip). Or Chat > Add to chat (+) > Create image > Photos.
steps: Open Images from the drawer, or open a chat, tap the + button, then tap Create image.
On Images, tap the button labelled Attach photos and choose a photo.
In the chat sheet, tap Photos and choose up to 4 photos (shown in the hint text under Image model).
Check that the chosen photos appear as attachments above the prompt box.
Send the prompt and check that the first photo is edited and the others guide the result.
items.needs: A photo to upload; a model that accepts reference photos (the chat sheet shows a note when it does not)

labels.text: Attach up to 4 photos. The first is edited; the rest guide it.

items.note: The attachment slots are shown as a strip on the Images screen (testID images.references); the visible word for each slot is not written as a label.

items.where: Chat > Add to chat (+) > Create image > Aspect ratio
steps: Open a chat in Cloud mode, tap the + button, then tap Create image.
Under the heading Aspect ratio, tap a different ratio.
Check that the tapped row is marked selected.
Send a prompt and open the generated image.
Compare the image shape with the ratio you picked.
items.needs: A Cloud account with image access; a model that offers more than one ratio (the section is hidden otherwise)
items.note: The option labels come from getImageAspectOptionsForModel; the tester sees whatever ratio names that returns.

items.where: Chat > Add to chat (+) > Create image > Transparent background
steps: Open a chat in Cloud mode, tap the + button, then tap Create image.
Pick an image model that accepts reference photos (the row only appears for those models).
Tap Transparent background so the row is marked selected.
Send a prompt and open the generated image.
Check that the background is removed (transparent) in the result.
items.needs: A Cloud account with image access and an editing-capable image model
items.note: The hint under the row reads Return the image without a background; the row is hidden for text-only models.

items.where: Chat > send an image prompt > tap Stop generating on the image card
steps: Send an image prompt in Cloud mode.
While the card shows Generating Image, tap the button labelled Stop generating.
Check that the card stops progressing and no image is added to the conversation.
Check whether a charge or credit use appears afterwards (not verifiable from the code).
items.needs: A Cloud account with image access; a fast enough moment to tap before the image finishes
items.note: The code only sends a stop request from the card; whether the job is cancelled and not billed is not shown on screen.

items.where: Chat > failed image card > Retry
steps: Make an image generation fail, or use one that shows Image Generation Failed.
Tap the button labelled Retry on the card.
Check that a new generation starts with the same prompt in the same place in the chat.
items.needs: A Cloud account with image access and a way to produce a failed generation
items.note: A stopped generation may not reach the failed state that shows Retry; the code does not confirm that. Long-press message actions also have Retry (src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx).

items.where: Drawer > Library > Images
steps: Open the drawer and tap Library.
Tap the filter chip labelled Images.
Look for the images in a grid of tiles.
Tap a tile to open it, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: At least one image created earlier on the account
items.note: The Images screen (Drawer > Images) also has a grid titled Your images.

items.where: Chat > tap a generated image. Or Drawer > Library > Images > tap a tile.
steps: Tap a generated image in a chat, or an image tile in Library.
Check that it opens full screen on a black background.
Use the zoom controls (Zoom in, Zoom out) or pinch to zoom.
Tap Close in the top bar to return.
items.needs: A generated image

items.where: Chat > tap a generated image > read the text under the picture
steps: Tap a generated image in a chat to open the full-screen viewer.
Read the prompt text shown under the image.
Read the caption that starts with Generated with, which shows the model name and the aspect ratio.
Compare with Expected: check whether quality and size are shown.
items.needs: A generated image made with a prompt
items.note: The caption shows only the model and aspect ratio. Quality and size are not written anywhere in the viewer code.

items.where: Drawer > Library > Images > long-press an image > Remix
steps: Open Library from the drawer and tap the Images chip.
Long-press an image tile to open its menu.
Tap Remix.
Check that the chat opens in image mode with the earlier prompt and model selected, and compare with Expected (ratio is not clearly set by this path).
items.needs: A Cloud account with a previously generated image
items.note: Remix is shown only in Cloud mode. The code sets the model and the prompt; it does not show a code path that sets the aspect ratio.

items.where: Chat (temporary chat) > long-press a generated image > Save to Library
steps: Open a temporary chat in Cloud mode and generate an image.
Long-press the image.
Tap Save to Library and wait for the message Saved to your Library.
Open Drawer > Library > Images and check that the image is there.
items.needs: A Cloud account with image access; a temporary chat for the Save to Library option
items.note: Images in normal chats are not shown with a Save to Library option; the code does not show a manual save there. Whether they reach the Library automatically is not confirmed by this audit.

items.where: Chat > tap a generated image > Save image to Photos
steps: Tap a generated image to open the full-screen viewer.
Tap the download icon labelled Save image to Photos.
Allow Photos access if the system asks.
Open the Photos app and find the saved image, then compare its size with Expected.
items.needs: A phone or simulator with Photos access allowed
items.note: The visible word is Save to Photos, not Download. Full quality is not confirmed by the screen text.

items.where: Chat > tap a generated image > Copy image
steps: Tap a generated image to open the full-screen viewer.
Tap the button labelled Copy image.
Check that the icon changes and the label reads Image copied.
Paste into a text field in another app and check that the image pastes.
items.needs: A phone with a text field in another app
items.note: The same action is in the long-press menu on the image in the chat (src/features/chat/components/GeneratedImage.tsx).

items.where: Chat > tap a generated image > Share image
steps: Tap a generated image to open the full-screen viewer.
Tap the button labelled Share image.
Choose another app from the share sheet, such as Messages or Mail.
Check that the image is attached in that app before sending.
items.needs: A phone with at least one other app that accepts images

items.where: Chat > tap a generated image > Change this image
steps: Tap a generated image in a chat whose model can edit images.
Tap the button labelled Change this image.
Type the change in the box labelled Describe the change, for example a colour change, and submit.
Compare the new image with the original and check that the same picture was changed.
items.needs: A generated image from an image model that can edit; the button is hidden for models that cannot
items.note: Edit an area of this image (Paintbrush) is the area-edit option on the same bar. The Change option is hidden for attachments.

items.where: Chat > tap a generated image > Report this image
steps: Tap a generated image to open the full-screen viewer.
Tap the flag button labelled Report this image.
Choose a reason in the report sheet and submit it (use a test image only).
Read the confirmation and check it says what happened to the report.
items.needs: A generated image; a test image only, since a report is sent to trust and safety
items.note: The same report is also in the chat message actions as Report… (the file text is Report with an ellipsis escape).

items.where: Not shown on the image in the app. The AI claim is sent with the file download.
items.needs: none
items.note: No visible AI-generated label was found in apps/mobile (searched AI-generated, AI generated, provenance). The legal screen EU AI Act Article 50 describes a C2PA-style claim; the file route sets the claim headers (apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/route.ts).

items.where: Add to chat (+ button at the left of the chat composer) > Photos > pick a photo; the photo then shows as an attachment in the composer, with Create image on in the same sheet
steps: Sign in and open a chat in AGI Cloud mode.
Tap the + button labelled Add to chat next to the message box.
Tap Create image in the sheet so the chat is in image mode.
Tap Photos in the top row of the sheet and choose a photo from your library.
Type a short prompt and tap send.
Check the sent message shows your photo and that the reply is an image made from it, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account on a plan that includes image generation, and a photo in the phone library or simulator; the image-generation rows only appear in AGI Cloud mode
items.note: The code reads the attached photo as the source to edit only when the chat is in image mode; I did not confirm the composer preview or send button wording on a device. The send button has no visible text label in the code (testID chat.composer.send).

items.where: Add to chat (+) > Create image, then type the change in the message box and send, with a photo attached through Photos
steps: Open a chat in AGI Cloud mode and tap the + button labelled Add to chat.
Tap Create image, then tap Photos and choose a photo.
Close the sheet and type a change in the message box, for example a colour or object change.
Tap send.
Compare the returned image with the photo: the requested change should appear while the rest stays similar, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account on a plan that includes image generation, and a photo to edit
items.note: The app refuses to edit when the selected image model cannot use a reference (message: This model uses text only. Pick an editing model to edit a photo.); the tester should check the model choice in the Image model list first. Whether the sheet closes after Create image is not confirmed in code.

items.where: Add to chat (+) > Create image > Photos (add up to 4 photos; the hint reads Attach up to 4 photos. The first is edited; the rest guide it.), then type a prompt and send
steps: Open a chat in AGI Cloud mode and tap the + button labelled Add to chat.
Tap Create image, then tap Photos and choose a first photo; tap Photos again to add a second photo for reference.
Read the hint Attach up to 4 photos. The first is edited; the rest guide it.
Type a prompt that says what to keep from the second photo, such as its subject, layout or style, and tap send.
Compare the result with the reference photo: subject, layout or style from the reference should carry over, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account on a plan that includes image generation, and two photos in the phone library or simulator

labels.text: Attach up to 4 photos. The first is edited; the rest guide it.

items.note: Code allows the first photo plus up to 3 more (MANAGED_MEDIA_MAX_IMAGE_REFERENCES = 3 in packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts); the guide photos are sent only with an editing model. Whether the reference is carried over visibly depends on the model, not checked here.

items.where: No control of its own: the photo you sent for an edit is attached to your request message in the chat, and the new image is a separate reply
steps: Do the steps for S45.01 and send the edit request.
Look at your request message in the chat: the photo you attached should still be shown there.
Look at the reply: it should be a new image, and your original photo should not be replaced, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account on a plan that includes image generation, and a photo to edit
items.note: The code attaches the source photo to the request message before generation (runImageGenerationTurn.ts lines 253-267) and returns a new reply; no visible label for this was found, and whether the bubble shows the original next to the result on screen was not checked.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+ button) > Create video > type a prompt in Message input and send
steps: Sign in and open a chat in Cloud mode.
Tap the Add to chat button.
Tap Create video. Under it, the Video model list appears.
Type a text prompt in the message box and send it.
Wait for the video card to appear in the chat.
Compare: a video clip comes back in the chat after generating.
items.needs: a Cloud-mode account whose plan includes video generation
items.note: The video option only appears in Cloud mode when the plan and granted capabilities allow it. I did not trace the send path that runs a video turn from the message box, so the exact send step is unverified.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Create video > Video model list
steps: Sign in and open a chat in Cloud mode.
Tap Add to chat.
Tap Create video.
Look at the list under Video model.
Tap a different model row.
Compare: the tapped row shows as selected, and the next clip uses that model.
items.needs: a Cloud-mode account whose plan includes video generation
items.note: Model names and prices come from the model registry, not from literal text. The model choice is saved with the chat view store; I did not check that the send step reads it.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Create video > Length
steps: Sign in and open a chat in Cloud mode.
Tap Add to chat, then Create video.
Look under the Length heading for rows such as 5 seconds.
Tap one of the Length rows.
Read the line that starts with About under the list.
Compare: the chosen length is marked selected and the About line changes for that length.
items.needs: a Cloud-mode account whose plan includes video generation
items.note: The Length section only shows when the model offers more than one duration. The row text is built as a template (N seconds), so the exact visible words are not a fixed string.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Create video > Aspect ratio
steps: Sign in and open a chat in Cloud mode.
Tap Add to chat, then Create video.
Find the Aspect ratio heading in the video options.
Tap one of the aspect ratio rows.
Compare: the tapped row is marked selected.
items.needs: a Cloud-mode account whose plan includes video generation
items.note: The words Aspect ratio also appear for images. The video section is gated on video mode. I did not confirm that the generated clip changes shape.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Create video > Quality
steps: Sign in and open a chat in Cloud mode.
Tap Add to chat, then Create video.
Find the Quality heading in the video options.
Tap one of the Quality rows.
Compare: the tapped row is selected. Some rows show a hint like N/Ns only.
Compare the clip's output resolution with the chosen row, if you can inspect the file.
items.needs: a Cloud-mode account whose plan includes video generation
items.note: The screen word is Quality, not Resolution. The resolution options come from getVideoQualityOptionsForModel. I did not confirm the delivered file's resolution matches the choice.

items.where: Chat screen > send a video prompt > video card in the chat shows Generating video
steps: Sign in and open a chat in Cloud mode with video mode selected.
Send a video prompt.
Look at the card in the chat.
Compare: the card shows Generating video, a percentage and bar only if the provider reports one, and the line about a minute or two.
items.needs: a Cloud-mode account whose plan includes video generation

labels.text: This usually takes a minute or two. You can keep using the app.

items.note: Other status words are Queued with the provider… and Video generation failed. The progress bar is shown only when a number is reported.

items.where: Chat screen > Add to chat > Create video > Video model rows and the About line under the options
steps: Sign in and open a chat in Cloud mode.
Tap Add to chat, then Create video.
Read the price text on each Video model row, such as per second.
Pick a Length and read the About line below the options.
Compare: the About line shows an estimated credit amount and says a failed video costs nothing.
items.needs: a Cloud-mode account whose plan includes video generation
items.note: Before generating, only the estimate is shown. I searched GeneratedVideo.tsx, VideoGenProgress.tsx and runVideoGenerationTurn.ts for a credit amount after generation and found none in the video card files.

items.where: Chat screen > send a video prompt > video card > Stop generating
steps: Send a video prompt and wait until the card shows Generating video.
Tap Stop generating under the progress text.
Look at the button while it works.
Compare: the button shows Stopping and then the card shows Video generation stopped, and the clip is not delivered.
items.needs: a Cloud-mode account whose plan includes video generation
items.note: The button only appears when the message has a video task id. Server-side stopping is in apps/web/lib/services/video-job-reconciliation-service.ts and I did not verify it from the app.

items.where: Chat screen > failed video card > Retry
steps: Make a video that fails, or wait for a timeout.
Look for the Retry button under the failed card.
Tap Retry.
Compare: the prompt is sent again as a video request and a new video card appears.
items.needs: a Cloud-mode account and a video that failed or timed out
items.note: Retry resends the prompt as a /video request through the chat send path in apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx. I did not verify that it reuses the earlier model, length, aspect ratio and quality, rather than the current selections.

items.where: Side menu > Library > Videos
steps: Sign in and open the side menu.
Tap Library.
Tap the Videos filter chip.
Look at the grid.
Compare: completed clips are shown as tiles, or the text Videos you generate will appear here shows if there are none.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one finished clip

labels.text: Videos you generate will appear here

items.note: The side menu row uses the navLibrary key. The gallery is the Library grid with the Videos filter. I did not confirm how the side menu is opened.

items.where: Chat screen > video card > Play, or Side menu > Library > tap a video tile
steps: Open a chat with a finished video card.
Tap Play on the card, or tap the video in the Library grid.
Look at the player screen that opens.
Use the player's controls to play, pause and scrub.
Compare: the clip plays, pauses and can be moved to another point.
items.needs: a finished video clip in the account
items.note: The player is a WebView (VideoPlayerModal.tsx). Its play, pause and scrub controls come from the player page built by apps/mobile/src/services/fileCreation, which I did not open, so the controls are unverified.

items.where: Chat screen > video card > Save, or the player's Save video icon
steps: Open a finished video card in a chat.
Tap Save under the card.
Wait for the share sheet to open.
Compare: the share sheet lists a save or send option for the video file.
items.needs: a finished video clip in the account
items.note: The app downloads the file and opens the system share sheet, so the file is saved through that sheet, not straight to a folder. The word Download is only in the icon and the hint.

items.where: Side menu > Library > long-press a video tile > Share
steps: Open Library from the side menu.
Tap the Videos filter.
Long-press a video tile.
Tap Share in the menu that opens, or tap Library options, Select saved files, pick one video, then tap Share.
Compare: the share sheet opens with the video file.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one finished clip
items.note: Share in the library also exists through the selection button. Sharing in chat is done by the Save button, not Share. If the library is not in cloud scope, the share function returns without showing anything.

items.where: Chat screen with an existing chat open > composer button "Start voice mode" (shown when the message box is empty)
steps: Sign in and open an existing chat from the chat list.
Leave the message box empty and find the round button on the right of the composer.
Tap the button labelled "Start voice mode".
Look for the voice bar with the status "Listening" or "Connecting live voice..." and the "End live voice" button, and confirm it is the chat you opened.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a microphone
items.note: The button only appears when the message box is empty and voice mode is available; the voice bar opens in the same chat (id is passed in chat/[id].tsx).

items.where: Chat screen (new chat, no conversation open) > composer button "Start voice mode"
steps: Sign in and open a new chat so the message box is empty.
Tap the button labelled "Start voice mode" on the right of the composer.
If the first-time intro appears, tap "Continue" and then "Start voice".
Look for the app moving to a chat that is created for the voice session, with the voice bar showing "Connecting live voice..." or "Listening".
items.needs: a signed-in account and a microphone
items.note: The new chat is created with the title "Voice chat" in app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx when the live path is used; the tab's visible name was not found in the code, so the tester should look for the first tab.

items.where: Chat screen > open a chat > "Start voice mode" > "Show captions"
steps: Open a chat and tap "Start voice mode" in the composer.
Tap "Show captions" in the top bar of the voice view.
Say something and wait for a reply.
Check that the spoken turns appear in a transcript above the voice orb, under the labels "YOU" and "AGI", and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a microphone, and a speaker
items.note: The spoken turns are shown in the voice bar's own transcript; the code did not show them appearing in the normal message list, so check that too.

items.where: Settings > Voice > "Open Voice Companion"
steps: Open Settings and tap "Voice".
Tap "Open Voice Companion" (this row only appears on phones that have on-device speech recognition).
Look for a full-screen view with a large orb, the text "Tap to speak" and "Speech stays on this device", and a close button.
Compare with Expected: voice fills the screen and no transcript is shown.
items.needs: a phone with on-device speech recognition and a microphone
items.note: The route to Settings from the first screen after sign-in was not found in the code, so the tester has to find the Settings screen first.

items.where: Chat > open a chat > "Start voice mode" > status text under the orb
steps: Open a chat and tap "Start voice mode".
Wait for the connection to finish.
Read the status text under the orb.
Check it shows "Listening" and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a microphone
items.note: The status text in the live voice bar has no live-region setting in the code, so whether a screen reader announces it was not confirmed; the full-screen companion does announce "Listening...".

items.where: Chat > open a chat > "Start voice mode" > status text under the orb while the reply plays
steps: Start voice mode in a chat and ask a question that gets a spoken answer.
While the reply is being spoken, read the status text under the orb.
Check it shows "Speaking, talk any time to interrupt" and that the orb moves.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a microphone, and a speaker

labels.text: Speaking, talk any time to interrupt

items.where: Chat > open a chat > "Start voice mode" > ask for a task > "Working on your request"
steps: Start voice mode in a chat and ask for something that needs work, such as a lookup.
While the assistant is working, look at the step with the text "Working on your request" under the status area.
Check that the "Stop the task" button appears next to it.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a microphone
items.note: Tool-specific wording comes from the server; the fallback is "Working on it" in src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceSession.ts.

items.where: Settings > Voice > "Open Voice Companion" (full-screen orb) ; also the orb in "Start voice mode" view
steps: Open Settings > Voice > "Open Voice Companion".
Speak and watch the orb while you talk.
Then wait for the reply and watch the orb while it speaks.
Compare with Expected: the orb should follow the sound level, not a fixed pattern.
items.needs: a microphone and a speaker
items.note: In the live voice bar the orb gets a fixed level (0.6) while the assistant speaks and 0 otherwise, so it does not follow the microphone level there.

items.where: Chat > open a chat > "Start voice mode" > "Mute microphone" button (bottom right)
steps: Start voice mode and wait for "Listening".
Tap the button labelled "Mute microphone".
Check the status changes to "Muted, tap the mic to talk" and the button now reads "Unmute microphone".
Tap "Unmute microphone" and check the call is still running (the voice bar stays open).
items.needs: a signed-in account and a microphone

labels.text: Muted, tap the mic to talk

items.where: Chat > open a chat > "Start voice mode" > "End live voice" button (X, bottom right)
steps: Start voice mode and wait for "Listening".
Tap the round button labelled "End live voice".
Check the voice bar closes and you are back at the chat.
Check that the chat shows no further voice activity (the session has ended).
items.needs: a signed-in account and a microphone
items.note: Usage settling is not visible on screen, so the tester cannot confirm it from the UI.

items.where: Settings > Voice > Mode > "Push to talk"; then Settings > Voice > "Open Voice Companion"
steps: Open Settings > Voice and under "Mode" tap "Push to talk".
Go back and tap "Open Voice Companion".
Check the orb hint "Hold to talk, release to send" and the status "Hold to talk".
Press and hold the orb, speak, release, and check the message is sent only after release.
items.needs: a phone with on-device speech recognition and a microphone
items.note: The live voice bar in chat has no push-to-talk behaviour in the code; the setting applies to the full-screen Voice Companion.

items.where: Settings > Voice > Mode > "Hands free"; then Settings > Voice > "Open Voice Companion"
steps: Open Settings > Voice and under "Mode" tap "Hands free".
Go back and tap "Open Voice Companion".
Speak, wait for the reply, and speak again without pressing the orb.
Check the app listens again on its own and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a phone with on-device speech recognition and a microphone
items.note: The orb hint in the companion reads "Tap to start or stop listening" in hands-free mode, which may be confusing next to the expected automatic listening.

items.where: Chat > "Start voice mode" > speak while the reply is playing
steps: Start voice mode and ask a question with a long spoken answer.
While the reply is speaking, say something new.
Check the status changes to "Go ahead" and the reply stops.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone, a speaker, and a signed-in account (the live voice service)

labels.text: Speaking, talk any time to interrupt

items.note: Barge-in is marked unverified in the plan and depends on the live service; the code was not run.

items.where: Settings > Voice > "Voice" > "Voice & Language" > "Voice mode" (list of voices)
steps: Open Settings > Voice and tap the row "Voice".
On the "Voice & Language" screen, find the group "Voice mode".
Tap a different voice and go back.
Start voice mode in a chat and check the conversation speaks with the chosen voice.
items.needs: a phone with the voices available and a microphone
items.note: The voice picker sheet with "Start voice" appears in the first-time voice intro; the voices also have a "Voice mode" list in Settings.

items.where: Chat > "Start voice mode" > first-time intro "Continue" > voice picker sheet > "Play sample"
steps: Use "Start voice mode" in a chat (the first-time intro appears only the first time).
Tap "Continue" on the intro, then select a voice in the picker.
Tap "Play sample" under the voice.
Listen and compare with Expected: a sample of the chosen voice plays.
items.needs: a microphone is not needed; a speaker and a phone that has not yet seen the voice intro
items.note: The plan says the sample files are not yet committed, so Play sample may do nothing; the code reads them from the sample map and falls back to none.

items.where: Settings > Voice > "Speech language"
steps: Open Settings > Voice and tap "Speech language".
Pick a language from the list (the first choice is "Uses your device language").
Go back and start voice mode in a chat.
Speak in the chosen language and check the app understands it.
items.needs: a microphone

items.where: Chat > open a chat > "Start voice mode" > "Show captions" (top bar of the voice view)
steps: Start voice mode and have a short exchange.
Tap "Show captions" in the top bar.
Check a transcript appears with the labels "YOU" and "AGI" for both speakers.
Tap "Hide captions" and check the transcript goes away.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a microphone, and a speaker
items.note: The captions panel only shows when there are turns to show.

items.where: Chat > open a chat > "Start voice mode" > "Show captions"; then check the chat after ending
steps: Start voice mode, turn on "Show captions", and have a short exchange.
Tap "End live voice".
Look at the chat and check the spoken turns are kept with it.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a microphone
items.note: Whether the turns are saved into the chat message store was not confirmed in this audit (the store reference was not read).

items.where: Chat > open a chat > "Start voice mode" > ask for an action > "What the actions returned"
steps: Start voice mode in a chat.
Ask for something that uses a tool (for example a lookup or an image).
When the result comes back, look for the section "What the actions returned" in the voice view.
Check the tool name, output and any image are shown.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a microphone

items.where: Chat > open a chat > "Start voice mode" > ask for an action that needs approval > "Waiting for your approval" > "Allow" or "Deny"
steps: Start voice mode and ask for an action that needs your approval.
Look for the panel with the title "Waiting for your approval" and the summary of the action.
Tap "Allow" or "Deny" without leaving the voice view.
Check the request continues or stops and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a microphone; an action that needs approval
items.note: The button text is taken from TOOL_APPROVAL_ACTION_LABELS; the rendered text itself was not read, so check the visible words on screen.

items.where: Chat > open a chat > "Start voice mode" > turn off Wi-Fi or mobile data > "Reconnecting live voice..."
steps: Start voice mode and wait for "Listening".
Turn off Wi-Fi and mobile data (or Airplane Mode) for a few seconds.
Look for the status "Reconnecting live voice...".
Turn the network back on and check the status returns to "Listening", or check for the error box with "Try again" if it does not reconnect.
items.needs: a phone you can switch networks on and off, a signed-in account
items.note: The message for a dropped connection is "The live voice connection dropped." in src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts; the exact retry wording after failure was not fully traced.

items.where: Chat > "Start voice mode" when the plan's voice allowance is used up > error box in the voice view
steps: Use up the voice allowance on the account (or use an account that has none left).
Tap "Start voice mode" in a chat.
Look for the error box in the voice view with a message that names the limit and when it resets.
Check the buttons "Try again" and "Use the keyboard" are shown.
items.needs: a signed-in account whose voice usage is used up
items.note: The limit sentence comes from the server (extendLiveVoiceSession in src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceSession.ts); the app shows whatever the server sends.

items.where: Chat > open a chat > "Start voice mode" > "Type instead" (bottom left of the voice view)
steps: Start voice mode in a chat.
Tap the bar labelled "Type instead" at the bottom left.
Check the voice view closes and the message box is ready to type in.
Type a message and send it, and check it continues the same chat.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat list > open an earlier voice chat > "Start voice mode" in the composer
steps: Open a voice chat from earlier (one started by voice).
Tap "Start voice mode" in the composer.
Say something that refers to an earlier turn.
Check the reply uses the earlier context and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an earlier voice chat and a signed-in account
items.note: The conversation is sent by id (src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceSession.ts); the use of earlier turns is decided by the server and was not traced.

items.needs: a signed-in account, a microphone, and a task that is running

labels.text: Stop the task and keep talking

items.note: The button "Stop the task" (aria label "Stop the task and keep talking") in LiveVoiceBar.tsx cancels the task only; no separate on-screen control to stop just the spoken reply was found, so the tester cannot check this part from the UI.

items.where: Settings > Voice > turn on "Voice Input"; then open any chat and tap the microphone button in the message field
steps: Open Settings, then Voice, and turn on "Voice Input" (it is a toggle row).
Open any chat so the message field and its controls show.
Tap the microphone button (idle label "Tap to record, hold for push-to-talk").
Speak a short sentence, then tap "Stop recording" (the square).
Compare: the spoken words should appear as text in the message field.
items.needs: a microphone, phone width or Mac/iPhone with mic permission; the mic button only appears when Voice Input is on and the on-device recognizer is available

labels.text: Tap to record, hold for push-to-talk

items.note: The mic is hidden when Voice Input is off or the on-device recognizer is missing (onDeviceRecognizerGuaranteed in VoiceInputButton.tsx); the Mac may not show a mic button at all.

items.where: Open a chat > microphone button > "Stop recording" (square); the text lands in the message field
steps: Open any chat with Voice Input turned on in Settings > Voice.
Tap the microphone button and speak a sentence with a mistake in it.
Tap "Stop recording" (the square, not the arrow).
Tap inside the message field and edit a word, then compare: the transcript should be there and editable, and nothing should be sent yet.
items.needs: a microphone; phone width recommended
items.note: The square "Stop recording" inserts; the arrow "Send recording" sends immediately, which is the opposite of an editable-first flow, so test the square. I did not read the insert handler body (handleTranscription) in full.

items.where: Settings > Voice > "Speech language"
steps: Open Settings, then Voice.
Tap the row labelled "Speech language" and pick a different language from the list.
Turn on Voice Input if it is off, open a chat, and dictate a sentence in the new language.
Compare: the transcript should be in that language. The choice is stored per Local and Cloud mode.
items.needs: a microphone
items.note: The row opens a language picker in the same screen; a separate screen with the title "Voice & Language" also exists (src/features/settings/voice-language/index.tsx). I did not verify which one the row opens in the UI.

items.where: Open a chat > microphone button > speak > "Stop recording"; the final transcript appears in the message field
steps: Turn on Voice Input, open a chat, and tap the microphone button.
Speak one full sentence, then tap "Stop recording".
Wait for the processing state to finish.
Compare: the full sentence should appear once as the final text. If nothing was heard, the alert "Didn't catch that" appears instead.
items.needs: a microphone
items.note: An empty transcript is dropped silently (VoiceInputButton.tsx only delivers text that is not blank), so an empty result shows nothing in the field.

items.where: Open a chat > microphone button > stay silent or fail > alert "Didn't catch that" > "Try again"
steps: Turn on Voice Input, open a chat, and tap the microphone button.
Stay silent for a few seconds, or speak so it cannot be heard, then tap "Stop recording".
When the alert "Didn't catch that" appears, tap "Try again".
Compare: recording starts again straight away without you retyping anything. The alert says the audio is not saved, so you must speak again.
items.needs: a microphone
items.note: Retry means a new recording, not a re-transcription of the old audio, because audio is not kept. Which failures trigger this alert was not fully traced.

items.where: Open a chat > microphone button > while recording tap "Cancel recording" (the X)
steps: Turn on Voice Input, open a chat, and type a few words so you can see the field's current text.
Tap the microphone button and speak a sentence.
Tap "Cancel recording" (the X button on the left of the recording bar).
Compare: the recording stops, nothing is added to the message field, and nothing is sent.
items.needs: a microphone
an iPhone with a short audio recording saved in the Files app
items.note: Found the batch path: TranscribeIntent.swift (title "Transcribe with AGI") hands an audio file to the app, and app/_layout.tsx (case 'transcribe') opens app/(app)/voice.tsx, which calls transcribeAudioFile in one request (voice.tsx lines 324-358, voiceInput.ts non-streaming path). I could not confirm from the code how a person starts that intent on the phone (the Shortcuts app or the Share sheet), so the path is left empty. Searched: rg for audioUri, transcribe and Transcribe with AGI in apps/mobile.

items.where: Settings > Voice > turn on "Voice Input"; open a chat > microphone button > speak; words appear in the field before you stop
steps: Turn on Voice Input in Settings > Voice, open a chat.
Tap the microphone button (the label becomes "Tap to stop recording").
Speak slowly for several seconds without tapping anything.
Compare: words should appear in the message field while you are still speaking, before "Stop recording" is tapped.
items.needs: a microphone; an iPhone with on-device speech recognition for the live text
items.note: Live partial text comes from interimResults in VoiceInputButton's recording path (VoiceInputButton.tsx onPartialTranscript to setLiveTranscript). The separate voice conversation mode (LiveVoiceBar.tsx, "Open Voice Companion" in Settings > Voice) is a different streaming feature, not the composer dictation; I did not confirm the on-screen rendering of the live text.

items.where: Settings > Voice > turn on "Voice Input"; open a chat > tap the microphone button the first time > "Dictation" sheet > "Continue"
steps: Turn on Voice Input in Settings > Voice, then open a chat.
Tap the microphone button for the first time (the sheet only appears once on this account or device).
Read the sheet: title "Dictation", the line "Speak instead of typing. Your words appear as text in your message.", and the disclosure line.
Compare: the disclosure should say where audio goes. Tap "Continue" to start recording; the sheet's X closes it without starting.
items.needs: a microphone; the sheet only appears the first time, so use an account or device that has not seen dictation yet

labels.text: Your voice is transcribed on this device and never recorded.

items.note: There is no separate checkbox: agreement is the "Continue" button. The disclosure shown depends on the mode (on-device or live); I did not confirm which mode dictation passes to the sheet.

items.where: Open a chat that has a dictated message > the chat's action menu > "Export" > "Export as Text" or "Export as Markdown" or "Export as PDF"
steps: Open a chat that contains a message written with dictation.
Open the chat's action menu and tap "Export".
Tap "Export as Markdown" (or "Export as Text").
Compare: the share sheet opens with a file that contains the dictated words in the conversation.
items.needs: a chat with at least one message
items.note: There is no export that is only the dictation transcript: the export covers the whole conversation. The exact trigger for the chat action menu was not traced.

items.needs: none
items.note: No recording or dictation retention or delete control was found. Audio is not kept (ChatInput.tsx: "Audio isn't saved, so say it again."). Transcripts are chat messages, so they follow chat deletion. The only "Data retention" row is cloud-only (src/features/settings/cloud-privacy/index.tsx:44). Searched rg for retention, recording delete and transcript delete in apps/mobile/app and src.

items.needs: a device
items.note: Searched rg -i undo in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx and apps/mobile/src/features/voice: no match. The dictated text is inserted by the app's own state update, so whether the normal undo action reverts it was not verified from code.

items.where: Chat > any assistant reply > Read aloud (Read aloud button in the reply's action row; it changes to Stop reading aloud while playing)
steps: Sign in and open a chat that already has an assistant reply.
Find the action row under the assistant reply (Copy, Read aloud, Regenerate response, More message actions).
Tap Read aloud.
Look for the reply being spoken aloud, and for the button label changing to Stop reading aloud. Compare with Expected: the reply plays as speech.
items.needs: a device with sound output; a chat with a finished assistant reply
items.note: The exact way the action row appears on screen (always shown or after a tap) was not verified; read-aloud can also show a 'not available' reason for some account states.

items.where: Settings > Voice > Voice & Language (open the Voice row, then the Voice row again; Speech language is the row above it)
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Tap Voice.
Tap the Speech language row and pick a language in the sheet, then close it.
Tap the Voice row to open the Voice & Language screen.
Look at the Speaking style list and the installed voice list, tap a voice, and compare what is shown as selected with Expected.
items.needs: none (a Free account works; voice-mode list only appears when live voice is available for the account)
items.note: The Settings menu label comes from the shared translation file packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/common.json; the side-menu gesture to open it was not verified; the Voice row on the Voice screen opens the Voice & Language screen, so its selection (voice) is shown there, not on the Voice screen itself.

items.where: Settings > Voice > Speed (slider with value shown as 0.50x to 2.00x)
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Tap Voice.
Drag the slider labelled Speed to a different value (range 0.5x to 2x, steps of 0.05).
Tap Read aloud on an assistant reply in a chat, then listen and compare with Expected: the speed of spoken playback changes with the slider.
items.needs: a device with sound output; a chat with an assistant reply
items.note: No separate support check for speed was found; the slider is always shown, and the value is passed to the device speech engine in apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/tts.ts (rate option); the rate for cloud server speech was not verified.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills
steps: Sign in and switch to AGI Cloud (the Cloud chat mode).
Open the side menu, tap Settings, then tap Customize in the Cloud group.
Tap Skills in the Customize list. The Skills screen opens with a Search skills field.
Scroll the list. Skills that are not installed show the status Not installed and an Install button, so the catalogue includes them.
Compare with Expected: you can browse skills not yet installed and tap Details on any of them.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: The Skills screen is also reachable from search under Go to > Skills (apps/mobile/src/features/search/mobileDestinations.ts).

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills
steps: Sign in and switch to AGI Cloud.
Open the side menu, tap Settings, tap Customize, then tap Skills.
Read the line at the top of the list: it shows a count such as 1 SKILL INSTALLED or N SKILLS INSTALLED.
Look at the status line on each card: Installed or Not installed.
Compare with Expected: the list shows which skills are installed for the account.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: The earlier DrawerContent.tsx:115 reference no longer exists and the drawer shows no skills list; the installed list lives only on the Skills screen.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > New skill
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud and open Settings > Customize > Skills.
Look for the New skill and Import buttons above the list. They appear only when the server says this account can author skills.
Tap New skill, fill in the Skill name, Skill description and Skill instructions fields, then tap Create skill.
Find the new skill in the list and check its source tag reads Personal.
Tap Details on it and check the Make your own section shows Edit instructions and Delete skill.
items.needs: A Cloud account that the server allows to author skills (if the buttons are missing the account is not allowed)
items.note: Whether a given account is allowed to author skills is decided by the server flag canAuthorSkills (apps/mobile/src/features/skills/service.ts), so the tester may not see these buttons; the plan's note that New skill is built is consistent with the code.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills
steps: Open Settings > Customize > Skills.
Read the bold name on each card, and the grey line under it.
Find a skill with no description and check it shows No description provided.
Tap Details on any card and check the name shows at the top of the skill screen.
Compare with Expected: each skill shows its name and a description of what it does.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills, then the + button (Add to chat) in a Cloud chat
steps: Open Settings > Customize > Skills and read the line under the Skills heading: Install a Skill to use it in your AGI Cloud messages.
Tap Details on an installed skill and read the line Turned-on skills load in your Cloud chats when a task needs them.
Open a Cloud chat and tap the + button (Add to chat); look for a Skills row showing Choose or the selected skill name.
In the chat box type @ and look for the Skills to use list.
Compare with Expected: the product states how a skill is used (a button, an @ mention, or automatic matching).
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account with Cloud mode on; at least one installed skill to see the Use in chat button

labels.text: Install a Skill to use it in your AGI Cloud messages.

items.note: The Turned-on skills line is in apps/mobile/src/features/skills/SkillDetailScreen.tsx and the @ trigger is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/fileMention.ts; the Skills row in the + sheet appears only in Cloud mode.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills (card line Needs ...), then Details (section Needs)
steps: Open Settings > Customize > Skills.
Find a card that has a line starting Needs followed by tool names.
Tap Details on that card.
Find the Needs section and check it lists Tools: followed by the same tool names.
Compare with Expected: the skill declares the tools it needs and the product shows them.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account and a skill that declares required tools
items.note: The card text is built in apps/mobile/src/features/skills/SkillsScreen.tsx (skillRequirementNote); enforcement when a turn is sent is in apps/mobile/src/features/skills/skillRequirements.ts and is not visible on screen.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > Use in chat (installed skill), then the chat box
steps: Open Settings > Customize > Skills and tap Use in chat on an installed skill.
Back in the chat, look for a chip with the skill name above the text box, with an x button labelled Clear selected Skill.
Type a message and send it in Cloud mode.
Read the reply and check whether it follows the chosen skill's instructions.
Compare with Expected: the picked skill is used for that message. The chip disappears after sending.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one installed skill, and Cloud mode
items.note: Whether the model actually used the skill is visible only in the reply content, not as a UI marker; the code only sends the skill name with the turn (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx).

items.where: Server side: when a Cloud message has no skill picked, the server offers installed skills whose descriptions match the message (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts)
steps: Install a skill that has a clear description, such as a skill about writing emails.
Open a Cloud chat without picking a skill and send a message that matches that description.
Read the reply and check whether it follows the skill's instructions.
Compare with Expected: the skill is used without being asked. No visible marker in the mobile app was found to confirm it.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account with an installed skill
items.note: No visible indicator of automatic matching was found in the mobile code; the mobile surface is not excluded from the offer (only vscode, cli and api are excluded).

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Customize > Skills
steps: Open the bottom bar item labelled Settings.
Under the section headed Cloud, tap Customize.
On the Customize screen, look for the card titled Skills, placed directly below the card titled Plugins.
Tap Skills and confirm the Skills screen opens. Compare with Expected: the Skills card sits beside Plugins in the customization area.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account (without sign-in the Cloud rows show the tag Sign in)
items.note: The Skills card is shown only when FEATURES.skills is true in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts (currently true). The Customize row itself is also hidden when that flag is off. The moved evidence in DrawerContent.tsx was not used because the drawer has no Customize or Skills entry.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Customize > Connectors
steps: Open the bottom bar item labelled Settings.
Under the section headed Cloud, tap Customize.
On the Customize screen, look for the card titled Connectors, below the Skills card.
Tap Connectors and confirm the Connectors screen opens. Compare with Expected: a Connectors section sits in the customization area.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account (without sign-in the Cloud rows show the tag Sign in)
items.note: A second route also exists: Settings > Cloud > Connectors (a row in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx) opens the same Connectors screen through /(app)/settings/cloud-connectors.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors. The screen opens with the title Connectors and the line Connect your tools to AGI Cloud. Each card shows name and publisher.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud, open Settings, and under the Cloud section tap Connectors.
Read the list of cards. Each card shows the connector name and, when given, the publisher after it (for example Name, Publisher).
Tap the Search connectors box at the bottom only to confirm the list is not empty; a connected card shows Connected with a date.
Compare with Expected: each entry shows name, publisher and state. Connectors that are not connected show no state label, only the name and publisher.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with connector access (the screen says Connectors are not available for this account otherwise)

labels.text: Connect your tools to AGI Cloud

items.note: The state label appears only on connected cards; a catalogue entry that is not connected shows no state text.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Search connectors box at the bottom of the screen.
steps: Open Settings > Cloud > Connectors and note the names of a few cards.
Tap the Search connectors box at the bottom and type part of a connector name you saw.
Watch the list: only matching cards should remain.

Clear the box, then type a publisher name or a word from a description, and check that matching cards appear. Then type a tool name (for example one you saw on a connector detail page) and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none beyond the Connectors screen
items.note: On the phone, the filter for connected cards matches name, publisher and description only, not tool names; the catalogue search is sent to the server, and whether it matches tool names could not be confirmed from the app code.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > the row of filter chips under the Add custom MCP box (chips All, Connected, Custom, and category names).
steps: Open Settings > Cloud > Connectors.
Look at the row of chips: All and Connected are always there. Scroll the row sideways to find category chips such as Productivity.
Tap a category chip such as Productivity.
Compare with Expected: the list should show only connectors in that category. Tap All to return to the full list.
items.needs: none beyond the Connectors screen; a category chip appears only when the directory has connectors in that category
items.note: The category list comes from the shared contracts; chips for categories with no listings are hidden, so not every category is always shown.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connector card. The detail screen shows the name, By publisher, the description, the Sign-in row, What it can do, and the link rows.
steps: Open Settings > Cloud > Connectors and tap a connector card that is not connected.
Read the name, the line By (publisher), and the description under it.
Check the row Sign-in (its value is Account sign-in, API key, Not needed or Checked on connect).
Scroll to What it can do and the link rows Documentation, Website, Support and Privacy policy. Compare with Expected: description, publisher, sign-in requirement, tools and links.
items.needs: none beyond the Connectors screen
items.note: Link rows appear only when the connector has that URL; the tools list appears only when the connector lists tools.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connector that is not connected > Connect.
steps: Open a connector that is not connected and shows the Connect button (not Coming soon).
Tap Connect.
In the alert titled Connect [name]?, read the text and tap Allow (or Deny to stop).
Compare with Expected: after Allow, the real sign-in or key step starts (a browser or in-app sign-in page for an account sign-in connector, or the API key form for an API key connector).
items.needs: a connector that is not connected and is released (Coming soon connectors have no Connect button); for a real sign-in step, an outside account for that provider
items.note: Connect is hidden for connectors that are Coming soon or whose setup is on desktop or CLI only; the alert text comes from a shared contracts function.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connector whose Sign-in row reads Account sign-in > Connect > Allow.
steps: Open a connector whose Sign-in row says Account sign-in and tap Connect.
Tap Allow in the alert Connect [name]?.
Wait for the provider's own consent page to open (in the app browser or the in-app sign-in sheet) and approve it there.

Return to the app and compare with Expected: the connector should now show Connected with a date under the Connected filter, and its detail page should show Connected to AGI Cloud and a Granted access section.
items.needs: an outside account for that provider (the account to approve the grant)
items.note: If the sign-in page is closed before finishing, the app shows an alert saying the connector is not connected yet; the grant is stored by the server, which the app code does not show directly.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connector whose Sign-in row reads API key > Connect > Allow > API key form.
steps: Open a connector whose Sign-in row says API key and tap Connect, then Allow.
In the form, tap the API key box (placeholder API key) and type a key.
Tap Test and save.
Compare with Expected: a bad key shows an error and nothing is saved; a good key closes the form and the detail page shows Connected to AGI Cloud. The encryption cannot be seen from the screen.
items.needs: an API key for that provider
items.note: The form opens only when the server asks for credentials; otherwise the connector may connect straight after Allow. Whether the key is stored encrypted is not visible in the UI.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connected connector > Connected to AGI Cloud > Granted access section.
steps: Open a connector that is connected (it shows a Connected date on the list).
On its detail page, read the Connected to AGI Cloud heading and the rows under it.
Find the Granted access section: each row shows a permission sentence and the word Read or Write.
If no sentence rows appear, look for a Granted access row listing scope names. Compare with Expected: the permissions shown should be what was granted.
items.needs: a connected connector (a connector that has granted permissions or scopes)
items.note: The section is hidden when the connection reports neither permission sentences nor scopes.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors: the state text on each card. On a connector detail page: the Not responding box, Authorization expired, and the Connection health card.
steps: Open Settings > Cloud > Connectors and read the state text on each connected card: Connected [date] means healthy; Not responding is amber; Authorization expired, reconnect is red.
Tap a connected card. Read the warning boxes: Not responding (with Check again), Authorization expired, or Needs to be reconnected.
Scroll to the section Connection health and read its state and summary text, or Not called in the last hour.
Compare with Expected: each connector shows whether it is healthy, needs reauthorization or is not responding.
items.needs: a connected connector; the not-responding and expired states depend on the provider and cannot be set up from the app
items.note: The word healthy is not shown; a healthy connector shows Connected with a date on the list and no warning box.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors: a card at the top with a Reconnect button, or a connector detail page with Reauthorize (under Authorization expired).
steps: Use a connector whose authorization has expired or been revoked (it shows Authorization expired, reconnect on the list).
On the Connectors screen, look for the card at the top and tap Reconnect; or tap the connector and scroll to the Authorization expired box.
Tap Reauthorize on the detail page.
Compare with Expected: the provider's authorization page should open for the same connector, and after approval the state should change to Connected.
items.needs: an account-sign-in (OAuth) connector whose grant has expired or been revoked, and an outside account for that provider
items.note: The top Reconnect card appears only for account-sign-in connectors whose grant expired; API key connectors show Replace API key instead.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connected connector > scroll to the bottom > Disconnect > Disconnect (in the alert).
steps: Open a connected connector and scroll to the bottom of its detail page.
Tap Disconnect. Read the alert Disconnect [name]? and its text about saved tool permissions.
Tap Disconnect in the alert.
Compare with Expected: the screen returns to Connectors and the connector no longer shows as connected. Whether the assistant still uses it is not shown on this screen; check it in a chat if needed.
items.needs: a connected connector you can reconnect afterwards
items.note: The effect on the assistant is not shown on the connector screens; it is an inner behaviour of the server and the chat.

items.needs: a connected connector, and an outside account for the provider to check the provider side
items.note: No Revoke wording exists in the mobile connector screens or services/connectors.ts (searched rg -i revoke in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors and services/connectors.ts). The nearest control is Disconnect, whose alert does not say the provider token is revoked; whether the provider is asked to revoke is not shown in mobile code.

items.needs: none
items.note: No folder or repository selection for a connector was found in apps/mobile (searched rg -i for repositor and folder in apps/mobile/src and app, filtered for connector, mcp, scope, github and drive). Only unrelated hits came back, such as GitHub repository URLs in the cloud code session sheet and src/features/settings/code/GitHubConnections.tsx, which was not checked as a connector control.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connected connector > Tool permissions > Write and delete tools > tap a tool's Allow, Ask or Block choice.
steps: Open a connected connector that has write tools and scroll to Tool permissions.
Find the group heading Write and delete tools and read the tool rows under it.
Tap Allow, Ask or Block on one write tool (Allow runs it automatically, Ask asks first, Block stops it).
Compare with Expected: the row should show the chosen level. Tap the reset control on a row (Reset [tool] to default) to return it to the default, which follows Action approvals.
items.needs: a connected connector that has write tools
items.note: The group-level level is read from the saved settings but the app only sends changes per tool, so there is no visible control to set all write tools at once; the global Action approvals row on the Connectors screen is a separate setting.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Gmail > Connect, then Add to chat > Connectors (turn Gmail on) in a new chat
steps: Open Settings, tap the Cloud group, then tap Connectors.
Tap Gmail, then tap Connect and finish the Google sign-in.
Open a new chat, tap Add to chat, tap Connectors and turn Gmail on.
Type: Find emails from [a sender you know] about [a subject you know].
Compare: the reply lists matching messages from that mailbox, as Expected says.
items.needs: a Google account; a cloud account that can use connectors
items.note: The ledger says the Gmail OAuth client pair is not yet in CONNECTOR_OAUTH_PROVIDERS_JSON, so Connect may fail or show Needs setup.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Gmail > Connect, then Add to chat > Connectors (turn Gmail on) in a new chat
steps: Connect Gmail as in S56.01 (Settings, Cloud, Connectors, Gmail, Connect).
Open a new chat, tap Add to chat, tap Connectors and turn Gmail on.
Type: Open the email from [a sender] about [a subject] and tell me what it says.
Compare: the reply shows the full text of that email or thread, not only a summary of the subject line.
items.needs: a Google account; a cloud account that can use connectors
items.note: Same Gmail OAuth gap as S56.01: the ledger says the client pair is not yet configured.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Gmail > Connect, then Add to chat > Connectors (turn Gmail on) in a new chat
steps: Connect Gmail and turn it on in a new chat (as in S56.01).
Type: Draft a reply to [a sender] saying [a short message].
Check the reply: it says a draft was created.
Open Gmail in a browser or the Gmail app and look in Drafts for the new draft, as Expected says.
items.needs: a Google account with Gmail; a cloud account that can use connectors
items.note: The directory lists a create_draft tool for Gmail; the Gmail OAuth gap in S56.01 applies.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Gmail > Connect, then in a chat with Gmail on, the approval card when a send is requested
steps: Connect Gmail and turn it on in a new chat (as in S56.01).
Type: Send the draft to [a sender you control] with the subject [test subject].
Look for the approval card that asks before the send runs.
Compare: nothing is sent until you approve; after approval the reply confirms the send.
items.needs: a Google account with Gmail; a second mailbox you control to receive the test
items.note: The approval card text was not read in the chat code; the approval rule is set per tool in Gmail's Tool permissions.

items.needs: a Google account with Gmail; a file to attach
items.note: Gmail is reachable, but I did not find an attachment tool in the Gmail directory list I read (the first eight tool names only), so the attachment behaviour is not confirmed.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Google Calendar > Connect, then Add to chat > Connectors (turn Google Calendar on) in a new chat
steps: Open Settings, tap Cloud, tap Connectors, tap Google Calendar, tap Connect.
Finish the Google sign-in, then open a new chat.
Tap Add to chat, tap Connectors and turn Google Calendar on.
Type: What is on my calendar on [a date] with [a word in an event title]?
Compare: the reply lists the matching events for that date or text.
