items.needs: a Cloud account with a finished tool call
items.note: View full output appears only for large results (more than 12 lines or a large size).

items.where: A long tool result in a Cloud chat: expand the row, then tap View full output
steps: In a Cloud chat with code execution on, ask for a program that prints many lines (for example 100 numbers).
Tap the Run code row to expand it.
Tap View full output to open the complete result in a full-screen sheet.
Compare with Expected: the full text is kept and can be opened later; the context reference itself is server-side and not visible.
items.needs: a Cloud account with code execution enabled
items.note: The large-result reference and store are server-side (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-result-store.ts, tool-loop.ts); only the phone full-output sheet is visible to the user.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors
steps: Open Settings and tap Cloud, then tap Connectors.
Wait for the connector list to load (a loading label may show first).
Look at the filter chips (All, Connected, Custom) and the connector rows; each row shows a status such as Connected or Not connected.
Compare with Expected: your configured MCP servers (custom ones show under the Custom filter) should appear in this list.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with Connectors access (tier-dependent) and at least one connector or custom MCP server added
items.note: The quoted Code lines moved; the list is rendered in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/index.tsx (ConnectorCard and the filtered rows). The Settings entry control (how the tester first opens Settings) was not confirmed; the path above starts at the Settings screen. Listing is per signed-in account; I found no workspace-level list.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Add custom MCP
steps: Open Settings, tap Cloud, then tap Connectors.
Scroll to the bottom of the list and tap Add custom MCP.
In the Add custom MCP connector sheet, type a Name, type an https:// Connector URL, and optionally an Auth token, then tap Add.

Look for the new server in the connector list (filter Custom) with a status; compare with Expected. Tool use in chat is at the + sheet under Connectors (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx), not confirmed on device.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with Connectors access, and a remote MCP server HTTPS URL to test with

labels.text: Add a remote MCP server by its HTTPS URL to use its tools in chat.

items.note: The URL must be HTTPS (the modal shows a reason line for a non-HTTPS URL). The Add button text is just Add; the sheet's accessibility label is Add connector.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Add custom MCP (Auth token field); for a listed connector, Settings > Cloud > Connectors > [connector name] > Connect
steps: For a custom server: open Settings, tap Cloud, tap Connectors, tap Add custom MCP.
Type the URL and fill the Auth token (optional) field; the field hides the text as you type.
Tap Add, then open the new server and check that it shows as connected.

For a listed connector: open it from the Connectors list and tap Connect. For an API-key connector, enter the key in the sheet and tap Test and save; for an account sign-in connector, follow the sign-in step that opens. Compare with Expected: the token or key is accepted and the connector shows as connected, with no key shown back.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with Connectors access, and a valid token or API key or an outside account to sign in to
items.note: Secure storage is server-side: the custom connector's description reads Your encrypted remote MCP endpoint (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/index.tsx). I did not confirm the on-device storage mechanism. The Connect button is shown only for listings not yet connected, so its exact condition was not traced.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > [a connected connector] > Tool permissions
steps: Open Settings, tap Cloud, tap Connectors, and tap a connector that is Connected.
Scroll down to the Tool permissions heading.
Wait for Loading tools to finish; if it fails, tap Retry loading tools.
Look at the groups Read-only tools and Write and delete tools and the tool names under them. Compare with Expected: the connector's tools are listed.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with Connectors access and a connected MCP server or connector
items.note: Tool names are read from the catalog only after the connector is connected; an unconnected listing shows a note that it lists tools once connected.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > [a connected connector] > Connection health (then Recent calls below it)
steps: Open Settings, tap Cloud, tap Connectors, and tap a connected connector.
Scroll to the Connection health card and read its state and summary line.
Tap Check again to refresh the health reading.
Scroll to the Recent calls section and read the rows (outcomes Worked, Failed or Blocked here). Compare with Expected: health and recent call history are visible for this server.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with Connectors access, a connected connector, and ideally a few tool calls made in chat first
items.note: The Recent calls copy says it shows what the connector was asked to do, without arguments or results. I did not confirm the empty-state text shown before any calls exist.

items.where: Chat > the tool call card in the transcript > Allow once or Deny
steps: Sign in and open a chat that can use tools (AGI Cloud).
Set Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals to Ask before every action.
Ask the agent for an action that needs approval, for example a write.
Tap Allow once on that one card.
Look: only that call runs, and the reply continues with its result.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can use tools
items.note: The quoted code lines in the plan are stale; the buttons are built in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CloudToolApprovalControls.tsx.

items.where: Drawer > AGI Work > open a run labelled Waiting for your approval > Approve
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Work (shown only when cloud tasks are on).
Open a run that has Waiting for your approval.
Read the listed tool calls in that section.
Tap Approve (it approves every pending call of that run at once).
Look: the run continues and the pending calls are no longer listed as waiting.
items.needs: a Cloud task run paused for approval with several pending calls
items.note: Deny is applied to all pending calls in the same way; the tab is labelled AGI Work, not Tasks.

items.where: Chat > the tool call card > Allow for this chat
steps: Open a chat with tools and trigger an approval for a tool.
Tap Allow for this chat on the card.
If the tool is marked destructive, confirm in the dialog that opens.
Ask the agent to use the same tool again in the same chat.
Look: the second call runs without a new card asking first.
items.needs: a Cloud account with a tool that asks for approval
items.note: The button appears only when the server offers the session scope for that tool.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > open a connector > Tool permissions
steps: Open Settings and go to the Cloud group, then tap Connectors.
Open a connected app.
Under Tool permissions, find a tool and read its Policy row.
Tap Allow, Ask or Block on that tool.
Look: the row shows the new choice, and the tool follows it on its next run.
items.needs: a Cloud account with a connected app
items.note: Code shows allow/ask/block per tool only; no single app-wide setting was found. Unset tools follow Action approvals.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals
steps: Open Settings, tap Capabilities, then tap Action approvals.
Choose Run read-only actions without asking.
Close the screen, force-quit the app and open it again.
Open Action approvals again.
Look: the same choice is still selected. Repeat on a second signed-in device if you have one.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account; a second device for the cross-device check
items.note: The sync code is in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/tool-approvals/useToolApprovalPolicySync; I did not read its storage details, so cross-device persistence is unverified.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals
steps: Open Settings, tap Capabilities, then tap Action approvals.
Read the three choices: Ask before every action, Run read-only actions without asking, Skip approvals.
Tap each choice in turn; a Recommended tag sits on Ask before every action.
Look: the selected choice moves, and the Safety default card below updates to match.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account
items.note: Skip approvals is disabled when the workspace blocks it. The short composer labels (Ask, Auto, Skip) are defined in the same file, but I did not find the composer control.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals > Run read-only actions without asking
steps: Open Settings, tap Capabilities, then tap Action approvals.
Tap Run read-only actions without asking.
In a chat, ask the agent to search or read something, then to write or send something.
Look: the read runs with no card; the write stops at an approval card.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with a tool that reads and one that writes

labels.text: Reads, searches, page fetches and sandboxed code run on their own; writes still ask.

items.note: No separate mode with this name exists; the behaviour is the middle option of the same selector.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals > Run read-only actions without asking
steps: Open Settings, tap Capabilities, then tap Action approvals.
Tap Run read-only actions without asking.
In a chat, ask for a search or page read, then for a riskier action such as a delete or a purchase.
Look: the search runs by itself; the riskier action shows a card and waits.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account
items.note: Same control as S59.10; the risk split comes from the server review.

items.where: Chat > the tool call card (above the Allow once and Deny buttons)
steps: Ask the agent for an action that needs approval.
Read the card: the tool summary line, the risk label, and the parameter rows.
Check any notice (for example the private-data notice for high risk).
Look: the card says what the tool will do and why it asks.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with a tool that asks for approval
items.note: The risk label text comes from TOOL_APPROVAL_RISK_LABELS, which I did not locate in packages, so the exact wording is unverified.

items.where: Chat > the approval card for a send (email, message or invite) > read the To row above Allow once
steps: Ask the agent to send an email or message that needs approval.
Read the card before tapping anything.
Find the row for recipients (To, Cc, Bcc, channel or attendees).
Look: the exact address or name appears above Allow once.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a send tool that needs approval
items.note: Row names come from the argument key (humanised), not a fixed string; the recipient key list is in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-stakes.ts.

items.where: Chat > the approval card for an outbound action > read the parameter rows above Allow once
steps: Ask the agent for an action that sends data to a web address or service.
Read the parameter rows on the card, in monospace.
Find the url, host or target row.
Look: the exact destination is shown before you tap Allow once.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a tool that reaches an outside service
items.note: The destination is shown as a parameter row, not as a dedicated label; the stakes code was not fully traced.

items.where: Chat > the approval card for a payment or purchase > read the amount row above Allow once
steps: Ask the agent for a purchase or payment that needs approval.
Read the card before tapping anything.
Find the amount row (for example Amount) and the item row.
Look: the exact amount and what is bought are shown before approval.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a payment tool that needs approval
items.note: Amount and item rows come from argument keys in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-stakes.ts; the exact wording depends on the tool.

items.where: Chat > the approval card for a command > read the parameter rows above Allow once
steps: Ask the agent to run a command that needs approval.
Read the parameter rows on the card (monospace text).
Open Raw JSON to see the full arguments.
Look: the exact command line is shown before Allow once.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a command or code tool that needs approval
items.note: Where the command runs is not shown as its own row; only the arguments are shown.

items.where: Chat > the approval card for a write > read the parameter rows and any stakes above Allow once
steps: Ask the agent to change or create files or records that needs approval.
Read the path and item rows on the card.
Open Raw JSON if you need the full arguments.
Look: the exact file or record names are shown before approval.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a write tool that needs approval
items.note: Records are shown as argument rows; there is no dedicated list of affected records in the code I read.

items.where: Chat > the approval card for a file edit > the diff block above Allow once
steps: Ask the agent to edit a file that needs approval.
Look at the card before tapping anything.
Read the proposed diff block (removed and added lines).
Look: the proposed change is visible before you tap Allow once.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a file edit tool that needs approval
items.note: The diff shows only when the arguments include a before and after shape (detectFileDiff); it is drawn by apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ToolFileDiffBlock.tsx.

items.where: Chat > the approval card > Allow once
steps: Ask the agent for an action that needs approval.
Tap Allow once.
Look: the card changes to Allowed and the tool runs; the result appears in the transcript.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with a tool that asks for approval

items.where: Chat > the approval card > Deny
steps: Ask the agent for an action that needs approval.
Tap Deny.
Look: the card shows Denied, the action does not run, and the agent replies that it was refused.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with a tool that asks for approval
items.note: The model's reply to a denial was not verified from code.

items.where: Chat > the approval card > Add guidance > type in the box > Allow once or Deny
steps: Ask the agent for an action that needs approval.
Tap Add guidance under the card.
Type what to do instead, for example Use the draft folder.
Tap Deny (or Allow once) to send it.
Look: the guidance is sent with the decision and the agent continues from it.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with a tool that asks for approval

labels.text: Tell the agent what to do instead

items.note: The agent's continuation after guidance is not verified from the code I read.

items.where: No control: a pending approval that is no longer live shows an expired line in the chat
steps: Leave an approval card unanswered in a chat for a long time, or let the run pause or end.
Reopen the chat.
Look: the card shows an expired line and its Allow and Deny buttons are not usable.
items.needs: a pending approval that is left unanswered

labels.text: This approval request expired or is no longer active.

items.note: I did not find a fixed time limit in the code read; expiry looks tied to the turn no longer being live (isApprovalTurnLive in stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts). Unverified.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals > Approval history
steps: Open Settings, tap Capabilities, then tap Action approvals.
Scroll to Approval history.
Tap an earlier entry if the list offers it.
Look: past requests appear with their decisions.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with past approvals
items.note: The section is hidden in local-only mode, and it shows a retry message when it fails to load.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > open a connector > Tool permissions > reset a tool
steps: Open Settings, go to Cloud, then tap Connectors.
Open a connector that has a tool set to Allow.
Under Tool permissions, find the tool and tap its reset control (labelled Reset to default).
Ask the agent to use that tool in a chat.
Look: the approval card asks again.
items.needs: a Cloud account with a connector tool set to Allow or an always-allow grant

labels.text: Unset tools follow your Action approvals setting.

items.note: The reset control's visible text was not found; only its accessibility label Reset <tool> to default was. Folder or site grants were not found in mobile code.

items.where: Drawer > AGI Work > open a run labelled Waiting for your approval > Approve (on a second device)
steps: Start a task that pauses for approval on device A.
Sign in to the same account on device B and open AGI Work.
Open the same run and tap Approve.
Look: device A shows the run moving on and the decision recorded.
items.needs: two signed-in devices on the same account and a paused task
items.note: The result on device A depends on a server refresh; I did not confirm the refresh path, so the first-device update is unverified.

items.where: Chat > the approval card for a destructive tool > Always allow or Allow for this chat > confirmation dialog
steps: Ask the agent to run a destructive tool (a delete or change that cannot be undone).
Tap Always allow or Allow for this chat on the card.
Read the dialog title and message; it has Cancel and a confirm button.
Look: the dialog warns before the permission is saved; Cancel leaves the tool asking.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a destructive tool that asks for approval

labels.text: This tool can change or delete data, and its effect may not be reversible.

items.note: The code shows a confirmation dialog for destructive tools; it does not remove the permanent option or force a re-ask. The high-risk private-data notice is in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts.

items.where: No control of its own: the same chat message continues after Allow once, Deny or Add guidance
steps: Ask the agent for a multi-step task that includes one approval.
Tap Allow once on that card.
Look: the same assistant reply continues below the card, without starting a new message.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with a multi-step task that asks for approval
items.note: Resume behaviour is in apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts; I did not trace it fully.

items.where: Chat > the approval card after a decision (the transcript row keeps the decision)
steps: Approve one action with Allow once and deny another with Deny.
Look at each card after the decision.
Read the decided label (Allowed or Denied) and the result or outcome line below it.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with two approval requests
items.note: The outcome text after a run was not traced in detail.

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work > New task
steps: On the chat screen, tap the "Open menu" button.
Tap "AGI Work" in the menu.
Tap the "New task" button (bottom right). On an empty list, the "Hand off a task" card also has a "New task" button.
In the sheet, type what the task should do in "What should it accomplish?", then tap "Start task".
Look for a new task card in the AGI Work list that shows it is running, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: A signed-in account that has AGI Work (the capability canUseAgiWork); the plan that grants it was not verified from the code.
items.note: The "New task" button and the start sheet only appear when the account has canUseAgiWork.

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work
steps: On the chat screen, tap "Open menu", then tap "AGI Work".
Read the title in bold on each task card.
Compare the title with Expected.
items.needs: A signed-in account with at least one AGI Work task.
items.note: The title is the chat's conversation title, or the fallback "AGI work task". The code has no control on the task screen to set or change it, and I did not find the conversation rename menu label, so changing the title is unconfirmed.

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work > New task
steps: Open "AGI Work" from the menu, then tap "New task".
Type the objective in "What should it accomplish?" and tap "Start task".
Open the new task card and read the preview line under its title.
Compare the objective you typed with what the card or task shows.
items.needs: A signed-in account that has AGI Work.
items.note: The objective is shown back as the card preview and the title; the task detail view has no separate objective section.

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work > New task
steps: Open "AGI Work" from the menu, then tap "New task".
Type a goal in "What should it accomplish?".
Type a deliverable in "Deliverable (optional)", for example "A one-page summary".
Tap "Start task", open the task, and compare the result with the deliverable you asked for.
items.needs: A signed-in account that has AGI Work.
items.note: The deliverable is sent with the goal in startWork.ts; whether the run produces it is not confirmed by reading the code.

items.where: Chat screen > "Work" mode switch > send a message > "Plan" card
steps: On a chat, tap "Work" in the mode switch above the input (it is the Work tab).
Type a multi-step request and send it.
When the "Plan" card appears, read the steps. Tap a step to edit it, or use "Add a step" or "Remove this step".
Tap "Start work" to approve, or "Cancel" to reject. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: A signed-in account with AGI Work, on Cloud mode (the plan card is shown only when the app mode is cloud).
items.note: The plan card is rendered from MessageBubble.tsx only when appMode is cloud; whether the agent always produces a plan first was not verified.

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work > tap a task card > Plan section
steps: Open "AGI Work" from the menu and tap a task card.
Scroll to the "Plan" section (its heading reads Plan with a step count).
Read each step line: number, description, then a status.
Compare each status with the work the run has done.
items.needs: A signed-in account with an AGI Work task that has a plan.
items.note: The heading "Plan · N" is built in CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx as a template string.

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work > tap a running task card > Plan section
steps: Start a task with "New task" in "AGI Work" or open one that is in the Running filter.
Tap its card and scroll to the "Plan" section while it runs.
Look for the one step whose status reads "In progress".
Wait a moment and check that the marked step moves on.
items.needs: A task that is still running.
items.note: A step that was running when the run stopped shows "Stopped" instead of "In progress" (CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx).

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work > Needs you > tap the task > answer the form
steps: Open "AGI Work" and tap the "Needs you" filter.
Tap a task that is waiting for a question.
Fill in the questions in the form that appears.
Tap "Send answer" (or "Continue" when there are no fields).
Check that the task moves back to Running and continues.
items.needs: A task where the agent asked a question. The tester cannot force this.
items.note: The form is shown from the run's pending input in CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx.

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work > Needs you > tap the task > Approve or Deny
steps: Open "AGI Work" and tap the "Needs you" filter.
Tap a task that is waiting for approval.
Read the pending action rows.
Tap "Approve" or "Deny", then check that the task continues or stops.
items.needs: A task that is waiting for approval. The tester cannot force this.
items.note: The Approve and Deny buttons are shown in CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx only when the run has a pending approval.

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work > tap a running task > Message the agent
steps: Open "AGI Work" and tap a task that is Running.
Scroll to the "Message the agent" section at the bottom of the task.
Type in "Add instructions or change course" and tap "Send to the agent".
Check that your message appears and that the task keeps going without starting over.
items.needs: A task that is still running, queued or paused.
items.note: The section is shown only while the run is steerable (CloudRunSteerSection.tsx), so it is not shown for finished tasks.

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work > tap a running task > Stop this task
steps: Open "AGI Work" and tap a task that is Running.
Scroll to the bottom and tap "Stop this task".
Read the dialog, then tap "Stop task" (or "Keep it running" to cancel).
Check that the task state changes to stopped, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: A task that is still running.
items.note: The server-side cancel is in apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/service.ts; the server result is not checked by reading the code.

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work > Finished > tap a finished task > Latest output
steps: Open "AGI Work" and tap the "Finished" filter.
Tap a finished task card.
Scroll to the "Latest output" section.
Read the result text and compare it with Expected.
items.needs: A finished AGI Work task.
items.note: There is no separate summary heading; the summary is the latest output section.

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work > tap a task with files > Files section
steps: Open "AGI Work" and tap a finished task that produced files.
Scroll to the Files section and read the file names and sizes.
Tap a file row to open or share it.
If it fails, read the alert text. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: A task that produced a file. A file to produce one may need to be asked for in the task.
items.note: The heading is a template string, "Files · N", in CloudRunFilesSection.tsx, so there is no fixed label to search for.

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work > Finished > tap a stopped task > plan list
steps: Open "AGI Work" and tap a task that was stopped (for example, one you stopped with "Stop this task").
Scroll to the "Plan" section and read the step statuses.
Read the line that says how many steps were done before it stopped.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: A task that was stopped before it finished.
items.note: The line is a template string in CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx: "Done N of M steps before it stopped.".

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work
steps: On the chat screen, tap "Open menu", then tap "AGI Work".
Tap each filter pill: "All", "Needs you", "Running", "Finished".
Scroll down and tap "Load more" if it appears.
Tap any card to open its detail, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: A signed-in account with several past AGI Work tasks.
items.note: The filter pill text comes from CLOUD_RUN_FILTERS in runPresentation.ts.

items.where: Open menu > AGI Work > tap the task > Resume this task (on the second device)
steps: On device A, start a task from "AGI Work" > "New task".
On device B, signed in to the same account, open "Open menu" and tap "AGI Work".
Find the same task card, tap it, and read its state and steps.
Tap "Resume this task" or "Pause this task" on device B, then check device A shows the change.
items.needs: Two devices (or a phone and the web or desktop app) signed in to the same account.
items.note: The task list is loaded from the server (service.ts); the cross-device result was not checked by reading the code.

items.where: Drawer (side menu) > AGI Work > open the task card that says "Waiting for connector input" > the sheet shows "<connector name> needs your input" with a "Send answer" button
steps: Sign in and switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open the side menu.
Tap "AGI Work". The list shows Cloud task cards.
Find a task whose card says "Waiting for connector input" and tap it to open the task sheet.
In the sheet, find the form headed "<connector name> needs your input" (or "Needs your input" when the connector has no name). Fill in the fields.

Tap "Send answer" (or "Decline" or "Cancel" to refuse). Check that the note "Sent. The reply continues once every request in it is answered." appears and the task moves on, matching Expected: the agent asks, waits, and continues after the answer.
items.needs: a Cloud-unlocked account and a running task that has paused to ask a connector for input (hard to trigger on demand; the agent must ask a question through a connector)
items.note: Only connector-input questions have an in-app answer form. Approval prompts are a separate flow ("Waiting for your approval"). The server push "Your agent has a question" (apps/web/lib/services/agent-notification-service.ts) is sent with the approval notification type, and the mobile notification tap opens the Companion screen rather than the task, so the push path to the question is inconsistent with the in-app path. The Tasks route is also named "AGI Work" in the drawer, and a tester may look for the word "Tasks" instead. The code for a question asked through a plain agent message, with no connector, was not found.

items.where: Chat > type "/" in the message box > "compare" > the "Compare Models" screen, read the two model pills at the top (name, then provider name under it)
steps: Sign in and switch the chat to AGI Cloud mode (Local Mode shows a notice and no compare command).
In the message box type "/" and tap "compare" in the list that appears.
On the "Compare Models" screen, look at the pill labelled A and the pill labelled B, separated by "vs".
Check that each pill shows a model name and, under it, the provider name, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account, signed in, on a plan that has at least two cloud models
items.note: The pill shows the provider name from the model registry; I did not verify which plans get two models, only that the screen says so when they do not.

items.where: Chat > type "/" > "compare" > type a prompt and tap send > watch panel A and panel B on the "Compare Models" screen
steps: Open "compare" from the "/" list as in S62.04.
Type a short prompt in the message box and send it.
Watch each panel while it works: the panel shows "Generating..." while its model is streaming.
When an answer finishes, check the panel shows its status (ms to first token, approximate tokens, total time) and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account, signed in, with two cloud models
items.note: Status is shown per panel only as text and small stat chips; the code has no separate status screen.

items.where: Chat > type "/" > "compare" > send a prompt > read the text inside panel A and panel B on the "Compare Models" screen
steps: Open "compare" from the "/" list.
Send a prompt and wait until both panels stop showing "Generating...".
Scroll the screen and read the answer text inside panel A, then inside panel B.
Check that each panel shows only its own model's answer and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account, signed in, with two cloud models
items.note: No separate transcript view was found; each panel's own answer text is the per-agent transcript.

items.where: Chat > type "/" > "compare" > send a prompt > read each panel's result and the "Faster" or "tie" tag on the "Compare Models" screen
steps: Open "compare" from the "/" list and send one prompt.
Wait until both panels finish.
Read panel A and panel B separately, each with its own answer.
Look for the "Faster" badge on one panel or "tie" in the model pills, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account, signed in, with two cloud models
items.note: The "Faster" tag only appears after both answers finish.

items.where: AGI Work (drawer) > Filter chip "Running" > task cards in one list, grouped under "Today", "Yesterday", "This Week" or "Older"
steps: Open the side menu and tap "AGI Work" (shown only in AGI Cloud mode on a plan that includes AGI Work).
Start two or more tasks, or use tasks already running.
Tap the filter chip "Running" to see only running tasks.
Check that several running tasks appear together in the list, each with its state label, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account with AGI Work, and two or more tasks running at once
items.note: The list is a single view of all runs; the section headers come from the code's time grouping.

items.where: AGI Work (drawer) > filter chip "Needs you"
steps: Open the side menu and tap "AGI Work".
Tap the filter chip "Needs you" to show only tasks that wait for you.
Check that tasks in "Waiting for input" or waiting for approval are listed, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account with AGI Work, and at least one task waiting for input or approval
items.note: The default "All" list is not reordered: it sorts by last activity time (runPresentation.ts), so waiting tasks are first only through the "Needs you" filter.

items.where: AGI Work (drawer) > tap a task card that is waiting > in the detail sheet, answer with "Send answer" or tap "Approve" or "Deny"
steps: Open "AGI Work" from the side menu and tap the filter chip "Needs you".
Tap a task card that shows a waiting state.
If the sheet shows "Waiting for your approval", tap "Approve" or "Deny". If it shows an input form, fill it and tap "Send answer".
Check that the task updates while you are still on the task list behind the sheet, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account with AGI Work, and a task waiting for input or for approval
items.note: The approval buttons take their words from TOOL_APPROVAL_ACTION_LABELS; I did not confirm the sheet closes or stays open after an answer.

items.where: AGI Work (drawer) > tap a task card > in the detail sheet scroll to "Latest output" and "Activity"
steps: Open "AGI Work" from the side menu.
Tap any task card.
Scroll the detail sheet to the section "Latest output" and then to "Activity".
Check that the task's output and activity lines match the task's history, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account with AGI Work, and a task that has run
items.note: No separate full-transcript screen was found; the sheet shows the stored transcript, which the store trims to a maximum length (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/store.ts).

items.where: Chat > type "/" in the message box > "compare" > the "Compare Models" screen with two model panels
steps: Sign in and switch to AGI Cloud mode.
Type "/" in the message box; the command list appears.
Tap "compare".
Check that the "Compare Models" screen opens with two model pills, A and B, and a message box, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account, signed in
items.note: In Local Mode the screen shows a notice instead of the comparison.

items.where: Chat > type "/" > "compare" > type a prompt and send > both panels show "Generating..." together on the "Compare Models" screen
steps: Open "compare" from the "/" list.
Type one prompt and tap send.
Check that panel A and panel B both show "Generating..." at the same time.
On a plan that allows one answer at a time, check that panel B shows "Your plan runs one answer at a time, so the second waits for the first." instead, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account, signed in; a plan that allows two answers at once to see true parallel answers

labels.text: Your plan runs one answer at a time, so the second waits for the first.

items.note: Whether the two answers really arrive at the same time depends on the plan's concurrency limit (runsOneAnswerAtATime in compare/index.tsx), which I did not check against the plan table.

items.where: Chat > type "/" > "compare" > tap the model pill A or B on the "Compare Models" screen > choose a model in the picker sheet
steps: Open "compare" from the "/" list.
Tap the pill labelled A (or B) at the top of the screen.
A model picker sheet opens; choose another model.
Check that the pill now shows the new model's name and that the choice is kept for the next prompt, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account, signed in, with at least two cloud models
items.note: Choosing a new model clears the current comparison; the picker offers only the cloud models the plan allows. The picker's own title text was not found.

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > scroll to the bottom > Try a template
steps: Tap the Open menu button (it has no visible text) and tap Schedules.
Scroll to the bottom of the list. If there are no routines, the empty screen shows the gallery.
Look under the heading Try a template for the ready-made cards (for example Weekly review).
Tap a card and check that the Create form opens with that template filled in.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
items.note: The gallery only shows when the account can create schedules; Free accounts see a lock message instead.

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > Schedule a task box at the bottom > Continue scheduling task (arrow) > Create Schedule
steps: Open Schedules from the Open menu.
Tap the Schedule a task box at the bottom and type a prompt, for example: Summarise today's news headlines.
Tap the arrow button (Continue scheduling task), type a time such as Every day at 9am in When should it run?, then tap Create Schedule.
Check that a new card with your prompt appears in the list.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
items.note: The arrow button is an icon with no visible text; its accessibility label is Continue scheduling task.

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > + (Create schedule) > Prompt
steps: Open Schedules and tap the + icon at the top right (accessibility label Create schedule).
Tap the Prompt box and type several lines of instructions; press return to start a new line.
Tap Create Schedule, then tap the new card to open it for editing.
Check that the Prompt box still shows the full multi-line text, then change one line and tap Save Changes.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > + (Create schedule) > Recurrence > Once > Date
steps: Open Schedules, tap the + icon (Create schedule).
Under Recurrence tap Once, then tap the Date field and pick a future date.
Set Preferred time, enter a name and prompt, then tap Create Schedule.
Check that the card shows Once on <month> <day> at <time> and that Next run shows a future time.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > + (Create schedule) > Recurrence > Daily, Weekly or Monthly
steps: Open Schedules, tap the + icon (Create schedule).
Under Recurrence tap Daily, Weekly or Monthly. For Weekly tap the day chips (Su to Sa); for Monthly pick a Day of Month.
Set Preferred time, enter a name and prompt, then tap Create Schedule.
Check the card text: Daily at <time>, Every <days> at <time>, or Monthly on the <n>th at <time>, and that Next run changes to match.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
items.note: The card note says runs are checked on a sweep, so a run can start later in the Cloud window.

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > + (Create schedule) > scroll down to Time zone
steps: Open Schedules, tap the + icon (Create schedule) and scroll down to the Time zone field.
Tap the Time zone field (accessibility label starts with Time zone:), type a city in Search time zones, and pick a zone.
Set a Preferred time, then tap Create Schedule.
Tap the card to edit it and check that Time zone still shows the zone you picked.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > card's More actions (...) button > Run now
steps: Open Schedules and find a routine whose switch is on.
Tap its More actions button (...), then tap Run now.
Watch the card: it shows Starting... and the History section opens.
Check that a new run row appears in Run History with a status and time, and that Last run updates once it finishes.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on and a routine that is switched on
items.note: A paused routine has no Run now; the card hint says Resume this schedule to run it now.

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > card, line Next run
steps: Open Schedules and look at the bottom left of a card.
Read the Next run text (for example in 2h, tomorrow, Overdue or Not scheduled).
Pause the routine with its switch, then check that the text changes to show it will not run.
Resume it and check that the text shows a time again.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > card, line under the prompt
steps: Open Schedules and read the line under each card's prompt.
Check the text: Last run <time ago>, Last run failed <time ago> (in red), or Not run yet.
Run a routine with Run now and check the line updates after the run.
Compare with Expected: the line should show when it last ran and whether it failed.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on and a routine that has run at least once

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > card > History > Run History
steps: Open Schedules and tap History at the bottom right of a card.
Read the Run History list under the card: each row shows a status, a duration and a time.
Tap the refresh icon (Refresh run history) to reload.
Tap the clock icon at the top (Scheduled runs) to see runs from all routines, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on and a routine that has runs
items.note: The card shows the latest five runs; the full list is on the Scheduled runs screen.

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > card > History > run row text
steps: Open Schedules, tap History on a card that has runs.
Look at a run row: the result text appears under its status line, up to six lines.
Long-press the result text to select it, or tap the flag icon (Report this run) if you want to report it.
Compare with Expected: the row should show what that run produced, not only its status.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on and a routine with a finished run that has output
items.note: There is no separate run page; the output shows inside the run row, and the Scheduled runs rows open the routine editor instead.

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > card switch (top right) or More actions (...) > Pause / Resume
steps: Open Schedules and turn off the switch at the top right of a card.
Check that the card stays in the list and its Next run text changes.
Tap its More actions button (...) and tap Resume.
Check the switch is on again and the routine was not deleted.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > tap the card (or More actions (...) > Edit) > Save Changes
steps: Open Schedules and tap a card's body, or open its More actions button (...) and tap Edit.
Change the Schedule Name, the Preferred time or the prompt.
Tap Save Changes.
Reopen the same card and check the new values are shown on the card and in the form.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
items.note: A routine with an unsupported cadence shows Edit this cadence on Web and cannot be edited on mobile.

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > card's More actions (...) > Delete > Delete schedule?
steps: Open Schedules and tap a card's More actions button (...), then tap Delete.
Read the Delete schedule? dialog, then tap Cancel and check the card is still there.
Repeat, and tap Delete in the dialog.
Check the card disappears from the list and its Run History no longer appears.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
items.note: The edit form also has a Delete Schedule button that goes to the same dialog.

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > card text Paused for your approval > History > Needs approval > Approve or Deny
steps: Open Schedules and find a card that says Paused for your approval, so approve or deny it in History.
Tap History on that card.
Find the run row marked Needs approval and read the tool action it asks for.
Tap Approve, then check the run continues; or tap Deny and check the run stops.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on and a scheduled run that is waiting for approval
items.note: The approval request is created by the server during an unattended run, so a tester cannot start one from the app; the approval block itself is in apps/mobile/src/features/schedules/components/ScheduleRunHistory.tsx.

items.where: Open menu > Schedules > card > History > Run History row note
steps: Open Schedules and tap History on a card.
Look at a run row for a note under its status line: Ran late: scheduled for <time>, or Skipped the run scheduled for <time>.
Read the reason in the note (missed by a set amount of time, and whether the schedule skips missed runs).
Compare with Expected: the run history should say that a run was skipped or late and why.
items.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on and a routine whose run was missed or skipped by the server
items.note: The note comes from the server's missed-run record, so a tester cannot force a missed run from the app; the mobile rendering is in apps/mobile/src/features/schedules/components/ScheduleRunHistory.tsx.

items.needs: none
items.note: No code reads the page open in the browser. The only page-related entry is the iOS share sheet, which passes the page URL and any selected text, not the page content. Searched apps/mobile for 'current page', 'currentPage', 'active tab', 'open page', 'browser tab' and 'pageContext' with no page-reading code found, and the cited chatExecutionStore.ts:3295 is cloud turn handling, not page capture.

items.where: Safari > Share button > Share with AGI > Save for AGI Review > open AGI Mobile > Send to Chat
steps: In Safari, select some text on a web page.
Tap the Share button and choose the AGI share extension, titled Share with AGI.
Tap Save for AGI Review.
Open AGI Mobile. The share preview screen shows the selected text.
Tap Send to Chat.
Look in the chat that opens: the assistant's reply should use the selected text as context.
items.needs: a signed-in account or local mode; an iPhone with Safari; the iOS app build with the share extension
items.note: The share extension is iOS only, and the preview screen's send and 'Send to Chat' flow was read from code but the tester should check whether a question can be typed before sending, which the code read did not confirm.

items.where: Safari > Share button > Share with AGI > Save for AGI Review > open AGI Mobile > Summarize this page
steps: In Safari, open a web page, tap the Share button and choose Share with AGI.
Tap Save for AGI Review, then open AGI Mobile.
On the share preview screen, find the two buttons under the shared text.
Tap Summarize this page.
Look in the new chat: a reply starting from the prompt 'Summarize this page.' should appear, with the page link in the message.
items.needs: a signed-in account or local mode; an iPhone with Safari; the iOS app build with the share extension
items.note: The button only appears when the shared text contains an http or https link, and it is disabled when files are attached. The code sends the link text and prompt; whether the assistant opens the page itself is not shown in the code.

items.where: Safari > Share button > Share with AGI > Save for AGI Review > open AGI Mobile > Ask about this page
steps: In Safari, open a web page, tap the Share button and choose Share with AGI.
Tap Save for AGI Review, then open AGI Mobile.
On the share preview screen, tap Ask about this page.
The chat opens with the shared text placed in the message box. Type your own question after it.
Send the question and look at the reply: it should answer using the page's content that was shared.
items.needs: a signed-in account or local mode (the button is disabled otherwise); an iPhone with Safari; the iOS app build with the share extension
items.note: The page content that reaches the answer is the shared text (usually only the URL plus any selected text), not a full read of the page; the code does not show the assistant opening the page.

items.where: Settings > Remote control > Connections (the computer status shows at the top of that screen; the status line reads "Offline" and the banner reads "Desktop unreachable")
steps: Sign in, open the side menu and tap Settings.
Tap Remote control, then tap Connections.
Make the paired computer unreachable (for example, quit AGI Desktop on it or turn its network off) and wait about 90 seconds.

Look for the red "Desktop unreachable" banner with "Reconnecting automatically." and the Reconnect button, or the "Offline" status line with "Make sure ... is running on this computer." Compare with Expected: the app should say the computer is offline and either wait or stop clearly.
items.needs: a computer already paired with AGI Desktop, and access to that computer to stop it
items.note: The Code line pointed to StatusBanners.tsx:42 and that text has moved to line 63 of the same file (the banner is shown when the computer status is 'stale'). The 'Offline' view (ConnectionStateViews.tsx OfflineDesktopView) appears only when a pairing code is held and the status is 'disconnected'; which of the two a tester sees depends on how the computer is stopped, and this was not verified.

items.where: Settings > Remote control > Connections, then the "Start on Desktop" card on the Remote screen (open once a computer is connected)
steps: Sign in, open the side menu and tap Settings.
Tap Remote control, then tap Connections. If no computer is paired, tap "Pair a computer" and scan the QR code shown by AGI Desktop on the other computer.
With the computer connected, find the "Start on Desktop" card and type a short task in the box "What should Desktop work on?".

Tap Send (accessibility label "Send task to Desktop"). Look for the task under "Recent Dispatch tasks" and check whether the other computer starts working on it and replies. Compare with Expected: the user directs work on their own permitted computer from this phone.
items.needs: a paid account that includes remote control (the app checks the remote_control plan capability), a computer paired with AGI Desktop that you own, and that computer turned on and connected
items.note: The live path is known to be unfinished: the dispatch.task.create, dispatch.task.cancel, dispatch.task.reply and dispatch.task.status actions are in the signaling-server allowlist (services/signaling-server/src/control-payload.ts lines 47-50), but the phone-to-computer reply after the signaling server redeploy was not checked here. The mobile code route is the Start on Desktop card in apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/DispatchTaskComposer.tsx, shown from apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/DesktopInfoCard.tsx when connected.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Code > tap a session row
steps: Open the side menu on the first screen after sign-in.
Tap AGI Code.
Look for a list of sessions. Each row shows a title, a status badge, and a line with the time and a location such as On <computer name> or In the cloud.
Tap one session. Its page should open, with the session title at the top.
items.needs: a paired computer with at least one coding session, or a cloud session
items.note: The list is built in apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/CloudCodeSessionsScreen.tsx and holds both computer and cloud sessions.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Code > tap a session > title at the top of the page
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Code.
Read the title on each session row.
Tap a session and read the title in the header. It should match the row.
If the title is empty, the header shows AGI Code instead.
items.needs: a paired computer with at least one coding session, or a cloud session
items.note: No rename action is offered on the coding session pages; the More menu lists only Changes, Plan usage and This computer.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Code > badge on each row, and the badge next to the title inside a session
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Code.
Read the badge on each computer session row: Idle, Running, Needs approval, Failed or Unknown.
Read the badge on each cloud session row: Ready, Running a command, Provisioning, Needs attention or Closed.
Tap a session. A spinner shows while it runs; a badge shows for Needs approval or Failed. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paired computer with coding sessions in different states, or cloud sessions
items.note: Computer sessions have no Closed status in the code; Closed and Archived appear only on cloud sessions.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Code > open a cloud session > Changes icon (top right) > Commands. For a computer session, tap the Ran N steps row in the transcript.
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Code.
Open a cloud session that has run commands, then tap the Changes icon at the top right.
Scroll to the Commands section. Each entry shows the command with a $ prefix, its output, and exit N.
For a computer session, tap the Ran N steps row in the transcript to expand the steps. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a session where commands have run
items.note: For computer sessions the expanded rows show each step's name and summary; no exit status line was found in the code for that view.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Code > open a computer session > Changes pill under the transcript. For a cloud session, Changes icon at the top right.
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Code.
Open a session where files changed.
Tap the Changes pill under the transcript (cloud sessions: the Changes icon at the top right).
Scroll to a file's diff. Added and removed lines should appear marked inside that file's section. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a session in which the agent changed files
items.note: On computer sessions a very long diff shows a note to open it on Desktop instead.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Code > open a computer session > Changes pill > Files
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Code.
Open a computer session where files changed.
Tap the Changes pill under the transcript.
Look at the Files section: each file path is listed. Created files show a New file label, and modified files show an edit icon. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paired computer with a session in which files were created or changed
items.note: The computer session data records only created and modified files, so a deleted file has no place in the summary.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Code > open a cloud session > the Task options control under the message box. For a computer session: More about this session (top right) > Plan usage.
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Code, then open a cloud session.
Tap the small control under the message box (accessibility name: Task options and usage).
Read the Usage section in Task options: Context window and usage buckets with percentages, plus See detailed usage.
For a computer session, tap the More about this session icon at the top right and choose Plan usage. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a cloud session
items.note: The screens show plan usage percentages, not money spent, as far as the code shows.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Code > open a computer session where tests ran > Tests passed or Tests failed pill under the transcript > Test results
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Code.
Open a computer session where tests were run.
Read the Tests passed or Tests failed text in the pill under the transcript.
Tap the pill. Under Test results, check each command, its Passed or Failed badge, the counts such as N passed · N failed, and the output of a failed run.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paired computer with a session in which tests were run
items.note: Cloud sessions show command exit codes and pull request checks, not a test-results panel, in the code read.

items.needs: none
items.note: Searched apps/mobile for continue, handoff, hand off, open on, pick up and move session in the cloud-code and companion folders. The only match is the text You can continue here, which refers to the same session. The More menu item This computer only opens the companion screen and does not move the session. No way to continue in another client was found.

items.where: AGI Code > New session > Describe a task or ask a question
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Code.
Tap New session, choose the repository under Where it runs, and make sure a folder is picked.
In the box Describe a task or ask a question, type: Explain this repository's structure: main parts, entry points, and how they fit.
Tap send and wait for the reply to finish.
Compare the reply with Expected: it should name main parts, entry points and how they connect.
items.needs: a plan that includes managed environments, a GitHub account with a connected repository

items.where: AGI Code > New session > Describe a task or ask a question
steps: Open the side menu, tap AGI Code, then tap New session and pick the repository.
In Describe a task or ask a question, type: Where is the function that starts a session implemented? Give the file and line.
Tap send and wait for the reply.
Compare with Expected: the reply should cite a file and line number.

steps: Open AGI Code, tap New session, and pick the repository.
In Describe a task or ask a question, type: Find every place that uses the name of a chosen function or type, across the repository.
Tap send and wait for the reply.
Compare with Expected: the reply should list references from across the repository.

Tap send and wait for the reply.
Compare with Expected: the reply should follow the call path step by step.

In Describe a task or ask a question, type a free question about the repository, for example: Which package holds the login code?
Tap send and wait for the reply.
Compare with Expected: the answer should come from reading the repository files.

steps: Open AGI Code, tap New session, and pick the repository.
In Describe a task or ask a question, type the feature request, for example: Add a copy button to the settings page.
Tap send and wait until the turn finishes.
Tap the branch icon labelled Changes in the top bar to see which files were created or edited.
Compare with Expected: new or edited files should appear in Changes.

items.where: AGI Code > New session > Describe a task or ask a question
steps: Open AGI Code, tap New session, and pick the repository.
In Describe a task or ask a question, describe the defect and the steps that show it.
Tap send and wait until the turn finishes.
Tap Changes in the top bar to see the edited files.
Compare with Expected: the cause should be named and the code changed to fix it.

steps: Open AGI Code, tap New session, and pick the repository.
In Describe a task or ask a question, type a refactor request, for example: Move the shared date helper into one module and update its callers, with no change in behaviour.
Tap send and wait until the turn finishes.
Tap Changes in the top bar and check that several files changed.
Compare with Expected: the files were restructured and the behaviour stays the same.

steps: Open AGI Code, tap New session, and pick the repository.
In Describe a task or ask a question, type: Write tests for the function in a chosen file.
Tap send and wait until the turn finishes.
Tap Changes in the top bar to see the new test file.
Compare with Expected: a new test file or new test cases should appear.

items.where: AGI Code > open a cloud session > Changes > Commands > Run a command
steps: Open AGI Code and tap an existing cloud session with a repository.
Tap the branch icon in the top bar (labelled Changes).
Scroll down to the Commands section.
Type the repository's test command in Run a command, then tap Run.

steps: Open the app on an iPad (the app is set to support tablets in app.config.js).
Look: the drawer stays on the left side as a fixed panel, not a slide-out.
Look: the chat area is wider and the message grid is laid out in more columns.
Turn the iPad or change split view width and check the layout adapts.
Compare with Expected: persistent drawer and wider layout on tablets.
items.needs: an iPad or iPad Simulator
items.note: The layout switches at 768 px (TABLET_MIN_WIDTH) and 1024 px (REGULAR_MIN_WIDTH) in src/shared/hooks/useTabletLayout.ts.

items.where: Effect seen when a phone is turned sideways with a chat open; the screen should stay upright
steps: Open a chat on a phone.
Turn the phone sideways (on the Simulator, use Cmd+Left or Cmd+Right).
Look: the chat stays in portrait layout.
Compare with Expected: Expected says landscape re-lays out the chat usefully, but the code locks phones to portrait.
items.needs: a phone or Simulator that can rotate
items.note: Phones are locked to portrait (app/_layout.tsx calls lockPhonePortrait; app.config.js sets orientation portrait). Landscape is only used while a video player or presentation viewer is open. The iPad behaviour was not checked.

items.where: Settings > Device > Storage
steps: Tap Settings, go to the "Device" section, tap "Storage".
Look at "Downloaded models (estimated)", "Cache" and "Free space" figures.
Tap "Clear cache" and confirm. Look: the cache figure drops and conversations and models stay.
If a downloaded model is listed, tap "Delete <model name>" and confirm. Look: the model is removed from the list.
Tap "Delete all local data" only on a test account, since it wipes conversations, memory and models from this device.
items.needs: a downloaded model (for the model delete step, see S71.30); a test account for the delete-all step
items.note: Clear cache asks first with the title "Clear cache?" (app/(app)/settings/storage.tsx around line 289).

items.where: Chat screen > "Model:" button beside the + in the composer (opens the model picker) > "On device" group > download a model
steps: Open a new chat. Tap the model button beside the + (it reads "Model:" followed by the model name).
In the model picker, find the "On device" group and tap a model to download it.
Tap "Download" in the confirmation. Look: the download starts and the storage size is shown.
When the download finishes, pick that model, type a message and send it.
Look: a reply comes from the model on the device. Turn Wi-Fi and cellular off on the phone to check it needs no cloud.
items.needs: Wi-Fi for the download; enough free storage; a phone (Simulator may not run on-device models)
items.note: I did not find the exact control that switches a chat from Cloud to Local mode; the picker's On device group is the route found. Check the mode before relying on the steps.

items.where: Settings > Account > Subscription > "Restore purchases"
steps: Tap Settings, go to the "Account" section, tap "Subscription".
Look: if the store is not live you will see "Purchases are not available right now".
Tap "Restore purchases". Look: a message appears such as "No purchases to restore" or "Restore purchases needs the store".
Compare with Expected: buying a plan or credits is not switched on in v1, so the buy path cannot be tested yet.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account; an App Store or Google Play test account for a real restore
items.note: Purchases are switched off: FEATURES.billing is false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts, and src/features/billing/service.ts throws 'cloud billing not available in v1'. Only the restore screen is reachable.

items.where: Settings > Device > Safety & Security > "App Lock" and "Permissions"
steps: Tap Settings, go to the "Device" section, tap "Safety & Security".
Under "Device boundary", turn on the "App Lock" switch and follow the device prompt.
Close the app and open it again. Look: an app lock screen asks you to unlock before the chat shows.
Tap "Permissions" and look at the list of phone permissions (camera, microphone, photos, notifications).
Compare with Expected: App Lock and OS permission management are present; no privacy cover on app switch was found in the code.
items.needs: a device with Face ID or Touch ID set up (not checked on the Simulator)
items.note: The privacy cover on app switch was not found: searched apps/mobile for privacy cover, app switch and AppState usage and found nothing.

items.where: Chat > Choose model > Images chip; then Chat > Add to chat > Photos

Tap the Images chip and check that only models able to read images stay in the list.
Tap Add to chat, then Photos, and choose a picture.
Pick a model that is not in the Images list and send the message.
Look for a refusal or a switch to an image model, and compare with Expected.

items.where: Chat > Add to chat > Photos

Select several pictures.
Pick a model with a low image limit and send.
Read the message shown if the count is over the limit, and compare with Expected.

items.where: Chat > Choose model > Files chip; then Chat > Add to chat > File

Tap Add to chat, then File, and choose a PDF.
Send the PDF with a model that is not in the Files list.
Compare the result with Expected.

items.note: The Files chip matches documentInput or pdf modality. Whether a PDF goes native to the model is in the web request path and is not visible in the app.

items.where: Chat > Start voice mode

Allow the microphone when asked.
Say a short question.
Listen for a spoken reply and watch the live voice bar.
Compare with Expected.

items.where: Chat > (assistant reply) > Read aloud

Listen to the spoken reply.
Tap Stop reading aloud to stop it, then compare with Expected.

items.note: The model used for speech is chosen in the code (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/serverSpeech.ts) and is not shown on screen. The exact control location within the reply was not traced beyond the label.

items.where: Chat > Start voice mode

Allow the microphone.
Ask a question out loud.
Check that the reply is spoken and the live voice bar shows the session.
Compare with Expected.

items.note: The speech-to-speech model is chosen on the server (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts) and is not named on screen.

Type a prompt and send.
Check that the image is made and compare with Expected.

items.note: The tool control is shown as Active chat tools in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx (accessibility label only), so the label is not a visible word.

items.where: Inner routing step; effect visible as the model in the footer under the answer

items.note: Modality classification is in packages/ai/routing/src/classify.ts and has no control of its own.

items.where: Inner routing step; no visible control
steps: Send a very short question and then a long multi-step question with Auto selected.
Compare the footer model under each answer.
items.needs: a Cloud account
items.note: The effort controls in the picker are chosen by the user and are not the routing classification.

items.where: Inner routing step; effect visible as an answer that uses current information
steps: Select Auto and ask about a current event, for example today's news.
Check that the answer shows current information and read the footer for the model used.
items.needs: a Cloud account and an internet connection
items.note: Freshness detection has no visible control; the routing code is in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts.

items.where: Inner filter applied before ranking; effect visible in the model picker list
steps: Open the model picker from Settings > General > Models.
Look for rows that are locked or unavailable and compare them with the models your plan includes.

items.note: The locked-row message is an accessibility hint in apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/components/ModelRow.tsx, not visible text, so no exact visible label was found.

items.where: Server-side route choice; no mobile screen shows which provider route served the answer

items.where: Picking a specific model keeps that model; effect visible in the answer footer
steps: Open Settings > General > Models and pick a specific model that is not Auto.
Send a message, then read the footer under the answer.
Check the footer shows the same model and that no Auto chose line appears.
items.needs: a Cloud account
items.note: The server-side lock is in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts.

items.where: Server-side route choice that considers remaining budget; no mobile control
steps: Note the remaining usage shown in the app, then send several requests with Auto selected.
Check the footer model under each answer as the usage is used up.

labels.text: Available while the provider-funded quota lasts.

items.where: Server-side fallback when a route fails; effect visible only as a different footer model
steps: Send a message with Auto selected and read the footer model.
Repeat during a provider outage if one is known, and check the footer shows a working model.
items.needs: a Cloud account
items.note: The fallback runs in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts; it cannot be forced from the app, so reproduction is not dependable.

items.where: Chat composer > Add to chat (attach an image) > send an image edit request with an image model that cannot edit it > Use <model name> in the alert
steps: Tap Add to chat and attach a photo.
Choose an image model that cannot edit images, then send an edit request.
Read the alert and check whether it offers Use <model name> beside Cancel.
Tap Use <model name> and check that the image model changes.
Compare with Expected: the switch is offered as a one-tap choice.

items.note: The offer exists only for blocked image-edit requests (alertBlockedImageRequest.ts); other plan blocks show a Choose model banner instead, which is not a switch offer.

items.where: Chat (Cloud mode) > message box > type / > compare (Compare model responses) > Compare Models
steps: Open a chat in Cloud mode.
Tap the message box and type /.
Tap compare, which reads Compare model responses.
On the Compare Models screen, choose a model for each slot and send one prompt.
Compare the two answers side by side with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in Cloud account

items.where: Chat > ask a question > read the line under the answer that starts Auto chose
steps: Select Auto and send a question.
Wait for the answer to finish.
Read the line under the answer that starts with Auto chose, with the reason after it.
Compare with Expected: the line should say why Auto picked or moved to a model.
items.needs: a Cloud account
items.note: The line appears only when the answering model differs from the requested one, so it may not show on every answer.

items.where: Chat > send a message > read the footer under the answer (provider · model)
steps: Send any message in a chat.
Wait for the answer to finish streaming.
Read the small grey footer under the answer, which shows provider and model.
Compare with Expected: the model named in the footer should be the one that answered.
items.needs: none
items.note: The footer is hidden while the answer is still streaming.

items.where: Not visible in the mobile app; the routing trace is recorded on the server
items.needs: none
items.note: Searched apps/mobile for routing policy version and trace; only the server-side trace in packages/ai/routing/src/routing-trace.ts and apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/routing-decision-trace-service.ts exist.

items.where: Server-side fallback to a safe default when classification fails; no visible control
steps: Send an unusual or ambiguous message with Auto selected.
Check the answer still arrives and read the footer for the model used.
items.needs: a Cloud account
items.note: A failed classification cannot be forced from the app, so the effect is hard to reproduce on demand.

items.where: Settings > Subscription > What your plan includes
steps: Sign in with a Free account and make sure chat is set to Cloud.
Open Settings and tap Subscription.
Tap What your plan includes.
Look for the Includes heading and the line A usage allowance, free models only, and compare with Expected.

labels.text: A usage allowance, free models only

items.where: Settings > Subscription > What your plan includes
steps: Sign in with a Basic account and make sure chat is set to Cloud.
Open Settings and tap Subscription.
Tap What your plan includes.
Look for the Includes list and the usage line, and compare with Expected.

items.note: No price appears on the plan screen; the price is only shown in the store sheet, which is off in this build.

items.where: Settings > Subscription > What your plan includes
steps: Sign in with a Premium account and make sure chat is set to Cloud.
Open Settings and tap Subscription.
Tap What your plan includes.
Look for the Premium heading and its Includes list, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Premium account
items.note: No plan is labelled Pro in the code; the tier id pro is shown on screen as Premium.

items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Subscription > What your plan includes
steps: Sign in with an Ultra account and make sure chat is set to Cloud.
Open Settings and tap Subscription.
Tap What your plan includes.
Look for the Ultra heading and its Includes list, and compare with Expected.
