items.where: Settings > Subscription > Compare plans
steps: Sign in with a Free account and make sure chat is set to Cloud.
Open Settings and tap Subscription.
Tap Compare plans and read the Includes list.
Trigger a gated feature in chat if one is available, then look for the sheet Not included in your plan and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: In this build the plan list shows only your own plan and the paywall Compare plans button is hidden, so differences are not shown side by side.

items.where: Chat > Model button (shows Model: and the model name) > model picker
steps: Open a chat with chat set to Cloud.
Tap the model button; its label starts with Model: and the hint is Opens the model picker.
Pick a model that supports effort and look for the effort labels such as Balanced, Deep and Maximum.
Tap a locked model on a Free account and look for the See plans alert, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Free account and a paid account to compare
items.note: Server-side clamping is not visible in the UI, and the picker upgrade path does nothing while purchases are off; the effort control has no visible heading text in the code I read.

items.where: Settings > Subscription > Usage > Weekly limits
steps: Sign in with a Cloud account and open Settings > Subscription.
Tap Usage.
Look under Weekly limits for the sub-bucket Most capable models, which appears only when the account has a flagship weekly reset.
Compare the percentage and reset time with Expected.
items.needs: a Cloud account; reaching the cap needs heavy use
items.note: The size of the flagship cap per plan is set on the server and is not shown as a number in the app.

items.where: Settings > Subscription > Upgrade plan
steps: Sign in with a Free account and open Settings > Subscription.
Look at the Upgrade plan row.
Note that the row shows Unavailable in the app and cannot be pressed.
Compare with Expected: no charge or renewal date is shown before confirming, because purchases are off.
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: Purchases are switched off (FEATURES.billing is false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts and nativePurchases is false in apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePurchases.json), so the effective-time text cannot be reached in this build.

items.where: Settings > Subscription (status card), and the Update billing paywall
steps: Use a test account whose renewal failed (past due).
Open Settings > Subscription and read the status card line that says the subscription is past due.
Trigger a paid feature and look for the Update billing button in the paywall.
Compare with Expected: check what access remains and how to fix it.
items.needs: a test account with a failed renewal
items.note: The code shows no grace window: the server comment says a lapsed paid plan is served as Free, and the support corpus says there is no grace period, so the Expected grace rule is not visible.

items.where: Settings > Subscription on each signed-in surface shows the same plan
steps: Sign in with the same account on the phone app and on the web or desktop app.
On the phone, open Settings > Subscription and read the card Your plan, usage, and payment details.
On the other surface, open its billing or subscription page.
Compare the plan name on both surfaces with Expected.
items.needs: a second surface signed in to the same account

labels.text: Your plan, usage, and payment details

items.note: The per-surface gate is enforced by the web gateway and was not checked here; the web comparison page was not located in this pass.

items.where: Settings > Subscription > Compare plans
steps: Sign in with a Free account and open Settings > Subscription.
Read the card In-app purchases are not available yet, which says Compare plans shows what each plan adds.
Tap Compare plans and read the Includes list for the plan.
Compare with Expected: each plan should explain what it adds over the current plan.
items.needs: a Free account

labels.text: In-app purchases are not available yet

items.note: In this build only your own plan is listed, so the Adds over lines and the paywall Compare plans button do not appear.

items.where: Side menu > Settings > Account > Subscription (row shows the plan name); on the Subscription screen, the "Current plan" row
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Tap Account, then the Subscription row (switch to AGI Cloud mode first if the Cloud rows are hidden).
Read the "Current plan" row on the Subscription screen.
Compare the plan name with the account's plan. It shows "Not confirmed" or "Checking…" while the server check is pending.
items.needs: a signed-in cloud account
items.note: The plan is read by the mobile billing screen; the cited apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts is not checked here.

items.where: Side menu > Settings > Account > Subscription > "Renews" row (or "Access ends" / "Trial ends")
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings, then Account, then Subscription.
Find the row labelled Renews (or Access ends, or Trial ends) under Current plan.
Compare the date on that row with the renewal or end date expected for the account.
items.needs: a paid account (the row is hidden on Free)
items.note: Row only appears for a paid, entitled, non-Free plan; the Usage screen also shows "This billing period" with "Resets …" text.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Plan usage" section: bars "Current session", "Weekly limits" and "This billing period"
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings.
Tap the Usage row in the Cloud group.
Under Plan usage, look at the bar labelled "This billing period" (the overall meter) and the "Current session" bar.
Compare each bar's fill and percent with the plan allowance.
items.needs: a paid account (a Free account sees only the "Free plan" screen with an Upgrade button)
items.note: Screen title "Usage" comes from the Settings Cloud group row in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Where your usage went" > "By model" list
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Scroll to the "Where your usage went" card.
Read the "By model" list: each row shows a model name and its request and credit totals.
Compare the rows with the models used in the account.
items.needs: a paid account with usage in the period
items.note: The card only lists rows once there are requests; the "flagship-model cap" bar is "Most capable models" under Weekly limits (packages/contracts/types/src/usage-vocabulary.ts).

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Where your usage went" > "By product area" list
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Scroll to "Where your usage went".
Read the "By product area" list under the period rows.
Compare the rows with the Chat, AGI Work, Deep Research, AGI Code and Browser areas.
items.needs: a paid account with usage

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "This month" card > "Voice" row
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "This month" card.
Read the "Voice" row: it shows minutes used of the monthly amount, or "no monthly cap".
Compare with the voice minutes used in the period.
items.needs: a paid account with a voice allowance
items.note: The card is hidden when the account has no allowance data; the Voice row is built from the server's unit list, not checked against a live response.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "This month" card > "Images" row
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "This month" card.
Read the "Images" row: image count and credits for the period.
Compare with the images generated this period.
items.needs: a paid account that has generated images this period
items.note: The Images row only appears when the account has image requests in the period.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "This month" card > "Video" row
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "This month" card.
Read the "Video" row: seconds used of the monthly amount.
Compare with the video seconds generated in the period.
items.needs: a paid account with a video allowance

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Where your usage went" > "By product area" > "Deep Research" row
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Scroll to "Where your usage went" and read "By product area".
Find the row labelled Deep Research and read its request and credit totals.
items.needs: a paid account that has run Deep Research

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Where your usage went" > "By product area" > "AGI Work" and "AGI Code" rows
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Scroll to "Where your usage went" and read "By product area".
Find the rows labelled AGI Work (agentic work) and AGI Code (coding).
Compare their totals with the coding and agent runs made.
items.needs: a paid account that has used AGI Work or AGI Code

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "File storage" card
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Scroll to the "File storage" card.
Read the "Used" row: used bytes of the plan limit, with a bar below it.
Compare with the files uploaded or generated.
items.needs: a paid account with a storage limit
items.note: The card is hidden when storage data is missing.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "This month" card > "Responses running now" row
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "This month" card.
Read the "Responses running now" row: active responses of the concurrent limit, "at a time".
Start a long response and compare the count.
items.needs: a paid account, and a response that is still running
items.note: The row only appears when the response allowance is returned by the server.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Credit balances" card ("Included in your plan" row, with "left" amount)
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "Credit balances" card.
Read "Included in your plan": credits left and the monthly total.
Compare with the credits expected to remain.

items.note: Bonus and purchased rows only appear in builds where native purchases are on (NATIVE_PURCHASES_AVAILABLE in apps/mobile/src/features/billing/nativePurchaseAvailability.ts).

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Credit balances" card > "Included in your plan" and "Purchased credits" rows
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "Credit balances" card.
Read "Included in your plan" and "Purchased credits" side by side.
Compare that the two rows are separate balances.

items.note: Without native purchases only "Included in your plan" shows.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Credit balances" card > "Bonus credits" row
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "Credit balances" card.
Read the "Bonus credits" row: remaining amount and its "Next expiry" line, or "None".
Compare with a promotion or referral credit the account received.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Credit balances" card ("Next expiry" and purchase expiry lines) and "This month" card ("Resets …" note)
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "Credit balances" card and read the detail under "Bonus credits" ("Next expiry …") and "Purchased credits".
Read the "Resets" note on the "This month" card and the "Resets" card if present.
Compare the dates with each credit's lapse date.
items.needs: an account with bonus or purchased credits
items.note: Purchased-credit expiry text is built in the same file (purchasedRow) and is shown only where native purchases are on.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Plan usage" section: a "Resets in …" line under each bar ("Current session", "Weekly limits", "This billing period")
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Under Plan usage, read the small line under each bar that starts "Resets in".
Wait a few minutes or compare with the clock and check the countdown moves.
items.needs: a paid account with active windows
items.note: The visible text is built from hours, minutes and days; the exact wording is the template in the vocabulary file.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Where your usage went" > segmented buttons "Days", "Weeks", "Months"
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Scroll to "Where your usage went".
Tap Days, then Weeks, then Months.
Compare that the period rows change to daily, weekly and monthly totals.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Work > open a finished task > details sheet with "Cost" and "Usage" rows
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Work.
Tap a task run in the list to open its details sheet.
Read the "Cost" row and the "Usage" row (calls and tokens) in the metadata area.
Compare with the task's work done.

steps: Open the side menu, tap AGI Work, then tap a task run that has finished.
Read the "Cost" row in the details sheet.
Compare with the credits shown on the Usage screen for that period.

Look above the message box for the usage banner with a gauge icon.

items.needs: none

steps: Sign in with an account whose payment has failed (past due or similar).

steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.

Tap Blue. A tick should appear on Blue.
Go back and look at selected controls and highlights. They should use the blue accent.
Tap Neutral to return to the default and check the colours go back.
items.needs: none
items.note: The accent is not applied while the system high-contrast setting is on (apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/useTheme.ts line 34), and the screen shows no notice of that; Neutral is the default.

items.where: Settings > Device > General > Models (then tap a model name)
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Under Device, tap General.
Tap Models. The row on General shows the current model name.
Tap a different model name in the list (a model that cannot be picked opens the model picker instead).
Go back to General and read the Models row, then start a new chat and check the model shown there matches.
items.needs: a Free account can pick free models; a paid account is needed for paid models
items.note: The Models screen has no 'default' wording; the tap sets the one selected model (models.tsx setModel). That new chats start with it was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: Settings > Device > General > Default effort (slider)
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Under Device, tap General.
Find the Default effort slider. If it is missing, the selected model has no effort steps, so choose a model with reasoning first on the Models row.
Drag the Default effort slider to another step.
Leave the screen, come back, and check the slider stays on the new step.
items.needs: a model that offers effort levels
items.note: The slider is shown only when the selected model has effort steps (general/index.tsx line 156); whether a new turn uses the saved value was not traced past the store.

items.needs: none
items.note: No Settings control for a default agent mode was found. The only default written from Settings is effort (setProjectDefault is called only from EffortSlider.tsx); the built-in default is mode 'auto' in apps/mobile/stores/agentControlStore.ts. The Chat or Work switch (WorkModeSwitch.tsx, label 'Chat or Work') is per chat, not a default. Searched apps/mobile for AGENT_MODE_LABEL, 'Ask before edits', 'Edit automatically', useScopedMode and setProjectDefault.

items.where: Settings > Device > General > Haptic Feedback (switch)
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Under Device, tap General.
Turn the Haptic Feedback switch off.
On a phone with haptics, copy a chat reply with its copy control, or trigger an approval prompt, and feel for a vibration. There should be none.
Turn Haptic Feedback on and repeat the same action. A short vibration should be felt.
items.needs: a real phone with haptics (a simulator will not vibrate)
items.note: Haptics are gated in apps/mobile/src/shared/utils/haptics.ts, useCopyAction.ts and ApprovalModal.tsx; the exact visible label of the copy control was not verified.

items.where: Settings > Device > Notifications > Notification Types > Chat replies > Push notifications (switch)
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Under Device, tap Notifications.
Under Notification Types, tap a category such as Chat replies.
Read the Push notifications switch and the Email notifications row under Delivery channels.
Turn Push notifications off, go back, and check the category now shows Off.
items.needs: none; a device that has allowed notifications for push
items.note: Only push can be switched in the app. Email shows 'On the web' and cannot be changed here, and no in-app or browser channel switch was found on the category screen.

items.where: Settings > Device > Time and focus > Enable quiet hours (or Settings > Device > Notifications > Quiet hours row, which opens Time and focus)
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Under Device, tap Time and focus.
Turn on Enable quiet hours.
Tap a day chip to choose days, then set Quiet Hours Start and Quiet Hours End times.
Go back to Notifications and check the Quiet hours row now reads On. Then check the held-notification behaviour against the note on this screen.
items.needs: none
items.note: The app's own reminder says 'This is a reminder, not a lock' (TimeFocusReminder.tsx), and the screen footnote says agent failures and approvals still come through. Whether notifications are actually held on the server was not verified.

items.where: Settings > Account > Email (Cloud mode, signed in). Photo: the badge "Change profile photo" on the top Settings card. Local name: Settings > Assistant > Personalization > Full Name
steps: Sign in and switch the mode toggle at the top of Settings to Cloud.
Open Settings > Account > Email. Tap the name under the avatar (accessible name "Edit display name"), type a new name and tap Save.
Back on the top Settings card, tap the photo badge ("Change profile photo") and choose a picture.
Check the name and photo on the top Settings card and on the Email screen match your change. Tap the Email row and check it starts an email-change flow, not a direct save.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and Cloud mode; a photo to choose
items.note: Name and email editing exist only on the Cloud Email screen; in Local mode the name is Full Name under Personalization. The Profile screen (tapping the top card) has no edit controls.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Personalization > Custom Instructions
steps: Open Settings > Assistant > Personalization.
Tap the field "Custom Instructions" and type a rule, for example "Answer in one short paragraph".
Tap Save at the top right.
Start a new chat, ask a question, and check the reply follows the rule. Clear the field, tap Save, and check the next reply no longer follows it.
items.needs: none (Local mode works; Cloud needs a signed-in account)

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Personalization > Style Preset, Response Length, Technical Level, Response Language
steps: Open Settings > Assistant > Personalization.
Change "Style Preset" and "Response Length", and "Technical Level" if you want.
Tap Save at the top right.
Start a new chat, ask the same question twice with different settings, and compare the tone, length and formatting with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Formatting is not a separate control here; the choices are Style Preset, Response Length, Technical Level and Response Language.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory
steps: Open Settings > Assistant > Memory.
Turn the "Memory" switch on. Tap the control whose accessible name is "Add memory" and type a fact, then save it.
Start a new chat and ask something that uses that fact; check the reply uses it.
Edit or delete the memory from the list, turn "Memory" off, ask again, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: "Add memory" is an accessible name with no visible text in the code.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory > Search and reference chats
steps: Open Settings > Assistant > Memory.
Turn on "Search and reference chats".
In a new chat, ask about a topic from an older chat and check the reply refers to it.
Turn "Search and reference chats" off, ask again, and compare. Check a Temporary Chat is not referenced.
items.needs: at least one earlier chat with known content

items.where: Settings > Device > General > Temporary Chat
steps: Open Settings > Device > General.
Turn "Temporary Chat" on, then start a new chat and send a message.
Open the chat list and check the chat is not saved there.
Turn "Temporary Chat" off, send another message and check that chat is saved.
items.needs: none
items.note: No separate on/off switch for chat history was found. Temporary Chat is the nearest control; Sync Local Chats to Cloud under Data Controls is a one-time copy.

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Privacy (Cloud mode, signed in), section "Model training"
steps: Switch to Cloud mode and make sure you are signed in.
Open Settings > Assistant > Privacy and scroll to the section "Model training".
Check the row "Only use models that do not train on your chats" and the "Use my chats" and "Use my voice" rows under the improvement heading.
Turn a row on or off and check it saves and stays after reopening the screen. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and Cloud mode

labels.text: Only use models that do not train on your chats

items.note: The code audit cited ProviderTrainingOptOutGroup.tsx, which no longer exists; its role is now in TrainingPreferenceGroups.tsx. The owner decision on this item is open.

items.where: Settings > Device > General > Temporary Chat
steps: Open Settings > Device > General and turn "Temporary Chat" on.
Start a new chat and send a message, then check it is not in the chat list.
Ask in that chat what you remember about the user and check no saved memory is used.
Turn "Temporary Chat" off and compare the next new chat.
items.needs: none
items.note: The same switch also appears under Settings > Privacy > Chat privacy. I did not verify that it applies to every new chat by default.

items.where: Settings > Cloud > Archived Chats (Cloud mode, signed in)
steps: Switch to Cloud mode and sign in.
Open Settings > Cloud > Archived Chats.
Tap "Restore" on one chat, then open the chat list (refresh if needed) and check it is back.
Tap "Delete" on another archived chat and confirm "Delete this chat?". Check it leaves the list.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least two archived chats

items.where: Settings > Data Controls > Chat history > Delete all chats (cloud), or Settings > Data Controls > Local chats > Delete all chats (this device)
steps: Open Settings > Data Controls.
Under "Chat history", tap "Delete all chats". Read the alert "Delete all chats?" and check it says archived chats are included and that the cloud copy says restorable on the web for 30 days.
Confirm through the second prompt ("Are you absolutely sure?" then "Yes, delete all chats").
Check the chat list and Archived Chats are empty. Use a test account only.
items.needs: a test account with several chats, some archived
items.note: The local version says it cannot be undone. Compare the copy against Expected for restore wording.

items.where: Settings > Account > Shared Links (Cloud mode, signed in)
steps: Switch to Cloud mode and sign in.
Open Settings > Account > Shared Links and check the list of shared links.
Tap "Revoke" on one link and confirm "Revoke this link?" > "Revoke".
Check the link now shows as revoked or gone, and that opening it no longer works.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one shared chat
items.note: The Shared Links screen lists shared chat links only; no published-pages list was found in the code.

items.where: Settings > Data Controls > Local data > Export Local Data (this device), or Settings > Data Controls > AGI Cloud account > Export Cloud data (cloud)
steps: Open Settings > Data Controls and tap "Export Local Data". Wait until "Exporting…" finishes.
Save or share the file it offers and open it.
For cloud, go to Settings > Data Controls > AGI Cloud account > Export Cloud data, tap "Export Cloud Data" and save the file.
Open the file and check it holds chats, memory, files and settings, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account for the cloud export

items.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory > upload icon (accessible name "Import memories", shown only when Memory is on)
steps: Open Settings > Assistant > Memory with Memory on.
Tap the upload control (accessible name "Import memories").
Choose a text or JSON file, or paste text, then tap "Preview" and select the memories.
Tap the import button ("Import N memories") and check the memories appear in the Memory list.
items.needs: a text or JSON file with memories from another assistant
items.note: The upload control has no visible text; its accessible name is "Import memories" in apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/memory.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Device > Storage > Delete everything ("Clear cache" is separate)
steps: Open Settings > Device > Storage.
Tap "Delete everything" and read the confirmation, which lists conversations, memory, settings and downloaded models.
Confirm only on a test device. Check that the chats, memory and settings are gone after the wipe.
Use "Clear cache" separately and check it only removes temporary files.
items.needs: a test device with local data
items.note: The on-screen copy says conversations, memory and models; the confirmation also names settings. This wipe is destructive.

items.where: Settings > Data Controls > AGI Cloud account > Delete account (signed in), then the Delete Account row
steps: Sign in and open Settings > Data Controls.
Tap "Delete account" under "AGI Cloud account". On the next screen tap "Delete Account" under "Your AGI Cloud data".
Read the "Delete Account" confirmation (scheduled deletion, sign in to cancel before the deadline, export first) and tap Cancel to stop.
Check the result. Do not confirm on a real account.
items.needs: a signed-in test AGI Cloud account
items.note: Deletion is only scheduled; cancellation is possible until the deadline shown after scheduling. Use a test account only.

items.where: Profile > Security and login > Manage (AGI Cloud section; also Settings > Security and login)
steps: Sign in with an AGI Cloud account and open the Profile tab.
Tap "Security and login" in the AGI Cloud section.
Read the "Sign-in methods" group: each linked sign-in appears as a row showing "Last used" or "Linked".
Tap "Passkeys and security keys" and look for "Add a passkey or security key".
Tap "Add or remove a sign-in method" to see that it opens the web security page.
Compare with Expected: password, passkeys and social/SSO identities are all visible, and methods can be added or removed.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account, cloud mode
items.note: Adding or removing sign-in methods other than passkeys is done on the web, not in the app.

items.where: Profile > Security and login > Change password
steps: Open Profile, tap "Security and login" in the AGI Cloud section.
Tap "Change password" (it reads "Set a password" if the account has none).
Fill "Current password", "New password" and "Confirm new password", then tap "Change password" in the sheet.
Read the "Password changed" alert and check that other sessions are signed out.
For a forgotten password, go to the sign-in screen and tap "Forgot password or try another way".
Compare with Expected: change works with the current password; reset is started from the sign-in screen.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account that has a password and its current password; an outside sign-in service for reset

labels.text: Forgot password or try another way

items.note: The forgot-password screen in the app only tells the user to visit the website and choose Forgot password; the reset itself is not done in the app.

items.where: Profile > Security and login > Two-factor sign-in
steps: Open Profile, tap "Security and login", then scroll to "Two-factor sign-in".
Tap "Set up authenticator app" and scan the QR code, or use "Copy setup key".
Type the code from the authenticator app into "Authenticator code" and tap "Turn on".
Check that the "Authenticator app" row now shows on and "Turn off two-factor" appears.
Tap "Turn off two-factor", then "Turn off" in the alert, and check the row goes back to off.
Compare with Expected: turning on makes a code required at sign-in, and it can be turned off.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and an authenticator app on a phone
items.note: The section appears only when the server reports two-factor as available or on; the code that asks for the second factor at sign-in was not found in this screen's code.

items.where: Profile > Security and login > Two-factor sign-in > Backup codes
steps: With two-factor on, open "Security and login" and scroll to "Two-factor sign-in".
Read the "Backup codes" row, which shows "Ready" or "Not set".
Tap "Generate new backup codes" and complete the step-up check if asked.
Tap "Copy codes" or "Save or share" on the codes screen.
Tap "I saved these codes" to finish.
Compare with Expected: codes can be viewed, saved and regenerated.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account with two-factor on
items.note: No control opens the existing codes; they are shown only right after generating new ones, so viewing an old set is not possible in the app.

items.where: Profile > Security and login > Sessions
steps: Open Profile, tap "Security and login", then scroll to the "Sessions" section.
Read the device rows under "Devices": each shows the device name and a last-active value.
Tap a row that is not this device.
Read the alert "Sign out this device?" and tap "Sign out".
Compare with Expected: the session is listed with device, place and last active, and can be ended.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account with at least one other signed-in session
items.note: The current device row has no tap action, and a row "This device could not be matched to a listed session" appears when the current session is not found; place is not shown in the row text.

items.where: Settings > AGI Code > Remote control
steps: Open Settings and tap "AGI Code".
Tap "Remote control" (shown only when the companion feature is on).
On the companion screen, read the desktop card with the "Paired" badge and its name.
Tap "Disconnect" and then "Disconnect" in the alert.
Compare with Expected: the desktop is listed as paired and the pairing can be removed.
items.needs: a desktop app already paired by QR code
items.note: Only one desktop card is shown; a browser-to-desktop pairing list was not found in this screen, and the "Remote control" row depends on a feature flag.

items.where: Profile > Log Out (AGI Cloud section)
steps: Open the Profile tab in cloud mode while signed in.
Scroll to the "AGI Cloud" section and tap "Log Out".
Read the alert "Log out of AGI Cloud on this device?".
Tap "Cancel" once to check it leaves you signed in, then tap "Log Out" again.
Compare with Expected: the app signs out on this device and returns to sign-in.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account, cloud mode

labels.text: Log out of AGI Cloud on this device?

items.note: This signs out only this device; the Log Out row is shown only in cloud mode with a cloud account.

items.where: Profile > Security and login > Sessions > Log out of all devices
steps: Open Profile, tap "Security and login", then scroll to the "Sessions" section.
Tap "Log out of all devices" (shown in cloud mode only).
Read the alert "Log out of all devices?" and tap "Log out everywhere".
Check that the app returns to sign-in.
Compare with Expected: one action signs out every browser, app and device.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a second signed-in device or browser to check
items.note: The app only calls the server action; whether every device credential is revoked is decided on the server and was not verified from the code.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > tap a connected connector > Disconnect
steps: Open Settings and tap "Connectors" (cloud mode).
Tap a connector that shows as connected.
Find the "Connected" row and the "Granted access" section.
Scroll to the bottom and tap "Disconnect", then "Disconnect" in the alert.
Compare with Expected: the connector leaves the list, or a notice says it is disconnected.
items.needs: a connected third-party connector

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Camera and files > Permissions > Microphone
steps: Open Settings and tap "Capabilities".
Tap "Camera and files".
Tap "Microphone" in the Permissions list.
Read the status and the level choices shown on the detail screen.
Tap the request button if shown, then compare with Expected: the user sees and can change microphone access.
items.needs: none; a phone with the microphone permission in either state
items.note: The app can only request the permission from the system; a permission already denied may need the iOS Settings app, which was not verified.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Camera and files > Permissions > Camera
steps: Open Settings and tap "Capabilities".
Tap "Camera and files".
Tap "Camera" in the Permissions list.
Read the status and the level choices on the detail screen.
Tap the request button if shown, then compare with Expected: the user sees and can change camera access.
items.needs: none; a phone with the camera permission in either state
items.note: The app can only request the permission from the system; a permission already denied may need the iOS Settings app, which was not verified.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > tap a connector > Tool permissions
steps: Open Settings and tap "Connectors".
Tap a connected connector.
Scroll to "Tool permissions".
Set a tool to "Allow" or "Block" and reopen the connector.
Check the choice is kept, and set it back to "Ask" to remove the saved choice.
Compare with Expected: saved always-allow and always-deny choices can be reviewed and removed.
items.needs: a connected connector that lists tools
items.note: The saved choices are listed per connector only; no single screen lists every saved approval, and removing by setting back to Ask was not verified.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals
steps: Open Settings and tap "Capabilities".
Tap "Action approvals".
Read the three choices: "Ask before every action", "Run read-only actions without asking" and "Skip approvals".
Tap one choice and check that it is marked as selected.
Ask chat to run a connector action and compare what AGI asks before doing it with Expected.
items.needs: a connected connector to test the approval
items.note: The "Skip approvals" choice is disabled when the workspace does not allow it; Expected names "auto-approve safe", but the middle choice is "Run read-only actions without asking".

items.where: Profile > Security and login > Lockdown mode
steps: Open Profile, tap "Security and login".
Scroll to the "Lockdown mode" switch, below "Recent security activity".
Read its description: "Blocks connectors, web access, code execution and Deep Research."
Turn it on, then try a chat that uses web search or running code.
Compare with Expected: stronger limits apply; turn it off again to restore normal use.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account, cloud mode
items.note: No control named hardened mode was found; "Lockdown mode" is the closest control, it shows only after its state loads, and "Advanced Account Security" opens a web page.

items.where: Settings > Account > Workspace (the row labelled "Workspace"), then the screen titled "Workspace"
steps: Sign in with a cloud account that is an owner or admin of a Team or Enterprise workspace.
Open Settings and tap the row "Workspace" in the "Account" section.
On the "Workspace" screen, look at the top card: the workspace name, its plan label, the line "N of M seats used" and the line "You are <role>".
Scroll down to the "Workspace administration" block and look at the "Seats and invitations" section and the security groups below it.
Compare with Expected: name, plan, members/seats and security posture should all be on screen and match the live workspace.
items.needs: a cloud account that is an owner or admin of a Team or Enterprise workspace; phone width
items.note: The security posture group titles and rows come from the server (fetchWorkspacePosture), so their exact wording is not in the app files. The overview card's name and plan lines were not checked line by line. The admin block only appears when canManage is true and a workspace exists. Non-entitled accounts see a plan message instead.

items.where: Settings > Account > Workspace, then the "Members" list on the "Workspace" screen
steps: Sign in with an owner or admin account in a workspace that has more than one member.
Open Settings, tap "Workspace" in the "Account" section.
Scroll to the "Members" heading.
Check each member row shows the name (your own row ends with " (you)"), the email under it, and the role title such as "Owner".
Compare with Expected: every member should appear with name, email and role.
items.needs: an owner or admin account in a workspace with at least two members (a second account in the same workspace helps); phone width
items.note: The member list is loaded by fetchWorkspaceMembers in apps/mobile/src/features/team/service.ts. Email is shown only when the member has one. The source path was used for the section in the code audit; the code at the cited line 600 was not re-read in full.

items.where: Settings > Account > Workspace > "Workspace administration" block > "Invite by email" row. Pending invitations are the rows under "Seats and invitations"
steps: Sign in with an owner or admin account and open Settings > "Workspace".
Scroll to "Workspace administration" and tap the row "Invite by email".
In the "Invite by email" sheet, type an email address, pick a role, then tap "Send invitation".
Look at the "Seats and invitations" list: the new invitation appears as a row with the email, and its value shows the role and expiry (for example "Member · <date>").

Tap a pending invitation row: choose "Resend invitation" or "Revoke invitation". Revoke asks "Revoke this invitation?" with "Cancel" and "Revoke". Compare with Expected: invite, see pending, renew, revoke.
Accepting is done by the invitee: open the invitation email on a second account and follow the link. The acceptance step was not traced in this scope.
items.needs: an owner or admin account; a second email address for the invitee; a seat available in the workspace
items.note: The invitee's accept step was not found in apps/mobile; it likely happens on the web via the emailed link (invitationLink in apps/mobile/src/features/team/administration.ts). Not verified. The invitation block is shown only when canManage is true and the workspace exists.

items.where: Settings > Account > Workspace > Members list > "Change role" under a member > role picker titled "Role for <name>"
steps: Sign in with an owner or admin account in a workspace with another member.
Open Settings > "Workspace" and find a member row that is not yourself.
Tap "Change role" under that member, then look at the sheet titled "Role for <name>" and read the radio options and the permissions list shown under the chosen role.
Pick a different role and tap "Save role". Look at the member row: the role title should now show the new role.
Compare with Expected: the roles and their permissions are shown, and the change sticks after reloading the screen. Owner is only offered to the current owner.
items.needs: an owner or admin account and a second member in the same workspace
items.note: The role names and permission wording come from BUILT_IN_ORGANIZATION_ROLES and ORGANIZATION_PERMISSION_COPY outside apps/mobile/src/features/team, not checked. Server enforcement is not visible in the app; a failed change shows the alert "Could not change role".

items.where: Settings > Account > Workspace > Members list > "Change role" under another member > choose Owner > "Transfer ownership"
steps: Sign in as the current owner of a workspace that has another member.
Open Settings > "Workspace", tap "Change role" under another member.
In "Role for <name>", tap the Owner option. Read the warning text that appears: it says the member takes over billing and every admin control, and that only they can give ownership back.
Tap "Transfer ownership" and complete the verification step if one appears.
Compare with Expected: after confirmation, the member row shows the role "Owner", and your own row no longer shows the owner role.
items.needs: the current owner account of a Team or Enterprise workspace and a second member; a way to complete the verification step
items.note: Ownership moves through withStepUp in apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/workspace.tsx, so a verification prompt is expected. The atomic server move was not checked. On failure the alert reads "Could not transfer ownership".

items.where: Open the side menu > Settings > About > Contact Support > New ticket
steps: Sign in with a Cloud account and make sure the app is in Cloud mode.
Open the side menu, tap Settings, then tap About.
Tap Contact Support (it only appears for a signed-in Cloud user; Email Support is always there).
Tap New ticket, type a Subject and What happened, then tap Raise ticket.
Open the new ticket from the list, type in Write a reply, tap Send reply.
Compare: the ticket shows in the list with its status, and replies from support appear in the ticket thread.
items.needs: a Cloud account (signed in) in Cloud mode; replies come from the support team, so a reply may not arrive during the test
items.note: The ticket list and ticket screens exist; whether support replies arrive cannot be checked from the code.

items.where: Open the side menu > Settings > Support > Report App Issue > Bug Report
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings.
In the Support group, tap Report App Issue.
Tap the Bug Report chip and type in the box (placeholder: What happened? What did you expect to happen?).
Tap Submit Feedback (Cloud mode) and read the Thank You! alert.
Compare: in Cloud mode the app sends the app version and platform with the report; in Local mode the button reads Email Feedback and opens the mail app.
items.needs: a Cloud account for the stored-report path; a mail app for Local mode
items.note: In Local mode the mailto link carries only the subject and message, not the build or platform, which differs from Expected.

items.where: Open the side menu > Settings > Support > Report App Issue > General Feedback
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings, then in the Support group tap Report App Issue.
General Feedback is selected by default; tap it to confirm.
Type a message in the box (placeholder: Tell us what you think...).
Tap Submit Feedback.
Compare: the Thank You! alert appears with Your feedback has been submitted.
items.needs: a Cloud account for server storage; a mail app for Local mode
items.note: The app shows only the confirmation; the team-side storage cannot be checked from the app.

items.where: Open the side menu > Settings > Support > Report App Issue > Feature Request
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings, then in the Support group tap Report App Issue.
Tap the Feature Request chip.
Type in the box (placeholder: Describe the feature you would like...).
Tap Submit Feedback.
Compare: the Thank You! alert appears with Your feedback has been submitted.
items.needs: a Cloud account for server storage; a mail app for Local mode

labels.text: Describe the feature you would like...

items.note: Storage for the team is not visible from the app.

items.where: Open the side menu > Settings > Support > Export Diagnostics
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings, then in the Support group tap Export Diagnostics.
Read the Share diagnostics? alert: it sends app, device and error details, never messages, files or passwords.
Tap Continue; the system share sheet titled Share your AGI diagnostics opens with a .json file.
If the share sheet lets you preview the file, open it to see the fields (app version, platform, locale, time zone, screen size, recent errors); otherwise cancel.
Compare: the Diagnostics exported alert shows a summary, and the user picks the share target in the share sheet.
items.needs: none
items.note: The app has no in-app list of bundle contents; the user sees them only in the .json file in the share sheet. The share sheet sends to any app the user picks, not a built-in support button.

items.where: Chat > the notice under a reply that failed
steps: Open Chat and send a message.
If the reply fails with an error notice, read the text under the reply.
Compare: the notice ends with Reference: followed by an id that the user can quote to support, and it may say Tap to try again.
If no id appears, the server did not log one for that failure.
items.needs: a reply that fails; this cannot be forced reliably from the UI
items.note: The id is shown only when the server logged one; the server side is in apps/web/lib/error-handler.ts and was not traced further.

items.where: Open the side menu > Settings > Privacy > Helpful resources > Data rights requests
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings, then tap Privacy.
Scroll to the Helpful resources group.
Tap Data rights requests; a web page (/privacy/requests) opens in the browser.
Compare: the web page should let the user submit access, correction or erasure requests and show their status.
items.needs: a Cloud account (the Privacy row sits in the Cloud section of Settings)
items.note: The app only opens a web page; the request form and status tracking live on that web page, which was not checked from the mobile code.

items.where: Chat > long-press an AI reply > Report…
steps: Send a message in Chat and wait for the AI reply to finish.
Long-press the AI reply.
Tap Report… ; the sheet titled Report this response opens.
Pick a category such as Harmful or dangerous, then type in the box (placeholder: Describe the issue...).
Tap Save report.
Compare: the sheet shows Report submitted for review (or Send this report to AGI? if it was saved on the device).
items.needs: a Cloud account for server delivery; in Local mode the report is saved on the device or sent by email
items.note: The MessageBubble.tsx file holds the ellipsis as the escape …, which renders as Report… ; the moderation intake was not traced past services/contentReport.ts.

items.where: Chat > the notice under a reply the model declined for safety reasons > Report
steps: Send a message in Chat that gets a safety refusal (cannot be forced reliably from the UI).
Read the notice: The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons.
Tap Report on the notice; the screen titled Report an incorrect refusal opens.
Type the reason and tap Submit Feedback (Cloud mode) or Email Feedback (Local mode).
Compare: the Thank You! alert appears and the app goes back.
items.needs: a reply that is refused for safety reasons; a Cloud account for server submission

labels.text: The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons.

items.note: The notice shows only for refusal finish reasons; in Local mode the appeal goes out through the mail app.

items.where: Chat: open a conversation > long-press the AI answer > Report… > choose a reason > Save report. Public page: Sites (drawer entry, shown as "Sites") > Shared with you > More options for <site name> > Report > choose a reason > Save report.
steps: Sign in, open a conversation that has an AI answer (not one still streaming).
Long-press the AI answer to open its action menu.
Tap "Report…" in the menu.
Tap a reason such as "Harmful or dangerous" (there is no infringement option; "Other" is the closest), then tap "Save report".
Read the result screen: "Report submitted for review" means it reached the server. "Send this report to AGI?" or "Report saved on this device" means it was kept on the phone; tap "Send" if shown.
For a public page: open Sites, switch to "Shared with you", tap "More options for <name>", tap "Report", then repeat the reason and "Save report" steps and compare the result screen with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account; an AI answer in a chat; for the Sites path, a site shared with you by a second account and an outside account is not needed
items.note: The Code line's quoted lines are gone, but the report flow exists: the menu item is written as 'Report…' (shown as "Report…") in MessageBubble.tsx, and the sheet is ReportFlagButton.tsx. The reason list has no infringement option, while Expected says harmful or infringing. The Sites report path is in SharedSitesList.tsx (Alert button "Report"). Whether the report reaches operators is not visible in the UI beyond the result text; I did not verify the server route apps/web/app/api/mobile/content-report/route.ts.

items.where: Chat > Message input > Add to chat (+) > Deep research; results appear in Reports (drawer)
steps: Sign in and open the Chat tab, in Cloud mode with a model that supports research and search.
Tap the + button (Add to chat) next to Message input.
Look for the Deep research row and switch it on. If the row is missing, the plan or model does not allow it.
Type a financial question, for example about a stock, an ETF or a company's filings, and send.
Open the Reports list from the drawer and open the report.
Compare with Expected: a research answer for markets, instruments or filings, with sources cited.
items.needs: a Cloud account on a plan that grants Deep research
items.note: No separate financial workspace exists on mobile. The FMP connector is listed only in the web vendor directory, and I did not confirm that the mobile Connectors row shows it. The + button's label is an accessibility label, not visible text.

items.where: Chat > Message input > Add to chat (+) > Deep research; results appear in Reports (drawer)
steps: Sign in and open the Chat tab in Cloud mode.
Tap the + button (Add to chat), then switch on Deep research.
Type a request for a company profile, for example business, financials, news and competitors, and send.
Open Reports in the drawer and open the new report.
Compare with Expected: a sourced profile of the company covering business, financials, news and competitors.
items.needs: a Cloud account on a plan that grants Deep research
items.note: No company-profile screen or card exists on mobile; the profile depends on the generic Deep research output and the FMP connector in the web vendor directory.

items.where: Chat > Message input > Add to chat (+) > Connectors (for CourtListener, Descrybe, Midpage) or Deep research
steps: Sign in and open the Chat tab in Cloud mode.
Tap the + button (Add to chat) and then Connectors.
Turn on a legal connector such as CourtListener.
Back in the chat, type a legal question, for example a case-law search on a point of law, and send.
Compare with Expected: case law and statutes returned with cited authorities.
items.needs: a Cloud account; a legal connector may need its own sign-in
items.note: No legal workspace screen exists on mobile. The legal connector names are in the web vendor directory, and I did not confirm that the mobile Connectors list shows them.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > find review-contract > Install > Use in chat
steps: Open Settings and tap Customize (Cloud section).
Tap Skills and find review-contract, or search for it.
Tap Install, then tap Use in chat.
In the chat, send a contract to review and ask for clauses, risks and redlines against a playbook.
Compare with Expected: clauses are extracted, risks flagged and redlines suggested against a playbook.
items.needs: a Cloud account, and a contract file to upload
items.note: The skill is in the repo as review-contract (triage-nda is a related skill). Mobile shows only the skills the Cloud catalog returns, so I did not confirm that this one is listed. Skills can also be picked from Add to chat > Skills.

items.where: Chat > Message input > Add to chat (+) > Connectors (Consensus, alphaXiv) or Deep research
steps: Sign in and open the Chat tab in Cloud mode.
Tap the + button (Add to chat) and then Connectors.
Turn on Consensus or alphaXiv.
Ask a science question, for example for a literature review on a topic, and send.
Compare with Expected: papers are searched and a cited synthesis is returned.
items.needs: a Cloud account
items.note: No scientific workspace screen exists on mobile. The connector names are in the web vendor directory, and I did not confirm that the mobile Connectors list shows them.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > find pipeline-review or deal-review > Install > Use in chat
steps: Open Settings and tap Customize.
Tap Skills, find pipeline-review or deal-review, and tap Install.
Tap Use in chat, or pick the skill from Add to chat > Skills.
Ask for a pipeline review or a deal review of a named opportunity, and send.
Compare with Expected: pipeline or deal health, risks and next actions from CRM data, if a CRM connector is on.
items.needs: a Cloud account; a CRM connector turned on for live data
items.note: Updating CRM records is not described by these skill files on mobile; I did not find a CRM-specific screen in apps/mobile.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > find ticket-triage, draft-response or customer-escalation > Install > Use in chat
steps: Open Settings and tap Customize.
Tap Skills, find ticket-triage, draft-response or customer-escalation, and tap Install.
Tap Use in chat, or pick the skill from Add to chat > Skills.
Paste a support ticket and ask for triage, a reply or an escalation package, and send.
Compare with Expected: the ticket is triaged, a reply is drafted, or an escalation is packaged.
items.needs: a Cloud account; a sample support ticket text
items.note: The Support screen reached from About is AGI's own support tickets, not these customer-support workflows. Ticket updates in a helpdesk are not shown in mobile code.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > find recruiting-pipeline or interview-prep > Install > Use in chat
steps: Open Settings and tap Customize.
Tap Skills, find recruiting-pipeline or interview-prep, and tap Install.
Tap Use in chat, or pick the skill from Add to chat > Skills.
Ask for an interview plan with a scorecard, or a recruiting pipeline update, and send.
Compare with Expected: structured interview questions and a scorecard, or pipeline stage status.
items.needs: a Cloud account
items.note: Job posts and candidate records are not shown as separate mobile screens in the code I read.

items.where: Chat > Message input: ask for a trip plan; the itinerary card appears in the reply, with Walking directions in Google Maps as a route link
steps: Open the Chat tab in Cloud mode.
Type a trip request with stops and a route, for example a day in a city, and send.
Look for the itinerary card in the reply with a title, a region and a map.
Tap the route link to open Google Maps directions.
Compare with Expected: an itinerary with places and routes. Reservations are not in the code I read.
items.needs: a Cloud account; the card appears only when the assistant returns one
items.note: No reservation or booking code was found in apps/mobile (searched for reserv, booking, book). The clarifyCard.ts quote is gone, but the itinerary.v1 capability is still listed there.

items.where: Home screen > add widget > AGI Mobile (iPhone widget or Android widget), then tap New chat, Camera or Voice on the widget. Quick-action widget and long-press app shortcuts also list New chat, Voice and Camera. There is no Mac menu-bar item in apps/mobile.
steps: Long-press an empty spot on the home screen and add the AGI Mobile widget (medium size shows New chat, Camera and Voice; small size shows New chat).
Tap New chat on the widget and check that the chat screen opens.
Go back to the home screen, tap Camera on the widget and check that the camera screen opens.
Tap Voice on the widget and check that voice mode opens (or the chat screen if on-device speech recognition is not available).
items.needs: a phone with the AGI Mobile app installed (iPhone or Android); no Mac menu bar exists in this app
items.note: The Expected line mentions a menu bar, which is not in this mobile app; the nearest match is the home-screen widget. The add-widget gesture is an OS step, not from code. Screenshot and quick ask were not found as widget actions.

items.needs: a paired desktop (not available in v1)
items.note: Feature is off in this build: apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts sets companion: false and dispatch: false. The companion screen (apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/index.tsx) returns early when these flags are off, and the Settings Remote control section with Connections is shown only when FEATURES.companion is on. The drawer 'Code' entry only matches the companion path. Nothing reachable found.

items.where: Siri: say 'Talk to AGI Mobile' or 'Ask AGI Mobile' (Siri shortcut 'Ask AGI'). Turn on first: Settings > Security and login > Ask from Siri.
steps: Open Settings, then Security and login, and turn on Ask from Siri (this needs AGI Cloud mode; the switch says to switch to Cloud mode otherwise).
Close the app to the home screen so it is not open.
Activate Siri (hold the side button or say 'Hey Siri') and say 'Talk to AGI Mobile', then say a question.
Check that Siri answers out loud and the answer is saved as a chat, without the app opening.
items.needs: an iPhone with Siri, a signed-in AGI Cloud account, and Ask from Siri turned on
items.note: Found only as Siri ask (AskAGIIntent, no app opening). No keyboard shortcut or Android voice command for global dictation was found. TranscribeIntent ('Transcribe with AGI') transcribes audio recordings, not live dictation. The Siri activation step is an OS step, not from code; the Settings entry label was not confirmed in code.

items.where: iPhone Control Center or Action Button: add the control 'AGI Mobile' (control named Open AGI Mobile); then press the control or Action Button to open AGI Mobile. No Stream Deck or macropad integration was found.
steps: On an iPhone with iOS 18 or later, add the AGI Mobile control to Control Center or the Lock Screen (the OS shows it as Open AGI Mobile).
Assign it to the Action Button if you want a hardware press (OS setting).
Press the control or Action Button with the phone locked or unlocked.
Check that AGI Mobile opens to the app.
items.needs: an iPhone running iOS 18 or later (the control is declared only for iOS 18+); a Stream Deck or macropad is not supported
items.note: Only the iPhone control and Action Button path was found; the Action Button assignment and Control Center add steps are OS steps, not from code. Action Button trigger opens the app only, not a chosen AGI action.

items.where: Siri via headset: say 'Talk to AGI Mobile' (or 'Ask AGI Mobile') with earbuds or a headset connected; turn on first in Settings > Security and login > Ask from Siri.
steps: Open Settings, then Security and login, and turn on Ask from Siri (needs AGI Cloud mode).
Connect the headset or earbuds to the iPhone.
Trigger Siri with the headset button or voice (OS behavior), then say 'Talk to AGI Mobile' and ask a question.
Check that the answer is spoken back and saved as a chat, with the phone not opened.
items.needs: an iPhone with Siri, AGI Cloud signed in, Ask from Siri turned on, and earbuds or a headset
items.note: No AGI-specific headset control was found; the headset trigger is the OS Siri behavior. The Settings entry label was not confirmed in code.

items.where: Settings > General > Models (opens the models screen), then tap a local model row with the Download badge.
steps: Open Settings, then General, then tap Models.
Find an on-device model row showing the Download badge and tap it (tap to download; long press to favourite).
Watch the row while it downloads; the row shows the downloading state (progress appears only in the accessibility label).
Tap Cancel download on the row and check that the download stops and the badge returns.
items.needs: a phone with enough storage for a local model; a Free or paid account (no subscription needed for the local model download)
items.note: No pause control was found. Visible download percentage was not confirmed in code (only in the accessibility label). The Settings entry label was not confirmed in code; the Models row is in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/general/index.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Storage (or Settings > General > Storage), then find Downloaded Models and tap the trash button on a model row.
steps: Open Settings, then Storage (or General, then Storage).
Read the Downloaded models (estimated) row and the Estimated size under each model in Downloaded Models.
Tap the trash button on a model row and read the Delete dialog that names the model.
Tap Delete and check that the model is removed and the Downloaded models (estimated) total goes down.
items.needs: at least one downloaded local model
items.note: The trash button has no visible text; it is named Delete <model> for assistive technology. The Settings entry label was not confirmed in code.

items.where: Settings > General > Performance, then read the Capabilities row (tier label, RAM and runtimes).
steps: Open Settings, then General, then tap Performance.
Read the tier badge and description at the top of the screen (device tier and ExecuTorch needs 3.5 GB RAM note).
Find the RAM row and compare it with the device's memory.
Find the Capabilities row and check the listed runtimes (AICore, ExecuTorch, llama.rn or Apple FM).
items.needs: none (reads the device; a local model is not needed to see the panel)
items.note: The Settings entry label was not confirmed in code; the Performance row is in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/general/index.tsx.

items.where: Settings > General > Performance, then tap Load (or Unload local models) under the selected local model.
steps: Open Settings, then General, then tap Performance.
Read the status line under the selected model (Not loaded; an installed model loads on use).
Tap Load and wait; the status changes to Loaded in memory.
Tap Unload local models and check the status returns to not loaded.
items.needs: a downloaded local model selected on the Performance screen
items.note: The button shows Load when no model is in memory and Unload local models when one is loaded; the Settings entry label was not confirmed in code.

items.where: Settings > General > Performance, then read the status line under the local model (Loaded in memory, Working…, or Failed to load/unload with the message).
steps: Open Settings, then General, then tap Performance.
Read the status line under the selected local model.
Tap Load; while it works the status shows Working….
Check the result: Loaded in memory when healthy, or a Failed to ... message with the error text when the runtime fails.
items.needs: a downloaded local model; a failure needs a model that cannot load (for example one that is not on the device)
items.note: No separate health indicator was found; health is shown only through this status line and the Failed to message. The Settings entry label was not confirmed in code.

items.where: Settings > General > Performance, then scroll to the stats rows (avg tok/s, avg TTFT, mem peak, thermal) and the Run Benchmark button.
steps: Open Settings, then General, then tap Performance.
Use a local model for a reply, or tap Run Benchmark, to create data.
Scroll to the stats rows: avg tok/s, avg TTFT, mem peak and thermal.
Compare the tok/s and TTFT values with the reply; mem peak may show no value because no runtime reports peak memory.
items.needs: a downloaded local model, and at least one local reply or a benchmark run
items.note: Partial: peak memory stays 0 because no runtime reports it and no memory sampler is installed; it is shown as a value only when above 0. The exact conditions for showing each stats row were not fully traced.

items.where: Chat > open a chat artifact card > Share generated file (the presentation is requested from the + (Add to chat) sheet, where the output format option is; its visible label was not found)
steps: Open a chat that has a generated file or artifact card.
Tap the artifact card to open the artifact screen.
Look for the file card showing the file name, kind and checksum.
Tap Share generated file (or Download artifact) to keep a copy.
Compare with Expected: a presentation opens or can be shared and kept.
items.needs: a chat that produced a presentation or a file, or a request for a presentation
items.note: Presentation (pptx) support is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/generatedFileArtifacts.ts and GeneratedFileCard.tsx; the visible name of the output-format option in the + sheet was not located, so the exact creation step is unverified.

items.needs: a spreadsheet file and a web account with E2B execution enabled
items.note: Chart artifacts open on the phone in the artifact screen (testID artifact-fullscreen-chart at apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:1886, not visible text). The chart-in-report step is web-side: apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts gates on AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1 and E2B_API_KEY. No mobile control that builds the report with a chart was found, and the spreadsheet upload control was not located.

items.where: Chat screen > Start voice mode (microphone button in the composer) > Start voice > speak the request > Work switch (Work) > AGI Work list in the side menu
steps: Open a chat and tap the Start voice mode button in the composer.
Tap Start voice (or pick a voice first) and allow the microphone.
Say a task, for example a request that needs several steps and tools.
Watch for the Work mode message the phone sends into the chat, then open the side menu and tap AGI Work.
Compare with Expected: the request appears as a task in AGI Work without retyping it.
items.needs: a microphone, a signed-in cloud account, and AGI Work available on the account
items.note: The voice tool agi_work (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/live-voice-tools.ts) only starts the task when the chat can request AGI Work (canUseAgiWork); the plan that grants it was not confirmed.

items.where: Side menu > chat list (cloud mode) > the conversation title
steps: Sign in with the same account on the web app and start a chat there.
On the phone, open the side menu and check the chat list in cloud mode.
Open the web conversation and confirm the full earlier history is shown.
Send a follow-up message on the phone.
Open the web app again and check the reply appears in the same conversation (compare with Expected).
items.needs: a web account and the same account signed in on the phone, with network access
items.note: The cloud header label comes from a constant (PRIVACY_MODE_DISPLAY.managed.label) in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/ChatsListScreen.tsx, and the side-menu open control and New chat key were not located. The label above appears only for untitled chats.

items.where: Side menu > AGI Code (or Settings > Remote control > Connections) > the paired computer > Start on Desktop
steps: Make sure a computer is paired and connected (Settings > Remote control > Connections).
Open the side menu and tap AGI Code, then open the paired computer.
In the Start on Desktop box, type a request in the field that says What should Desktop work on?.
Tap the send control and wait.
Look under Recent Dispatch tasks for the task and expand its result to check it matches Expected.
items.needs: a paired and connected desktop computer, a signed-in account, and Remote Control on the plan
items.note: The send control's visible label was not found and the desktop's approval rules are applied on the computer; the settings page says Remote Control comes with paid plans (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/remote-control.tsx).

items.where: Chat > + (Add to chat) > Project (shows Choose or the project name)
steps: Create or open a project under Projects in the side menu and add a source or instruction.
Open a new chat and tap the + (Add to chat) button in the composer.
Tap Project and choose the project; the row shows its name in place of Choose.
Ask a question that the project's sources should answer.
Compare the answer with the project's sources and instructions (Expected).
items.needs: an existing project with sources or instructions
items.note: The Projects side-menu label is a translation key (navProjects) whose text was not found, and the grounding of answers in project sources was not traced to a visible control.

items.where: Chat > send a message when usage is used up > paywall sheet > Choose a standard model or View upgrade options
steps: Send a message on an account that has reached its usage limit.
Read the sheet: it names the blocked feature and the reset time if one applies.
If offered, tap Choose a standard model to continue with a standard model in one step.
Otherwise tap View upgrade options (or Choose a plan) and check the plan options shown.
Compare with Expected: an eligible alternative is offered and can be taken in one step.
items.needs: a Free account or an account at its usage limit
items.note: Which option appears depends on the server's quota error code (classifyManagedQuotaErrorCode in apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx); the reset-time wording was not checked, and purchase options vary by platform.

items.where: Open a chat artifact > More artifact actions > Republish artifact link (or Publish artifact to a public link) > Edit source > Save as a new version > Version N of M > Restore version N
steps: Open a chat artifact and tap More artifact actions, then Publish artifact to a public link and confirm Publish.
Tap Edit source, change the text, and tap Save as a new version.
Tap More artifact actions again and tap Republish artifact link; confirm the same link updates.
Tap Show changes and use the version counter (Previous version / Next version) to compare versions.
Tap Restore version to go back to an earlier version, then check the link and version history (Expected).
items.needs: a signed-in cloud account and an artifact that can be published
items.note: Edit source is shown only when the artifact can be edited; Restore version is an accessibility label built from a template in ArtifactFullScreen.tsx, and the version history sheet is apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactVersionHistorySheet.tsx.
